Discrepancy on dyadic partitions with each edge charged at its own level

16 October 2026 · Working proof; two-level test not decided · Telescoping over levels. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The entry adds a tool lemma and leaves the test undecided; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. Can a cell function on an arbitrary dyadic partition pay each edge only its own scale's Leighton–Shor factor? The log-log deviation entry's reviewer sketched telescoping the function over levels with a local contraction of block averages; this entry proves it and uses it on the third route review's two-level test. The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\).

General statement. lem:local-factor-discrepancy, for every partition of the square into dyadic squares down to the Leighton–Shor scale and every function constant on its cells; and, for Lipschitz functions, every such partition in which neighbouring cells differ in side by a factor at most \(2\).

Local-factor discrepancy

Setting. \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), \(\ell_1\) the Leighton–Shor scale. A dyadic partition \(\mathcal P\) is a partition of \([0,1]^2\) into dyadic squares of sides \(2^{-i}\), \(1\le i\le\ell_1\); its edges are the maximal segments of cell sides containing no cell vertex inside, so an inner edge has the length of the smaller of its two cells, \(\ell(e)=2^{-i(e)}\). For \(H\) constant on the cells, \(\Delta_eH\) is the jump across an inner edge \(e\), and for an open set \(U\), \(|DH|(U)=\sum\ell(e)|\Delta_eH|\) over the inner edges inside \(U\). Write \(F(i)=i^{3/4}+(2+\log_2i)\sqrt{\log\log N}\), at most \(i^{3/4}+C(\log\log N)^{3/2}\) for \(i\le\ell_1\). \(\mathcal P\) is balanced if neighbouring cells (sharing a side segment) differ in side by a factor at most \(2\).

Statement. There is a universal \(L\) such that with probability tending to one: (a) for every dyadic partition \(\mathcal P\) and every \(H\) constant on its cells, \[\Big|\sum_{i\le N}H(X_i)-N\int H\Big|\le L\sqrt N\sum_{e\text{ inner}}\ell(e)\,|\Delta_eH|\,F(i(e));\] (b) for every balanced dyadic partition and every Lipschitz \(G\), \[\Big|\sum_{i\le N}G(X_i)-N\int G\Big|\le L\sqrt N\sum_{Q\in\mathcal P}F(i(Q))\int_Q(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)+L\sqrt{N\log N}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\,\lambda(Q),\] \(i(Q)\) the level of the cell \(Q\).

Proof. We work on the intersection of the events of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation (for lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy at every pair of meshes, with factors at most \(f(j)=2j^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log\log N}\)), of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, and of the per-cell event in the proof of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, which covers every dyadic square of side at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\) (at most \(2N\) of them).

Three deterministic inequalities. They are one-dimensional variation arguments and hold for any \(H\) of bounded variation, with \(|DH|_1(U)=|D_1H|(U)+|D_2H|(U)\) (for a cell function the edge sum above, for a Lipschitz function \(\int_U(|\partial_1H|+|\partial_2H|)\)); the squares below are dyadic. (A) For a dyadic square \(B\) of side \(s\) and squares \(R_t\subset B\) of sides \(s_t\) along one side \(\sigma\) of \(B\), with disjoint projections onto \(\sigma\): \(\sum_ts_t|\operatorname{avg}_{R_t}H-\operatorname{avg}_BH|\le|DH|_1(B)\). Proof: for almost every \(x\in\sigma\), let \(h_x\) be \(H\) along the segment of \(B\) perpendicular to \(\sigma\) at \(x\), \(m(x)\) its average and \(\operatorname{Var}\) the variation; then \(|h_x(t)-\operatorname{avg}_BH|\le\operatorname{Var}(h_x)+|m(x)-\frac1s\int m|\le\operatorname{Var}(h_x)+\operatorname{Var}(m)\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(m)\le\frac1s\int_0^s\operatorname{Var}(\text{row at depth }t)\,dt\). Averaging over \(R_t\) and multiplying by \(s_t\) gives \(s_t|\operatorname{avg}_{R_t}H-\operatorname{avg}_BH|\le\int_{\pi(R_t)}(\operatorname{Var}(h_x)+\operatorname{Var}(m))\,dx\); summing over \(t\), \(\le\int_\sigma\operatorname{Var}(h_x)\,dx+s\operatorname{Var}(m)\le|D_\perp H|(B)+|D_\parallel H|(B)=|DH|(B)\). (B) For two adjacent squares \(R,R'\) of side \(s\) sharing a side: \(s|\operatorname{avg}_RH-\operatorname{avg}_{R'}H|\le|DH|(R\cup R'\cup\text{shared side})\), by the translation sweep. (C) For adjacent squares \(Q\) of side \(s\) and \(q\) of side \(s_q\le s\), with \(R\subset Q\) the square of side \(s_q\) beside \(q\): \(s_q|\operatorname{avg}_QH-\operatorname{avg}_qH|\le s_q|\operatorname{avg}_QH-\operatorname{avg}_RH|+|DH|(R\cup q\cup e)\), by (B); summed over the \(q\) along one side of \(Q\), the first terms are at most \(|DH|(Q)\) by (A).

Telescoping. Let \(j_k=\min(2^{k-1},\ell_1)\), \(k=1,\dots,m\), \(m=\lceil\log_2\ell_1\rceil+1\). Let \(\mathcal P_k\) consist of the cells of \(\mathcal P\) of side at least \(2^{-j_k}\) and the dyadic squares of side \(2^{-j_k}\) that contain smaller cells (the refined blocks of level \(k\)), and \(H_k\) the averages of \(H\) on \(\mathcal P_k\); \(H_m=H\), and \(H=H_1+\sum_{k\ge2}D_k\), \(D_k=H_k-H_{k-1}\). \(D_k\) vanishes on every cell of \(\mathcal P\) of side at least \(2^{-j_{k-1}}\); on a refined block \(B\) of level \(k-1\) it is \(H_k-\operatorname{avg}_BH\). So \(D_k\) is constant on a graded partition with sides in \([2^{-j_k},2^{-j_{k-1}}]\) (the cells of \(\mathcal P_k\) inside refined blocks, and the cells of \(\mathcal G_{j_{k-1}}\) elsewhere), on whose coarse edges it is \(0\) on both sides. lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy with \(c=0\) and the smaller deviation gives \(|\sum_iD_k(X_i)-N\int D_k|\le2L\sqrt Nf(j_k)V^0(D_k)\). The jumps of \(D_k\): inside a refined block \(B\), those of \(H_k\), bounded by (B) and (C) applied to averages of \(H\) over the cells of \(\mathcal P_k\) in \(B\); on \(\partial B\) and on \(\partial[0,1]^2\), the two values \(H_k(q)-\operatorname{avg}_BH\) on either side, each summed along the side by (A). Each cell has four sides, so \(V^0(D_k)\le C\sum_B|DH|(B)\), over the refined blocks \(B\) of level \(k-1\). An inner edge \(e\) of \(\mathcal P\) inside such a \(B\) lies between cells smaller than \(B\), so \(i(e)>j_{k-1}\); hence \(e\) is counted only for levels \(k\le\kappa(e)\), \(\kappa(e)\) the least \(k\) with \(j_k\ge i(e)\), once each. Since \(j_\kappa\le2i(e)\) and the \(j_k\) double up to the cap at \(\ell_1\), \(\sum_{k\le\kappa}2j_k^{3/4}\le2j_\kappa^{3/4}+2j_{\kappa-1}^{3/4}/(1-2^{-3/4})\le C\,i(e)^{3/4}\); and \(\kappa\le\log_2i(e)+2\), so \(\sum_{k\le\kappa}\sqrt{\log\log N}\le(2+\log_2i(e))\sqrt{\log\log N}\). Finally \(H_1\) is constant on the four quarters: by lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b) with the smaller deviation and its part (c), \(|\sum_iH_1(X_i)-N\int H|\le L\sqrt Nf(1)\cdot4V^{\mathrm{in}}_1(H_1)\), and (B) bounds \(V^{\mathrm{in}}_1(H_1)\) by \(2|DH|([0,1]^2)\). Summing gives (a).

Part (b). Write \(G=E_{\mathcal P}G+R\). For the averages, (B) and (C) applied to \(G\) (whose \(|DG|_1\) is \(\int(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)\)) bound each jump \(\ell(e)|\Delta_eE_{\mathcal P}G|\) by a constant times the gradient mass of the two cells beside \(e\), each charged at most a bounded number of times; in a balanced partition \(i(e)\) is within \(1\) of the levels of both cells, so (a) gives the first term. The remainder is bounded cell by cell exactly as in lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, whose per-cell event covers every cell of \(\mathcal P\): \(|\sum_{X_i\in Q}R(X_i)|\le L\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\sqrt{N\log N}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(X_i\) i.i.d. uniform and cells of side at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\): the events used, through lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy, lem:mesh-function-discrepancy and the per-cell bound. \(H\) constant on cells: the layer cakes inside those lemmas. Dyadic cells: the coarsenings \(\mathcal P_k\) are partitions because dyadic squares are nested or disjoint. Balance, in (b) only: to compare the factor of an edge with those of its two cells, and to bound the multiplicity with which each cell's gradient mass is charged when each jump is bounded separately. (A) does not need \(H\) constant on cells (it holds for functions of bounded variation), and in (b) the remainder needs \(G\) Lipschitz only on each cell; for such \(G\) the same proof holds with the jumps of \(G\) across edges added to \(|DG|_1\) at their edges' factors. The conclusions hold for all partitions and functions simultaneously. Two items the two-mesh partition entry left open are settled here: the per-cell remainder on mixed partitions (the per-cell event covers every dyadic square down to the scale), and the boundary ring on mixed partitions, which (a) does not need since it has no boundary term.

Baseline. The bound needing no idea is lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b) at the finest mesh the partition uses, \(2^{-j_{\max}}\): every edge then pays \(j_{\max}^{3/4}\). This lemma adds that each edge pays only its own level's factor, so coarse parts of a partition are charged as if the fine parts were absent.

Degenerate cases. \(\mathcal P=\mathcal G_j\): every inner edge has \(i(e)=j\), and (a) is lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b) with the smaller deviation and the ring absorbed, up to \((2+\log_2j)\sqrt{\log\log N}\) in place of \(\sqrt{\log\log N}\); at small \(j\) it is weaker than lem:loglog-mesh-deviation's (b) by that \(\log j\). \(H\) constant: both sides vanish. A partition with one tiny cell: only the edges of that cell pay its factor.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters, for context (the lemma does not depend on the pair), with \(N\) large: \(\mathcal P\) the four quarters with the lower left one replaced by its cells of side \(2^{-j}\), \(j=\lfloor\frac13\log_2N\rfloor\), and \(H\) the indicator of the upper right quarter plus that of the lower left cell of side \(2^{-j}\): its inner edges are the two inner sides of the upper right quarter, of factor \(F(1)\), and the two inner sides of the small cell, of factor \(F(j)\), so (a) gives at most \(L\sqrt N(F(1)+2\cdot2^{-j}F(j))\), where lem:mesh-function-discrepancy at mesh \(2^{-j}\) charges the quarter's sides \(j^{3/4}\). For (b): \(\mathcal P\) the four quarters (balanced) and \(G(x)=x_1\); the bound is \(L\sqrt NF(1)+L\sqrt{N\log N}\).

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The third route review's test (the class bound at \((4,4)\) for two gradient levels \(y_1<y_2\), constant independent of the levels) was attempted with part (b); neither outcome occurred, and the attempt located the remaining condition. Take a balanced partition whose cells have level about \(j^*(y_2)\) on the level-\(y_2\) support \(S_2\), about \(j^*(y_1)\) on the rest of the level-\(y_1\) support \(S_1\) (with \(j^*(y)=\min(\ell_1,\lfloor(\log N)^{2/3}(\log y)^{1/3}\rfloor)\) as in lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split), and graded rings between. By order estimates (constants not computed): at its own level each part pays \(F(j^*(y))\le C\sqrt{\log N}(\log y)^{1/4}\) per unit of gradient mass, within a constant of its cost weight \((\log y)^{1/4}\) times \(\sqrt{\log N}\), so the first term of (b) is of order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) times the cost, except for the level-\(y_1\) mass lying in ring cells of level above \(j^*(y_1)\), which pays \(F(i)\) there; the second term is of order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) times the cost when each level's support is thick at its own cell size, as in lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split. So the two-level bound follows, at constant independent of the levels, under two conditions: (i) thickness of each support at its cell size, and (ii) the ring term \(\sum_{i>j^*(y_1)}F(i)\int_{\text{cells of level }i}|\nabla G|_1\) on \(S_1\) of order \(\sqrt{\log N}(\log y_1)^{1/4}y_1\lambda(S_1)\). Condition (ii) can fail: for a level-\(y_1\) ramp with \(y_1\) bounded and \(n\) level-\(y_2\) bumps spread at spacing \(n^{-1/2}\) finer than \(2^{-j^*(y_1)}\), the rings cover the square up to level about \(\frac12\log_2n\), and the ramp's mass pays about \((\log n)^{3/4}\), above \(\sqrt{\log N}(\log y_1)^{1/4}\) by up to \((\log N)^{1/4}\) when \(n\) is a power of \(N\) (an order computation, not a lower bound on the discrepancy). No partition avoids this in (b) when the bumps' total area is small (the reviewer's check, unverified): a cell of side \(2^{-j^*(y_1)}\) containing bumps pays \(y_2\) times its area in the second term of (b), so cells are forced down to the bump spacing; this concerns the bound (b), not every method. In that example the discrepancy is linear in \(G\): \(G\) is the ramp plus the bumps, each piece satisfies (i) and (ii) alone, and the costs add up to a constant, not by alignment (the bump gradients change sign) but because off the bumps \(G\) is the ramp, on them \(|\nabla G|\ge|\nabla(\text{bump})|/2\) once \(y_2\gg y_1\), and \(\psi_4^*(2s)\le C\psi_4^*(s)\) for large \(s\). The thickness condition (i) is a different matter: a single band of level \(y\) and width \(2^{-j}\) with \(j^*(y)<j\le\ell_1\) along a long curve keeps a fixed fraction of its gradient on a thin set under every split into boundedly many pieces (the reviewer's observation, unverified), so the upper bound pays \(j^{3/4}/(\sqrt{\log N}(\log y)^{1/4})>1\) times the target there; whether the discrepancy reaches that is what lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound (vertically scaled tents) and lem:band-overlap-penalty (band functions) bear on. It stopped there: whether every class function splits into pieces satisfying (ii) with costs adding up to a constant was not decided, and whether thin bands beyond \(j^*(y)\) exceed the target, which would make thickness a property of the class rather than of the method, was not checked against those two lemmas.

New mathematics. lem:local-factor-discrepancy: on any dyadic partition down to the Leighton–Shor scale, a cell function's discrepancy is at most \(L\sqrt N\) times the sum over inner edges of length times jump times \(F(i(e))=i(e)^{3/4}+(2+\log_2i(e))\sqrt{\log\log N}\), the edge's own level's factor; and, for a Lipschitz function on a balanced partition, the same with each cell's gradient mass at its own level's factor plus the cellwise Lipschitz term.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), for every Lipschitz \(G\) and balanced dyadic partition, \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le L\sqrt N\sum_QF(i(Q))\int_Q|\nabla G|_1+L\sqrt{N\log N}\sum_Q\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\). Not covered. The choice of partition for a general class function and the comparison of both terms with its cost, and the conversion to the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\).

Dominant-level split and its bound on the Leighton–Shor witness

16 October 2026 · Working proof; against Lebesgue measure · Thin bands. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The entry adds a refinement and a witness check; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The local-factor discrepancy entry's attempt needed each gradient level's support to be thick at its cell size, and its reviewer asked whether the class lower bound's tents are thin bands beyond the mesh \(j^*(y)\), which would make thickness a property of the class. The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\); this entry states the single-level bound in terms of the cellwise Lipschitz sum directly and evaluates it on the lower bound's witness.

General statement. lem:dominant-level-split, for every Lipschitz function of the class at \((4,4)\) whose larger partial is at least \(y\) on its gradient's support, and every mesh up to \(j^*(y)\).

Dominant-level split

Statement. There is a universal \(L\) such that with probability tending to one, for \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\): for every \(y\ge e^{16}\), every \(j\) with \(1\le j\le j^*(y)=\min(\ell_1,\lfloor(\log N)^{2/3}(\log y)^{1/3}\rfloor)\), and every Lipschitz \(G\) with \(\int\sum_i\psi^*_4(|\partial_iG|)\le2\) and \(\max(|\partial_1G|,|\partial_2G|)\ge y\) almost everywhere where \(\nabla G\ne0\), \[\Big|\sum_{i\le N}G(X_i)-N\int G\Big|\le L\sqrt{N\log N}\,\big(1+\Lambda_j(G)\big),\] \(\Lambda_j(G)=\sum_Q\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\) over the cells of mesh \(2^{-j}\). The same holds with \(\Lambda_j\) replaced by \(\sum_Q\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\) over the cells of any balanced dyadic partition whose cells have level at most \(j^*(y)\), by lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) in place of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, the gradient-mass step being unchanged.

Proof. On the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, the discrepancy is at most \(8L\sqrt N(j^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\|\nabla G\|_1+L\sqrt{N\log N}\Lambda_j(G)\). Where \(\nabla G\ne0\), the larger partial \(t\) is at least \(y\ge e^{16}\), so \(\psi^*_4(t)\ge\frac12t(\log t)^{1/4}\ge\frac12t(\log y)^{1/4}\) (as in that lemma's corollary), and \(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|\le2t\le4\psi_4^*(t)(\log y)^{-1/4}\le4(\log y)^{-1/4}\sum_i\psi_4^*(|\partial_iG|)\); so \(\|\nabla G\|_1\le8(\log y)^{-1/4}\). For \(j\le j^*(y)\), \(j^{3/4}(\log y)^{-1/4}\le\sqrt{\log N}\), and the first term is at most \(128L\sqrt{N\log N}\) (the step uses \(\log t\ge\log y\)); on a balanced partition the first term of lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) is at most \(\sum_QF(i(Q))\int_Q|\nabla G|_1\le F(j^*(y))\|\nabla G\|_1\), bounded the same way. \(\square\) It refines the corollary of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split: that corollary asked each partial to lie in \(\{0\}\cup[y,2y]\) and bounded \(\Lambda_j\) through a thickness ratio; here only the larger partial is constrained, and \(\Lambda_j\) is kept.

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(X_i\) i.i.d. uniform and \(j\le\ell_1\): the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, intersected for the partition version with that of lem:local-factor-discrepancy. The class's cost and the larger partial at least \(y\ge e^{16}\): the bound on \(\|\nabla G\|_1\). \(j\le j^*(y)\): the first term's comparison with \(\sqrt{\log N}\). \(G\) Lipschitz: \(\Lambda_j\) finite and that lemma's corollary. The conclusion holds for all such \(y\), \(j\) and \(G\) simultaneously.

Baseline. The bound needing no idea for the lemma is lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split itself with \(\|\nabla G\|_1\) left as it is; the lemma adds that the class's cost, through the larger partial, makes that term of the target's order for every mesh up to \(j^*(y)\), so only \(\Lambda_j(G)\) remains to compare. For the witness below there is an elementary baseline (the reviewer's): it is \((A/w)\int_0^w1_{S(f+u)}\,du\), so its discrepancy is at most \(A\sup_u|\sum_i1_{S(f+u)}(X_i)-N\lambda(S(f+u))|\); rounding each hypograph to the union of the cells of mesh \(2^{-\ell_1}\) below its graph costs at most the points and area of the cells meeting the graph, of order \(Nm\), and the union's boundary has length \(O(1)\) since \(\int|f'|\le1\), so lem:mesh-function-discrepancy at \(j=\ell_1\) gives \(O(A\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4})=O(\sqrt{N\log N})\). The split's bound on the witness is therefore a check of the method, not new information about that function.

The lower bound's witness

Example. The witness of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound at \((4,4)\) (its Step 2: \(\kappa=1\), \(w=\delta\) the reduction's grid side, \(A=(\log N)^{-1/4}/2\), \(G=A\min\{1,\max\{0,(f(x)+w-y)/w\}\}\) over the Leighton–Shor graph \(f\)) satisfies the hypotheses with \(y=A/w\), and \(\Lambda_{\ell_1}(G)\le297/L\le2.25\) for \(L\ge132\) and \(N\) large, so it has \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le3.25L'\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(L'\) the lemma's constant: the split is of the conjectured order on this witness, against Lebesgue measure.

Proof. On the band \(\partial_2G=-A/w\) and \(\partial_1G=Af'/w\), so the larger partial is at least \(y=A/w\); \(s/33\le w=\delta\le s/32\) with \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), so \(y\ge\frac{16}L\sqrt N(\log N)^{-3/4}\) and \(\log y\ge\frac12\log N-\log\log N\) for large \(N\), which gives \(y\ge e^{16}\) and \((\log N)^{2/3}(\log y)^{1/3}\ge0.78\log N>\ell_1\), so \(j^*(y)=\ell_1\). Let \(m=2^{-\ell_1}\); since \(\ell_1\) is the largest integer with \(2^{-\ell_1}\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) (the setting of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy), \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\le m\le2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), and \(w\le\frac L{32}\sqrt{\log N/N}<m\) for large \(N\). On a column of cells of width \(m\) where \(f'\) is constant, equal to \(\sigma\), the band meets at most \(3+|\sigma|\) cells, each with \(\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\le(A/w)(1+|\sigma|)\). The breakpoints of \(f\) lie on the grid \(2^{-cr-1}\mathbb Z\) with \(2^{cr}\le N^{1/100}\), so at most \(4N^{1/100}+2\) columns contain one (a breakpoint on a column boundary counted in both), each contributing at most \(3(A/w)m^2(1+\sqrt r)^2\) with \(r\le\log N\) (a breakpoint on a column boundary counted in both columns). So \[\Lambda_{\ell_1}(G)\le\frac Awm\Big(\int_0^1(1+|f'|)(3+|f'|)\,dx+12N^{1/100}m(1+\sqrt{\log N})^2\Big)\le\frac Awm\,(8+o(1))\le9\frac Awm\] for large \(N\), using \(\int|f'|\le(\int f'^2)^{1/2}\le1\). And \(\frac Awm\le\frac{(\log N)^{-1/4}}2\cdot\frac{33}{L}\sqrt{\frac N{\log N}}\cdot\frac{2(\log N)^{3/4}}{\sqrt N}=\frac{33}L\). \(\square\)

Degenerate cases. \(G\) constant: \(\Lambda_j=0\) and both sides vanish. \(G\) at a single gradient level with a support thick at the mesh: \(\Lambda_j(G)\le2\sqrt2y\lambda(U_j)\), and the bound is the corollary of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split. All gradients below \(e^{16}\): excluded; such \(G\) is \(e^{16}\sqrt2\)-Lipschitz and (4.38) bounds it directly. Functions with some gradients below \(y\) and some above are excluded by the hypothesis on the larger partial.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\): the lower bound's witness above, with \(L\ge132\) and \(N\) large, satisfies every hypothesis, with \(y=A/\delta\), \(j=\ell_1=j^*(y)\) and \(\Lambda_{\ell_1}\le2.25\).

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The third route review's test (two gradient levels at \((4,4)\), constant independent of the levels) was not decided; this entry examined the thickness condition the previous attempt left. It is replaced by the condition \(\Lambda_j(G)=O(1)\) at some mesh up to \(j^*\), which the class lower bound's witness meets although it is thinner than every allowed mesh. Where the condition fails, by an order computation (constants not computed): a band of width \(w\) near \(\delta\) at a small gradient level \(y\) has amplitude \(yw\), so the cost allows total length about \(1/(yw(\log y)^{1/4})\), many parallel or separate bands; at mesh \(2^{-j}\), \(\Lambda_j\) is about \((2^{-j}/w)(\log y)^{-1/4}\), and lowering it to \(O(1)\) needs \(j\) near \(\ell_1\), where the first term of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split exceeds the target by about \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\). That excess is of the upper bound, and the layer-cake bound (total variation of the profile times the Leighton–Shor set bound) has the same excess, so it is not specific to the split (the reviewer's check). Whether such families have discrepancy beyond \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) is a superposition question. Part (1) of lem:aligned-superposition-bound, the exact convex inequality, bears on it and reduces stacks of bands aligned in both partials to single bands (or does so at the penalty \(\sigma\) where their partials disagree in sign, cf. lem:band-overlap-penalty); its part (2), the \(1+o(1)\) gain, needs gradients at least \(N^\theta\) and does not apply at small levels; lem:band-overlap-penalty concerns bands of one vertical orientation and says nothing about alternating slopes. The reviewer's computation, unverified, settles one family: a sawtooth on one Leighton–Shor graph with teeth no wider than \(\delta\) has discrepancy \(O(\sqrt{N\log N})\); what remains is teeth of width between \(\delta\) and the mesh, and bands on many distinct graphs with alternating signs. It stopped there.

New mathematics. lem:dominant-level-split: for class functions at \((4,4)\) whose larger partial is at least \(y\) on their gradient's support, the discrepancy against Lebesgue measure is at most \(L\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\Lambda_j(G))\) for every mesh up to \(j^*(y)\); on the class lower bound's witness \(\Lambda_{\ell_1}\le297/L\), so the split is of the conjectured order there.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), the class lower bound's single thin band is within the split's reach: it is bounded against Lebesgue measure at the order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\). Not covered. A method's bound was computed on an example before the plainest bound, which gives the same; a more general recorded version, listed by the resemblance tool, was not read as such; a dependency was cited beyond its hypotheses. Prevention. tools/claim_resemblance.py now prints, under each claim's matches, a line asking whether each listed statement is more general or a special case; AGENTS.md now asks for an example's own baseline before the method's bound on it; citing beyond hypotheses falls under the reviewer audit already in .claude/agents/medium-reviewer.md, which caught it.

Fourth route review: thin bands cheap, plateau scale gains open

16 October 2026 · Goal-level route review; no statement registered · Fourth route review. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A review proves nothing; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

The line's general claim. The thread tests Talagrand's Ultimate Matching Conjecture (conj:ultimate-matching) on its curve through the sufficient class bound conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy. Since the third review the line has worked that review's candidate coarea mechanism: bound a class function's discrepancy by splitting it into cell averages on a partition adapted to its gradient levels, charged at Leighton–Shor factors truncated at each scale, and a cellwise Lipschitz remainder.

What the goal needs. One matching at every pair of the curve with one universal \(L\), or a refutation at one pair; in the route's terms, the class bound at \(\frac L2\sqrt{N\log N}\) for every class function, at every pair, for the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\).

The six entries

The mesh-function discrepancy truncates the Leighton–Shor bound at a mesh \(2^{-j}\) (factor \(j^{3/4}\), and for a curve the logarithm of its length in mesh units) and bounds the boundary ring. The cellwise Lipschitz split bounds any Lipschitz function by its averaged part plus \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) times its cellwise Lipschitz sum. The two-mesh partition and log-log deviation entries prepare the local-factor discrepancy: on any dyadic partition each edge pays only its own level's factor \(i^{3/4}+(2+\log_2i)\sqrt{\log\log N}\). The dominant-level split bounds single-level class functions at \((4,4)\) at the conjectured order when their cellwise Lipschitz sum is bounded at an allowed mesh, which the class lower bound's thin witness meets. Each entry reported the third review's two-level test not decided; each left the goal unchanged.

Falsification attempt. The class lower bound's witness was checked against the split and is bounded at the conjectured order, by the split and by an elementary layer-cake bound; a sawtooth of thin bands on one Leighton–Shor graph is bounded by the dominant-level entry's reviewer's computation, unverified. No function beyond the target was found; the families left open (many thin bands of one small gradient level on distinct graphs with alternating signs; a small-gradient ramp under dense bumps at the ring condition) are ones the upper bounds do not reach, with no lower bound computed for them.

Assessment of this line. The line now has, for the first time, an upper-bound mechanism above exponent \(2\) that is proved in pieces: every edge charged its own scale's factor, single-level functions of bounded cellwise sum at the target order, the lower bound's witness inside its reach. It has not closed the assembly: functions whose cellwise sum is large at every allowed mesh are open, as is the ring condition at several levels, and the result is against Lebesgue measure, not yet the class's smeared measures. The open-item count stays at four, as at the second review twelve research entries back, so this review is goal-level; but unlike the previous period the open steps are sharply posed (superposition at one level, the ring condition at several, the smearing conversion) rather than an absent mechanism.

Obstacle

The line is stuck on superposition at one gradient level: a class function made of many thin bands of a small gradient level, on distinct Leighton–Shor graphs and with alternating signs, has cellwise Lipschitz sum large at every allowed mesh, and both the split and the layer-cake bound exceed the target on it by up to \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\); whether its discrepancy does is unknown. The same question appears at several levels as the ring condition. The record's superposition results apply only to aligned members (lem:aligned-superposition-bound part (1)) or to large gradients (its part (2)).

Outside leads

  • Hammersley's process and the Vershik–Kerov and Logan–Shepp theorem (recalled, not read here: the longest increasing path through \(N\) uniform points has about \(2\sqrt N\) points), with Baik–Deift–Johansson's fluctuation theorem behind it. Translation: the discrepancy of a strip of width \(d\) along an adaptively chosen curve is a last-passage value, a sum of local gains along the path; a hypograph instead accumulates gains at every scale from \(1\) down. It targets conjugate-class-discrepancy at the obstacle's thin bands. Answers. If strips carry only local gains, a thin band of width \(d\) and amplitude \(a\) along a curve of length \(\ell\) has discrepancy about \(a\ell\sqrt N\) times a factor depending on \(d\sqrt N\) only, not on \(N\) at fixed \(d\sqrt N\), so many thin bands on distinct graphs would cost \(\sqrt N\sum_ka_k\ell_k\) times that factor, against the \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\) excess of the split and the layer-cake bound. Test. Not run for the translation: the computation made could not have failed. Computation (research/results/ultimate_matching_review4_20261016/strip_dp.py, expectations committed before the run; output strip_dp.json and strip_dp-run.txt): \(N=2^{12},2^{14},\dots,2^{22}\) uniform points, four seeds, an \(M\times M\) grid with \(M=\sqrt N/2\), paths taking one row per column with row changes of at most one, the maximal excess over \(\sqrt N\) of a strip of \(q\) rows above the path and of the hypograph below it (medians). At \(q=4\) the strip's value is \(1.758\) at \(2^{12}\) and \(1.776\) at \(2^{22}\) (ratio \(1.010\); \(q=1,2,8\): \(0.918\), \(0.948\), \(1.080\)), while the hypograph, the positive control, grows from \(1.438\) to \(2.020\) (ratio \(1.405\)); at \(2^{22}\) the strip's value rises by about \(0.27\) per doubling of \(q\) (\(1.227\), \(1.511\), \(1.776\), \(2.043\), \(2.306\) for \(q=1,\dots,16\)). Both written expectations held, but the first was fixed in advance (the stage-two reviewer's finding): at fixed \(q\) the bare count (points in the strip plus \(N\) times its area, area \(2q/\sqrt N\)) bounds the strip's excess by about \(4q\sqrt N\) uniformly in \(N\), so no growth in \(N\) could appear; only the \(30\%\) band was a numerical test. The strips also lie at or below the class's grid side (\(d\sqrt N=2q\le32\) against \(\delta\sqrt N=L\sqrt{\log N}/32\approx12\) to \(16\) for \(L=132\) at these \(N\)), where the cell smearing and the bare count settle every case. The ratio at \(q=16\) is better read from \(2^{14}\), where \(M\) is no longer \(32\): \(1.116\) against \(1.361\) for the hypograph. At \(2^{22}\) the values are consistent with a gain of about \(\log(W/w_r)\) for a strip of \(W/w_r=q\) cells, without separating other slowly growing forms. Retrieval. tools/held_sources.py "Hammersley Logan Shepp" found no held file; no retrieval was tried, since the translation, not the theorem, is untested and the theorem's statement would not decide it.
  • Bernstein-type generic chaining, Theorem 4.5.16 of [T4] (read in this cycle): for a class \(\mathcal F\) of functions on \([0,1]^2\) with \(0\in\mathcal F\), \(\mathbb E\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\sum_{i\le N}(f(X_i)-\int f\,d\lambda)\le L(\sqrt N\gamma_2(\mathcal F,d_2)+\gamma_1(\mathcal F,d_\infty))\). It targets conjugate-class-discrepancy through the family of thin bands, which is the stage-one reviewer's second mechanism. Answers. For tent bands of amplitude \(a\) and width \(w\) along curves, the \(d_2\) distance of two bands is about \((a/\sqrt w)\) times the \(L^2\) distance of their curves truncated at \(w\), a smooth geometry, while a hypograph's \(d_2\) is the square root of an \(L^1\) distance, a rough one; the smooth geometry makes \(\gamma_2\) of order \(a\ell\sqrt K\), \(K\) the graphs' slope bound, with no sum over scales, so the thin-band case of the obstacle would close for widths at least \(K\sqrt{\log N/N}\) (\(a\ell\sqrt{KN}\) is within the target since \(K\le\log N\)). Test. Passed, by computation of the two functionals, whose arithmetic the stage-two reviewer checked: for bands along graphs \(f\) over an interval of length \(\ell\) with \(K=\|f'\|_\infty\), \(d_2(b_f,b_g)\le C(a/\sqrt w)\|\min(|f-g|,w)\|_2\) and \(d_\infty(b_f,b_g)\le(2a/w)\|f-g\|_\infty\); the entropy numbers of such graphs are of order \(K\ell2^{-n}\) in \(L^\infty\) and \(K\ell^{3/2}2^{-n}\) in \(L^2\), so \(e_n(d_2)\le C\min(a\sqrt{w\ell},(a/\sqrt w)K\ell^{3/2}2^{-n})\), whose weighted sum crosses over at \(2^{-n}=w/(K\ell)\) and gives \(\gamma_2\le Ca\ell\sqrt K\), plus \(Ca\sqrt{w\ell\log(1/(w\ell))}\) for the band's placement; and \(e_n(d_\infty)\le\min(a,(aK\ell/w)2^{-n})\) summed with weights \(2^n\) down to the resolution \(\varepsilon\le w\ell/\sqrt N\) (rounding the graphs there costs at most \(2a\ell/\sqrt N\) per point, within the target) gives \(\gamma_1\le C(aK\ell/w)\log N\). So the expected supremum over one family is at most \(Ca\ell(\sqrt{KN}+\sqrt{N\log N\,w/\ell}+K\log N/w)\), at most \(C'a\ell\sqrt{N\log N}\) for \(\ell\ge w\ge K\sqrt{\log N/N}\). For a sum of bands, \(|\operatorname{disc}(\sum_k\varepsilon_kb_k)|\le\sum_ka_k\ell_k\cdot\max\) over normalized families by linearity alone; disjointness is used only for the additivity of costs. The union over dyadic widths and lengths needs Talagrand's or Bousquet's concentration inequality (variance \(w/\ell\le1\), range \(1/\ell\)), not bounded differences, whose deviation \(\sqrt N/\ell\) is too large for short bands. With the class cost \(\sum_ka_k\ell_k\le C(\log y)^{-1/4}\) the sum is \(O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) at \((4,4)\), where \(K\) is bounded; at other pairs of the curve the scaled graphs have \(K\) up to \(\sqrt{\log N}\), and the cost must be measured by the full gradient mass \((1+K)a\ell\). Break point. Three places. Bands narrower than \(K\sqrt{\log N/N}\) make \(\gamma_1\) too large; there the trivial count \(a(2Nw\ell+\text{points in the band})\) of the dominant-level entry's reviewer applies. Plateau bands (flat top of width \(W\), ramps of width \(w_r\)) have a rough \(d_2\) between the scales \(w_r\) and \(W\), so the same computation gives the factor \(\log(W/w_r)\) on top of \(a\ell\sqrt N\), not the Leighton–Shor exponent \(3/4\); by concavity of the logarithm and the packing \(\sum_kW_k\ell_k\le1\) of disjoint bands, \(\sum_ka_k\ell_k\log(W_ky/a_k)\le B\log(y/B)\) for \(B=\sum_ka_k\ell_k\), so with \(B\le C(\log y)^{-1/4}\) the plateau charge is within the target only for \(\log y\le c(\log N)^{2/3}\). And the bound needs a function written as disjoint bands with additive costs; how a general single-level function splits so is open.
  • The Ajtai–Komlós–Tusnády ellipsoid argument, Lemma 4.5.9 of [T4] (read in this cycle: \(\gamma_{2,2}\) of the \(1\)-Lipschitz functions vanishing on the boundary is finite, through the Fourier ellipsoid \(\sum(p^2+q^2)|c_{p,q}|^2\le1\), which uses only \(\|\nabla f\|_2\le1\)), rescaled to each cell, as the stage-one reviewer's first mechanism: replace the cellwise Lipschitz remainder \(\operatorname{Lip}(G|_Q)\lambda(Q)\) by \(r\|\nabla G\|_{L^2(Q)}\) for cells of side \(r\). Answers. It would bound the remainder of thin bands by their \(L^2\) gradient, which is far smaller than their Lipschitz constant times the cell area, closing the obstacle if the gain were complete. Test. Falsified as an answer to the obstacle. For a tent band of amplitude \(a=yw/2\) and width \(w<r\) crossing \(\ell/r\) cells, \(\|\nabla G\|_{L^2(Q)}\approx y\sqrt{wr}\), so the remainder sum is about \(\ell y\sqrt{wr}=2a\ell\sqrt{r/w}\), against \(2a\ell(r/w)\) for the Lipschitz remainder: the gain is \(\sqrt{w/r}\), and the excess \(\sqrt{r/w}\) remains unbounded as \(w/r\to0\). Also, Theorem 4.5.5's proof in [T4] reaches its finite class through Lipschitz functions to control the \(d_\infty\) term of Bernstein's inequality (Corollary 4.5.7), which an \(L^2\) gradient bound does not control in two dimensions (\(H^1\) does not embed in \(L^\infty\) there); the per-cell Sobolev bound itself was the stage-one reviewer's unproved proposal and stays unproved.
  • The Federer–Fleming deformation theorem of geometric measure theory (recalled, not read): a normal current deforms onto the cubical grid of side \(\varepsilon\) with mass and boundary mass multiplied by a constant, the difference lying in the \(\varepsilon\)-neighbourhood of its boundary. Translation: each level set of a class function splits into a union of cells (the mesh lemma) and a thin set near its boundary (the thin-band bound above). Answers. It would give the canonical split of a single-level function into a cell part and thin parts that the second lead's bound needs. Test. Not run: the test would be the split of the plateau band, and there the cell part at side \(\varepsilon\) pays the mesh factor \((\log(1/\varepsilon))^{3/4}\) from scale \(1\) down, which is the charge the obstacle already exceeds with; the deformation does not localize scales, so the item answers only the tent-band part, which the second lead covers directly. Retrieval. tools/held_sources.py "Federer Fleming" found no held file; no further retrieval was tried, since the step at which the item stops is the mesh factor, which no form of the deformation theorem changes.

Absurd bridges

  • Ewald summation from crystal chemistry (Ewald, 1921; recalled): a slowly converging Coulomb lattice sum is split at a screening length into a short-range part summed in real space and a smooth long-range part summed in Fourier space. Translation: split a class function at scale \(W\) as \(G=(G-\rho_W*G)+\rho_W*G\), \(\rho_W\) a mollifier of width \(W\); the long-range part is smooth and the short-range part lives in tubes of width about \(W\) around the places where \(G\) is not affine at scale \(W\). Answers. It localizes the obstacle: what remains after the smooth part is confined to tubes, so a Leighton–Shor bound localized to tubes would close the single-level case. Test. Not run for the translation: the test made reached only the support claim, and the localization, the translation's point, is untested (the stage-two reviewer's reading). The instance computed is the smallest one, the plateau band of width \(W\) with ramps of width \(w_r\) (computed here, unreviewed until the stage-two review): \(\rho_W*G\) is, up to constants, a tent band of amplitude \(a\) and width about \(W\), which the second Outside lead bounds by \(Ca\ell\sqrt{N\log N}\); \(G-\rho_W*G\) vanishes where \(G\) is affine on \(B(x,W)\), so it is supported in the tubes of width about \(W\) around the two plateau edges, with amplitude at most \(a\). For a single plateau the split localizes nothing at the plateau's own scale: the two edge tubes of width about \(2W\) cover the whole band (the stage-two reviewer's correction). Its use is where the spacing between features is smaller than their extent, as in a staircase of plateaus spaced \(W\) apart, which the mollification at \(W\) turns into a gentle ramp plus tubes around each step; the decisive test below takes it up with a spacing that varies. For one plateau the split moves the whole difficulty into the short-range part: inside each tube, \(G-\rho_W*G\) is a smoothed hypograph indicator minus its mollification, whose discrepancy has Leighton–Shor gains at the scales from \(W\) down to \(w_r\); the Ewald split gives no bound on it, and the bound it needs is the tube-localized one of the decisive test below. The decisive test's Operation carries the split forward with a spacing that varies. Retrieval. tools/held_sources.py "Ewald Holtsmark Chandrasekhar" found no held file; no retrieval was tried, since only the split itself, which needs no source, is used.
  • The Holtsmark distribution of stellar dynamics (Holtsmark, 1919; Chandrasekhar, 1943; recalled): the force at a point from randomly placed stars has a stable, non-Gaussian law. Translation: the per-point value of a flow linear in \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\), such as the heat-smoothed Poisson flow \(\nabla\Delta^{-1}(\mu^t-1)\) of Ambrosio, Stra and Trevisan, is the field of random unit charges with kernel \(z/|z|^2\). Answers. A non-Gaussian per-point law with lighter tails than Gaussian would give a linear flow with \(\psi_4\) tails, a primal route around thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, and then the class bound through lem:flow-matching-bound. Test. Falsified. In the plane, the variance contributed by charges at distance between \(2^{-k-1}\) and \(2^{-k}\) is the same for each \(k\) between the cut-off and \(1\) (about \(N4^{-k}\) charges, each of size about \(2^k/N\), so about \(1/N\) per annulus, about \(\log N\) annuli), so the per-point value is a sum of about \(\log N\) independent terms of equal variance and the Lindeberg theorem makes it Gaussian; the stable Holtsmark law needs three dimensions, where the nearest charges dominate. The Lindeberg ratio is about \(1/\log N\), and Gaussian behaviour at bounded \(u\) suffices, since \(\int\psi_\alpha\) exceeds its budget already from tails at bounded \(u\). This is the stage-one reviewer's structural lead in another language: a flow linear in the data whose per-point variance is at least \(cN\log N\) on a set of positive measure and whose kernel is \(o(\sqrt N\log N)\) has Gaussian per-point tails on the curve's scale, so a primal route needs an adaptive flow.

Architecture review

Necessary target. The two-sample statement at every pair of the curve with one universal \(L\), or its negation at one pair. Downstream. Through cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction and lem:two-sample-matching-transfer, conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy gives it: the goal. Through lem:flow-matching-bound, a flow of bounded cost gives it: the goal. The lemmas of this period give, through lem:dominant-level-split, the class bound's order against Lebesgue measure for class functions at \((4,4)\) whose larger partial is at least \(y\) where the gradient is nonzero, with bounded cellwise sum at a mesh \(2^{-j}\), \(j\le j^*(y)\): weaker than the goal, a case of the sufficient statement without the smearing conversion.

Extra requirements. The mechanism asks for more than the class bound in three places. It splits functions by gradient level, which the class does not require; it bounds against Lebesgue measure, while the class uses the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\), a conversion the dominant-level entry's reviewer sketched on the \(X\) side; and its single-level step asks for a bounded cellwise sum, which is sufficient, not necessary (the elementary layer-cake bound reaches the witness without it). The first is the mechanism's choice and could be replaced by a split by values, whose pieces are aligned (the local-factor entry's reviewer's remark), if a value split met the conditions.

Independent alternative. The review's medium reviewer received the goal, the survey's Section 5 and the registered statements of this thread with their assessments, and the open conjectures with their evidence, and the earlier stage-one proposals so as not to repeat them, without the route (stage-one record). It found no materially different architecture. It gave one structural lead, unverified: every flow linear in \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\) whose per-point variance is at least \(cN\log N\) on a set of positive measure and whose kernel is \(o(\sqrt N\log N)\) has Gaussian lower tails up to \(u\asymp\log N\), so its \(\psi_\alpha\) integrals diverge for \(\alpha>2\); this covers the heat-smoothed Poisson flow, so any primal route needs an adaptive flow. For the open step it ranked: a Sobolev remainder per cell through the ellipsoid argument, with an induction on \(N\) (tested above as the third Outside lead: falsified as a complete answer, the gain being \(\sqrt{w/r}\)); Bernstein-type chaining \(\sqrt N\gamma_2+\gamma_1\) on the band family (tested above as the second Outside lead: passed for tent bands, with the plateau break point); coarea in values with a mesh per level set, which it judged to reduce to the first. Its counterexample attempt (a smoothed Leighton–Shor region of width \(w\) and amplitude \(A\)) found the ratio \((\log1/w)^{3/4}(\log(A/w))^{-1/4}(\log N)^{-1/2}=O(1)\), no counterexample. Compared with the current route, both of its mechanisms are refinements of the coarea route's remainder, not a different architecture; the second, read here in [T4], is the review's main new tool.

Rank normalization. No dimension counts arise; the analogous question, whether the upper bound's charges and the cost are measured in the same units, is answered per scale by the local-factor lemma, both being sums over edges or cells at their own level.

Decision. Core: conjugate-class-discrepancy stays the core statement, worked through the same line, with the obstacle restated by what the leads found: thin tent bands are cheap, since their \(d_2\) geometry is smooth and they gain no scales (second Outside lead, its arithmetic checked by the stage-two reviewer), and the scale gains live in plateaus, at the scales between a plateau's width and its ramps' width. Lemma first, as the stage-two reviewer's Attempt check found the tube localization reachable from the record (Verification gate): the next entry's lemma is a tube-localized discrepancy bound, \(Ca\ell\sqrt N((\log(W/w_r))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\) for plateau bands of amplitude \(a\), flat width \(W\) and ramp width \(w_r\) along curves of length \(\ell\) and bounded slope, by a union bound over the coarse cell approximations at scale \(W\) (Corollary 4.5.7 of [T4]) and lem:mesh-function-discrepancy rescaled to each cell of side \(W\), with its absolute-level form if it comes cheaply, and with the band-family corollary for disjoint bands (tent bands being the case \(W=w_r\)) and the packing bound \(B(\log(y/B))^{3/4}\). If it holds with these hypotheses (disjoint bands, additive costs, widths at least \(K\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(K\) bounded at \((4,4)\)), it would close, against Lebesgue measure, the dominant-level entry's open families (teeth between \(\delta\) and the mesh, bands on many graphs) and disjoint plateau families at every level with \(\log y\le C\log N\), where the packing bound gives \(B(\log(y/B))^{3/4}\lesssim(\log y)^{1/2}\). The decisive test is the step after it. The queue head stays sandpile-odometer-flow; the next entry takes the picked chaining lead, entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2, with a Chosen paragraph, since it bears directly on conjugate-class-discrepancy.

Decisive test. Test disposition. New operation. Operation. Split a single-level class function at \((4,4)\) at a locally chosen scale: with the support of \(\nabla G\) split into components by the sign of the normal derivative \(\partial_\nu G\), \(\nu\) a chosen normal to the level curves along each ramp (only a sign split separates adjacent up- and down-ramps), \(W(x)\) for \(x\) on a ramp the width of its own component plus the distance to the nearest other component, capped at \(1\), extended to the whole square by its Lipschitz envelope \(\inf_z(W(z)+c|x-z|)\) over ramp points \(z\), and made balanced (the stage-two reviewer's definition; it gives about half the tooth width on a sawtooth, \(w_r+W\) on a plateau band and \(w_r\) plus the spacing on a staircase) (neighbouring dyadic cells of the partition by \(W\) differ by at most a factor \(2\)), write \(G=\rho_{W(\cdot)}*G+(G-\rho_{W(\cdot)}*G)\), bound the first part by lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) on that partition and the second, a sum of pieces in tubes of width about \(W\), by the tube-localized lemma, and compare the summed charges with the class cost. Prediction. Three outcomes. (A) The charges sum to at most \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\) for every single-level class function: the single-level case is closed against Lebesgue measure, leaving the coupling of several levels and the smearing conversion. (B) The charges exceed the target only through the \((2+\log_2i)\sqrt{\log\log N}\) term of lem:local-factor-discrepancy's factor, by at most a factor \(C\log\log N\): the class bound holds up to that factor, which still leaves the conjecture open. (C) Some single-level function's spacing varies so that no balanced choice keeps the charges within its cost: that function is a candidate counterexample to the class bound at \((4,4)\), to be tested against the Leighton–Shor lower-bound construction with that spacing; it would refute only the sufficient statement. Trivial cases. A function of bounded cellwise sum at a mesh up to \(j^*(y)\) needs no tubes and is decided by lem:dominant-level-split; the families of constant spacing (one plateau, the class lower bound's witness, at \(W=1\); a staircase of plateaus spaced \(W\)) are decided by the Attempt below in favour of (A), if the tube-localized lemma holds; a sawtooth, where adjacent teeth share crests, is open under the first definition of \(W\) the reviewer read, and the sign split above was written for it, unchecked on it beyond the reviewer's count of its spacing. Adding a linear function to \(G\) is not a trivial transformation here: it changes the class cost and the single-level property. Another presentation of the same function, with \(W\) measured between level curves, would be circular (at value gap \(h\) they are spaced \(h/y\)), which is why \(W\) is measured between ramps. The open instances are functions whose spacing varies over many scales across the square. Power. The recorded bounds decide the constant-spacing families as above and give nothing for variable spacing: lem:local-factor-discrepancy charges each edge from scale \(1\) down, without spacing, and the tube-localized lemma needs one width per tube. What outcome (A) needs is a cancellation inequality, \(\sum_QF(i(Q))\int_Q|\nabla(\rho_W*G)|\lesssim(\log N)^{1/2}\) over the balanced partition by \(W\): the gradient mass surviving mollification at scale \(W\) must decay like \((\log(1/W))^{-3/4}(\log N)^{1/2}\) (the stage-two reviewer's formulation, unverified). No computation reaches the question: the supremum is over a function class at variable spacing, and the difference between (A) and (B) is a factor of \(\log\log N\), a few units at reachable sizes. The instance lies within the goal's parameter window: single-level class functions at \((4,4)\), on the curve's parameters, at every \(N\); the other pairs of the curve need the scaled graphs, where the slope \(K\) up to \(\sqrt{\log N}\) enters every charge. Attempt. Tried before posing it, from the statements cited and the second Outside lead: with constant spacing \(W\), \(\rho_W*G\) is a function of gradient at most its local amplitude over \(W\), whose cellwise sum at mesh \(W\) is bounded by its gradient mass, and \(G-\rho_W*G\) is supported in tubes of width about \(W\) around the curves where \(G\) is not affine at scale \(W\); for the staircase this gives a gentle ramp plus one tube per step, with the packing bound, and outcome (A) if the tube-localized lemma holds. With variable spacing, the mollification at \(\rho_{W(x)}\) adds terms in \(\nabla W\) to the gradient of the smooth part; the stage-two reviewer showed this step routine (unverified): with the Lipschitz envelope \(\tilde W(x)=\inf_z(W(z)+c|x-z|)\) and \(\partial_W\rho_W\) of mean zero, \(|\nabla(\rho_{\tilde W}*G)|\le C(1+|\nabla\tilde W|)\) times the average of \(|\nabla G|\) over \(B(x,\tilde W)\), so the smooth part's cellwise sum on a balanced Whitney-type partition is at most \(C\int|\nabla G|\). The attempt stops at the substantive step after it: lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) charges the smooth part's gradient mass on a cell of level \(i=\log(1/W)\) at \(F(i)\approx i^{3/4}\), and mollifying at \(W\) lowers that mass only where \(G\) oscillates at scale \(W\); whether the surviving mass obeys the cancellation inequality above was not decided. Record search. tools/search-claims.py "strip tube band family chaining gamma one gamma two Bernstein curves width", "localized Leighton Shor confined tube plateau ramp width scales" and "variable scale mollification spacing between level curves decomposition staircase" returned lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, lem:loglog-mesh-deviation, lem:local-factor-discrepancy, lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy, lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound, thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion and lem:band-overlap-penalty, and claims of other notebooks; none localizes to tubes or chooses a scale by spacing, so the record does not answer the test.

Tube-localized Leighton–Shor bound and disjoint band families

16 October 2026 · Working proof; against Lebesgue measure · Tube localization. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The entry adds a lemma toward the core statement; the goal's state in Where we stand is unchanged.

Question. The fourth route review found that thin tent bands carry no scale gains and that the gains of a class function live in plateaus, at the scales between a plateau's width and its ramps' width; its Decision put first a Leighton–Shor bound localized to a tube of width \(W\), with the factor \((\log(W/w_r))^{3/4}\) in place of the mesh lemma's \((\log(1/w_r))^{3/4}\). The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\); this entry proves the localization and evaluates it on families of disjoint bands, the case the dominant-level split left open.

Chosen. The queue head is sandpile-odometer-flow, a primal flow simulation; this entry takes entry-2026-10-16-fourth-route-review:2, the Bernstein-type chaining lead, because it bears directly on conjugate-class-discrepancy, the core statement the review kept, and the review's Decision named its band-family bound as the next lemma.

General statement. lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, for every mesh \(2^{-j}\), \(j\le\ell_1\), every localization scale \(2^{-k}\), \(k\le j\), every union of cells and every cell function, with its corollaries for bands and for disjoint band families at their own gradient levels, and the per-cell count bound for bands.

Tube-localized discrepancy

Statement. There is a universal \(L\) such that, on the event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (probability tending to one), for all integers \(0\le k\le j\le\ell_1\), with \(W=2^{-k}\) and \(\Phi_{j,k}=(2(j-k)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\):

(a) every union \(A\) of cells of \(\mathcal G_j\) has \(\big|\sum_i1_A(X_i)-N\lambda(A)\big|\le L\sqrt N\,\Phi_{j,k}\,\big(\ell(\partial A)+4W\,\#T_k(A)\big)\), \(T_k(A)\) the cells of \(\mathcal G_k\) that contain a cell of \(A\);

(b) every \(H\) constant on the cells of \(\mathcal G_j\) has \(\big|\sum_iH(X_i)-N\int H\big|\le L\sqrt N\,\Phi_{j,k}\big(V^0_j(H)+4W\sum_{Q\in\mathcal G_k}(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-)\big)\), \(V^0_j(H)\) the sum over the edges of \(\mathcal G_j\) of length times jump, an edge on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) counting \(|H|\) of its cell; on the event of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation, (a) and (b) hold with \(\sqrt{j+\log\log N}\) in place of \(\sqrt{\log N}\) in \(\Phi_{j,k}\);

(c) for a plateau band \(G(x,y)=a\,\varphi(y-f(x))\) on \([0,1]^2\), \(f\) Lipschitz with \(|f'|\le K\), \(a>0\), \(\varphi\) rising linearly from \(0\) to \(1\) on \([0,w]\), equal to \(1\) on \([w,w+W_0]\), falling linearly to \(0\) on \([w+W_0,2w+W_0]\) and \(0\) elsewhere, with ramp width \(w\ge2^{-\ell_1}\) and band width \(W'=W_0+2w\le1\), \[\Big|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G\Big|\le L(1+K)^2a\sqrt N\Big(\big(2\log_2(W'/w)+9\big)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\Big);\]

(d) for bands \(G_1,\dots,G_n\) as in (c), each inside the square, with disjoint supports, slopes at most \(K\), ramp gradients \(y_r=a_r/w_r\) with \(e^{16}\le y_r\le N\), signs \(\varepsilon_r=\pm1\), \(G=\sum_r\varepsilon_rG_r\) and \(B=\sum_ra_r\), \[\Big|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G\Big|\le L(1+K)^2\sqrt N\Big(\sum_ra_r(2\log_2y_r)^{3/4}+B\big(2\log_2(1+1/B)+9\big)^{3/4}+B\sqrt{\log N}\Big),\] and if \(\int\sum_i\psi_4^*(|\partial_iG|)\le2\), then \(\sum_ra_r(\log y_r)^{1/4}\le2\), \(B\le1\), and the right side is at most \(L'(1+K)^2\sqrt{N\log N}\); for one common level \(y\) the first two terms are at most \(L''B(\log(y/B))^{3/4}\);

(e) on the event that every cell \(Q\) of every dyadic mesh of side at least \(3\sqrt{\log N/N}\) has \(|n_Q-N\lambda(Q)|\le L(\sqrt{N\lambda(Q)\log N}+\log N)\) and the cellwise event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split extended to those meshes (probability tending to one), a band as in (c) with any ramp width \(w\ge6\sqrt{\log N/N}\), possibly below \(2^{-\ell_1}\), has \[\Big|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G\Big|\le L(1+K)^2\Big(1+\frac{W'}w\Big)a\sqrt{N\log N},\] the plain per-cell count bound: of the conjectured order for tent bands (\(W'=2w\)) and for every band with \(W'/w\) bounded; (c) adds to it only when \(W'/w\) is large.

Proof. (a) Since \(k\le j\), every cell \(Q\) of \(\mathcal G_k\) is a union of cells of \(\mathcal G_j\), and \(1_A=\sum_{Q\in T_k(A)}1_{A\cap Q}\) off the grid. Fix \(Q\in T_k(A)\). By Step 2 of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, the boundary edges of \(A\cap Q\) split into closed simple curves \(C_1,\dots,C_r\) traced on \(\mathcal G_j\), each edge in exactly one, with \(1_{A\cap Q}=\sum_s\varepsilon_s1_{\mathring C_s}\) off the grid and \(\sum_s\ell(C_s)=\ell(\partial(A\cap Q))\). Every \(C_s\) lies in the closed square \(\bar Q\), whose grid \(\mathcal G_j\) has \(2(W2^j)(W2^j+1)\le4W^24^j\) edges, so \(\ell(C_s)\le4W^22^j\) and \(\log_2(2^{j+3}\ell(C_s))\le2(j-k)+5\). Part (a) of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy gives \(|\sum_i(1_{\mathring C_s}(X_i)-\lambda(\mathring C_s))|\le L\sqrt N\ell(C_s)\Phi_{j,k}\). Summing, \(|\sum_i1_A(X_i)-N\lambda(A)|\le L\sqrt N\Phi_{j,k}\sum_{Q\in T_k(A)}\ell(\partial(A\cap Q))\). An edge of \(\partial(A\cap Q)\) either is an edge of \(\partial A\), and then a boundary edge of \(A\cap Q\) for exactly one \(Q\), the one containing the cell of \(A\) beside it, or lies on \(\partial Q\) with \(A\) on both sides; the latter have total length at most \(\ell(\partial Q)=4W\) for each \(Q\). So the sum is at most \(\ell(\partial A)+4W\#T_k(A)\). The argument uses part (a) of the mesh lemma and nothing else, so lem:loglog-mesh-deviation's form of that part, with the deviation \(\sqrt{j+\log\log N}\), carries over unchanged.

(b) Off the grid, \(H=\int_0^\infty1_{\{H>t\}}dt-\int_0^\infty1_{\{H<-t\}}dt\), the sets being unions of cells of \(\mathcal G_j\). By (a) inside the integrals, the discrepancy of \(H\) is at most \(L\sqrt N\Phi_{j,k}\) times \(\int_0^\infty(\ell(\partial\{H>t\})+\ell(\partial\{H<-t\}))dt+4W\int_0^\infty(\#T_k\{H>t\}+\#T_k\{H<-t\})dt\). An inner edge between cells of values \(u\) and \(v\) lies on \(\partial\{H>t\}\) for \(t\ge0\) in \([\min(u,v),\max(u,v))\) and on \(\partial\{H<-t\}\) for \(t\ge0\) in \([-\max(u,v),-\min(u,v))\), together a set of \(t\) of length \(|u-v|\); an edge on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) beside a cell of value \(u\), for a set of length \(|u|\); so the first integral is \(V_j^0(H)\). A cell \(Q\) of \(\mathcal G_k\) is in \(T_k\{H>t\}\) exactly for \(0\le t<\max_QH^+\), and in \(T_k\{H<-t\}\) for \(0\le t<\max_QH^-\); so the second integral is \(\sum_Q(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-)\).

(c) Let \(j\) be the least integer with \(2^{-j}\le w\), so \(w/2<2^{-j}\le w\) and \(j\le\ell_1\) because \(w\ge2^{-\ell_1}\) (and \(j\ge1\) since \(w\le\frac12\); the mesh lemma needs \(j\ge1\), and \(j=0\) is the trivial case of one cell); let \(k\) be the largest integer with \(2^{-k}\ge W'\), so \(W'\le W=2^{-k}<2W'\) (for \(W'\in(\frac12,1]\), \(k=0\)) and \(k\le j-1\) because \(W'\ge2w\ge2\cdot2^{-j}\). Then \(2^{j-k}<4W'/w\), so \(\Phi_{j,k}\le(2\log_2(W'/w)+9)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\). On the same event, the proof of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split gives \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le|\sum_iE_jG(X_i)-N\int E_jG|+L\sqrt{N\log N}\Lambda_j(G)\), \(E_jG\) the cell averages; that proof bounds the remainder on each cell without using the mesh lemma, so the first term may be bounded by (b) instead. Remainder: \(G\) is Lipschitz with constant \((a/w)\sqrt{1+K^2}\) and is constant off the two ramp strips, each of vertical width \(w\le2\cdot2^{-j}\) along a graph of slope at most \(K\); a column of cells of \(\mathcal G_j\) meets each strip in a vertical extent at most \((K+2)2^{-j}\), so in at most \(K+4\) cells, at most \(2(K+4)2^j\) cells meet the ramps and \(\Lambda_j(G)\le2(K+4)2^j\,4^{-j}(a/w)\sqrt{1+K^2}\le2(K+4)(1+K)\,a\). Main part: by the inner part of the corollary of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, the inner edges contribute to \(V^0_j(E_jG)\) at most \(8\|\nabla G\|_1\), and \(\|\nabla G\|_1=\int(|\partial_1G|+|\partial_2G|)=2a\int_0^1(1+|f'|)\le2a(1+K)\); the edges on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) contribute at most \(a\) times their total length beside the support, at most \(2+2(W'+(K+2)2^{-j})\le6+2K\). The support of \(E_jG\) lies in the cells of \(\mathcal G_j\) meeting the band, of vertical extent at most \(W'+(K+2)2^{-j}\) in a column of cells of \(\mathcal G_j\); a column of cells of \(\mathcal G_k\) (width \(W\)) meets the band in a vertical extent at most \(W'+KW+2\cdot2^{-j}\le(K+2)W\), hence in at most \(K+4\) cells of \(\mathcal G_k\), and there are \(2^k=1/W\) columns; with \(0\le E_jG\le a\), \(4W\sum_Q\max_Q(E_jG)^+\le4(K+4)a\). So (b) bounds the first term by \(L\sqrt N\Phi_{j,k}(16(1+K)+6+2K+4(K+4))a\), and both terms are at most the display with a larger \(L\).

(d) By linearity, \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le\sum_r|\sum_iG_r(X_i)-N\int G_r|\) (disjointness is used only below), and (c) bounds each term with \(x_r=W'_r/w_r=y_rW'_r/a_r\). Since \(x_r\le y_r(1+W'_r/a_r)\) and \((u+v)^{3/4}\le u^{3/4}+v^{3/4}\) for \(u,v\ge0\), \((2\log_2x_r+9)^{3/4}\le(2\log_2y_r)^{3/4}+k(W'_r/a_r)\) with \(k(x)=(2\log_2(1+x)+9)^{3/4}\), concave and increasing on \([0,\infty)\). By Jensen's inequality with the weights \(a_r/B\), \(\sum_ra_rk(W'_r/a_r)\le Bk(\sum_rW'_r/B)\le Bk(1/B)\): at every \(x\in[0,1]\) the vertical intervals \([f_r(x),f_r(x)+W'_r]\) lie in \([0,1]\), the bands being inside the square, and are disjoint, so \(\sum_rW'_r\le1\). This is the display. For the cost: on the ramps of \(G_r\), \(|\partial_2G|=a_r/w_r=y_r\), on an area \(2w_r\) inside the square, and the supports are disjoint; \(\psi_4^*(x)\ge\frac12x(\log x)^{1/4}\) for \(x\ge e^{16}\) (as in the corollary of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split), so \(2\ge\sum_r2w_r\psi_4^*(y_r)\ge\sum_ra_r(\log y_r)^{1/4}\), and \(B\le2/16^{1/4}=1\). Then \(\sum_ra_r(2\log_2y_r)^{3/4}\le(2/\ln2)^{3/4}\sqrt{\log N}\sum_ra_r(\log y_r)^{1/4}\le L\sqrt{\log N}\) since \(\log y_r\le\log N\); \(Bk(1/B)\) is bounded for \(B\in(0,1]\); and \(B\sqrt{\log N}\le\sqrt{\log N}\). For one level \(y\), \(B\le2(\log y)^{-1/4}\) and the first two terms are \(B(2\log_2y)^{3/4}+Bk(1/B)\le L''B(\log(y/B))^{3/4}\) for \(y\ge e^{16}\).

(e) Bernstein's inequality and a union bound over the at most \(2N\) cells of the at most \(\log_2N\) meshes give the count event; for the cellwise event, the proof of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split uses \(Nw_Q^2\ge(\log N)^{3/2}\) only in Chernoff's bound \(n_Q\le2Nw_Q^2\), whose failure probability \(\exp(-Nw_Q^2/3)\) is at most \(N^{-3}\) for \(Nw_Q^2\ge9\log N\), which holds for cells of side at least \(3\sqrt{\log N/N}\). Let \(j\) be the least integer with \(2^{-j}\le w\), so \(2^{-j}>w/2\ge3\sqrt{\log N/N}\). Split \(G=E_jG+(G-E_jG)\) as in (c). The remainder is at most \(L\sqrt{N\log N}\Lambda_j(G)\le2L(K+4)(1+K)a\sqrt{N\log N}\), as in (c). The cell function \(E_jG\) is supported in the cells meeting the band, at most \(2W'/w+K+4\) per column of cells, \(2^j\) columns, and \(0\le E_jG\le a\), so \(|\sum_iE_jG(X_i)-N\int E_jG|\le\sum_Qa|n_Q-N\lambda(Q)|\le a(2W'/w+K+4)2^jL(2^{-j}\sqrt{N\log N}+\log N)\), and \(2^j\log N\le2\log N/w\le\sqrt{N\log N}/3\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy: part (a) of that lemma in (a), and for (c) and (d) the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split as well (both hold with probability tending to one). \(k\le j\): the \(W\)-cells are unions of \(j\)-cells in (a); every \(k\) from \(0\) to \(j\) is allowed and the statement holds for all at once, \(k=0\) giving a weaker form of the mesh lemma and \(k=j\) the one-cell form below. \(1\le j\le\ell_1\): the mesh lemma's range, hence \(w\ge2^{-\ell_1}\) in (c). \(|f'|\le K\): the cell counts per column in (c) and (e). \(W'\le1\): \(W\le1\) in (c). Each band inside the square: \(\sum_rW'_r\le1\) and the ramp area \(2w_r\) in (d). Disjoint supports: \(\sum_rW'_r\le1\) and the additivity of the cost in (d); the display before the cost needs only \(\sum_rW'_r\le1\). \(e^{16}\le y_r\le N\): the cost bound and the comparison \(\log y_r\le\log N\) in (d); no common level is needed. The class cost in (d) only for \(\sum_ra_r(\log y_r)^{1/4}\le2\). \(w\ge6\sqrt{\log N/N}\) in (e): Chernoff's bound for the cells of side \(2^{-j}\) and \(2^j\log N\le\sqrt{N\log N}/3\). Conclusions: (a) for every union of cells, (b) for every cell function, (c) and (e) for each band (tent bands are \(W_0=0\)), (d) for every such family; (c), (d) and (e) are bounds against Lebesgue measure, not against the cell-smeared \(\mu_X-\mu_Y\).

Baseline. The plainest bound on a band is the per-cell count bound (e), the case \(k=j\) of (a) in substance: it gives the conjectured order for tent bands and for every band with \(W'/w\) bounded, so (c) adds over it only when \(W'/w\to\infty\), the plateaus. The next plainest is lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split at mesh \(w\): \(L\sqrt N(\log_2(1/w)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\cdot16a\sqrt{1+K^2}+L\sqrt{N\log N}\Lambda\), the factor counting all scales from \(1\) down. The lemma replaces \(\log(1/w)\) by \(\log(W'/w)\), at an extra cost proportional to \(4W\) per localization cell met, which is of order \(a\) for a band. For a family at one level, the bound before Jensen's inequality would add the logarithms band by band; the packing \(\sum_rW'_r\le1\) is what turns many small plateaus into \(B(\log(y/B))^{3/4}\).

Degenerate cases. \(A\) empty or \(H=0\): both sides vanish. \(k=0\): \(\Phi_{j,0}=(2j+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) and the extra term is \(4\) times the number of the unit square's cells met, \(4\) or \(0\): the mesh lemma's (b) up to constants and an additive \(4\Phi\) (for sets). \(k=j\): \(A\cap Q\) is \(Q\) or empty, so \(\partial(A\cap Q)=\partial Q\) and each cell of \(A\) pays \(4\cdot2^{-j}\Phi_{j,j}\), a cell's deviation scale, the one-cell-thick bound. A tent band (\(W_0=0\), \(W'=2w\)): the factor is \((11)^{3/4}\), no scale gain. A band of height \(W'\) of order \(1\): the factor is about \((2\log_2(1/w))^{3/4}\), the full one, as for the class lower bound's witness, and the amplitude decides.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\), for (c) and (d) with plateau bands along a curved graph: \(y=(\log N)^4\), \(w=2^{1-\ell_1}\) (so \(w\ge2^{-\ell_1}\)), \(a=yw\), band width \(W'=yw\) (\(W_0=(y-2)w\)), \(n=\lfloor(\log y)^{-1/4}/(4a)\rfloor\) bands along \(f_r(x)=\frac18+\frac{3(r-1)}{4n}+\frac1{16}\sin(2\pi x)\), slope at most \(\pi/8\), so \(K=1\). With \(2^{-\ell_1}\) between \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) and twice that, \(a\) lies between \(2\) and \(4\) times \((\log N)^{4.75}/\sqrt N\) and \(n\) is of order \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{-4.75}(\log\log N)^{-1/4}\). Inside the square: \(f_r\in[\frac1{16},\frac{15}{16}]\) and \(W'=a\le\frac1{16}\). Disjoint: the vertical spacing \(\frac3{4n}\ge3a(\log y)^{1/4}\ge a=W'\). Cost: \(|\partial_2G|=y\) and \(|\partial_1G|=y|f'|\le y\) on the ramps, of area \(2w\) per band, and \(\psi_4^*(x)\le x(\log(1+x))^{1/4}\) (the class test entry's bound), so the cost is at most \(4na(\log(1+y))^{1/4}\le(\log(1+y)/\log y)^{1/4}\le2\). \(e^{16}\le y\le N\) for large \(N\). Then (d) gives at most \(L(1+K)^2\sqrt N(B(2\log_2y)^{3/4}+O(1)+B\sqrt{\log N})\) with \(B=na\le\frac14\). Plainest bound. The per-cell count bound (e) gives \(L(1+K)^2(1+y)B\sqrt{N\log N}\), a factor \((\log N)^4\) too large; for this one fixed stack the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality applies (this entry's reviewer's finding): all \(f_r\) share the term \(\sin(2\pi x)/16\), so \(G\) is a function of \(z=y-\sin(2\pi x)/16\), a measure-preserving shear, and gives \(O(B\sqrt N)\); what fails is uniformity over the graphs, which the class bound needs, and which only \(K=0\) or one fixed shear gives a one-dimensional estimate for, so the witness shows the hypotheses hold together while the lemma's content is the uniform bound; lem:dominant-level-split's cellwise sum at every mesh \(j\le j^*(y)\), about \((\log N)^{2/3}(4\log\log N)^{1/3}\), is of order \(y(1+K)\), since the spacing \(\frac3{4n}\), of order \((\log N)^{4.75}/\sqrt N\), is far below \(2^{-j}\), so it is unbounded; and lem:local-factor-discrepancy at mesh \(2^{-\ell_1}\) charges \(\ell_1^{3/4}\|\nabla G\|_1\), of order \((\log N)^{3/4}B\), above the target.

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The fourth route review's decisive test splits a single-level class function at its local spacing; its Decision put this lemma first, and this entry proves it, so none of the test's outcomes (A), (B), (C) occurred yet. What the lemma settles for the test: disjoint families of bands inside the square with ramps at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\), at any gradient levels up to \(N\), are bounded at the conjectured order against Lebesgue measure, by (c) and (d); the variable-spacing split and its cancellation inequality remain the test.

Record search. tools/search-claims.py "union of cells cut along coarse cells closed curves length mesh units disjoint plateau bands packing" (the objects of the proof) returned lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy, lem:mesh-function-discrepancy and lem:local-factor-discrepancy, which charge each edge from scale \(1\) down and do not localize; "one cell thick set discrepancy perimeter cells meeting boundary sum of cell deviations" returned lem:mesh-function-discrepancy and lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound. tools/claim_resemblance.py on the spec: lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split (0.34) and lem:dominant-level-split (0.28), both related in the spec and neither more general (each charges the scales from \(1\) down, through \(j^{3/4}\)); lem:loglog-mesh-deviation (0.19), whose sharper deviation this lemma's (a) and (b) take over, now stated; lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound (0.16), a lower bound; and one claim of another notebook.

Follow-up

Owed attempt. The attempt named for this item was the band-family bound proved in full from Theorem 4.5.16 of [T4]. It was not made as named, for two reasons from the mathematics. For plateau bands, the review's computation of \(\gamma_2\) (whose arithmetic its stage-two reviewer checked) gives the factor \(\log(W'/w)\), which with the packing bound is within the target only for \(\log y\le c(\log N)^{2/3}\), while the mesh lemma's curve chaining gives the exponent \(3/4\), which (d) turns into \(\sqrt{\log N}\) at every level; so (c) came first. For tent bands and bands with \(W'/w\) bounded, this entry's reviewer pointed to the plain per-cell count bound, verified here as (e), which needs no chaining. What the Theorem 4.5.16 route would still bear on is the case neither reaches.

Follow-up. Continuing. The item still bears on conjugate-class-discrepancy through plateau bands with ramps between \(6\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(W'/w\) large, which (c) does not reach (its mesh must be at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\)) and (e) charges \(W'/w\). Next attempt: for such a band, apply (c) at mesh \(2^{-\ell_1}\) to \(E_{\ell_1}G\), and bound \(G-E_{\ell_1}G\), supported in the cells of side \(2^{-\ell_1}\) that meet the ramps, by layers: the differences \(E_{i}G-E_{i-1}G\) for meshes between \(2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(w\) are supported in one-cell-thick sets along the graph's trace, bounded by Bernstein's inequality and a union bound over traces, \(C\sqrt N\) per unit length and per layer, about \(\log_2(2^{-\ell_1}/w)\le\frac14\log_2\log N\) layers. Smallest case. One plateau band along a horizontal line at height \(c\): \(G\) depends on the second coordinate only. Plainest bound. For a function of one coordinate, \(|\sum_iG(X_i)-N\int G|\le\mathrm{TV}(G)\sup_t|\#\{i:X_i^2\le t\}-Nt|\), with \(\mathrm{TV}(G)=2a\) and the supremum of order \(\sqrt N\) by the Dvoretzky–Kiefer–Wolfowitz inequality, so the smallest instance decides nothing; the attempt's content is the curved graph, whose traces carry the entropy.

New mathematics. lem:tube-localized-discrepancy: cutting a union of cells along the cells of side \(W\) charges each closed piece only the logarithm of its own length, so the Leighton–Shor factor becomes \((2\log_2(W/2^{-j})+5)^{3/4}\) at an extra \(4W\) per \(W\)-cell met, for sets and cell functions; for a band inside the square with ramps at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\) the factor \((\log(W'/w))^{3/4}\); for disjoint such bands at their own gradient levels \(y_r\le N\), by packing, at most order \((1+K)^2\sqrt{N\log N}\) under the class cost; and the plain per-cell count bound, \((1+W'/w)(1+K)^2a\sqrt{N\log N}\) for ramps at least \(6\sqrt{\log N/N}\), which already covers tent bands.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. On the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\): every family of disjoint plateau or tent bands, each inside the square along a full-width graph of slope at most a constant \(K\), at gradient levels \(e^{16}\le y_r\le N\), with ramps at least \(2^{-\ell_1}\) and class cost at most \(2\), has discrepancy against Lebesgue measure at most \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\); for tent bands and bounded \(W'/w\) that much follows from the plain per-cell count bound (e), down to ramps of \(6\sqrt{\log N/N}\), and what (c) and (d) add is the plateau families with \(W'/w\) large, such as the Nonvacuity witness, which neither (e) nor the dominant-level split reaches. Not covered. Plateau bands with ramps between \(6\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(W'/w\) large; bands over part of \([0,1]\), with ends; overlapping or nested bands (staircases); general single-level functions, which are not disjoint families of bands; slopes \(K\) growing with \(N\), as at other pairs of the curve; the cell-smeared measures.

Process assessment. Three of the stand-in review's objections were right: builds queued without the reason they were not built in the turn; a reviewer audit that had caught a mistake offered as its prevention, twice; a reply that narrowed an open case on a reviewer's unverified computation without the label. This entry's reviewer found three more: the next attempt (entropy chaining) aimed at a case the plain per-cell count bound settles; the Nonvacuity witness, tent bands along horizontal lines, was elementary, checked only against the dominant-level split; and summaries dropped qualifiers (bands inside the square, ramp range, the tent families being elementary). Meta. The habit behind these is relaying and reaching: what a reviewer, a tool or an earlier turn found is passed on by its gist, without its qualifier, and a method is reached for before the bare count is written; the morning's rule about baselines did not change the evening's order of work. The changes are in CLAUDE.md: a relayed finding is restated from its source with its qualifiers, and the first lines drafted for any proof, test, witness or next attempt are its plainest bound.
