Box exits cannot refute the curve

17 October 2026 · Working proof, an elementary corollary; queue item closed · Varying-aspect subgraphs. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A queue item's entry: an elementary corollary that changes no statement of Where we stand.

Chosen. The queue's head, two-choice-routing, has had two entries in a row with no bearing, so this entry develops another item; varying-aspect-subgraphs bears on conj:ultimate-matching from the refutation side, while the last four research entries all declared the obligation conjugate-class-discrepancy, and it is second in the queue (tools/lead_queue.py head), after the head.

Question. The item, queued by the first route review, asks to "test whether Leighton–Shor subgraphs whose vertical scaling varies across the tent scales gain an unbounded factor over constant scaling on the curve, which would refute a pair of the curve; a test of the conditional maximal-displacement barrier". That barrier was later proved without its condition, as thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold in the maximum-displacement threshold entry. The missing implication is a refutation of conj:ultimate-matching at a pair of the curve; the test is whether an argument of the item's kind could give one, decided from the recorded statements before any construction.

Target form. The goal's form is the conjecture's condition for one matching; a Leighton–Shor subgraph argument concludes that every matching moves some points out of given boxes, so this entry asks what such a conclusion must say to violate the condition, and whether the record already excludes it.

General statement. cor:box-exit-exclusion: for every pair on or above the curve and every family of boxes, possibly depending on the position, the scale, \(N\) and the sample, that contains the threshold box at every position.

Box exits

Setting. \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in(0,\infty]\) with \(1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2\ge1/2\), \(u_j=(\log N)^{1/\alpha_j}\), \(s_0=\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(X\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\) and \(Y\) evenly spread or an independent uniform sample, \(\Delta_i=X_i-Y_{\pi(i)}\) as in the threshold theorem, and \(K\) the universal constant of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold. A box family is a map \(x\mapsto B(x)\) from \([0,1]^2\) to subsets of \(\mathbb R^2\), which may depend on \(N\) and the sample; an argument with boxes \(B_k(x)\) at several scales \(k\) that concludes an exit from some scale's box concludes an exit from \(\bigcap_kB_k(x)\), the family it is read with here; the threshold box is \(R_K=[-Ku_1s_0,Ku_1s_0]\times[-Ku_2s_0,Ku_2s_0]\).

Statement. (a) With probability tending to one there is a matching \(\pi\) with \(\Delta_i\in B(X_i)\) for every \(i\), simultaneously for every box family with \(B(x)\supseteq R_K\) at every \(x\). (b) Hence no argument concluding, with probability bounded away from zero, that every matching has a pair with \(\Delta_i\notin B(X_i)\), for a family containing \(R_K\) everywhere, is correct; in particular a refutation of a pair of the curve by one pair's exit, which needs its boxes to contain the conjecture's maximum box \([-Lu_1's_0,Lu_1's_0]\times[-Lu_2's_0,Lu_2's_0]\), \(u_j'=(\log2N)^{1/\alpha_j}\), for every \(L\), fails at every \(L\ge K\), since that box contains \(R_K\) there.

Proof. (a) On the event of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold some matching has \(|\Delta_i^j|\le Ku_js_0\) for \(j=1,2\) and every \(i\), so \(\Delta_i\in R_K\subseteq B(X_i)\); the event does not depend on the family, so it serves every family at once, with no union over families. (b) An argument of the kind stated would give, along some sequence of \(N\), events of probability bounded away from zero on which every matching has an exit; along that sequence the event of (a), on which some matching has none, has probability tending to one, so the two meet with positive probability, a contradiction. For a refutation by one exit, every exit must break the conjecture's maximum bound, \(|\Delta^1|>Lu_1's_0\) or \(|\Delta^2|>Lu_2's_0\), since the exit's coordinate and position are not chosen by the argument, so the boxes must contain the conjecture's maximum box; and a refutation must hold for every \(L\), in particular for one with \(L\ge K\), where \(u_j'\ge u_j\) makes that box contain \(R_K\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. On or above the curve: the threshold theorem's hypothesis, in (a). \(B(x)\supseteq R_K\) at every \(x\): (a), the containment. Nothing about the boxes' shapes, their variation with position or scale, or their dependence on the sample is used, the containment being deterministic. In (b), that the argument concludes an exit for every matching with probability bounded away from zero.

Degenerate cases. \(B(x)=R_K\) everywhere: (a) is the threshold theorem. \(B(x)=\mathbb R^2\): trivial. A family that misses \(R_K\) at some position (a box thin in one coordinate there): outside (a), and an exit from it need not break the conjecture's maximum bound, which is why (b) asks for the maximum box.

Nonvacuity. At \((4,4)\) on the curve's parameters, the boxes \(B_k=[-Ku_1s_0,Ku_1s_0]\times[-Ku_2s_0\,2^{k/10},Ku_2s_0\,2^{k/10}]\) at the scales \(k=0,1,\dots\), the vertical scaling varying across the scales, have intersection \(R_K\) at every position; (a) gives a matching with no exit from it, so none from any \(B_k\). Plainest bound. The threshold theorem itself, of which (a) is the containment step; the corollary adds that varying the boxes, across positions or scales, changes nothing.

Baseline. The construction that needs no idea is the threshold matching; the corollary says that any Leighton–Shor subgraph argument, with whatever scaling across tent scales, concludes at best an exit from boxes that the threshold matching never leaves, unless its boxes are smaller than \(R_K\) somewhere, and then one exit does not break the conjecture.

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The sixth review's retained test, the gap-charged bound for nested chains, was neither proved nor refuted; this entry is on the refutation side and does not bear on it.

Record search. tools/search-claims.py "every matching has a pair outside box position dependent anisotropic box exit lower bound Leighton Shor subgraph varying aspect" returned thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion, lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound, thm:per-level-count-matchings and thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold; the last decides the item's first reading.

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion uses the vertically scaled Leighton–Shor subgraph with one scaling \(\kappa=(\log N)^{1/\alpha_2-1/\alpha_1}\) below the curve, where its exit breaks the maximum bound; thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold proves the maximum bound attainable on and above the curve, and the Where we stand already says that no argument using only maximal displacements refutes a pair of the curve; thm:per-level-count-matchings proves each level of the condition common to both coordinates alone. The threshold entry of 16 October 2026 already settled the barrier this item tests, so the item's first reading was superseded then; (a) is that theorem's containment step and (b) its contrapositive, stated for box families of every shape, and the corollary records the supersession; it is elementary.

New mathematics. cor:box-exit-exclusion: on and above the curve, with probability tending to one, one matching stays inside every box family that contains the threshold box at every position, whatever its shape or its variation across positions and scales; so no Leighton–Shor subgraph argument, with any scaling across the tent scales, refutes a pair of the curve through one pair's exit.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. At the goal's own parameters it gives nothing toward a proof or a refutation: it closes one family of refutation arguments, those concluding a single exit, as the threshold theorem already implied; what the cycle could have given is a refutation, which (b) excludes for this family.

Follow-up

Follow-up. Closed: merged into mixed-level-counts. The item's words allow two readings. Read as a maximal-displacement argument, one exit from boxes scaled differently across the tent scales, it is decided by (b): such boxes must contain the conjecture's maximum box at every position to refute, and the threshold matching never leaves them; the varying scaling gains nothing, a supersession by thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold. Read as a count argument, at least \(M\) pairs leaving boxes \(B(x)\) whose sides differ in the two coordinates and may vary with position, its exits count against the condition separately in each coordinate, the conjecture allowing at most \(2Ne^{-t}\) pairs with \(|\Delta_i^j|\ge Ls_0t^{1/\alpha_j}\) at each level \(t\). Round each box's half-side \(b_j(x)\) down to the largest integer level \(t_j(x)\) with \(Ls_0t_j^{1/\alpha_j}\le b_j(x)\) (for \(\alpha_j=\infty\), where every level has the same threshold, the largest admissible one), capped at \(\lfloor\log N\rfloor\), and put a half-side below \(Ls_0\) at level \(0\), whose allowance \(2N\) no exit can exceed; an exit with \(|\Delta^j|>b_j(x)\) is then beyond level \(t_j(x)\) for the same \(L\), and the rounding changes the allowance at most by the factor \(e\). The at most \((\lfloor\log N\rfloor+1)^2\) pairs of levels split the exits, and by pigeonhole some pair \((t_1,t_2)\) carries at least \(M/(\lfloor\log N\rfloor+1)^2\) of them, each beyond \(t_1\) in coordinate \(1\) or beyond \(t_2\) in coordinate \(2\), while the conjecture allows at most \(2N(e^{-t_1}+e^{-t_2})\). So a count refutation implies, up to the factor \((\lfloor\log N\rfloor+1)^2\) in the count and \(e\) in the allowance, a refutation of the mixed-level count question at some pair of levels, the question the queued item mixed-level-counts asks at \(t_1\ne t_2\); a pair with \(t_1=t_2\) falls under thm:per-level-count-matchings, which for two independent samples bounds both coordinates at one level within one matching; and a mixed-level refutation is a count argument with one fixed box. Part of the mixed-level question thm:low-level-mixed-counts already decides, and this reading's wording joins that item. Stakes. A yes to the item's question, an unbounded gain, would have refuted a pair of the curve; a no for single exits is (b), and for counts it is the mixed-level question up to the pigeonhole's factor, whose yes would refute the conjecture and whose no would leave the coupling of levels within one matching as the only refutation route; thm:low-level-mixed-counts, for two independent samples only, already gives the no at levels with \(t_1^{1/\alpha_1}/t_2^{1/\alpha_2}\to\infty\) and \(e^{2t_2}\le\frac{L^2}8\log N\,t_1^{1/\alpha_1}t_2^{1/\alpha_2}\), and the case with the coordinates exchanged follows by exchanging them, so the pairs of levels left open are those of bounded box ratio or with the smaller box's level high, and every pair in the evenly spread setting. Sources read. Recorded results only: the registered statements of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold, thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion, thm:per-level-count-matchings, thm:low-level-mixed-counts and lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound, the maximum-displacement threshold entry, and the first route review's falsification attempt and its item (D), which queued the item. Not examined. The item names Leighton–Shor subgraphs with varying vertical scaling: no such subgraph was built, and the closure stands without it because (b) holds for every box family whatever subgraph produced it; the "tent scales" are not examined separately, the corollary covering any dependence of the boxes on scale. Owed attempt. None was named: the item has no earlier entry. The reviewer's record of this closure: review record.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • Leighton–Shor-type arguments force crossings through an excess \(E\), at most \(N^{1/2+o(1)}\) for the region classes used (a discrepancy bound not proved here); applied to the threshold matching, the forced pairs have \(|\Delta^j|\le Ku_js_0\), so their exponential terms total at most \(E\,N^{(K/L)^{\alpha_j}}<N\) for large \(L\), and a count violating level \(t\) needs more than \(2Ne^{-t}\) exits, which forces \(t\ge(\frac12-o(1))\log N\), where the level's box contains \(Ku_js_0\) for large \(L\); so every excess-based quantity would fail on the curve, and what escapes is a lower bound from the unforced pairs, the coupling of levels within one matching. Record. lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy and lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound may supply the bound on \(E\); thm:low-level-mixed-counts; search "Leighton Shor lower bound tent scales vertical scaling subgraph matching count outside box".

The first checked (a), (b) and the fairness of reading one, and required: the pigeonhole over levels for reading two, whose "the same question" had not been shown; thm:low-level-mixed-counts, which it found by a search under other words; scales read through the intersection of their boxes; a well-defined witness; (b) along a subsequence. Simultaneous rule lowers pooled kurtosis

At the goal's own parameters the best outcome is a gap growing with \(J\): evidence, not proof, of a local mechanism with per-point tails lighter than the dyadic flow's, which thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction proves fail above exponent \(2\); beating that theorem needs a proof for every \(J\), which a run cannot give, so the best outcome would name the mechanism for the next proof attempt.

General statement. lem:equalized-flow-separable, for every \(J\) and every count configuration; the run, ex:simultaneous-rule-tails, at \(J=6,7,8\).

The hand step: the equalized flow

Setting. The model of the sequential rules entry: on a level-\(j\) square \(S\) of side \(\rho\), coordinate \(2\) gets \((\bar\varphi+\psi(t_1))\mathrm{tent}(t_2)-\mathrm{tent}'(t_1)\Psi(t_2)\) and coordinate \(1\) on half \(b\) gets \((-2d_b/\rho+\chi(t_2))\mathrm{tent}(t_1)-\mathrm{tent}'(t_2)\Phi(t_1)\), \(\Phi'=\psi\), \(\Psi'=\chi\) on each half, all vanishing at the ends, \(\bar\varphi=-E_0/\rho\). The equalized flow takes, at every square, \(\chi=0\) and \(\Phi(t_1)=-(d_0-d_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/(2\rho)\), so \(\psi=\Phi'\) is \(-(d_0-d_1)/\rho\) on the left half and \(+(d_0-d_1)/\rho\) on the right, of zero mean.

Statement. (a) The equalized flow is the dyadic flow with its order of splits transposed: each square is split into left and right halves first and each half then vertically; its coordinate-\(1\) contribution is \(-((d_0+d_1)/\rho)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)\) in both halves, \(d_0+d_1\) being the left half's excess, and its coordinate \(2\) on each half in \(t_1\) is that half's vertical move. (b) Hence, as for the dyadic flow, every coarser field is separable on every finer square, the flow is linear in the counts, and, by the symmetry of the square, thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction applies to it with the coordinates exchanged. (c) The equalized \(\Phi\) is the exact minimizer of the square's coordinate-\(1\) cost alone, for every convex cost; for the quartic cost of both coordinates it is a descent direction at the dyadic choice, the derivative along \(\delta\Phi=(a_0-a_1)/4\) being \(-(a_0-a_1)^2(a_0^2+a_0a_1+a_1^2)\) per column, averaged over its points, \(a_b\) the coordinate-\(1\) loads of the two halves; the simultaneous rule's own step is not this direction, the steepest descent being proportional to \(a_0^3-a_1^3\), nonlinear in the counts.

Proof. (a) In half \(b\), \(-\mathrm{tent}'(t_2)\Phi=\mp2\Phi=\pm(d_0-d_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/\rho\) (minus in the bottom half, where \(\mathrm{tent}'=2\)), so the bottom half gets \((-2d_0+d_0-d_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/\rho\) and the top \((-2d_1-d_0+d_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/\rho\), both \(-(d_0+d_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/\rho\); with \(d_b=(e_{0,b}-e_{1,b})/2\) and \(\sum e=0\), \(d_0+d_1=e_{0,0}+e_{0,1}\), the left half's excess, and on the left half the vertical coefficient \(-E_0-(d_0-d_1)\) equals \(-2(e_{0,0}-(e_{0,0}+e_{0,1})/2)\), the left half's own vertical move (both identities also checked on random excesses); the divergence is kept, \(-\mathrm{tent}'(t_2)\psi+\psi\,\mathrm{tent}'(t_2)=0\). (b) The transposed flow is the dyadic flow of the square with its axes exchanged, so the sequential rules entry's (a) and thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction carry over by that exchange, the uniform points being invariant under it; linearity is that each contribution is a fixed function times an excess. (c) For each column the coordinate-\(1\) cost is \(\sum C(a_0-2\Phi)+C(a_1+2\Phi)\) over the two halves' points, the sum \((a_0-2\Phi)+(a_1+2\Phi)\) fixed, so by convexity it is least at \(a_0-2\Phi=a_1+2\Phi\), the equalized \(\Phi\), which vanishes at \(t_1=0,1\) since \(a_0-a_1\) is a multiple of \(\mathrm{tent}(t_1)\) (the coarser load cancelling in the difference); the derivative is \(\frac12(-8a_0^3+8a_1^3)\cdot\frac{a_0-a_1}4\); coordinate \(2\) is stationary at the dyadic choice because the coarser load there depends on \(t_2\) alone and \(\sum\psi=0\), so the first-order change \(\sum_{t_1,t_2}4F_2^3\psi(t_1)\mathrm{tent}(t_2)\) vanishes. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The nesting of dyadic squares and the symmetry of the square under exchanging the axes: (b). The tent profiles: (a). Convexity of the cost: the first part of (c); the quartic cost: its second part. No probability is used in (a), (c); (b)'s obstruction is thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction's, with its hypotheses.

Degenerate cases. \(d_0=d_1\): \(\Phi=0\), the two orders agree at that square. One level: the transposed split of the one square.

Nonvacuity. Any count configuration with \(d_0\ne d_1\) at the top square: there the equalized flow differs from the dyadic one, (a) and (b) hold at every level of every \(J\), and the descent in (c) is strict. Plainest bound. The dyadic flow itself, of which the equalized flow is the transpose, with the same per-point obstruction.

Baseline. The dyadic flow; the lemma shows that the exact minimizer of the coordinate-\(1\) cost alone is the transposed dyadic flow, still obstructed, so a gain can only come from the rule's balance of the two coordinates, nonlinear in the counts.

The run

Run. research/results/ultimate_matching_simultaneous_rule_20261017/simultaneous_rule_test.py, its expectations committed before the run (an exploratory smoke run at \(J=3,4\), not kept, came first), \(J=6,7,8\), \(N=16\cdot4^J\), eight seeds each, results.json beside it; the per-run times there sum to \(766.8\) s over \(24\) runs in eight processes. The Prediction of the sequential rules entry named \(J=6,\dots,9\); the run stops at \(J=8\), less general, by the time of the largest level's Newton solves, and the band \(0.15\) is kept. Control 1: the largest relative cost increase over a square's dyadic choice was \(0.0\), but the damped line search makes this nearly automatic, so it shows little; the negated first Newton step raised the cost on every seed, which shows only that the step descends the coded cost. No convergence check: Newton stops after at most \(30\) iterations and no residual is recorded. Control 2: global averages agree to \(4.6\cdot10^{-16}\). Positive control: the variance ratios rule/dyadic were \(0.579,0.642,0.650\) in coordinate \(1\) and \(1.364,1.341,1.260\) in coordinate \(2\) at \(J=6,7,8\) (seed means): the rule acts, and the ratios drift toward \(1\). Kurtosis of the pooled values divided by the dyadic flow's per-position standard deviation, dyadic against rule: coordinate \(1\) \(2.882\) against \(2.505\), \(3.030\) against \(2.674\), \(3.108\) against \(2.669\); coordinate \(2\) \(3.019\) against \(2.621\), \(2.966\) against \(2.530\), \(2.962\) against \(2.583\); gaps \(0.376,0.356,0.439\) and \(0.398,0.435,0.379\), half-sample seed spreads at most \(0.131\). Prediction: gap growth from \(J=6\) to \(8\) of \(+0.062\) and \(-0.019\), inside the band \(0.15\), but twice the seed spread (\(0.221\), \(0.263\)) exceeds the band, so the run does not tell a constant offset from a slow trend. The rule's pooled kurtosis is below \(3\) at every size, by more than the dyadic flow's own shortfall (the dyadic flow, asymptotically Gaussian per point, gives \(2.882\) at \(J=6\), since the positions of one seed share its coarse counts and eight seeds sample those only eight times, so the scale-mixture bound of \(3\) holds for the population and not for this estimate): this suggests, and does not establish, platykurtic per-point laws. What the run does not show: the tails at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) standard deviations, which kurtosis does not decide; any \(J\) beyond \(8\).

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The sixth review's retained test, the gap-charged bound for nested chains, was neither proved nor refuted; this entry tests a local flow construction on the primal side.

From the record's side: ex:greedy-circulation-tails, a one-parameter circulation per square chosen by the same quartic cost, gave a kurtosis lower by \(0.2\)–\(0.3\) without trend at \(J=6,\dots,10\); the simultaneous rule, with a function's worth of freedom per square, gives \(0.36\)–\(0.44\) at \(J=6,7,8\), its trend undecided; lem:sequential-rules-dyadic shows the sequential rules give the dyadic flow; lem:equalized-flow-separable is elementary, the transposed dyadic flow written in the rule's variables, and its (b) is the sequential rules entry's (a) and thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction after exchanging the axes; the run is a finite check of the greedy circulation's kind. The nearest registered statement by tools/claim_resemblance.py, lem:sequential-rules-dyadic (0.38), is neither a more general version nor a special case: it concerns rules that reproduce the dyadic flow, and this lemma its transpose.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. At the goal's own parameters it gives nothing toward a bound: a constant shape change in the fourth moment does not decide the per-point tails at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) standard deviations, which the obstruction is about; what the cycle could have given is a gap growing with \(J\), which the run's noise neither shows nor excludes.

Follow-up

Follow-up. Continuing. The item's readings: what a routing cannot change, answered (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux); sequential rules, the dyadic flow (lem:sequential-rules-dyadic); the simultaneous rule, here: its coordinate-\(1\) part alone is the transposed dyadic flow, and the rule itself lowers the pooled kurtosis by about \(0.4\) at the sizes run, with its trend undecided and its tails unmeasured; the discrete two-choice rule with integer units, the balls-into-bins dynamic the item names, not examined; costs weighing the tails, \(\psi_\alpha\) or a higher power, not examined. Next attempt: the tails the item asks about, for the simultaneous rule and the dyadic flow at \(J=6,7,8\): the fraction of positions with \(|F_k|/\sigma>t\) at the fixed thresholds \(t=2.2\) and \(3.3\) at every \(J\), and also at \(c\sqrt{2\log G^2}\) for \(c=\frac12,\frac34\), each with \(\sigma\) both the dyadic flow's analytic per-position standard deviation and the rule's own, estimated across seeds and symmetric positions, so that the rule's lower coordinate-\(1\) variance does not lower its exceedances by itself; from the existing script with those statistics added and expectations committed first. Smallest case. At \(J=6\) the evaluation grid has \(G^2=2^{14}\) points, \(\sqrt{2\log G^2}=4.4\), and the dyadic flow's Gaussian per-point values give an expected exceedance fraction at \(c=\frac12\), \(2.2\) standard deviations, of about \(0.028\), about \(460\) positions per seed, enough to compare; at \(c=\frac34\), \(3.3\) standard deviations, about \(0.001\), \(16\) positions per seed, \(130\) over eight seeds. Nontrivial because: the rule's pooled kurtosis at this size is below the dyadic flow's by about \(0.4\), so its exceedance fractions can differ from the Gaussian ones there, and the comparison reads the tail the item asks about rather than the fourth moment. Own statements. ex:simultaneous-rule-tails measures the fourth moment and not the exceedances; thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction gives the dyadic flow's Gaussian tails and not the rule's; lem:equalized-flow-separable decides the coordinate-\(1\) minimizer only; none decides the attempt. Plainest bound. For a Gaussian per-point law of standard deviation \(\sigma\), the exceedance at \(t\sigma\) is \(\mathrm{erfc}(t/\sqrt2)\), \(0.028\) at \(t=2.2\) and \(0.001\) at \(t=3.3\); the rule's should be lower if its lower fourth moment comes from the tails. Prediction. At the fixed threshold \(t=3.3\), with the rule's own \(\sigma\), the ratio of the rule's exceedance fraction to the dyadic flow's stays constant at \(J=6,7,8\); refuted if it falls with \(J\) by more than its seed spread. The fixed threshold matters: at \(c\sqrt{2\log G^2}\) the threshold rises with \(J\) (\(3.3\) to \(3.74\) standard deviations at \(c=\frac34\)), and a law that does not change but has lighter tails than a Gaussian already gives a falling ratio there. Process assessment. The first draft closed the item on a run whose noise exceeded its band, called the result a falsification while its own kurtosis, below the dyadic flow's, pointed the other way, and closed with a named part listed as unexamined; it described the rule's first-order move from the equalized direction without computing the rule's gradient; it presented a control the line search makes automatic as one that could fail. Prevention. The figure read as support when it pointed against the conclusion: AGENTS.md's order-of-work line on computations that agree with expectations now asks, in this commit, that each figure be read for what it says against the conclusion before the conclusion is written. The automatic control: the queued build control-can-fail.

Meta. The way of working behind the failed closure is wanting the item finished: the run agreed with the prediction, so I wrote the closure and read the figures as its support, without asking what the kurtosis below the dyadic flow's said against it; the correction then took the reviewer's stronger inference, that it rules out Gaussian laws, without checking it against the dyadic flow's own \(2.882\). It shows wherever a result is summarized toward the decision it was run for, or a reviewer's inference is adopted because it points the right way. The change is in PROMPTS.md's Spin step (commit of 17 October 2026): a queue item's Follow-up is drafted Continuing and changed to Closed or Developed only after the review has read the run's figures and the readings.

Rule's per-point tails lighter at 3.3σ

17 October 2026 · Finite check, reviewed · Two-choice routing. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A queue item's entry: a finite check that changes no statement of Where we stand.

Question. The queue head, two-choice-routing, with the next attempt of the simultaneous rule entry: "the tails the item asks about, for the simultaneous rule and the dyadic flow", the exceedance fractions at the fixed thresholds \(2.2\) and \(3.3\) standard deviations, with both the dyadic flow's and the rule's own per-position \(\sigma\). The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through its primal form; the test is whether the rule's per-point tails are lighter than Gaussian, and whether that changes from \(J=6\) to \(J=7\).

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters the best outcome is a lighter tail that grows with \(J\): evidence of a local mechanism escaping thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, which is proved for the dyadic flow alone and which a flow proof through a local rule must escape; a run at two sizes can show only a difference, so the best outcome would name a mechanism for a proof, not give one.

Target form. The goal's form is the class bound, of which the cheapest flow on the cells is a sufficient form by lem:grid-flow-duality (c) and (d); the quantity measured is the rule's per-point law, whose dyadic counterpart thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction bounds from below.

Owed attempt. The simultaneous rule entry's next attempt was made, in two runs. The straight-cut forced flux entry (its Follow-up: "The item's words allow three readings. First, what a two-choice routing cannot change") and the sequential rules entry (its Follow-up: "a rule that chooses a square's two moves together, not covered by (b), and the next attempt") named the attempts made since.

General statement. No all-parameter claim is proved here: the entry registers the finite check ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances, bearing on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through the flow route.

Two runs

First run. research/results/ultimate_matching_exceedance_20261017/exceedance_test.py, expectations committed first, \(J=6,7,8\), eight seeds, the exceedance fractions pooled over the positions of the seeds (results.json). Its Control 1, that the dyadic flow's fractions are Gaussian, failed: at \(3.3\) standard deviations the dyadic flow gave \(0.000198\) to \(0.00101\) against \(0.00097\), and at \(2.2\) from \(0.0178\) to \(0.0321\) against \(0.0278\), outside the stated bands at several sizes. This is consistent with the cause the simultaneous rule entry's second review pass named for the kurtosis, that the positions of one seed share its coarse counts and eight seeds sample the coarse levels only eight times; that cause is supported only by the second run's Control 1 passing once the seeds are many. The run decides nothing about the rule; its Prediction, not refuted, is not reported as passed. Its first launch failed at once on a pickling error, fixed before the run.

Second run. research/results/ultimate_matching_exceedance_20261017/many_seeds_test.py, expectations committed first, \(J=6,7\), \(512\) independent seeds, each position standardized by its own standard deviation across the seeds, for each flow (many_seeds_results.json; \(324\) s). The standard deviation includes the value standardized (population form): for Gaussian values this lowers the exceedance at \(3.3\) by \(3.4\%\) at \(512\) seeds, computed exactly for a centred numerator (the run's is uncentred, a difference of order \(1/S\)) and in a simulation (research/results/ultimate_matching_exceedance_20261017/self_inclusion_bias_check.txt), nearly equally for both flows, so the ratios below stand. The per-position means were not subtracted and not checked; a nonzero mean of the rule would raise its exceedances, so its lightness would be understated, not invented. Control 1 held: the dyadic flow's fractions were \(0.0276\)–\(0.0281\) at \(2.2\) (Gaussian \(0.0278\)) and \(0.00090\)–\(0.00111\) at \(3.3\) (Gaussian \(0.00097\)). Control 2 held: the empirical per-position variance of the dyadic flow over its analytic one averaged \(0.988\)–\(0.995\). The positive control, a planted lighter law (sign times \(|v|^{0.8}\), rescaled), gave ratios to the dyadic flow at \(3.3\) of \(0.036\)–\(0.063\); its outcome was fixed analytically (about \(0.04\) for a Gaussian input) far below its threshold \(0.7\), so it checks the code, not the statistic's resolution near the rule's ratios. The rule, standardized by its own \(\sigma\): fractions \(0.0197\)–\(0.0200\) at \(2.2\), about \(0.71\) of the dyadic flow's, and at \(3.3\) ratios to the dyadic flow of \(0.245\) at \(J=6\) and \(0.309\) at \(J=7\) in coordinate \(1\) (half-sample values \(0.228,0.260\) and \(0.307,0.311\)), and \(0.364\) and \(0.330\) in coordinate \(2\) (\(0.332,0.393\) and \(0.345,0.313\)). Prediction (constant ratio, refuted if it falls by more than the half-sample spread): not refuted; in coordinate \(1\) the ratio rose by \(0.064\), more than the larger spread \(0.031\), toward the dyadic flow's, and in coordinate \(2\) it fell by \(0.034\), within its spread \(0.062\); each spread is the difference of one split into halves, a single draw, so the coordinate-\(1\) rise is suggestive, not established. What the run does not show: a trend in \(J\), two sizes giving only a difference; the tails at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) standard deviations, \(3.3\) being below them (\(\sqrt{2\log G^2}=4.4\) and \(4.7\) at these sizes); larger \(J\).

Nonvacuity. The finite check's instances are the runs' own: \(J=6,7\), \(N=16\cdot4^J\), \(512\) seeds, every position of the evaluation grid, at which Control 1 shows the estimator reading the dyadic flow's tails as Gaussian. Plainest bound. Gaussian fractions \(\mathrm{erfc}(t/\sqrt2)\), \(0.0278\) at \(2.2\) and \(0.00097\) at \(3.3\), which the dyadic flow meets and the rule does not.

Baseline. The dyadic flow's per-point law, Gaussian at these thresholds by Control 1; the run adds that the simultaneous rule's per-point law has a lighter tail at \(3.3\) standard deviations by a factor of about \(3\) to \(4\) at \(J=6,7\).

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

Process assessment. The draft summarized a difference between two sizes as "not growing" on one split's spread, called the dyadic flow Gaussian by a theorem that gives a lower bound, presented a control fixed by arithmetic as one that tests the statistic, chose the next attempt's seed count by its cost without computing what it does to the estimator, and committed to a new compute.sh check after trying only the case that prompted it and one variant. Prevention. The single-split spread and the cost-chosen seed count: COMPUTATION_RULES.md now says, in this commit, that a spread from one split of the seeds is one draw and is stated as such, a decision resting on the spread of many splits or a bootstrap, and that a sample size changed between sizes for cost is checked first for what it does to the estimator's bias. The control fixed by arithmetic: the queued build control-can-fail. "Gaussian by the theorem": tools/draft_claim_sentences.py lists that sentence beside the theorem's statement, and I did not read the two together; the rule stands, the stage being my reading.

Meta. The habit behind these is fixing a design or a summary by what is cheap or by the case in front of me (the run that fits the time, the check that refuses the command that hit me, the word that matches my picture of the theorem) and then asking only whether the result passes, not what the choice did to the quantity measured or the class covered. It shows in seed counts, in checks fitted to one case and in summaries written from a source's gist. The change is in AGENTS.md's order of work (commit of 17 October 2026): a choice made to save cost or fitted to the case at hand (a sample size, a check's scope, a summary word) is written beside what it changes in the quantity measured or the class covered, before it is used.

Seventh review: one cut, two regimes

17 October 2026 · Route review · Seventh review. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: A route review: it changes no statement of Where we stand.

Open statements. conj:ultimate-matching and its sufficient form conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy, both open, with the two special-case statements of the list unchanged. The six entries since the sixth review proved the discrete form of the class bound sufficient, bounded what straight cuts force on a flow, closed the box-exit refutations, and tested local routing rules on the primal side; none changed an implication toward the goal.

The line's general claim. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy on the curve, now in its discrete form: by lem:grid-flow-duality (c), if with probability tending to one every grid function \(G\) with \(\sum_e\delta^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(|\Delta_eG|/\delta)\le2\) has \(\sum_QG_Q(n_Q-N\delta^2)\le\frac L2\sqrt{N\log N}\), on grids with \(1/\delta\) an integer, \(\delta\le s/32\) and \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\), then a matching has the conclusion of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction; by (d) of the same lemma the class supremum is a minimal edge flow cost.

What the goal needs. That discrete bound at every pair of the curve, or a matching built directly; equivalently, by lem:grid-flow-duality (d), an edge flow carrying the cell counts to the background at cost of order \(N\), with one universal \(L\).

The six entries

Cell flow duality (lem:grid-flow-duality): finite Fenchel–Rockafellar duality for edge flows, the Raviart–Thomas field of an edge flow, and with them the discrete \(X\)-term class bound suffices for the goal at every \(\alpha\in[1,\infty]^2\). Straight-cut forced flux (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux): every flow carries out of each subset \(A\) of a block its excess, so the cut forces cost at least \(m\Psi(|E_S(A)|/(m\lambda))\); straight cuts of disjoint blocks force at most \(\frac N2\psi_4(8\sqrt8/L)\). Sequential rules (lem:sequential-rules-dyadic): every sequential rule of two kinds reproduces the dyadic flow. Box exits (cor:box-exit-exclusion): no refutation through one pair's exit of a box containing \(R_K\) is correct. Simultaneous rule (lem:equalized-flow-separable, ex:simultaneous-rule-tails): its coordinate-\(1\) minimizer is the transposed dyadic flow; the full rule lowers the pooled kurtosis by about \(0.4\). Exceedances (ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances): at \(3.3\) standard deviations the rule's per-point tail is \(0.25\)–\(0.36\) of the dyadic flow's Gaussian one at \(J=6,7\), its change with \(J\) undecided.

Falsification attempt. Against the class bound in its primal form at \((4,4)\), through the period's new tool: the cost unions of cells force on every flow. Let \(\delta\) be dyadic with \(s/64\le\delta\le s/32\) (one exists; for \(L\ge256\) it meets lem:grid-flow-duality (c), \(N\delta^2\ge L^2\log N/4096\ge16\log N\), and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor with \(\kappa=L/64\ge4\), \(\delta\le2^{-\ell_1}\) holding for \(N\) large), and write \(L_f\) for the constant of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) at \(\kappa=4\), which serves for every \(\kappa\ge4\), a larger \(\kappa\) admitting fewer grids. For a union \(A\) of cells of perimeter \(P\), with \(m=P/\delta\) cut edges, lem:straight-cut-forced-flux (a) and (b), stated "for each subset \(A\) of \(S\)" (Jensen over the cut's edges), give for every flow carrying the counts to the background a cost \(\lambda'\delta^2\sum_e\psi_4(|\theta_e|/(\delta\lambda's))\), the functional of lem:grid-flow-duality (d) at \(\lambda'=N/4\) (that is \((1-2h)N/2\) with \(h=1/4\), as in its (c)), of at least \(\lambda'\delta^2m\,\psi_4\big(|E(A)|/(m\delta\lambda's)\big)\), \(E(A)=N\lambda(A)-n(A)\). With \(|E(A)|=c\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}P\) the argument is \(4c(\log N)^{1/4}/L\) for every \(P\), and the forced cost is \(\frac N4\delta P(N^a-1)\), \(a=256(c/L)^4\); by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), \(c\le L_f\) for every such \(A\) at once, so one union forces at most \(\frac L{128}P\sqrt{\log N}\,N^{1/2+a}\), which is \(o(N)\) at \(P\) of order one when \(L>512^{1/4}L_f=4.757\,L_f\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_review7_20261017/single_set_forced_cost.txt). Its weaker form is recorded, as the stage-two reviewer found and I checked: the forced cost of one cut is, by conjugacy, \(\sup_t\) of the dual value of lem:grid-flow-duality (d) at \(G=t\mathbf 1_A\), a single layer, and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) bounds single layers at every level \(y\ge2e^{16}\) by \(C'\sqrt{N\log N}\), which through homogeneity bounds one set's dual value by about \(C'N/L\), at most \(N/2\) for \(L\ge2C'\): no refutation, but not \(o(N)\); the \(o(N)\) and the threshold come from lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) as computed here. Unions with pairwise edge-disjoint boundaries (nested, disjoint or crossing; nested unions may share edges) add their forced costs. At the top argument, each at the Leighton–Shor order, about \(N^{1/2-a}\) of them, up to logarithms, reach cost \(N\) (\(N^{0.30}\) at \(L/c=6\), \(N^{0.47}\) at \(L/c=10\)), which the grid's \(\sum_kP_k\le2/\delta\) admits, a fraction about \(N^{-a}\) of the edges lying on such boundaries; but sets whose excess gives intermediate arguments \(u\), \(1\ll u^4\ll\log N\), on a fraction about \(e^{-u^4}\) of the edges could also add to \(N\), no such family being known, and that regime, levels \(y=e^{\Theta(u^4)}\) with \(\log y=o(\log N)\), is where the sixth review's loss \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\) lives. At the top argument the layers sit at polynomial levels \(y\) of order \(N^a\), where lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) loses no logarithm: there the gap between the recorded bound and the target is a constant ratio, about \(2(L_f/c)L\sqrt{N\log N}\) against \(\frac L2\sqrt{N\log N}\) (the reviewer's estimate, unverified, the conventions \(\psi^*(|\Delta|/\delta)\) and \(\psi^*(|\Delta|/(2\delta))\) shifting the constants). Not decided: the attempt names two regimes among the ways a family could reach cost \(N\), Leighton–Shor-order layers at polynomial levels, a question of constants, and intermediate levels, the sixth review's Obstacle; bounded arguments \(u=O(1)\) on a fixed fraction of the edges, and mixtures across classes of \(u\), are not covered. The level an argument \(u\) corresponds to, about \(\psi_4'(u)=4u^3e^{u^4}\), is derived here by conjugacy, not recorded.

Assessment of this line. The period settled two questions of form and none of substance: the discrete class bound suffices (so the dual and primal problems are one problem up to constants), and refutations through one pair's box exit or through straight cuts are excluded. On the primal side, the two families of local rules the lemmas cover (sequential rules of the two kinds of lem:sequential-rules-dyadic, and the coordinate-\(1\) part of the simultaneous rule, lem:equalized-flow-separable) reproduce the dyadic flow or its transpose; the full simultaneous rule, nonlinear, has lighter per-point tails at \(3.3\) standard deviations, a finite check at two sizes near \(N=10^6\), where \((\log N)^{1/4}\) is about \(1.9\), saying nothing at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) standard deviations. The falsification attempt finds that one set cannot refute the bound for large \(L\) (in its weak form recorded already, in dual form, by lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) at \(K=1\); \(o(N)\) by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a)); among the ways families of sets with disjoint boundaries could reach \(N\) are the Leighton–Shor order at polynomial levels, a question of constants, and intermediate levels, the sixth review's Obstacle, bounded arguments and mixtures being not covered. Five research entries in a row declared no bearing on the goal; the queue, draining since before the sixth review, holds \(38\) items against \(33\) then (the review's data-queue-items), the period having added seven builds (the items stamped after the sixth review, listed under Builds) and closed none.

Obstacle

The line is stuck where the sixth review put it, with its primal form now written: for chains of many nested layers, each a union of cells fitted to the points at its own scale (\(K\ge N^{1/7}\), increments or pile-ups reaching \(N^c\) at levels \(y=N^{o(1)}\)), the dual bounds lose \((\log N/\log y)^{1/4}\) (lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c)); on the primal side, the forced costs of lem:straight-cut-forced-flux (b) of sets with edge-disjoint boundaries could reach \(N\) through intermediate arguments \(1\ll u^4\ll\log N\), which correspond to those levels by conjugacy (derived here, not recorded), while at the top argument, polynomial levels, the recorded bound misses the target by a constant ratio only (unverified estimate); no family of either kind is known. The forced cost one set's cut gives is \(o(N)\) for \(L>4.757L_f\).

Architecture review

Necessary target. The weakest endpoint: at every pair of the curve, with probability tending to one, one matching with \(\sum_i\exp[(|X^j_i-Y^j_{\pi(i)}|/s)^{\alpha_j}]\le2N\) for both \(j\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L\) universal; evenly spread \(Y\) suffice by lem:two-sample-matching-transfer. Downstream. Through lem:grid-flow-duality (c) the discrete \(X\)-term class bound on grids with \(\delta\le s/32\) and \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\) gives that endpoint at every pair with \(\alpha\in[1,\infty]^2\), which covers the curve; through its (d) the bound is a minimal edge flow cost; the proved downstream statements bound parts of that discrete class at \((4,4)\) (lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), lem:guided-chain-bound (d), lem:discrete-flow-bound (c)) and the straight-cut part of the primal cost (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux (c)); weaker than the goal.

Extra requirements. The route still demands the uniform class bound where the goal needs one matching; lem:grid-flow-duality (d) makes the two one problem for the discrete class, so the demand is now no stronger than building one cheap flow, and is justified. The \((4,4)\) restriction of the period's dual lemmas remains unjustified for the goal: the interior pairs need anisotropic versions (the queued idea anisotropic-fine-grid). The primal tests asked for per-point Gaussian tails to be lost; the goal needs only the total cost, so per-point tails are a convenience: a flow could have Gaussian per-point values and still cost order \(N\) if its large values are rare enough, which thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction excludes for the dyadic flow only.

Independent alternative. The stage-one reviewer (stage-one record, its brief stage1.txt saved beside it) was given the goal, the thread's registered results and the open conjectures with their evidence, and asked open questions; its independence was compromised, as it reported itself: the brief's folder also held the sixth review's text, which a reviewer told that the brief's files were its sources could read, so its architecture (A), the dual route breaking at intermediate levels, matches the sixth review's and is not independent evidence. It proposed two more. (B) Exact assignment duality: for one cost \(C\), \(\min_\pi\sum_iC(X_i-Y_{\pi(i)})=\max\{\sum_if(X_i)+\sum_ig(Y_i):f(x)+g(y)\le C(x-y)\}\), the assignment polytope being integral, with no smearing and no tube density; at a weight \(\theta\in[0,1]\), potentials with \(\min_\pi\sum(\theta c_1+(1-\theta)c_2)>2N\) refute the conjecture; its first lemma compares \(c\)-concave potentials with the reduction's class, and it breaks where \(c\)-concavity at scale \(s\) is weaker than a gradient penalty, jumps over distances below \(s\) being cheap for a superlinear \(C\). (C) A nonlinear primal construction with negatively correlated levels, its break mass conservation. It found the endpoint \((2,\infty)\) untried, the obstruction acting only on coordinate \(2\) there, and checked by hand that composing matchings at the two endpoints gives only \((2,2)\). Compared with the current route: (B)'s weighted refutation criterion is a necessary condition for the goal free of tube density, in potential form; I checked its two steps: a matching with both sums at most \(2N\) has every \(\theta\)-weighted sum at most \(2N\), and for one cost the assignment linear program has integral extreme points, so its dual is exact. What it does not give is the class form: comparing \(c\)-concave pairs with the gradient-penalized class is the sixth review's tube-density converse in another shape. A \(\theta\)-certificate refutes the conjecture, but its absence proves nothing: \(\min_\pi\max_j\) of the two sums can exceed \(\max_\theta\min_\pi\) of the weighted one, the minimax holding only over doubly stochastic matrices. So, by judgement, (B) joins the queued idea tube-density-reroute as its sub-idea, not as an item, although (B) could also refute directly through \(c\)-concave potentials without any converse to the class, which that item does not cover. (C) is the period's primal work, whose local rules either reproduce the dyadic flow or are nonlinear with lighter tails at \(3.3\) standard deviations. Its flags on registered results were already recorded, as registry edges of research/claims/index.json: thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion refines lem:common-exponent-cap ("Implies it: every pair in (4,infinity]^2 lies below the curve"), and lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound cites lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound ("Gives the same order at every pair, endpoints included, by the Lipschitz baseline that lemma left unchecked"); its doubt on thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential as a rediscovery is answered in that claim's assessment: "Talagrand and Yukich (Ann. Appl. Probab. 1993, Theorem 1, statement read 16 October 2026, proofs unread) prove the isotropic two-sample pair (2,2) as an expectation bound on a set of probability 1-n^(-2)".

Mixed counts in column windows

17 October 2026 · Working proof; low second levels, any box ratio · Mixed levels. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

The queue head is two-choice-routing, which has had two entries in a row declaring no bearing, so the finisher refuses a third; the seventh review chose mixed-level-counts, which bears on ultimate-matching directly: the condition implies the mixed level counts, so a refutation of them would refute the conjecture.

Question. The owed attempt of the low-level mixed counts entry (its Follow-up: "Next attempt: the reviewer's \(m\)-column windows, to remove \(\rho_N\to\infty\)"): does the construction there, with leftovers matched within windows of \(m\) columns instead of three, give the mixed counts for bounded box ratios? The missing implication is the mixed counts at every pair of levels, a consequence of conj:ultimate-matching; this entry extends the region where they are proved, and the test ends at the extended statement's proof or its failure.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, the mixed consequence for every bounded box ratio at low second levels, so that a refutation through two levels must use second levels with \(e^{2t_2}\) above about \(\log N\,t_1^{\beta_1}t_2^{\beta_2}\); it must beat thm:low-level-mixed-counts, which needs \(\rho_N\to\infty\).

Target form. The goal's own form, a matching, at two of its levels; no surrogate class or measure is used.

Owed attempt. The low-level mixed counts entry named two attempts: the \(m\)-column windows, made here (the theorem below), and the both-high instance \(t_1=\log N\), \(t_2=\sqrt{\log N}\) at \((4,4)\) against a test-set argument tolerating \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) exceptions, not made as named; its plainest form was tried, on the reviewer's pointer: thm:per-level-count-matchings at the level \(t=t_2\), with its universal constant \(L_0\) (so for \(L\ge L_0\)), gives a matching with at most \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) pairs beyond \(L_0s_1t_2^{1/4}\) in some coordinate, and its first-coordinate box \(L_0s_1t_2^{1/4}\) is within \(D=Ls_1(\log N)^{1/4}\) (\(2.9\) against \(8.4\) at \(\log N=5000\), witness.txt), so at the both-high instance every pair but those \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) already meets both levels, and what is missing is only the first-coordinate bound for the bad pairs, all but two of which must have \(|\Delta^1|\le D\). The instance is then a repair question, which the Follow-up takes; a refutation stays one of two directions, not forced by the failure of one class of construction. The test-set argument waits for that reason: the plainest form reduced the instance to a repair whose cost is the open quantity, so the repair comes first, and the refutation is tried if the repair's cycles are shown long.

General statement. thm:windowed-mixed-counts, for every exponent pair, every \(L>0\) and every sequence of levels and window widths meeting its two conditions.

Windowed mixed counts

Theorem. Let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in(0,\infty]\), \(\beta_j=1/\alpha_j\), \(s_1=\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L>0\), levels \(t_1=t_{1,N},t_2=t_{2,N}\in[1,\log N]\), \(\rho_N=t_1^{\beta_1}/t_2^{\beta_2}\), \(\Lambda_N=\log N\,t_1^{\beta_1}t_2^{\beta_2}\), and integers \(m=m_N\ge1\) with (i) \((m+1)e^{2t_2}\le\frac{L^2}2\Lambda_N\) and (ii) \(m\rho_N\to\infty\). No curve condition is assumed. For \(X_1,\dots,X_N\), \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\) independent and uniform on \([0,1]^2\), with probability tending to one there is a matching \(\pi\) with \(|X_i^1-Y^1_{\pi(i)}|\le Ls_1t_1^{\beta_1}\) for every \(i\) and \(\#\{i:|X_i^2-Y^2_{\pi(i)}|>Ls_1t_2^{\beta_2}\}\le2Ne^{-t_2}\).

Proof. The low-level mixed counts entry's construction, with its three columns replaced by \(m\); each step is that entry's, rerun at \(m\). Put \(D=Ls_1t_1^{\beta_1}\), \(H=Ls_1t_2^{\beta_2}\). Cells: columns of width \(a\in[D/(2(m+1)),D/(m+1)]\) with \(1/a\) an integer (\(D\to0\)), each cut into cells of height \(h\in[H/2,H]\) with \(1/h\) an integer, so a cell has mean count \(k=Nah\ge NDH/(4(m+1))=\frac{L^2\Lambda_N}{4(m+1)}\ge\frac12e^{2t_2}\) by (i), in particular \(k\ge e^2/2>1\). In each cell match \(\min(n_X,n_Y)\) of its points; its \(|z|\) others, \(z=n_X-n_Y\), are its leftovers. Leftovers: ordered by column and matched by rank; with \(\Lambda(c)\) the difference of the two samples' leftover counts in the columns up to \(c\), if every window of \(m\) consecutive columns holds at least \(\sup_c|\Lambda(c)|\) leftovers of each sample, then the \(i\)-th \(X\) leftover, in column \(c\), has rank at most the \(X\) count up to \(c\), which the \(Y\) count up to \(c+m\) reaches (it is at least the \(Y\) count up to \(c\), which is at least the \(X\) count up to \(c\) less \(|\Lambda(c)|\), plus the window's supply), and symmetrically the \(Y\) count up to \(c-m-1\) is below that rank; (where a window would run past the last column, or \(c-m-1<1\), the bound holds trivially, the count up to the last column being the total and the count up to column \(0\) being zero), so matched leftovers lie at most \(m\) columns apart and \(|\Delta^1|\le(m+1)a\le D\) for every pair, the cell pairs having \(|\Delta^1|\le a\). As there, \(\Lambda(c)=U_X(ca)-U_Y(ca)\) with \(U_X(x)=\#\{i:X^1_i\le x\}-Nx\), and by Doob's inequality for the martingale \(U_X(x)/(1-x)\) and the reflection \(x\mapsto1-x\), \(\sup_x|U_X-U_Y|\le\omega_N\sqrt N\) with probability tending to one for every deterministic \(\omega_N\to\infty\); take \(\omega_N=(m\rho_N)^{1/4}\), deterministic by (ii). Supply: a window has \(M=m/h\) cells; under Poissonization its \(Y\) leftovers \(S=\sum z_Q^-\) are a sum of \(M\) independent nonnegative variables with \(\mathbb Ez^-\ge\frac14\sqrt k\) (\(k\ge1\)) and \(\mathbb E(z^-)^2\le k\), so the lower tail of such sums (Maurer 2003, as cited there) gives \(\Pr(S\le M\sqrt k/8)\le e^{-M/128}\); over at most \(1/a\le2(m+1)/D\le N\) windows, two samples and the de-Poissonization factor \(e^2N\), the failure probability is at most \(2e^2N^2e^{-M/128}\to0\), since \(M\ge1/H\). And \(M\sqrt k/8=\frac m8\sqrt{Na/h}\ge\frac m8\sqrt{\frac{N\rho_N}{2(m+1)}}\ge\frac1{16}\sqrt{m\rho_N}\sqrt N\) (as \(D/H=\rho_N\), \(h\le H\) and \(m^2/(2(m+1))\ge m/4\)), which exceeds \((m\rho_N)^{1/4}\sqrt N\) once \(m\rho_N>2^{16}\), so for \(N\) large by (ii). Second level: only leftover pairs may have \(|\Delta^2|>H\); they number \(\frac12\sum_Q|z_Q|\), of mean at most \(N/\sqrt{2k}\) (Cauchy–Schwarz with \(\mathbb Ez^2\le2k\) per cell) and variance at most \(4N\) (Efron–Stein, one point moving changes the sum by at most \(2\)), so with probability tending to one they number at most \(\sqrt2N/\sqrt k\) (as \(\sqrt N=o(N/\sqrt k)\), \(k\le NDH=L^2\Lambda_N\) being polylogarithmic), which is at most \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) since \(k\ge\frac12e^{2t_2}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. (i) gives \(k\ge\frac12e^{2t_2}\), used in the second level's count and for \(k\ge1\) in the supply's mean bound; the factor \(m+1\) in it is the column width \(D/(m+1)\) that keeps \(m\) columns within \(D\). (ii) gives the supply \(\frac1{16}\sqrt{m\rho_N}\sqrt N\) beating the strip discrepancy \(\omega_N\sqrt N\). \(t_j\le\log N\) with fixed exponents: \(D\to0\), and \(k\le L^2\Lambda_N\) polylogarithmic for the leftover count's concentration; \(t_1\ge1\): \(D\ge Ls_1\), so at most \(2(m+1)/D\le N\) windows; \(t_2\ge1\): only \(k\ge1\), which needs \(t_2\ge\frac12\log2\). \(m\ge1\): a window, and \(m^2/(2(m+1))\ge m/4\). Independence and uniformity of the two samples: Poissonization, Doob and Efron–Stein. No condition on the exponents, \(L\) or the curve is used; the conclusion holds for every pair, below the curve too, which does not conflict with thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion (that concerns the whole condition, this two of its levels).

Degenerate cases. \(m=3\): (i) is \(e^{2t_2}\le\frac{L^2}8\Lambda_N\) and (ii) is \(\rho_N\to\infty\), thm:low-level-mixed-counts exactly. \(\alpha_1=\infty\): \(\rho_N=t_2^{-\beta_2}\), and the largest \(m\) allowed by (i) gives \(m\rho_N\) of order \(L^2\log N\,e^{-2t_2}\), so the theorem holds when \(e^{2t_2}=o(\log N)\), which thm:low-level-mixed-counts excluded. \(t_1=t_2\) on and above the curve: covered already by thm:per-level-count-matchings; here for every pair. (i) failing for \(m=1\), \(e^{2t_2}>\frac{L^2}4\Lambda_N\): outside the theorem. A scheme of cells of area at most \(DH\) (so that cell pairs meet both boxes, \(k\le L^2\Lambda_N\)) whose leftovers may all violate the second level fails for \(e^{2t_2}>64L^2\Lambda_N\): its leftover pairs have mean at least \(\frac{N}{k}\cdot\frac{\sqrt k}2\cdot\frac12=\frac N{4\sqrt k}\ge\frac N{4L\sqrt{\Lambda_N}}\), above \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) there (the Hölder bound \(\mathbb E|z|\ge(2k)^{3/2}/(12k^2+2k)^{1/2}\ge0.756\sqrt k\) for \(k\ge1\), witness.txt), with concentration as in the second-level step; between \(\frac{L^2}4\Lambda_N\) and \(64L^2\Lambda_N\) neither the theorem nor this count decides. Taking \(h=H/r\) instead gives the same two conditions with \((m+1)r\) for \(m+1\), so inside this scheme (i) cannot be weakened beyond constants.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters: \((4,4)\), \(t_1=\frac23\log\log N\), \(t_2=\frac13\log\log N\), so \(\rho_N=2^{1/4}\) is bounded and thm:low-level-mixed-counts does not apply; \(\Lambda_N=\log N(t_1t_2)^{1/4}\), \(e^{2t_2}=(\log N)^{2/3}\), and \(m+1=\lfloor\frac{L^2}2\Lambda_Ne^{-2t_2}\rfloor\), of order \((\log N)^{1/3}(\log\log N)^{1/2}\), gives \(m\rho_N\to\infty\): at \(L=1\), \(m+1=17\), \(127\), \(18045\) and \(m\rho_N=19.0\), \(149.8\), \(21458\) at \(\log N=5000,10^6,10^{12}\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_windowed_counts_20261017/witness.txt). The levels differ, so thm:per-level-count-matchings does not cover it, and the step the theorem adds, windows of \(m\to\infty\) columns, is used. Plainest bound. The both-low baseline of the low-level mixed counts entry, cells of size \(D\times H\) with any matching inside, needs \(e^{2t_1}\) at most about \(L^2\Lambda_N\) too; at the witness \(e^{2t_1}/(L^2\Lambda_N)=8.5\), \(39\), \(2771\) at those sizes (same file), growing as \((\log N)^{1/3}\), so it does not decide the witness.

Baseline. The both-low cells, which serve when both \(e^{2t_j}\lesssim L^2\Lambda_N\), and thm:low-level-mixed-counts, which serves when \(\rho_N\to\infty\); the theorem adds bounded and vanishing box ratios at low second levels, the condition being on the product \(m\rho_N\) rather than on \(\rho_N\), at the cost of the factor \(m+1\) in (i).

Column crossing obstruction at mixed levels

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed · Mixed levels. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

The windowed mixed counts entry left the both-high instance, \((4,4)\), \(t_1=\log N\), \(t_2=\sqrt{\log N}\), as a repair: the per-level matching leaves \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) bad pairs whose first coordinate must be brought within \(D_1\). Before the cycle bound its lead asks for, which constructions can a repair take at all? The missing implication is the mixed counts at both-high levels; the test is whether the one-dimensional strip discrepancy already excludes a class of constructions, and which.

At the goal's own parameters, an obstruction excluding every construction of a named kind at the both-high instance, so that a construction of the mixed counts there, or of the conjecture, must have a property the record can name; it must beat thm:windowed-mixed-counts, which stops below this instance, and thm:position-blind-cell-exits, which excludes another kind.

The windowed mixed counts entry's next attempt, "the repair, by the reviewer's lead (unverified)", the alternating cycles of the per-level and maximum-displacement matchings, was not made: the plainest quantity on any repair, the net crossing count of each vertical line, came first, since it constrains where the repaired pairs must lie and so which cycles can be short; the theorem below is that count summed over a family of lines, and the cycle attempt is carried to the Follow-up in the form it leaves.

General statement. lem:column-crossing-count, deterministic, for every point configuration, every \(D\ge0\), every matching and every family of vertical lines with gaps below \(\frac12\); and its corollary thm:column-crossing-obstruction, for every exponent pair, every \(L>0\), all levels and line spacings meeting its three conditions, and every family chosen after the samples.

Column crossing count

Lemma. For points \(X_1,\dots,X_N\), \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\) of \([0,1]^2\), let \(U(x)=\#\{i:X^1_i\le x\}-\#\{i:Y^1_i\le x\}\) and \(\Omega_w=\sup_{|x-x'|\le2w}|U(x)-U(x')|\). For every \(D\ge0\), every \(w\in(0,1/2)\), every family \(F\) of vertical lines with consecutive gaps, and gaps to \(0\) and \(1\), at most \(w\), and every matching \(\pi\): with \(A\) the pairs with \(|\Delta^1|\le D\) that cross a line of \(F\) and \(B\) the pairs with \(|\Delta^1|>D\), \[(D+w)\,|A|+(1+w)\,|B|\ \ge\ \tfrac12\int_0^1|U|-\Omega_w.\]

Proof. Crossing identity: pairs with both ends left of \(x\), or both right, cancel in \(U(x)\), so \(|U(x)|\le\#\{\text{pairs crossing }x\}\). Subfamily: take \(x_1\) the first line of \(F\) at or beyond \(w\), and each next one the first at least \(w\) beyond the last taken; consecutive taken lines are between \(w\) and \(2w\) apart, the original gaps being at most \(w\). With \(I_k\) the interval ending at \(x_k\) since the previous taken line (from \(0\) for \(k=1\)) and a last interval from the last taken line to \(1\), all of length at most \(2w\), and \(U(1)=0\): \(\int_0^1|U|\le\sum_k|I_k|\big(|U(x_k)|+\Omega_w\big)+2w\,\Omega_w\le2w\sum_k|U(x_k)|+2\Omega_w\), so \(\sum_k|U(x_k)|\ge(\int|U|-2\Omega_w)/(2w)\). Counting: a pair of horizontal extent \(\delta\) crosses at most \(\delta/w+1\) taken lines, and only pairs of \(A\cup B\) cross any; so \(\sum_k|U(x_k)|\le|A|(D/w+1)+|B|(1/w+1)\). Multiplying by \(w\) gives the lemma. \(\square\)

Theorem. Let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in(0,\infty]\), \(\beta_j=1/\alpha_j\), \(s_1=\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L>0\), \(D_j=Ls_1t_j^{\beta_j}\), levels \(t_1,t_2\in[1,\log N]\) and \(w=w_N\) with (a) \(Ne^{-t_1}=o(\sqrt N)\), (b) \(e^{-t_2}\big(\sqrt N\,w+L\sqrt{\log N}\,t_1^{\beta_1}\big)\to0\), (c) \(w\log N\to0\) (so \(w<1/2\) for \(N\) large). Call a pair an exception when \(|\Delta^1|>D_1\) or \(|\Delta^2|>D_2\). For \(X_1,\dots,X_N\), \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\) independent and uniform on \([0,1]^2\), with probability tending to one: for every family \(F\) of vertical lines with gaps at most \(w\), chosen after the samples, every matching with at most \(2Ne^{-t_1}\) pairs beyond \(D_1\) in the first coordinate and at most \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) beyond \(D_2\) in the second has at least \(\varepsilon_N\sqrt N/(8(D_1+w))\) pairs that are not exceptions and cross a line of \(F\), for some \(\varepsilon_N\to0\); in particular it has one.

Proof. The lemma with \(D=D_1\): \(B\) is the pairs beyond \(D_1\) in the first coordinate, at most \(2Ne^{-t_1}\); \(A\) splits into its exceptions, which are beyond \(D_2\) in the second coordinate, at most \(2Ne^{-t_2}\), and its non-exceptions \(A'\). So \((D_1+w)|A'|\ge\frac12\int|U|-\Omega_w-2Ne^{-t_2}(D_1+w)-2Ne^{-t_1}(1+w)\), and the subtracted allowance terms are \(2\sqrt N\,e^{-t_2}\big(L\sqrt{\log N}\,t_1^{\beta_1}+\sqrt N\,w\big)+4Ne^{-t_1}=\eta_N\sqrt N\) with \(\eta_N\to0\) by (a) and (b). Probability: \(U/\sqrt{2N}\) converges in distribution, in the uniform norm, to a Brownian bridge \(B\) (Donsker for the two independent empirical processes of the first coordinates); \(f\mapsto\int|f|\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz there and \(\int|B|>0\) almost surely, so for every \(\varepsilon_N\to0\), \(\Pr(\int|U|<\varepsilon_N\sqrt N)\to0\). And \(\Omega_w\) is at most twice the largest deviation \(|\#\{X^1\in I\}-N|I||\) over intervals \(I\) of length at most \(2w\), plus the same for \(Y\); by Bernstein for each interval with endpoints on the grid of mesh \(1/N\) (at most \((N+1)^2\) of them, variance at most \(N(2w+2/N)\)) and the rounding to that grid, which moves at most the counts of two grid cells, at most \(3\log N\) each with probability tending to one, \(\Omega_w\le C(\sqrt{Nw\log N}+\log N)=\theta_N\sqrt N\) with \(\theta_N=C(\sqrt{w\log N}+\log N/\sqrt N)\to0\) by (c), with probability tending to one. With \(\varepsilon_N=4\max(\sqrt{\eta_N},\sqrt{\theta_N},N^{-1/8})\to0\): on the intersection of the two events, \(\frac12\int|U|-\Omega_w-\eta_N\sqrt N\ge(\frac12\varepsilon_N-\theta_N-\eta_N)\sqrt N\ge\frac18\varepsilon_N\sqrt N\) once \(\eta_N,\theta_N\le1/16\) (as \(\theta_N\le\sqrt{\theta_N}\le\varepsilon_N/4\) and \(\eta_N\le\sqrt{\eta_N}/4\le\varepsilon_N/16\)), so \(|A'|\ge\varepsilon_N\sqrt N/(8(D_1+w))>0\). The events involve neither \(F\) nor \(\pi\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The lemma is deterministic and holds for every \(D\), every matching and every family; it uses only the first coordinates. In the theorem, (a) and (b) bound the allowance terms, (b)'s two parts coming from \(D_1\) and \(w\) in the crossing count; (c) gives \(\Omega_w=o(\sqrt N)\) and \(w<1/2\). Independence and uniformity of the first coordinates: Donsker and Bernstein. The second coordinate and \(D_2\) enter only through the allowance \(2Ne^{-t_2}\); no condition on the exponents, \(L\) or the curve; the family may depend on the samples because the events involve no family.

Degenerate cases. \(F\) a single line: the gaps condition then forces \(w\ge1/2\), outside (c); one line alone gives \(|U(x)|\) crossings, of order \(\sqrt N\), far below \(2Ne^{-t_2}\), and decides nothing (Plainest bound). \(w\) of order \(e^{t_2}/\sqrt N\) or above: (b) fails and the theorem is silent, a limit of the method; whether coarser families must be crossed is not decided, the per-level matching, whose cells are that coarse, failing the first level \(t_1=\log N\) and so saying nothing here. \(t_1\) below \(\frac12\log N\): (a) fails; the first-coordinate allowance \(2Ne^{-t_1}\) then exceeds \(\sqrt N\).

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters: \((4,4)\), \(t_1=\log N\), \(t_2=\sqrt{\log N}\), \(w=D_1\): (a) \(Ne^{-\log N}=1\); (b) \(e^{-t_2}(\sqrt N\,D_1+L(\log N)^{3/4})=2L(\log N)^{3/4}e^{-\sqrt{\log N}}\), \(\exp(-64.3)\) at \(\log N=5000\) and \(L=1\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_column_crossing_20261017/instance.txt); (c) \(D_1\log N\to0\). The theorem's conclusion is about every matching meeting the two allowances, so it needs no member of a class; the step it adds over one line, the sum over about \(1/w\) lines, is used. Plainest bound. One line: \(|U(x)|\) crossings, of order \(\sqrt N\), against \(2Ne^{-t_2}\), whose logarithm exceeds \(\frac12\log N\) by \(2430\) at \(\log N=5000\). The column-imbalance pigeonhole: columns of width \(w\) have \(\frac12\sum_c|n_X(c)-n_Y(c)|\), about \(\sqrt{N/w}\), pairs leaving their column, above \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) only for \(w<e^{2t_2}/(4N)\), \(\exp(-4860)\) at \(\log N=5000\), short of \(D_1\) (\(\exp(-2493.6)\)); the theorem reaches \(o(e^{t_2}/\sqrt N)\) (\(\exp(-2429.3)\)), a gain of about \(\sqrt N\,e^{-t_2}\) (same file).

Baseline. The windowed mixed counts entry's own count: a scheme of cells of area at most \(D_1D_2\) whose leftovers may all violate has about \(N/(4\sqrt k)\) leftover pairs with \(k\le L^2(\log N)^{11/8}\) at this instance, so it fails there; and thm:position-blind-cell-exits excludes rules whose exits from square cells are chosen by labels and memberships. The theorem adds, at mixed levels with \(Ne^{-t_1}=o(\sqrt N)\): every rule, position-aware included, cells of any height, and any family of vertical lines with gaps \(o(e^{t_2}/\sqrt N)\) chosen after the samples, must have pairs inside both boxes crossing the lines, at least \(\varepsilon_N\sqrt N/(8(D_1+w))\) of them; so a scheme whose bookkeeping counts every pair crossing a column line as an exception, as the windowed construction's does, cannot meet the both-high instance with columns that fine.

Architecture test

Architecture test. Not decided. The seventh review's retained nested-chain test was not run; the obstruction is on the primal side at two levels and does not bound chains.

Record search. tools/search-claims.py "strip discrepancy vertical lines crossing pairs columns cells matching exceptions one dimensional flux" returned thm:low-level-mixed-counts, lem:grid-flow-duality, thm:windowed-mixed-counts, lem:smeared-y-term, lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound and lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound; none bounds the pairs crossing a family of lines.

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:windowed-mixed-counts and thm:low-level-mixed-counts use the strip discrepancy \(U\), bounded above by Doob, to match leftovers; here it is bounded below, by Donsker, and turned into a count of crossings. thm:position-blind-cell-exits is the nearest exclusion: square cells, exits chosen without positions, every coordinate; this theorem needs no square cells and allows positions, at the price of mixed levels with a small second allowance and a fine family of lines. thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion counts forced exceptions of one test set with at most two allowed; here a whole family of lines, with \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) allowed. The low-level mixed counts entry, whose follow-up reads "bounded box ratio and a high second level remain, and a refutation there would refute the conjecture", recorded among its reviewer's unverified suggestions that re-matching the bad pairs of a per-level matching by column order fails, their density \(e^{-t_2}\) being too low against the strip discrepancy; the lemma here is the proved form of that count for every scheme whose crossing pairs are all exceptions, and the Smallest case below meets the same density question at one cell boundary. The registry's nearest statements by wording: thm:per-level-count-matchings is neither more general nor a special case: it constructs, at one level common to both coordinates, a matching with at most \(2Ne^{-t}\) pairs beyond the level in some coordinate, and at the both-high instance its matching at level \(t_2\) has about \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) pairs beyond \(D_1\), far above the allowance \(2Ne^{-\log N}=2\), so it is outside the theorem's hypotheses and the two do not meet; thm:range-negativity, a statement on off-line pairs of zeros and a kernel \(G_L\) in another thread, shares words only and is neither.

New mathematics. thm:column-crossing-obstruction: at mixed levels with \(Ne^{-t_1}=o(\sqrt N)\), \(e^{-t_2}(\sqrt N\,w+L\sqrt{\log N}\,t_1^{\beta_1})\to0\) and \(w\log N\to0\), every matching meeting the two allowances has at least \(\varepsilon_N\sqrt N/(8(D_1+w))\) pairs inside both boxes crossing any family of vertical lines with gaps at most \(w\), the family chosen after the samples; at the both-high instance, columns of width \(o(e^{\sqrt{\log N}}/\sqrt N)\) must be crossed by pairs inside both boxes. Both rest on lem:column-crossing-count, a deterministic inequality for every matching: \((D+w)|A|+(1+w)|B|\ge\frac12\int|U|-\Omega_w\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:ultimate-matching changed. Bearing. On the curve's parameters, at \((4,4)\) with \(t_1=\log N\) and \(t_2=\sqrt{\log N}\): a matching meeting the conjecture's two levels there must move horizontally, through pairs inside both boxes, across every family of vertical lines with gaps \(o(e^{\sqrt{\log N}}/\sqrt N)\), at least \(\varepsilon_N\sqrt N/(8(D_1+w))\) such pairs for each family; a scheme counting every pair that crosses its column lines as an exception, as the windowed construction does, cannot meet the instance with columns that fine, and the theorem is silent for the per-level cells, of width about \(e^{t_2}\log N/\sqrt N\). Not covered. Families coarser than \(e^{t_2}/\sqrt N\), horizontal lines, curved boundaries, and constructions whose both-box pairs cross the lines; the theorem refutes nothing of the conjecture.
