Adapted partitions fail above exponent two

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; local rules of fixed rank spread · Two-choice routing. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. The eighth review's Decision: does the equal-count partition, in which each cell is cut where its two halves hold equal counts, so that the forced means of thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction vanish, give a matching that escapes the square-mean obstruction above exponent \(2\)? That theorem does not apply to it: its cuts depend on the points' positions, not on dyadic counts.

Target form. The goal's own form, a matching: the cost \(\sum_i\psi_\alpha(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|/s)\) of every matching that follows the partition's transport map up to a small error, for any \(Y\); not a flow's per-point values.

Architecture test. Not decided. The eighth review's Decisive test is the seventh review's retained one, the gap-charged bound for nested chains of many layers on the dual side, with outcomes (A) the bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\); none of them occurred here, as this entry works on the primal side, on the lemma the review's Decision asked for first.

Owed attempt. The last entry on this item named "the adapted partition, where each cell is cut where its two halves hold equal counts, so that the forced means vanish at every level": made here, with the outcome that the partition fails at every pair of the curve (theorem below).

Earlier entries on the item. Read this cycle, each from its Follow-up: straight-cut forced flux ("First, what a two-choice routing cannot change: (a)–(c) answer it"); sequential rules ("what a routing cannot change, answered by the straight-cut forced flux entry"); simultaneous rule tails ("the rule itself lowers the pooled kurtosis by about \(0.4\) at the sizes run"); simultaneous rule exceedances ("lighter than Gaussian by a factor of \(3\) to \(4\) at \(J=6,7\)"); exceedance slopes ("its drift with \(J\) out of reach of tail counts at \(512\) seeds"); square means ("what a routing cannot change (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux); sequential rules, the dyadic"), whose next attempt this entry makes. None treats a partition cut at order statistics.

Setting

\(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\). An adapted partition of depth \(2J\) with rank spread \(A>0\): the root cell is \([0,1]^2\); at step \(j=0,1,\dots,2J-1\) every cell \(C\) of step \(j\) is cut in coordinate \(k_j\), \(k_j=1\) for even \(j\) and \(k_j=2\) for odd \(j\), along the line through its pivot, the point of rank \(r_C\) in coordinate \(k_j\) among the cell's \(n_C\) interior points, where \(r_C\) is any function of the cuts of the earlier steps with \(|r_C-n_C/2|\le A\sqrt{n_C}\). The pivot lies on the cut and is interior to neither child, which have \(r_C-1\) and \(n_C-r_C\) interior points. The equal-count partition is the case \(r_C=\lceil n_C/2\rceil\), within \(A\sqrt{n_C}\) for every \(A\ge1/(2\sqrt{n_C})\), so for every fixed \(A>0\) once \(N\) is large; a rule choosing \(r_C\) against the running displacement with offsets up to \(A\sqrt{n_C}\) is another. Each step-\(j\) cell \(C\), a rectangle, has a target \(Q_C\), the dyadic rectangle with the same address (the parent's target cut at its middle in coordinate \(k_j\)), and on each step-\(j\) cell the map \(T_j\) sends \(C\) onto \(Q_C\) coordinatewise affinely and increasingly; \(T=T_{2J}\) is the partition's transport. \(R_j(x)=T^k_j(x)-x_k\) is the running displacement in coordinate \(k\). \(J\) satisfies \(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\); \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\); \(\psi_\alpha(t)=e^{t^\alpha}-1\) for \(\alpha<\infty\); \((L,\infty)\)-good in coordinate \(k\) means \(\max_i|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|\le s\). Constants: \(x_A=4(A+\frac12)/\sqrt3\), \(m_A=\lceil128x_A^2\rceil\), \(p_A=64^{-m_A}\), \(\lambda_A=\log_2(4/p_A)=2+6m_A\).

Theorem (adapted partition obstruction)

Statement. Let \(k\in\{1,2\}\), \(A>0\), \(L,\kappa,K,M>0\), \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\), \(0<\theta<1/(2+2\lambda_A)\) and \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\). Fix, for each \(N\), an adapted partition rule of rank spread \(A\) and depth \(2J\) that is local at step \(j_0=2J-2m\): each rank \(r_C\) of a cell of step at least \(j_0\) is a function of the cuts of steps before \(j_0\) and of the cuts inside the step-\(j_0\) ancestor of \(C\). With probability tending to one, every permutation \(\pi\) and all \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\in[0,1]^2\) with \(|Y^k_{\pi(i)}-T^k(X_i)|\le m/(18\sqrt N)\) for every \(X_i\) interior to its final cell have, for \(\alpha<\infty\), \(\sum_i\psi_\alpha(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|/s)\ge MN\), and for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(\max_i|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|>s\). The equal-count partition is such a rule, and so is a rule choosing \(r_C\) from the running displacement \(U(C)\) of the cell, which depends only on the cell's sides and target, provided \(|r_C-n_C/2|\le A\sqrt{n_C}\). A matching sending each interior point to a \(Y\) in its target \(Q_C\) or a neighbouring dyadic rectangle meets the hypothesis for large \(N\) (error at most \(2\cdot2^{-J}\le2\sqrt{K\log N/N}\), below \(m/(18\sqrt N)\)); so at every pair of the curve, where some \(\alpha_k\ge4\), such a matching meets the conjecture's conclusion for no \(L\), with probability tending to one.

Proof

Conditional uniformity. Let \(\mathcal G_j\) be generated by the cuts of steps before \(j\) (each pivot's coordinate along its cut direction). Given \(\mathcal G_j\), the interior point sets of the step-\(j\) cells are independent, each \(n_C\) i.i.d. uniform points of \(C\) (unordered). By induction on \(j\): at \(j=0\) it is the hypothesis. Given \(\mathcal G_j\), \(r_C\) is fixed, a cell's interior points are i.i.d. uniform, and conditionally also on the \(r_C\)-th order statistic \(c\) of their \(k_j\)-coordinates, the \(r_C-1\) points below are i.i.d. uniform on \(C\cap\{x_{k_j}<c\}\) and the \(n_C-r_C\) above i.i.d. uniform on \(C\cap\{x_{k_j}>c\}\), independent of each other and of the pivot's other coordinate (the joint density of a uniform sample factors given an order statistic); distinct cells stay independent.

Counts. The children of a cell with \(n\) interior points have between \(n/2-A\sqrt n-1\) and \(n/2+A\sqrt n\), that is \(\frac n2(1\pm\beta(n))\) with \(\beta(n)=2A/\sqrt n+2/n\). By induction every step-\(j\) cell has \(n_C\in[N2^{-j}e^{-2\gamma_N},N2^{-j}e^{2\gamma_N}]\) with \(\gamma_N=\sum_{i<2J}\beta(N2^{-i}/2)\le\frac{2\sqrt2A}{\sqrt{N4^{-J}}}\sum_{l\ge0}2^{-l/2}+\frac{4}{N4^{-J}}\sum_{l\ge0}2^{-l}\le\frac{9.7A}{\sqrt{\kappa\log N}}+\frac8{\kappa\log N}\to0\) (each factor \(1-\beta\ge e^{-2\beta}\) for \(\beta\le\frac12\), and the cells' counts stay above \(N2^{-i}/2\) along the way). So every cell has \(n_C\ge\kappa\log N/2\), which exceeds \(32m_A/3\) for large \(N\).

The walk of cell means. For a step-\(j\) cell \(C\) with \(k\)-side \([a,a+\ell]\) and target \(k\)-side \([a',a'+\ell']\), \(R_j\) on \(C\) is affine in \(x_k\) and its mean over \(C\) (Lebesgue measure) is \(U(C)=(a'+\ell'/2)-(a+\ell/2)\), the difference of the centres, \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable. At a step cutting coordinate \(k_j\ne k\) the children keep the \(k\)-sides and targets of \(C\), so \(U\) is unchanged. At a step cutting coordinate \(k\) at \(a+(\frac12+\eta)\ell\), the lower child \(C_-\) has \(k\)-side \([a,a+(\frac12+\eta)\ell]\) and target \([a',a'+\ell'/2]\), the upper \(C_+\) has \([a+(\frac12+\eta)\ell,a+\ell]\) and \([a'+\ell'/2,a'+\ell']\); from the centres, \(U(C_-)-U(C)=-\ell'/4+\ell/4-\eta\ell/2\) and \(U(C_+)-U(C)=\ell'/4-\ell/4-\eta\ell/2\), that is \[U(C_\pm)=U(C)+\xi_C+\delta_\pm,\qquad\xi_C=-\frac{\eta\ell'}2,\quad\delta_-=\frac{(\ell-\ell')(1-2\eta)}4,\quad\delta_+=-\frac{(\ell-\ell')(1+2\eta)}4,\] \(\xi_C\) being the mean of the step's increment over \(C\). With \(\sigma_C=\operatorname{sign}U(C)\) (\(+1\) at \(0\)), let \(C_*=C_-\) if \(\sigma_C(\ell-\ell')\ge0\) and \(C_*=C_+\) otherwise, a \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable choice with \(\sigma_C\delta_{C_*}\ge0\) since \(|\eta|<\frac12\). Then \(|U(C_*)|\ge\sigma_C(U(C)+\xi_C+\delta_{C_*})\ge|U(C)|+\sigma_C\xi_C\).

The push. Given \(\mathcal G_j\), let \(C\) be cut in coordinate \(k\), with \(n=n_C\), \(r=r_C\) and \(\varepsilon=1/(4\sqrt n)\). The cut lies at or above \(a+(\frac12+\varepsilon)\ell\) exactly when at most \(r-1\) interior points lie below that line, that is when \(S=\sum_z\big(q-1\{z\text{ below}\}\big)\ge nq-r+1\), \(q=\frac12+\varepsilon\), and \(nq-r+1\le n\varepsilon+A\sqrt n+1\le(A+\frac12)\sqrt n\) for \(n\ge16\). The terms are i.i.d., mean \(0\), variance \(q(1-q)\ge3/16\), size at most \(1\); with \(s_n=\sqrt{nq(1-q)}\ge\sqrt{3n}/4\) the needed deviation is at most \(x_As_n\). lem:block-lower-tail at \(x=x_A\ge1\) needs \(m_A\le n\) and \(1\le s_n^2/(2m_A)\), both true for \(n\ge32m_A/3\), and gives \(P(\eta\ge\varepsilon\mid\mathcal G_j)\ge p_A\). The cut lies at or below \(a+(\frac12-\varepsilon)\ell\) when at least \(r\) points lie below that line, a deviation of at most \(n\varepsilon+A\sqrt n\le x_As_n\) of the terms \(1\{z\text{ below}\}-(\frac12-\varepsilon)\), so \(P(\eta\le-\varepsilon\mid\mathcal G_j)\ge p_A\). As \(\sigma_C\) is \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable, \(P(\sigma_C\xi_C\ge\ell'/(8\sqrt n)\mid\mathcal G_j)\ge p_A\). Cutting coordinate \(1\), \(j=2i\) and \(\ell'=2^{-i}\); cutting coordinate \(2\), \(j=2i+1\) and \(\ell'=2^{-i}\); in both \(\ell'\ge\sqrt{2^{-j}}\), and with \(n\le N2^{-j}e^{2\gamma_N}\), \(\ell'/(8\sqrt n)\ge e^{-\gamma_N}/(8\sqrt N)\ge h:=1/(9\sqrt N)\) for large \(N\).

A chain of cells. Let \(j_0=2J-2m\); the fine steps \(j_0\le j<2J\) include \(m\) cutting coordinate \(k\). Let \(\mathcal A_{j_0}\) be all step-\(j_0\) cells, and \(\mathcal A_{j+1}=\{C_-:C\in\mathcal A_j\}\) at a step not cutting \(k\) (either child keeps \(U\); \(C_*\) is defined at \(k\)-steps only), \(\{C_*:C\in\mathcal A_j,\ \sigma_C\xi_C\ge h\}\) at a step cutting \(k\). By the walk, \(|U(C)|\ge|U(\text{its step-}j_0\text{ ancestor})|+mh\ge mh\) for \(C\in\mathcal A_{2J}\). With \(V_j=\sum_{C\in\mathcal A_j}n_C/N\) and \(n_{C_*}\ge\frac{n_C}2(1-\beta(n_C))\), and as membership in \(\mathcal A_j\) and the choice of \(C_*\) are \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable, \(\mathbb E[V_{j+1}\mid\mathcal G_j]\ge\frac{p_A}2(1-\bar\beta_j)V_j\) at a \(k\)-step and \(V_{j+1}\ge\frac12(1-\bar\beta_j)V_j\) at the others, \(\bar\beta_j=\beta(N2^{-j}e^{-2\gamma_N})\). Since \(\prod_j(1-\bar\beta_j)\ge e^{-4\gamma_N}\to1\) (the same geometric sum) and \(V_{j_0}=1-\#\{\text{pivots of steps before }j_0\}/N\ge1-2^{j_0}/N\ge1-1/(\kappa\log N)\), \(\mathbb E[V_{2J}\mid\mathcal G_{j_0}]\ge\mu/2\) for large \(N\), with \(\mu=(p_A/4)^m\ge N^{-\theta\lambda_A}\).

Many cells. \(V_{2J}=\sum_TV(T)\) over the step-\(j_0\) cells \(T\), \(V(T)\in[0,n_T/N]\) the chain's share inside \(T\), a function of \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\) and the interior points of \(T\): inside \(T\) the chain uses the cuts, sides and targets of cells inside \(T\) and \(U(T)\), which is \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\)-measurable, and every cut inside \(T\) is a function of \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\) and the points of \(T\), its rank being so by the locality of the rule and the targets being fixed by the cells' addresses. Given \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\) the \(V(T)\) are independent, so \(\operatorname{Var}(V_{2J}\mid\mathcal G_{j_0})\le\sum_T(n_T/N)^2/4\le\max_Tn_T/(4N)\le e^{2\gamma_N}4^mK\log N/(4N)\le N^{2\theta}K\log N/(2N)\) for large \(N\). By Chebyshev, \(P(V_{2J}<\mu/4\mid\mathcal G_{j_0})\le16\operatorname{Var}/\mu^2\le8K\log N\,N^{(2+2\lambda_A)\theta-1}\to0\).

From cells to points. Given \(\mathcal G_{2J}\), the interior points of the final cells are independent and uniform in their cells, and on a final cell \(C\) the displacement \(R\) is affine in \(x_k\) with mean \(U(C)\), so \(R(X)\) is symmetric about \(U(C)\) and \(P(\sigma_CR(X)\ge\sigma_CU(C))\ge\frac12\) for each interior point. The number \(Z\) of interior points of cells of \(\mathcal A_{2J}\) with \(|R(X_i)|\ge mh\) dominates a binomial with \(NV_{2J}\ge N\mu/4\) trials and success \(\frac12\), of mean at least \(N\mu/8\); by Chernoff, \(P(Z<N\mu/16)\le e^{-N\mu/64}\to0\), as \(N\mu\ge N^{1-\theta\lambda_A}\to\infty\).

Cost. For each of these points, \(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|\ge|R(X_i)|-|T^k(X_i)-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|\ge mh-m/(18\sqrt N)=m/(18\sqrt N)\), an argument \(u_N=m/(18\sqrt Ns)\ge\frac{\theta\log_2N-1}{18L\sqrt{\ln N}}=\frac{\theta\sqrt{\ln N}}{18L\ln2}-o(1)\) (\(\log=\ln\) in \(s\)). For \(\alpha<\infty\) the cost is at least \(\frac{N\mu}{16}(e^{u_N^\alpha}-1)\ge\frac{N^{1-\theta\lambda_A}}{16}(e^{u_N^\alpha}-1)\ge MN\) once \(u_N^\alpha>\theta\lambda_A\ln N+\ln(16M)+1\), true for large \(N\) since \(u_N^\alpha\) grows as \((\ln N)^{\alpha/2}\) and \(\alpha>2\). For \(\alpha=\infty\), \(u_N>1\) for large \(N\) and \(Z\ge1\). The events concern \(X\) and the fixed rule alone, so the conclusion holds simultaneously for every \(\pi\) and \(Y\) meeting the hypothesis. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(X\) i.i.d. uniform: conditional uniformity, hence the push and the transfer to points. Ranks functions of the earlier cuts: conditional uniformity (a rank reading the current cell's points would break it). Ranks within \(A\sqrt{n_C}\) of \(n_C/2\): the push (a deviation of at most \(x_As_n\)) and the counts (\(\gamma_N\to0\)); the weakest form the push needs is \(|r_C-n_C/2|\le A\sqrt{n_C}\) at the fine \(k\)-steps only, the counts needing \(\sum_i|r-n/2|/n\) over a cell's ancestors to tend to \(0\). Locality at step \(j_0\): the independence of the \(V(T)\) in Chebyshev. Alternating coordinates and dyadic targets: the push's size, which needs \(\ell'\ge c\sqrt{2^{-j}}\) at each fine \(k\)-step, and \(m\) fine \(k\)-steps; the weakest form is a schedule with at least \(c'\theta\log_2N\) fine \(k\)-steps where the target's \(k\)-side is at least \(c\) times the square root of its area, with the constants then entering \(h\) and \(\theta\). \(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\): \(\kappa\) for \(n_C\ge32m_A/3\) and \(\gamma_N\to0\), \(K\) for the variance. \(\theta<1/(2+2\lambda_A)\): Chebyshev; \(N\mu\to\infty\) follows. The error bound \(m/(18\sqrt N)\) on \(\pi\): the cost step, where an error of at most \(c\,m/\sqrt N\) with any \(c<1/9\) would do, giving the argument \((1/9-c)m/(\sqrt Ns)\). \(\alpha>2\): the cost step (\(u_N^\alpha\) against \(\theta\lambda_A\ln N\)). The conclusion holds for every \(\pi\) and every \(Y\) meeting the error bound, \(Y\) being any points, not necessarily a sample.

Degenerate cases. A cell already equal to its target in coordinate \(k\) (\(\ell=\ell'\)): \(\delta_\pm=0\), either child keeps the inequality. \(U(C)=0\): \(\sigma_C=+1\), and the walk grows from \(0\). \(\eta\) exactly \(0\): probability \(0\) for every \(n\), the pivot's coordinate having a continuous law; the proof uses only \(P(\pm\eta\ge\varepsilon)\ge p_A\). \(A=0\): only ranks \(r_C=n_C/2\), whose children have \(n_C/2-1\) and \(n_C/2\) points, one of them odd, so no rule of spread \(0\) exists at depth \(2\) or more and the case is vacuous; the equal-count rule \(\lceil n_C/2\rceil\) needs \(A\ge1/(2\sqrt{n_C})\), and any fixed \(A>0\) covers it for large \(N\). \(\alpha=\infty\): one point beyond \(s\) suffices, given. Small \(N\): \(m=0\) for \(\log_2N<1/\theta\), and the statement says nothing at any fixed \(N\); it is asymptotic. A matching that ignores the transport (\(Y\) far from \(T(X)\)) is outside the hypothesis.

Nonvacuity. On the curve parameters: \(N=2^{20000}\), \(\ln N=13863\); \(\kappa=1\), \(K=4\), \(J=9993\), so \(N4^{-J}=2^{14}=16384\in[13863,55452]\); the equal-count rule \(r_C=\lceil n_C/2\rceil\) with \(A=1\) (\(|r_C-n_C/2|\le\frac12\le\sqrt{n_C}\)), local, with \(x_1^2=12\), \(m_1=1536\), \(\lambda_1=9218\) and \(\theta=5\cdot10^{-5}<1/18438\); \(m=\lfloor\theta\cdot20000\rfloor=1\); \(Y_i=T(X_i)\) for the interior points and \(Y_i=X_i\) for the pivots, \(\pi\) the identity, error \(0\). The cuts are order statistics of the points' positions, the feature thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction does not cover; the statement applies to this sequence of \(N\) as \(N\to\infty\) along \(2^{20000l}\), and the conclusion is asymptotic, not a claim at this \(N\). Plainest bound. On this witness, the second moment of a point's displacement, of order \(J/N\), that is \(s^2\) up to constants, bounds the fraction beyond \(us\) by \(O(1/u^2)\), consistent with a cost of order \(N\) at exponent \(2\) and deciding nothing above it; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction does not apply, the cuts being order statistics.

Plainest bound. On the instance, the second moment of one point's displacement: given the coarser cuts, each \(k\)-step adds an increment of conditional mean about \(0\) and size about \(\ell'/(2\sqrt n)\le1/\sqrt N\), so \(\mathbb ER(x)^2\) is of order \(J/N\), that is \(s^2\) up to \(L\)- and \(\kappa\)-dependent constants; Chebyshev then bounds the fraction beyond \(us\) by \(O(1/u^2)\), which is consistent with a cost of order \(N\) at exponent \(2\) and gives nothing above it, a second moment being unable to show an exponential moment of order \(\alpha>2\) infinite. The oldest recorded lemmas on such costs, thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, need steps measurable in dyadic counts, which order-statistic cuts are not; thm:position-blind-cell-exits needs exits chosen by labels blind to position, the opposite of this rule.

Baseline. The construction needing no idea is the dyadic flow, excluded above exponent \(2\) by thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction; the statement adds every adapted partition whose ranks stay within \(A\sqrt n\) of the median, chosen by any local rule, including rules steering against the running displacement by up to \(A\sqrt n\) points per cut, and it concludes on the matching's own cost at the sample points, not on a flow.

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction (its walk of square means, chain of squares, Chebyshev over the level-\(j_1\) squares and the push from lem:block-lower-tail) is the template; the chain, Chebyshev and push steps here are those steps on other cells, a citation of its proof, not new. lem:conditional-push-obstruction is pointwise, for fields measurable in counts at Lebesgue points, and is not used; it is neither a more general version of the theorem (order-statistic cuts are not measurable in counts, and it concludes on a flow's integral, not on sample points) nor a special case of it. The nearest registered statements by the resemblance tool, thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold, thm:low-level-mixed-counts and lem:discrete-flow-bound, concern other objects (the first two the existence of other matchings, by maxima or by mixed level counts, the first also excluding pairs below the curve; the third a discrepancy bound for grid functions), consistent with this exclusion and neither more general nor special cases of it. thm:position-blind-cell-exits excludes exits chosen by labels; this rule chooses by position. The record holds no statement on equal-count or order-statistic partitions (searched: "equal count partition median cut order statistics transport map displacement cell centre walk matching fails above exponent 2", which returned thm:per-level-count-matchings, lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, thm:below-curve-matching-exclusion and a claim of another thread). New here: the exact walk of cell means as differences of centres, with a common push \(-\eta\ell'/2\) and a deviation whose sign is known before the cut, so that the chain's choice is predictable; counts that are functions of the earlier cuts, which removes the exceptional events of the dyadic proof; weights by counts in place of areas; and the transfer from cell means to the sample points by the symmetry of an affine image of a uniform point.

General statement. thm:adapted-partition-obstruction, for every \(L,\kappa,K,M\), every \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\) and both coordinates.

New mathematics. thm:adapted-partition-obstruction: for every local adapted partition rule whose ranks stay within \(A\sqrt n\) of the median (the equal-count partition and steering rules of that size among them), with alternating cuts and dyadic targets at the depth of the flow bound, every matching that follows the partition's transport up to \(m/(18\sqrt N)\) in coordinate \(k\) has, with probability tending to one, cost at least \(MN\) for every \(L\) and \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\) in that coordinate; for \(\alpha=\infty\), a displacement beyond \(s\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: the theorem excludes a class of constructions and proves no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy or conj:ultimate-matching. Bearing. At every pair of the curve, where some \(\alpha_k\ge4\), and every \(L\): no matching that follows, up to \(m/(18\sqrt N)\) in coordinate \(k\), the transport of a local adapted partition of fixed rank spread \(A\) with alternating cuts and dyadic targets meets the conjecture's conclusion, with probability tending to one. Not covered. Ranks farther than \(A\sqrt n\) from the median for every fixed \(A\), in particular steering with offsets \(A_N\sqrt n\), \(A_N\to\infty\); rules reading points outside the cell's step-\(j_0\) ancestor; schedules without enough fine \(k\)-steps with targets of bounded aspect; partitions applied to both samples, whose two displacements may cancel; matchings farther from the transport than \(m/(18\sqrt N)\); and every flow or matching not built from a hierarchical partition, where the eighth review's boundary-flux escape lives.

Follow-up. Continuing. The item's readings: what a routing cannot change (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux); sequential and simultaneous rules on dyadic squares (thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction); the adapted partition, here, closed at every fixed rank spread, steering rules of that size included. Next attempt: proportional steering, the cut's rank \(r_C=n_C/2+\sigma_C\Delta_C\) with \(\Delta_C=\min(\kappa'|U(C)|\sqrt{Nn_C},\,n_C/2-2)\), against the running displacement and in proportion to it, capped so that neither child is empty. The theorem's proof does not reach it (by hand, checked by the reviewer up to constants): along its chain \(|U|\ge t/(9\sqrt N)\) after \(t\) pushes, so the offset is at least \(\kappa't\sqrt n/9\) until the cap binds, and a push along \(\sigma\) needs the count below the cut to deviate by about \(2\kappa't/9\) of its standard deviation \(\sqrt n/2\), of probability at most \(e^{-c\kappa'^2t^2}\) by Hoeffding's inequality; over \(t\le m\) the chain's probability is at most \(e^{-c'\kappa'^2m^3}\), far below the polynomial budget \(N^{-\theta\lambda}\) of the Chebyshev step. That shows only that this proof fails for the rule, not that the rule succeeds. The cap binds once \(t\gtrsim4.5\sqrt n/\kappa'\), about \(\sqrt{\log N}\) steps at the finest cells, and a capped cut leaves one child with two points. Smallest case. One cut, by hand: the cut at rank \(n/2+\sigma\Delta\) lies at about \((\frac12+\sigma\Delta/n)\ell\) plus a fluctuation of \(\ell Z/(2\sqrt n)\), so \(\xi=-\eta\ell'/2\approx-\sigma\Delta\ell'/(2n)-\ell'Z/(4\sqrt n)\), and with \(\Delta=\kappa'|U|\sqrt{Nn}\) and \(\ell'/\sqrt n\ge1/\sqrt N\) the mean step is about \(-\kappa'U/2\) (at least that in coordinate \(1\), \(\sqrt2\) times it in coordinate \(2\)): for \(\kappa'<\sqrt2\), so that the coordinate-\(2\) step does not overshoot and flip the sign of \(U\), the walk contracts by about \(1-\kappa'/2\) per \(k\)-step, an autoregressive walk with noise of order \(1/\sqrt N\). The children then hold \(n/2\pm\Delta\) points against target halves of equal area, a relative surplus \(2\kappa'|U|\sqrt N/\sqrt n\). Two cuts in one coordinate carry it: each child's own cut is again steered by its \(U\), and its surplus, against a target of fixed area, passes to its final cells, where the relative deviations add as \(\sum_i2\kappa'|U_i|\sqrt N/\sqrt{n_i}\), dominated by the finest steps. With \(|U|\sqrt N\) of order \(1/\sqrt{\kappa'}\) where the walk is near its stationary size (checked below for the linearized, uncapped step), that is of order \(\sqrt{\kappa'/n}\), so about \(\sqrt{\kappa'n}\) points per final cell, the order of the counts' own fluctuation; so the question becomes whether a matching following \(T\) absorbs those surpluses within its slack \(m/(18\sqrt N)\), about \(m/(18\sqrt{\kappa\log N})\) final cells, and what the rare cells with \(|U|\sqrt N\) near \(\sqrt{\log N}\), where the cap binds, cost. Plainest bound. On this instance, the second moment without steering: the free walk's \(\mathbb EU^2\) grows by about \(1/(16N)\) per \(k\)-step, \(t/(16N)\) after \(t\) steps, which shows nothing about the steered walk; and the bare cap bounds one cut's surplus by \(n/2-2\) points, far above the \(\sqrt{\kappa'n}\) the computation gives, so neither decides whether the surpluses are absorbed. Tried. The free walk's second moment and the cap, above; the theorem's push step alone (lem:block-lower-tail at the cut), which gives a push along \(\sigma\) of probability \(64^{-m_A}\) with \(A=\kappa'|U|\sqrt N\), positive at each cut but vanishing as \(e^{-c\kappa'^2t^2}\) along the chain by Hoeffding, so it decides no single cell's fate; the counts' induction alone, whose \(\gamma_N\) bound needs offsets at most \(A\sqrt n\) with \(A\) fixed and gives, with \(A=\kappa'|U|\sqrt N\) of order \(1/\sqrt{\kappa'}\) typically, a relative deviation of order \(\sqrt{\kappa'/n}\) at the finest cells, the figure above, but no bound in the rare cells where the cap binds. Nontrivial because: the rule reads each cell's running displacement \(U(C)\) and moves the cut's rank by it, a choice the equal-count rule never makes, so one cut already shows the contraction and the count surplus that the equal-count rule lacks. The earlier sketch for uniform caps stays a sketch: with \(\theta\) of order \(1/A^2\) the argument \(u_N\) is of order \(\sqrt{\ln N}/(LA^2)\), and the cost step needs \(u_N^\alpha\gg\ln N\), so the same steps would reach \(A_N=o((\log N)^{(\alpha-2)/(4\alpha)})\), \((\log N)^{1/8}\) at \(\alpha=4\) (not checked; where this proof stops, not a threshold of the question). Own statements. thm:adapted-partition-obstruction decides every fixed \(A\), and its proof, run with \(\theta_N\), reaches \(A_N=o((\log N)^{1/8})\) at \(\alpha=4\) (a sketch, unchecked; \((\log N)^{1/8}\) is where this proof stops, not a threshold of the question); it does not decide proportional steering, whose offsets exceed every fixed multiple of \(\sqrt n\) exactly on the chain, where the push probability \(e^{-c\kappa'^2t^2}\) at step \(t\) falls below the polynomial budget of the Chebyshev step. thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction and lem:conditional-push-obstruction need steps measurable in dyadic counts and decide nothing there; thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold, thm:low-level-mixed-counts and lem:discrete-flow-bound concern other matchings and a grid discrepancy and decide nothing about steering either. ex:exceedance-curve-slopes and ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances measure the simultaneous rule's per-point tails on dyadic squares at \(J\le7\); no steered or adapted partition is among the flows they run, so they decide nothing about proportional steering; their figures bear on it only as the kind of measurement whose reachable sizes, \(J\le7\), the record found unable to decide tails at the scale where the cost is decided. Record search. "equal count partition median cut order statistics transport map displacement cell centre walk matching fails above exponent 2" (above); none of the matches bears on steering ranks.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • Steering with a constant offset \(A\) makes \(U\) a reflected walk with drift-to-noise ratio about \(2A\), equilibrating in \(O(1/A^2)\) steps with tail about \(e^{-cAx}\) at \(x/\sqrt N\); the largest displacement among \(N\) points is then about \(\sqrt{\ln N}/(cAL)\) in units of \(s\), so the cost stays of order \(N\) only for \(A\gtrsim(\ln N)^{(\alpha-2)/(2\alpha)}/L\), \((\log N)^{1/4}\) at \(\alpha=4\): steering with uniform caps should still fail up to \((\log N)^{1/4}\), and a proof would replace the per-step push by a large deviation of the reflected walk. Record. "reflected walk drift stationary tail steering cut rank count imbalance final cell" returned claims of other threads only.
  • The counts may be the real constraint: offsets \(A\sqrt n\) leave final-cell counts off by about \(A\sqrt{\log N}\) from \(N4^{-J}\), to be absorbed within the hypothesis's slack before steering is called open on that side. Record. The same search; nothing on count imbalances of adapted cells.
  • With a pull proportional to \(U\) the walk is an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with a Gaussian stationary law of variance of order \(1/(\kappa'N)\), well below the free walk's \(\log N/N\), typical offsets \(O(\sqrt n)\), and only rare cells steering harder, so the open question is what those rare cells cost (second pass). Record. "Ornstein Uhlenbeck autoregressive contraction running displacement stationary Gaussian partition cells" returned claims of other threads only; the entry's Smallest case derives the contraction \(1-\kappa'/2\) by hand.

Suggestion checked. The reviewer's autoregressive suggestion, which the next attempt uses for the walk's stationary size, checked here for the linearized, uncapped step \(U'=(1-a)U+\zeta\), \(a=\kappa'/2\): given the earlier cuts, \(\zeta\) is the cut's binomial fluctuation, a martingale difference of conditional variance about \(v=\ell'^2/(16n)\approx1/(16N)\), so the cross term vanishes and \(\mathbb EU'^2=(1-a)^2\mathbb EU^2+v\), with fixed point \(v/(2a-a^2)=1/(16\kappa'N(1-\kappa'/4))\approx1/(16\kappa'N)\) for small \(\kappa'\) (\(2a=\kappa'\)): \(|U|\sqrt N\) of order \(1/\sqrt{\kappa'}\), as used (coordinate \(1\); in coordinate \(2\), \(a=\kappa'/\sqrt2\) and \(v\approx1/(8N)\), the same order); the walk takes about \(J\gg1/a\) \(k\)-steps, so it reaches this size. Not checked: the deviation terms \(\delta_\pm\) of the walk, the cap's effect, and the Gaussian shape of the stationary law; the next entry must treat them.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read this cycle: lem:block-lower-tail's registered statement, and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's statement and proof in its record (the walk, chain, Chebyshev and push steps adapted here); the item's six earlier entries. One medium reviewer, given the draft, its commit message and those excerpts (record: research/results/ultimate_matching_adapted_partition_20261017/review.txt). Its verdict: pass with corrections; it checked every step of the proof (conditional uniformity, the walk's formulas and the predictable child choice, the push's deviation bound and lem:block-lower-tail's conditions in both signs, \(h\), the counts' induction and \(\gamma_N\), the count-weighted recursion, locality and Chebyshev, the transfer to points, the cost step at \(\alpha=\infty\)) and found no gap, and no unused hypothesis. Its corrections, all made: the Nonvacuity's \(\lambda_1\) was \(9224\) by a floating-point ceiling, exactly \(9218\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_adapted_partition_20261017/ceil-check.txt), with \(\theta<1/18438\); two Degenerate cases sentences were wrong (\(P(\eta=0)=0\) for every \(n\); spread \(A=0\) is vacuous at depth two or more, so the statement's class moved from \(A\ge0\) to \(A>0\), no smaller, the case having no member); the Setting and Degenerate cases disagreed on the equal-count rule's spread (\(1/(2\sqrt{n_C})\)); the Statement's sentence on rules reading \(U(C)\) lacked the spread condition; the error-bound sentence was garbled; the Follow-up's growing-cap sketch is where this proof stops, not a threshold of the question; and the claim spec's rationale and next action stated more than the Not covered list, rewritten. Its follow-up read those corrections and the proportional-steering paragraph written after its review: pass with corrections, asking for the cap (uncapped, the offset exceeds \(n/2\) after about \(\sqrt{\log N}\) steps), a Smallest case for the proportional rule (the old one worked a uniform cap), and Hoeffding named for the upper tail; all made, the Smallest case rewritten with the one-cut contraction \(1-\kappa'/2\) and the carried surplus, which its last pass checked as order-of-magnitude heuristics (the mean step \(-\kappa'U/2\), \(\sqrt2\) times it in coordinate \(2\), so that \(\kappa'<\sqrt2\) avoids overshoot, now stated; the relative surplus and its sum dominated by the finest steps; about \(\sqrt{\kappa'n}\) points per final cell), the stationary size \(1/\sqrt{\kappa'}\) resting on its own unverified autoregressive heuristic, now labelled; verdict pass, with no remaining required change. A fourth pass read the Suggestion checked paragraph and the Smallest case's Plainest bound and Tried clauses, written after the third: pass, the fixed point \(1/(16\kappa'N(1-\kappa'/4))\) right and the unchecked parts listed honestly, with the advice, adopted, that the constants are coordinate \(1\)'s and coordinate \(2\)'s are of the same order. Process audit. The reviewer proposed the title "Adapted partitions fail above exponent two", adopted, and found pre-review metadata in the claim spec, a constant computed in floating point and unchecked, and two degenerate sentences written without being worked; strength count \(3\), then \(0\) after the corrections.

Process assessment. Three mistakes found by the reviewer, and three found before it read them or at registration, listed after them. The reviewer's: the Nonvacuity's constant \(\lambda_1\) was computed through a floating-point ceiling and was wrong by six (\(9224\) for \(9218\)); two Degenerate cases sentences (\(\eta=0\), \(A=0\)) were written without being worked through, one of them describing a vacuous case as a covered one; and the claim spec's rationale and next action, written before the review, stated more than the entry's Not covered list allowed. The first draft's statement also lacked the locality its proof's Chebyshev step needs, found while writing that step and added before the review; and the Suggestion checked paragraph first gave the stationary variance as \(1/(8\kappa'N)\), a factor \(2\) off (\(2a=\kappa'\)), found while writing its brief and corrected before the reviewer read it; and the class correction from \(A\ge0\) to \(A>0\) reached the gate and the spec but not the Setting and Statement, caught by the registration's comparison of the spec's summary with the entry's Statement. Prevention. For the ceiling: COMPUTATION_RULES.md's exact-arithmetic rule now covers a floor, ceiling or comparison of a constant that may be an integer or a boundary, with this case (research/results/ultimate_matching_adapted_partition_20261017/ceil-check.txt: the float ceiling \(1537\), the exact \(1536\)); no mechanical check can tell such a constant from others. For the degenerate sentences: AGENTS.md already asks each degenerate input worked through, and this is the rule's first miss here, so no check is added. For the spec: its rationale and next action are rewritten from the entry's Not covered list and Follow-up, and the status it records is registered only after this gate.

Meta. The six share one habit: writing a closing paragraph (a witness's constant, a degenerate case, a metadata note) from the shape of the result rather than by doing the small computation it reports, because the main proof had absorbed the attention. The change is in the Spin's self-review step, PROMPTS.md: the closing paragraphs are worked before the brief as computations of their own, each number in exact arithmetic beside its formula and each degenerate case run through the proof's steps; AGENTS.md's summary rule now also names the claim spec's notes.

Split-matched hierarchical transports also fail

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; target splits fixed before each cut · Two-choice routing. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. The adapted partition obstruction left steering open: cut ranks moved against the running displacement by more than a fixed multiple of \(\sqrt n\). Can steering, or any other choice of cut ranks and target splits in a hierarchical transport, escape the walk of cell means above exponent \(2\)?

Target form. The goal's own form, a matching: the cost \(\sum_i\psi_\alpha(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|/s)\) of every matching that follows a hierarchical transport up to a small error, for any \(Y\).

Architecture test. Not decided. The eighth review's Decisive test is the seventh review's retained one on the dual side (outcomes (A) the gap-charged bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\)); none occurred here, the entry working on the primal side, where the review's Decision placed the steering test after the adapted partition lemma.

Owed attempt. The last entry named "proportional steering, the cut's rank \(r_C=n_C/2+\sigma_C\Delta_C\) ... against the running displacement and in proportion to it, capped so that neither child is empty": made here, by a different route than its count-surplus question. One cut, written for a general target split, shows that steering acts on the walk only through the gap between the target split and the count split; with targets split in proportion to the counts it does nothing, and the theorem below covers every rule, fixed before each cut and local, whose gap is at most \(A/\sqrt n\), under (ii)–(iv) below.

Earlier entries on the item. Read this cycle: adapted partitions ("proportional steering, the cut's rank ... against the running displacement and in proportion to it"); square means ("what a routing cannot change (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux); sequential rules, the dyadic"); exceedance slopes ("its drift with \(J\) out of reach of tail counts at \(512\) seeds"); simultaneous rule exceedances ("lighter than Gaussian by a factor of \(3\) to \(4\) at \(J=6,7\)"); simultaneous rule tails ("the rule itself lowers the pooled kurtosis by about \(0.4\) at the sizes run"); sequential rules ("what a routing cannot change, answered by the straight-cut forced flux entry"). None splits targets other than dyadically.

Setting

\(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\). A hierarchical transport of depth \(D\): the root cell and the root target are \([0,1]^2\); at step \(j<D\) every cell \(C\) of step \(j\), with target \(Q_C\), is cut in coordinate \(k_j\) (\(k_j=1\) for even \(j\), \(2\) for odd \(j\)) through its pivot, the interior point of rank \(r_C\) in that coordinate among its \(n_C\) interior points, and its target is cut in the same coordinate at the fraction \(\tau_C\in(0,1)\) of its side, the lower child's target taking the lower part; \(r_C\) and \(\tau_C\) are functions of the cuts of the earlier steps (and of the targets, which those cuts fix), so both are fixed before the cut. The pivot is interior to neither child. On each step-\(j\) cell, \(T_j\) maps \(C\) onto \(Q_C\) coordinatewise affinely and increasingly; \(T=T_D\). Write \(q_C=r_C/n_C\) for the count split. With \(\psi_\alpha\), \(s\) and \((L,\infty)\)-goodness as in the adapted partition entry; \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\), the fine steps \(j_0=D-2m\le j<D\).

Theorem (split-matched transport obstruction)

Statement. Let \(k\in\{1,2\}\), \(A\ge0\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12]\), \(\delta\in(0,1)\), \(\Gamma\ge1\), \(L,\kappa,K,M>0\), \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\), \(x=(A+\frac12)/\sqrt{(1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)}\), \(m_x=\lceil128x^2\rceil\), \(p=64^{-m_x}\), \(\lambda=\log_2(1/(p\varepsilon^2))\), \(0<\theta<1/(2\lambda+2\log_2(1/\varepsilon))\). Fix for each \(N\) a hierarchical transport of some depth \(D\ge2m\), whose rule is local at step \(j_0\) (the ranks and target splits of cells of step at least \(j_0\) are functions of the cuts before \(j_0\) and of those inside the step-\(j_0\) ancestor), such that (i) \(|\tau_C-q_C|\le A/\sqrt{n_C}\) for every cell; (ii) \(q_C,\tau_C\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) for every cell; (iii) every final cell has \(\kappa\log N\le n_C\le K\log N\); (iv) at each fine step cutting coordinate \(k\), the target's sides satisfy \(\ell'_{3-k}\le\Gamma\ell'_k\). With probability tending to one, every permutation \(\pi\) and all \(Y_1,\dots,Y_N\in[0,1]^2\) with \(|Y^k_{\pi(i)}-T^k(X_i)|\le m/(18\sqrt{\Gamma N})\) for every \(X_i\) interior to its final cell have, for \(\alpha<\infty\), \(\sum_i\psi_\alpha(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|/s)\ge MN\), and for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(\max_i|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|>s\).

Refinement checked. thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction implies thm:adapted-partition-obstruction. That theorem's class (\(\tau_C=\frac12\), \(|q_C-\frac12|\le A'/\sqrt{n_C}\)) meets (i) with \(A=A'\), (ii) with any \(\varepsilon<\frac12\) for large \(N\), (iii) with \(\kappa/2\) and \(2K\) in place of its \(\kappa\) and \(K\) (its counts lie in \(N4^{-J}e^{\pm2\gamma_N}\)), and (iv) with \(\Gamma=1\) (a dyadic target at a \(k\)-step has \(\ell'_{3-k}\le\ell'_k\)). Its error bound \(m/(18\sqrt N)\) is this one's at \(\Gamma=1\). Its range \(\theta<1/(2+2\lambda_A)=1/(12m_A+6)\), \(m_A=\lceil128x_A^2\rceil\), \(x_A^2=16(A+\frac12)^2/3\), lies inside this one's \(\theta<1/(12m_x+6\log_2(1/\varepsilon))\) once \(\delta=\frac1{10}\) and \(\varepsilon\) is close to \(\frac12\): then \(x^2\) tends to \(40(A+\frac12)^2/9\), about \(0.83\,x_A^2\), so \(m_x<m_A\) and the denominator \(12m_x+6\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\) is below \(12m_A+6\) : for every \(A\ge0\), at \(\varepsilon=\frac12\), \(128x^2=\frac56\cdot128x_A^2\le m_A-\frac{128}6x_A^2\le m_A-28\), as \(x_A^2\ge\frac43\); \(x\) is continuous in \(\varepsilon\), so \(m_x\le m_A-1\) for \(\varepsilon\) close enough to \(\frac12\); then \(12m_x+6\log_2(1/\varepsilon)\le12m_A-12+6\log_2(1/\varepsilon)<12m_A+6\), as \(\varepsilon>\frac18\). Examples, exact at \(\varepsilon=\frac12\): \(A=0\) gives \(m_x=143\) against \(m_A=171\), bounds \(1/1722\) and \(1/2058\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_split_matched_20261017/implication-check.txt). So every instance of that theorem is one of this one, with the same conclusion. It also covers targets split in proportion to the counts (\(\tau_C=q_C\), \(A=0\)) with ranks meeting (ii)–(iv), that is with steering that keeps (ii) and (iii).

Proof

Conditional uniformity. As in the adapted partition proof, with \(\mathcal G_j\) the cuts before step \(j\): given \(\mathcal G_j\), \(r_C\) and \(\tau_C\) are fixed and the interior point sets of the step-\(j\) cells are independent, each i.i.d. uniform in its cell (the order-statistic factorisation, the rank being fixed in advance of the cut).

The walk. For a step-\(j\) cell \(C\) with \(k\)-side \([a,a+\ell]\) and target \(k\)-side \([a',a'+\ell']\), the mean of \(R_j=T^k_j(x)-x_k\) over \(C\) is \(U(C)=(a'+\ell'/2)-(a+\ell/2)\). At a step cutting the other coordinate \(U\) is unchanged. Cutting coordinate \(k\) at \(a+c\ell\), \(c\in(0,1)\) the pivot's relative position, the lower child has \(k\)-side \([a,a+c\ell]\) and target \([a',a'+\tau\ell']\), the upper \([a+c\ell,a+\ell]\) and \([a'+\tau\ell',a'+\ell']\), so \(U(C_-)-U(C)=-(1-\tau)\ell'/2+(1-c)\ell/2\) and \(U(C_+)-U(C)=\tau\ell'/2-c\ell/2\). With \(\xi_C=(\tau-c)\ell'/2\), these are \(U(C_\pm)=U(C)+\xi_C+\delta_\pm\), \(\delta_-=(1-c)(\ell-\ell')/2\), \(\delta_+=-c(\ell-\ell')/2\), and \(c\delta_-+(1-c)\delta_+=0\). Let \(C_*=C_-\) if \(\sigma_C(\ell-\ell')\ge0\) and \(C_+\) otherwise (\(\sigma_C=\operatorname{sign}U(C)\), \(+1\) at \(0\)), a \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable choice with \(\sigma_C\delta_{C_*}\ge0\); then \(|U(C_*)|\ge|U(C)|+\sigma_C\xi_C\). For \(\tau=\frac12\) this is the adapted partition's walk with \(c=\frac12+\eta\).

The push. Given \(\mathcal G_j\), with \(n=n_C\), \(r=r_C\), \(\tau=\tau_C\) and \(\varepsilon_n=1/(4\sqrt n)\): \(c\le\tau-\varepsilon_n\) exactly when at least \(r\) interior points lie below the relative level \(\tau-\varepsilon_n\), that is when \(S=\sum_z(1\{z\text{ below}\}-(\tau-\varepsilon_n))\ge r-n\tau+n\varepsilon_n\), and by (i) \(r-n\tau=n(q-\tau)\le A\sqrt n\), so the threshold is at most \((A+\frac14)\sqrt n\le(A+\frac12)\sqrt n\). The terms are i.i.d., mean \(0\), size at most \(1\), variance \((\tau-\varepsilon_n)(1-\tau+\varepsilon_n)\ge(1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\) by (ii) once \(\varepsilon_n\le\delta\varepsilon\), that is \(n\ge1/(16\delta^2\varepsilon^2)\) (at \(\tau=\varepsilon\) the product is at least \(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)(1-\varepsilon_n/\varepsilon)\), and it is larger nearer \(\frac12\)); so \(s_n\ge\sqrt{(1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)n}\) and the threshold is at most \(xs_n\); lem:block-lower-tail at \(x\) (needing \(m_x\le n\) and \(1\le s_n^2/(2m_x)\), true for \(n\ge2m_x/((1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon))\)) gives probability at least \(p\). Symmetrically, \(c\ge\tau+\varepsilon_n\) when at most \(r-1\) points lie below \(\tau+\varepsilon_n\), a deviation of at most \(n\varepsilon_n+A\sqrt n+1\le(A+\frac12)\sqrt n\) for \(n\ge16\), of variance \((\tau+\varepsilon_n)(1-\tau-\varepsilon_n)\ge(1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\), probability at least \(p\). So \(P(\sigma_C\xi_C\ge\ell'/(8\sqrt n)\mid\mathcal G_j)\ge p\).

Counts and capacities. A child of a cell with \(n\) interior points holds \(r-1\) or \(n-r\), between \(\varepsilon n-1\) and \((1-\varepsilon)n\) by (ii); so going up from a final cell the counts grow at least by the factor \(1/(1-\varepsilon)\) per step, less one point, and every cell of a chain above a final cell has \(n_i\ge\kappa\log N(1-\varepsilon)^{-l}/2\) at \(l\) steps above it. Write \(\rho_C=n_C/(N|Q_C|)\), with \(\rho=1\) at the root. A child's count over its parent's is \(q\) or \(1-q\) up to \(1/n\), its target's area over its parent's is \(\tau\) or \(1-\tau\), and by (i) and (ii) their ratio is \(1\pm\beta(n)\), \(\beta(n)=(A/\sqrt n+1/n)/\varepsilon\). So \(\rho_C\in[e^{-2\gamma_N},e^{2\gamma_N}]\) for every cell, with \(\gamma_N=\sum_{l\ge0}\beta(\kappa\log N(1-\varepsilon)^{-l}/2)\le\frac{\sqrt2A}{\varepsilon(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon})\sqrt{\kappa\log N}}+\frac{2}{\varepsilon^2\kappa\log N}\to0\) (each factor \(1-\beta\ge e^{-2\beta}\) for \(\beta\le\frac12\)). At a fine \(k\)-step, \(n_C=\rho_CN\ell'_1\ell'_2\), so by (iv) \(\ell'_k/\sqrt{n_C}=\sqrt{\ell'_k/\ell'_{3-k}}/\sqrt{\rho_CN}\ge e^{-\gamma_N}/\sqrt{\Gamma N}\), and the push of the previous step is at least \(h=1/(9\sqrt{\Gamma N})\) for large \(N\). Every cell has \(n_C\ge\kappa\log N\ge\max(2m_x/((1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)),1/(16\delta^2\varepsilon^2),16)\) for large \(N\), as the push needs.

A chain of cells. \(\mathcal A_{j_0}\) is every step-\(j_0\) cell; \(\mathcal A_{j+1}\) is \(\{C_-:C\in\mathcal A_j\}\) at a step not cutting \(k\) (\(U\) unchanged in either child) and \(\{C_*:C\in\mathcal A_j,\ \sigma_C\xi_C\ge h\}\) at a step cutting \(k\). By the walk, \(|U(C)|\ge mh\) on \(\mathcal A_D\). With \(V_j=\sum_{C\in\mathcal A_j}n_C/N\) and \(n_{\text{child}}\ge\varepsilon n_C(1-1/(\varepsilon n_C))\), and membership and the choice of \(C_*\) being \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable, \(\mathbb E[V_{j+1}\mid\mathcal G_j]\ge p\varepsilon(1-\bar\beta_j)V_j\) at a \(k\)-step and \(V_{j+1}\ge\varepsilon(1-\bar\beta_j)V_j\) at the others, \(\bar\beta_j\) the largest \(1/(\varepsilon n_C)\) at step \(j\); \(\prod_j(1-\bar\beta_j)\to1\) by the same geometric sum. The cuts before \(j_0\) number fewer than the step-\(j_0\) cells, at most \(N/(\kappa\log N)\), so \(V_{j_0}\ge1-1/(\kappa\log N)\), and \(\mathbb E[V_D\mid\mathcal G_{j_0}]\ge\mu/2\) for large \(N\), \(\mu=(p\varepsilon^2)^m\ge N^{-\theta\lambda}\).

Many cells. By locality, \(V_D=\sum_TV(T)\) over the step-\(j_0\) cells, \(V(T)\in[0,n_T/N]\) a function of \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\) and the points of \(T\), independent given \(\mathcal G_{j_0}\). Going up \(2m\) steps from a final cell multiplies the count by at most \(1/\varepsilon\) per step, plus one point, so \(n_T\le2K\log N\,\varepsilon^{-2m}\le2K\log N\,N^{2\theta\log_2(1/\varepsilon)}\), and \(\operatorname{Var}(V_D\mid\mathcal G_{j_0})\le\max_Tn_T/(4N)\). By Chebyshev, \(P(V_D<\mu/4\mid\mathcal G_{j_0})\le16\operatorname{Var}/\mu^2\le8K\log N\,N^{2\theta\log_2(1/\varepsilon)+2\theta\lambda-1}\to0\).

From cells to points, and cost. As in the adapted partition proof: given \(\mathcal G_D\) the interior points of final cells are independent and uniform, \(R\) is affine on each final cell with mean \(U(C)\), so at least \(N\mu/16\) interior points of chain cells have \(|R(X_i)|\ge mh\) with probability tending to one (Chernoff, \(N\mu\to\infty\) as \(\theta\lambda<\frac12\)). For each, \(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|\ge mh-m/(18\sqrt{\Gamma N})=\frac{m}{18\sqrt{\Gamma N}}\), an argument \(u_N\ge\frac{\theta\sqrt{\ln N}}{18L\sqrt\Gamma\ln2}-o(1)\to\infty\); the cost is at least \(\frac{N^{1-\theta\lambda}}{16}(e^{u_N^\alpha}-1)\ge MN\) for large \(N\) when \(\alpha<\infty\), as \(u_N^\alpha\) grows as \((\ln N)^{\alpha/2}\), and for \(\alpha=\infty\) some displacement exceeds \(s\). The events concern \(X\) and the fixed rule only, so the conclusion holds for every \(\pi\) and \(Y\) meeting the hypothesis. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(X\) i.i.d. uniform: conditional uniformity. Ranks and target splits functions of earlier cuts: conditional uniformity, and the predictable child choice. Locality at \(j_0\): Chebyshev's independence. (i), the gap \(|\tau_C-q_C|\le A/\sqrt{n_C}\): the push (a threshold of \((A+\frac12)\sqrt n\)) at the fine steps, and the capacities over all steps; the capacities need only \(\rho_C\) bounded above and below, which a bounded \(\gamma_N\) gives with \(h\) changed by a constant, so their weakest form is a bounded sum \(\sum|\tau-q|/\varepsilon\) along every chain (the step \(1-\beta\ge e^{-2\beta}\) needs \(\beta\le\frac12\); finitely many levels with larger \(\beta\) change \(\rho\) by a bounded factor only, both splits lying in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\)). (ii), splits in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\): the push's variance, the chain's weights, the geometric growth of counts, and the capacities. (iii), final counts: \(\kappa\) for the push's lower bound on \(n\), for \(\gamma_N\) and for \(V_{j_0}\ge1-1/(\kappa\log N)\); \(K\) for the variance bound. (iv), the target's aspect at fine \(k\)-steps: the push's size \(h\). Alternating coordinates: \(m\) fine \(k\)-steps. The error bound \(m/(18\sqrt{\Gamma N})\): the cost step. \(\alpha>2\): the cost step.

Degenerate cases. \(\tau_C=q_C\) exactly (targets in proportion to counts): \(A=0\), \(x=1/(2\sqrt{(1-\delta)\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)})\), the push driven by the order statistic's own fluctuation; covered. \(\ell=\ell'\): \(\delta_\pm=0\). \(U(C)=0\): \(\sigma=+1\). Splits near \(0\) or \(1\): excluded by (ii); without it a child can hold one point, the push's variance vanishes, and capacities can drift. \(\Gamma\) large (targets thin in coordinate \(k\)): \(h\) shrinks as \(1/\sqrt\Gamma\), and the statement weakens with it, the error bound scaling the same way. Steering by more than \(A\sqrt n\) with dyadic targets: violates (i), not covered. Steering with proportional targets: covered while (iii) holds, for instance when the splits' deviations from \(\frac12\) are summable along each path at the fixed depth, as with offsets up to \(n^{3/4}\) points; steering by a fixed fraction (\(|q_C-\frac12|\) bounded below) gives final counts spread over a polynomial range at any fixed depth and violates (iii), not covered. Small \(N\): asymptotic only.

Nonvacuity. On the curve parameters: proportional targets with steering, \(\tau_C=q_C=r_C/n_C\) and \(r_C=\lfloor n_C/2\rfloor+\sigma_C\min(\lfloor\kappa'|U(C)|\sqrt{Nn_C}\rfloor,\lfloor n_C^{3/4}\rfloor)\), steering against the running displacement by up to \(n^{3/4}\) points, far beyond any fixed multiple of \(\sqrt n\). Its splits deviate from \(\frac12\) by at most \(n_C^{-1/4}+1/n_C\), which is at most \(\frac14\) once \(n_C\ge300\) (\(0.2436\) there, \(0.2539\) at \(256\)), so (ii) holds with \(\varepsilon=\frac14\), every cell holding at least \(\kappa\log N\) points; along a path the count factors are \(\frac12(1\pm2n_i^{-1/4}\pm3/n_i)\), whose deviations sum geometrically to \(O((\kappa\log N)^{-1/4})\to0\), so at depth \(D=2J\) with \(2\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N/2\) every final count lies in \([\kappa\log N,K\log N]\) for large \(N\), (iii); the target sides are \(\frac12(1\pm2n_i^{-1/4})\) of their parents', so their aspect stays within \(2e^{\pm o(1)}\) and (iv) holds with \(\Gamma=3\); (i) holds with \(A=0\); the rule reads \(U(C)\), the cell's and its target's sides, so it is local. With \(\varepsilon=\frac14\), \(\delta=\frac14\), \(A=0\): \(x^2=\frac14/(\frac34\cdot\frac3{16})=16/9\), \(m_x=228\), \(\lambda=6m_x+4=1372\), and \(\theta=10^{-4}<1/2748\); at \(N=2^{20000}\), \(\ln N=13863\), \(\kappa=\frac12\), \(K=8\) and \(J=9993\), \(N4^{-J}=16384\in[13863,55452]\), and \(m=2\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_split_matched_20261017/witness-constants.txt, exact arithmetic). Plainest bound. On this witness, thm:adapted-partition-obstruction does not apply (its targets are dyadic and its ranks within \(A\sqrt n\) of the median, here \(n^{3/4}\)), and the second moment of a displacement, of order \(s^2\), decides nothing above exponent \(2\).

Plainest bound. On the Nonvacuity witness, the second moment of a point's displacement is of order \(s^2\), which bounds the fraction beyond \(us\) by \(O(1/u^2)\) and decides nothing above exponent \(2\); thm:adapted-partition-obstruction, the oldest applicable lemma, does not cover it (dyadic targets, ranks within \(A\sqrt n\)).

Baseline. The construction needing no idea is the equal-count partition with dyadic targets, excluded by thm:adapted-partition-obstruction; the statement adds every target split within \(A/\sqrt n\) of the count split, chosen by a local rule before the cut, with splits bounded away from \(0\) and \(1\), final counts within constants and targets of bounded aspect: in particular targets split in proportion to the counts with steering that keeps (ii) and (iii).

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:adapted-partition-obstruction is implied by this theorem (Refinement checked, after the Statement: its class is the case \(\tau_C=\frac12\), its error bound this one's at \(\Gamma=1\), and its \(\theta\) range inside this one's with \(\delta=\frac1{10}\)), so this theorem refines it; thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction concerns the dyadic flow, a flow and not a transport, and neither implies the other; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, thm:low-level-mixed-counts and thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold, the next nearest by the resemblance tool, concern count-measurable fields and the existence of other matchings, neither more general versions nor special cases of this one; the adapted partition proof's conditional uniformity, transfer to points and cost steps, and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's chain and Chebyshev steps, are used here on other cells, citations, not new. The record holds no statement on hierarchical transports with non-dyadic target splits (searched: "k-d tree transport order statistic cut target split proportional to counts Knothe Rosenblatt hierarchical transport exponent", which returned claims of other threads only). New here: the walk for a general target split, \(\xi=(\tau-c)\ell'/2\) with deviations \((1-c)(\ell-\ell')/2\) and \(-c(\ell-\ell')/2\), which shows that a cut's rank acts on the walk only through the gap \(\tau-q\); the capacity ratio \(\rho_C\) and its control by (i) and (ii); and counts weighted by splits bounded below in place of halves.

General statement. thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction, for every \(A\ge0\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12]\), \(\Gamma\ge1\), \(L,\kappa,K,M\), \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\) and both coordinates.

New mathematics. thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction: for a hierarchical transport whose rule, local at the fine steps and fixed before each cut, keeps the target split within \(A/\sqrt n\) of the count split, all splits in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), final counts in \([\kappa\log N,K\log N]\) and the targets' aspect at fine steps at most \(\Gamma\), every matching following the transport up to \(m/(18\sqrt{\Gamma N})\) in coordinate \(k\) has cost at least \(MN\) in that coordinate for every \(L\), \(M\) and \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\), with probability tending to one (an asymptotic statement). It implies thm:adapted-partition-obstruction, and covers targets split in proportion to the counts with steering up to \(n^{3/4}\) points per cut. Recorded also: with target splits chosen at the cut itself, \(\tau=c\) at every cut, every cell equals its target and the transport is the identity.

Goal progress. Unchanged: the theorem excludes a wider class of constructions and proves no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy or conj:ultimate-matching. Bearing. At every pair of the curve, where some \(\alpha_k\ge4\), and every \(L\): no matching that follows, up to \(m/(18\sqrt{\Gamma N})\) in coordinate \(k\), a hierarchical transport meeting (i)–(iv) with a local rule fixed before each cut meets the conjecture's conclusion, with probability tending to one. Not covered. Target splits chosen after the cut (\(\tau_C\) depending on the cut's position), or differing from the count split by more than \(A/\sqrt n\); steering by a fixed fraction, which at a fixed depth violates (iii); cell-dependent depths; targets of unbounded aspect; non-local rules; partitions of both samples; matchings farther from the transport; and flows or matchings not built from hierarchical transports.

Follow-up. Continuing. The item's readings: what a routing cannot change (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux); rules on dyadic squares (thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction); adapted partitions near the median (thm:adapted-partition-obstruction); and here every hierarchical transport whose target split is fixed before the cut and within \(A/\sqrt n\) of the count split, steering included. Target splits chosen at the cut itself, \(\tau=c\) at every cut, make every cell its own target by induction from the root, so the transport is the identity and correcting its counts is the original matching problem, the goal itself: that reading is a restatement, not an attempt. Next attempt: target splits that follow the cut partly, \(\tau=q+w(c-q)\) with a fixed \(w<1\) (the reviewer's suggestion, outline checked by hand below), to show the dichotomy that every \(w<1\) falls to the walk and only \(w=1\), the identity, escapes. Smallest case. One cut, by hand: \(\xi=(\tau-c)\ell'/2=(1-w)(q-c)\ell'/2\), so the push is the order statistic's deviation from \(q\) in either sign, the event of the theorem's push with \(A=0\) and probability at least \(p\), at size \((1-w)\ell'/(8\sqrt n)\); the capacities see \(|\tau-q|=w|c-q|\), which is not fixed before the cut but is at most \(C\sqrt{\log N/n}\) for every cell at once with probability tending to one (Hoeffding over the at most \(N\) cuts), so \(\gamma_N\) is bounded, of order \(w/(\varepsilon^2\sqrt\kappa)\) (with the \(\beta\le\frac12\) caveat of the Hypotheses), not tending to \(0\), which changes \(h\) by a constant factor only. Two repairs the proof needs (the reviewer's follow-up): the chain's membership must be the order-statistic event \(\sigma_C(q-c)\ge1/(4\sqrt n)\), which is fixed in probability given \(\mathcal G_j\), since \(\sigma_C\xi_C\ge h\) uses \(\ell'\) and the Hoeffding event, not \(\mathcal G_j\)-measurable; on the Hoeffding event each such step adds at least \((1-w)\) times a constant over \(\sqrt{\Gamma N}\); and the aspect condition (iv) depends on the cuts once \(w>0\), the target sides deviating by \(w(c-q)=O(\sqrt{\log N/n})\), so it holds with a bounded \(\Gamma\) on the same event and must be proved there. Plainest bound. On this instance, the second moment of a displacement, of order \(s^2\), decides nothing above exponent \(2\), and the theorem does not apply as stated, \(\tau\) depending on the cut. Tried. Which local completion forms glue levels

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; nested bipartite graphs, existential and universal readings · Local completion. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. The first route review queued, as the head item local-completion-hall now is: "A 'local completion' form of per-level Hall conditions, in which vertices unmatched at level \(k\) must be matchable within \(G_{k+1}\), escapes the counterexample and may hold for random samples". Does such a condition, at every level, let the per-level deficiencies be glued into one matching at a constant factor?

Target form. The goal's own form at the level of certificates: one perfect matching \(P\) whose layered cost \(\sum_kw_k|P\setminus G_k|\) is within a constant of \(\sum_kw_km_k\), the form in which lem:per-level-gluing-fails refuted plain per-level conditions.

Architecture test. Not decided. The eighth review's Decisive test (outcomes (A) the gap-charged bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\)) concerns the dual side; none occurred here, the entry developing the queue's head while the queue drains.

Owed attempt. None was named before this entry, the item's first.

Setting

\(X\), \(Y\) finite with \(|X|=|Y|=n\); nested bipartite graphs \(G_{k_0}\subseteq\dots\subseteq G_K\) between them, \(k_0\) an integer or \(-\infty\), \(G_K\) complete; \(m_k=n-\nu(G_k)\) the deficiency; weights \(w_k\ge0\) with \(W_j=\sum_{k_0\le k\le j}w_k\) finite. The layered cost of a perfect matching \(P\) is \(\sum_{k<K}w_k|P\setminus G_k|\), its minimum \(\Gamma\), and \(S=\sum_{k<K}w_km_k\); always \(\Gamma\ge S\), since \(|P\setminus G_k|\ge m_k\). The item's words "vertices unmatched at level \(k\) matchable within \(G_{k+1}\)" allow these readings, each asked at every level \(k<K\), for some maximum matching \(M_k\) of \(G_k\) with leftover \(U_k\) (the vertices it leaves unmatched): completion with constant \(C\ge0\), a matching \(L_k\subseteq G_{k+1}\) inside \(U_k\) with \(|L_k|\ge m_k-Cm_{k+1}\) (\(C=0\): all of the leftover matched among itself); cover, one matching of \(G_{k+1}\) covering every vertex of \(U_k\), partners anywhere; and augmenting, \(M_k\) extended to a maximum matching of \(G_{k+1}\) by augmenting paths. "Must be matchable" may also quantify over every maximum matching: the universal form of a reading asks it for every maximum matching \(M_k\) of \(G_k\), the plain form for some.

Theorem (local completion dichotomy)

Statement. (a) Completion with \(C<1\) at a level \(k\) forces \(m_{k+1}=0\); so it holds at every level only if every level above \(k_0\) has a perfect matching, and then \(\Gamma=S\). With \(C=1\), \(M_k\cup L_k\) is a maximum matching of \(G_{k+1}\). The augmenting reading holds for every family. (b) Let \(C>1\), let some \(m_k>0\), \(k^*\) the largest such \(k\), \(j\ge k^*+2\), and \(M\) an integer with \(M\ge\max_{k\le j-2}(m_k-Cm_{k+1})/(C-1)\) (\(m_k=0\) for \(k\ge K\)). Add \(M\) new pairs \(x'_iy'_i\): \(G'_k=G_k\cup\{x'_iy'_i:i\le M\text{ if }k\ge j\}\) for \(k_0\le k<K'=\max(K,j)+1\), with \(G_k\) complete on \(X\times Y\) for \(k\ge K\) and any weights \(w_k\ge0\) on the new levels \(K\le k<K'\), and \(G'_{K'}\) complete. Then every level satisfies completion with constant \(C\), the deficiencies are \(m_k+M\) for \(k<j\) and \(0\) for \(k\ge j\), \(\Gamma'=\Gamma+MW_{j-1}\) and \(S'=S+MW_{j-1}\). (c) On the line, for \(n\ge1\), \(h=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\), \(C>1\), \(M=\lceil h/(C-1)\rceil\), \(d=\lceil eh\rceil\), \(\Delta=2(n+h+d)\): \(X=\{1,\dots,n\}\), \(Y=X+h\), \(x'_i=n+h+i\Delta\), \(y'_i=x'_i+d\) (\(i\le M\)), levels \(G_k=\{|x-y|\le e^{k-1}\}\) for \(k_0\le k\le K''\) (\(k_0\le1\) any integer, or all integers \(k\le K''\)), \(K''\) least with \(e^{K''-1}\) at least the diameter, weights \(e^k\): every level satisfies completion with constant \(C\), \(\Gamma\ge nh+Md-n-M\) and \(S\le(e^2(h^2+Md)+eh)/(e-1)\), so \(\Gamma/S\ge(1+o(1))\sqrt n\,(e-1)(C-1)/(e^2(C-1+e))\). (d) For \(L\ge1\) and \(t\ge4\), \(X=\{x_1,\dots,x_L,u\}\), \(Y=\{y_1,\dots,y_L,v\}\), \(A=\{x_iy_i\}\), \(G_1=A\), \(G_2=A\cup\{vx_1\}\cup\{y_ix_{i+1}:i<L\}\), \(G_3=\dots=G_{t-1}=G_2\cup\{uy_L\}\), \(G_t\) complete: completion with \(C=1\) holds at every level, \(S=w_1+w_2\) and \(\Gamma=\min(w_1(L+1)+w_2,\ \Gamma_{\rm out})\) with \(\Gamma_{\rm out}\ge W_{t-1}\); with \(w_k=e^k\) and \(t\ge2+\ln(L+1+e)\), \(\Gamma/S=(L+1+e)/(1+e)\). (e) For \(L\ge1\) and \(t\ge3\), the same \(X\), \(Y\), \(A\), with \(G_1=A\), \(G_2=\dots=G_{t-1}=A\cup\{vx_1\}\cup\{y_ix_{i+1}:i<L\}\cup\{uy_L\}\), \(G_t\) complete: the cover reading holds at every level, \(S=w_1\) and \(\Gamma=\min(w_1(L+1),\Gamma_{\rm out})\) with \(\Gamma_{\rm out}\ge W_{t-1}\); with \(w_k=e^k\) and \(t\ge2+\ln(L+1)\), \(\Gamma/S=L+1\). (f) The universal form of completion with \(C=1\) at every level gives \(\Gamma=S\) for every nonnegative weights; the families of (b), (c) and (e) satisfy the universal forms of their readings, and that of (d) does not satisfy the universal form of completion with \(C=1\).

Proof

(a). \(M_k\cup L_k\) is a matching (\(L_k\) lies inside the leftover), lies in \(G_{k+1}\supseteq G_k\), and has size \(n-m_k+|L_k|\ge n-Cm_{k+1}\), while every matching of \(G_{k+1}\) has at most \(n-m_{k+1}\) edges: \((1-C)m_{k+1}\le0\). For \(C<1\), \(m_{k+1}=0\); at every level this makes every level above \(k_0\) perfect (for \(k_0=-\infty\), every level), and at \(k_0\) the perfect matching \(M_{k_0}\cup L_{k_0}\) of \(G_{k_0+1}\) has \(|P\setminus G_{k_0}|\le m_{k_0}\) and \(|P\setminus G_k|=0\) above: \(\Gamma\le S\). For \(C=1\) the size is \(n-m_{k+1}\), maximum. Augmenting paths never unmatch a vertex, so augmenting a maximum matching of \(G_k\) inside \(G_{k+1}\) until none remains gives a maximum matching of \(G_{k+1}\).

(b), deficiencies. For \(k<j\) the new vertices have no edges in \(G'_k\), so the deficiency is \(m_k+M\). For \(j\le k<K'\), \(k>k^*\), so \(G_k\) has a perfect matching (nestedness gives \(m_k\le m_{k^*+1}=0\), and \(G_k\) is complete for \(k\ge K\)), and with the \(M\) pairs the deficiency is \(0\).

(b), completion. For \(k\le j-2\) both \(k\) and \(k+1\) are below \(j\): \(m'_k-Cm'_{k+1}=m_k-Cm_{k+1}-(C-1)M\le0\) by the choice of \(M\), so any maximum matching with \(L_k=\emptyset\) serves. At \(k=j-1>k^*\), a perfect matching of \(G_k\) is a maximum matching of \(G'_k\) (size \(n\), deficiency \(M\)); its leftover is \(X'\cup Y'\), and the \(M\) pairs lie in \(G'_j\): \(|L|=M=m'_{j-1}-Cm'_j\). For \(k\ge j\) the deficiency is \(0\).

(b), costs. \(S'=S+M\sum_{k<j}w_k\), the base terms with \(k\ge K\) vanishing. In a perfect matching \(P'\) of the union, a pair \(x'_iy'_i\) costs \(W_{j-1}\); every other edge meeting a new vertex lies only in \(G'_{K'}\) and costs \(W_{K'-1}\); a base edge costs at most \(W_{K-1}\le W_{K'-1}\), its absent levels lying below \(K\). If \(P'\) has \(q\) edges from \(X\) to \(Y'\), it has \(q\) from \(X'\) to \(Y\); pairing their \(X\)-ends with their \(Y\)-ends arbitrarily completes its base edges to a perfect matching of \(X\) and \(Y\), so they cost at least \(\Gamma-qW_{K-1}\); its \(M\) edges at \(X'\) cost at least \(W_{j-1}\) each, and its \(q\) edges from \(X\) to \(Y'\) cost \(W_{K'-1}\ge W_{K-1}\) each. So \(\Gamma'\ge\Gamma+MW_{j-1}\), with equality at an optimal base matching with the \(M\) pairs.

(c). A new vertex lies at least \(\Delta\) from every base vertex, and \(|x'_i-y'_l|\ge\Delta-d\) for \(i\ne l\). At radius \(r=e^{k-1}<\Delta-d\) the components are separate and the deficiency is \(m^b_k+M[r<d]\), \(m^b_k\) the base's; lem:per-level-gluing-fails's proof gives \(m^b_k=h-\lfloor r\rfloor\le h\) for \(1\le r<h\), \(h\) for \(r<1\), and \(0\) for \(r\ge h\). At radius \(r\ge\Delta-d>d>h\) the base shift and the \(M\) pairs are a perfect matching. Completion, by the radius: if \(r<h\), then \(er<eh\le d\), the next deficiency is at least \(M\), and \(m^b_k+M-CM\le h-(C-1)M\le0\); if \(h\le r\) and \(er<d\), both deficiencies are \(M\) and \(M-CM<0\); if \(r<d\le er\), then \(r\ge d/e\ge h\), the shift by \(h\) is a perfect matching of the base within \(r\), with the new vertices isolated it is maximum, and its leftover, the \(M\) pairs, is matched within \(er\ge d\), the next deficiency being \(0\); if \(r\ge d\), the deficiency is \(0\). Cost: every perfect matching has \(\sum(y-x)=\sum Y-\sum X=nh+Md\), so \(\sum|y-x|\ge nh+Md\); its \(n+M\) edges of length at most \(1\) contribute at most \(n+M\), and an edge of length \(\delta\ge2\) costs \(c(\delta)=\sum_{k:e^{k-1}<\delta}e^k\ge\delta\) (lem:per-level-gluing-fails's proof; no level is cut off, as \(\delta\le e^{K''-1}\)): \(\Gamma\ge nh+Md-n-M\). The base's deficiency sum is at most \(\frac{e^2}{e-1}h^2+\frac e{e-1}h\) (that lemma, levels below \(1\) included), and the new pairs add \(M\sum_{k\le j-1}e^k\le Me^j/(e-1)\) with \(j-1\) the largest index with \(e^{j-2}<d\), so \(e^j<e^2d\). With \(h\sim\sqrt n\), \(M\sim\sqrt n/(C-1)\), \(d\sim e\sqrt n\), the bound on \(\Gamma\) is \(n^{3/2}(1+o(1))\) and that on \(S\) is \(e^2n(1+e/(C-1))(1+o(1))/(e-1)\).

(d). \(G_1=A\) leaves one vertex on each side: \(m_1=1\). \(G_2\) is the path \(v,x_1,y_1,x_2,\dots,x_L,y_L\) on \(2L+1\) vertices with \(u\) isolated: \(m_2=1\). In \(G_3\), \(u\)'s only edge is \(uy_L\), and the rest is the path \(v,x_1,\dots,x_L\) on \(2L\) vertices, whose only perfect matching is \(B=\{vx_1\}\cup\{y_ix_{i+1}\}\): \(G_3\) has exactly one perfect matching, \(P_0=B\cup\{uy_L\}\), and \(m_k=0\) for \(k\ge3\). Completion with \(C=1\): at level \(1\), \(m_1-m_2=0\) and \(L_1=\emptyset\) serves; at level \(2\), \(B\) is a maximum matching of \(G_2\) leaving \(u\) and \(y_L\), and \(uy_L\in G_3\): \(|L_2|=1=m_2-m_3\); above, deficiencies are \(0\). Cost: \(P_0\) contains no edge of \(A\) and one edge outside \(G_2\): \(w_1(L+1)+w_2\); every other perfect matching has an edge outside \(G_{t-1}\) and costs at least \(W_{t-1}\). With \(w_k=e^k\), \(W_{t-1}\ge e^{t-1}\ge e(L+1)+e^2\) once \(t\ge2+\ln(L+1+e)\).

(e). \(G_2\) is the path \(v,x_1,y_1,\dots,x_L,y_L,u\) on \(2L+2\) vertices, whose only perfect matching \(P_0=\{vx_1\}\cup\{y_ix_{i+1}\}\cup\{uy_L\}\) contains no edge of \(A\); \(m_1=1\) and \(m_k=0\) for \(k\ge2\). Cover: \(A\) is the only maximum matching of \(G_1\), its leftover is \(\{u,v\}\), and \(P_0\subseteq G_2\) covers both; above, deficiencies are \(0\). (Completion with \(C=1\) fails at level \(1\): \(uv\notin G_2\).) Cost: \(P_0\) costs \(w_1(L+1)\), every other perfect matching at least \(W_{t-1}\ge e^{t-1}\ge e(L+1)\) once \(t\ge2+\ln(L+1)\).

(f) (the reviewer's argument, checked). The graphs are nested on finite sets, so they take finitely many values; let \(G_{k_1}\) be the smallest (for \(k_0=-\infty\), every lower level equals it). Take any maximum matching \(M_{k_1}\); by the universal form at \(k_1\) it lies in a maximum matching \(M_{k_1+1}\) of \(G_{k_1+1}\), which is again a maximum matching, so the universal form at \(k_1+1\) applies to it; inductively \(M_{k_1}\subseteq M_{k_1+1}\subseteq\dots\subseteq M_K=P\), \(P\) perfect. Then \(P\cap G_k\supseteq M_k\), so \(|P\setminus G_k|\le n-|M_k|=m_k\) at every level (\(k\le k_1\) by \(M_{k_1}\)), and \(\Gamma\le S\le\Gamma\). In (b) and (c) the only maximum matchings at level \(j-1\) are a perfect base matching with the new vertices unmatched, and the levels below are vacuous for every maximum matching; in (e) \(A\) is the only maximum matching of \(G_1\). In (d), \(A\) is a maximum matching of \(G_2\) (\(L\) edges, \(m_2=1\)) leaving \(u\) and \(v\), and \(uv\notin G_3\): the universal form fails at level \(2\). \(\square\)

Structural reason. A condition asked for some maximum matching at each pair of consecutive levels lets each level pick its own matching: at levels of equal deficiency it asks nothing (d), where the deficiency drops it can be met by components added for the purpose (b), and covering the leftover says nothing about which matched edges must be given up to do it (e); the gluing cost comes from a chain of levels whose chosen matchings conflict, and a condition over every maximum matching (f), or one forcing every higher level perfect (a), rules the conflict out. As a judgement, untested on geometric instances (the families (d) and (e) use repeated levels and arbitrary graphs), the same reason would apply to any certificate relating consecutive levels through one chosen matching.

Hypotheses, each with its step. (a): \(G_k\subseteq G_{k+1}\) and the size bound for matchings of \(G_{k+1}\); \(C<1\) or \(C=1\) as stated. (b): \(C>1\) and \(M\ge\max_{k\le j-2}(m_k-Cm_{k+1})/(C-1)\), in the vacuity of the levels up to \(j-2\), its weakest form; nestedness, in \(m_k=0\) for \(k>k^*\); \(G_K\) complete, so that perfect matchings exist and base edges cost at most \(W_{K-1}\); \(w_k\ge0\) and \(W_{j-1}\) finite, in the cost and sum formulas; \(j\ge k^*+2\), so that level \(j-1\) has a perfect base matching. (c): \(C>1\) and \(M\ge h/(C-1)\), in the case \(r<h\); \(d\ge eh\), so that every level of radius below \(h\) has the new pairs unmatched one level up; \(\Delta=2(n+h+d)\), so that components separate below radius \(\Delta-d\); \(h=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor\) from lem:per-level-gluing-fails's instance, whose \(n\ge4\) no step of (c) uses (\(n\ge1\) suffices). (d), (e): \(t\) large enough that \(W_{t-1}\) exceeds the forced matching's cost. (f): nestedness and finiteness, in the chain; \(G_K\) complete, so that the chain ends at a perfect matching; weights only nonnegative. The class: (a) every nested family; (b) every family with a deficient level, every \(C>1\), nonnegative weights; (c) the line instance with geometric levels and weights \(e^k\), every \(C>1\); (d) and (e) the stated families, every \(L\).

Degenerate cases. Process assessment. The review's findings, above, share two habits: closing an enumeration on the forms in hand (readings with one quantifier; a Smallest case naming its instance and leaving it uncomputed), and writing summaries from the newest part of a result (three titles). Prevention. For the uncomputed Smallest case: commit "notebook-append: a Smallest case may not leave its instance uncomputed" refuses such a sentence unless it is a judgement or gives a measured cost, replayed over the 61 recorded Smallest case paragraphs (8 refused; research/provenance/framework/smallest-case-uncomputed-replay-20261017.txt) and tried against rewordings (two closed, three left with their reason; research/provenance/framework/smallest-case-uncomputed-bypass-20261017.txt). For the readings: AGENTS.md's rule on readings before a closure now asks each quantifier to be varied, a written rule since which readings a sentence allows is a judgement no pattern decides. For the titles: the written rule (title written after the review, from the reviewed body) let an overstated title through three times in this entry, so it is backed by a check, commit "draft_claim_sentences: the title and status line are answered like summing-up sentences": the answers form the append requires now holds rows for the title and the status line, each answered with what it rests on, and an answer carrying a limit ("only", "one direction") the title lacks is listed as a gap; it forces the title beside the statement's parts, and cannot judge an answer that names them wrongly (the bypass, an answer naming the whole theorem, still passes).

Meta. The way of working behind both habits is stopping at the first complete-looking story: four refuted readings looked like a closure, one computed example looked like a smallest case, the newest part looked like the result. Where else it shows: in the previous entry's "neither implies" and in the next attempts of earlier entries decided by their own formulas. The change, in the Spin self-review of PROMPTS.md: before an item is closed as refuted, the strongest positive form its words allow is written and a proof of it tried, since counterexamples to the forms in hand do not refute the form not yet written.
