Universal completion fails on random lines

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; bipartite graphs, line samples between two radii, square samples at one scale · Local completion. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: Its local-completion clause, that per-level Hall conditions do not glue when some maximum matching completes one level up though all completing glues, stays exact; this cycle's results concern a unit-density line, a family the goal does not use, and small components, and change no statement the section makes.

Question. The local completion entry proved that completion asked for every maximum matching glues levels at constant \(1\) (thm:local-completion-dichotomy (f)), and named the next attempt: "decide whether random samples satisfy the universal form of completion with \(C=1\) at the level graphs, first on the line with radius levels, then at the goal's box levels". Do they?

Target form. The goal's own form at the level of certificates: whether the goal's random samples carry the one local condition that glues per-level matchings into one matching.

Architecture test. Not decided. The eighth review's Decisive test (outcomes (A), (B), (C) on the dual side's gap-charged bound) did not occur; the entry develops the queue's head while the queue drains.

Owed attempt. The last entry named the attempt above. Made on the line: (b) below, the universal form fails with probability tending to one. At the goal's box levels it is made only for components of at most four vertices, which (c) shows do not occur there for \(L>1/\sqrt2\); the non-isolated case is the next attempt.

Setting

As in the local completion entry: nested bipartite graphs \(G_k\) on \(X\), \(Y\), \(|X|=|Y|=n\), deficiencies \(m_k\). For a bipartite graph \(G\), \(\mathcal U_X(G)\) is the family of sets of \(X\)-vertices left unmatched by some maximum matching of \(G\), and \(\mathcal U_Y(G)\) likewise. The universal form at level \(k\): every maximum matching \(M_k\) of \(G_k\) has a matching \(L_k\subseteq G_{k+1}\) inside its leftover with \(|L_k|\ge m_k-m_{k+1}\).

Theorem (universal completion criterion)

Statement. (a) For every bipartite graph \(G\), every \(U_X\in\mathcal U_X(G)\) and every \(U_Y\in\mathcal U_Y(G)\), some maximum matching of \(G\) leaves exactly \(U_X\cup U_Y\) unmatched. Hence the universal form holds at level \(k\) if and only if \(\nu(G_{k+1}[U_X\cup U_Y])\ge m_k-m_{k+1}\) for every \(U_X\in\mathcal U_X(G_k)\), \(U_Y\in\mathcal U_Y(G_k)\); in particular it fails at a level with \(m_{k+1}<m_k\) where some such pair spans no edge of \(G_{k+1}\). (b) Let \(0<r_1<r_2\) be fixed, \(X\) and \(Y\) independent samples of \(n\) i.i.d. uniform points of \([0,n]\), and \(G_1\subseteq G_2\) the graphs of pairs within distance \(r_1\) and \(r_2\). Take \(a,b,\delta>0\) with \(\delta\le a\), \(a+2\delta<r_1<b-2\delta\), \(b+2\delta<r_2<2a+b-2\delta\) (possible: \(a=0.8r_1\) and \(b\) between \(\max(r_1,r_2-1.6r_1)\) and \(r_2\)), an offset \(c>r_2+\delta\) and a window length \(W>\max(4,\,c+2a+b+\delta+r_2)\), and \(p_n=\big(n(n-1)(2\delta/n)^2(1-W/n)^{n-2}\big)^2\to\big((2\delta)^2e^{-W}\big)^2>0\). For \(n>2W\), with probability at least \(1-1/(\lfloor n/W\rfloor p_n)\), the universal form fails at level \(1\). (c) Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be independent samples of \(N\) i.i.d. uniform points of \([0,1]^2\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), and \(H\) any graph containing every pair within \(s\) in both coordinates. For every \(L>1/\sqrt2\), the expected number of points of \(X\cup Y\) with at most three points of the other sample within \(s\) in both coordinates tends to \(0\) (it is at most \(N^{1-4L^2+o(1)}\) from points at least \(s\) from the boundary and \(N^{1/2-L^2+o(1)}\) from the others): so with probability tending to one no component of the bipartite graph \(H\) has at most four vertices. The range \(L>1/\sqrt2\) is this proof's accounting, which bounds every boundary point by a corner's area; below \(L=1/2\) the interior expectation itself diverges, since a box of area \(4s^2\) holds no point of the other sample with probability \((1-4s^2)^N=N^{-4L^2(1+o(1))}\), against \(2N(1-o(1))\) interior points.

Proof

(a). Let \(M_1\), \(M_2\) be maximum matchings leaving \(U_X\) and \(U_Y\), \(A=X\setminus U_X\) and \(B=Y\setminus U_Y\). Each component of \(M_1\cup M_2\) is an alternating cycle or path; its interior vertices are covered by both. On a path with a \(Y\)-endpoint covered by \(M_2\) alone take \(M_2\)'s edges, and on every other component \(M_1\)'s. Taking \(M_1\)'s, the only vertex left uncovered is an endpoint covered by \(M_2\) alone, which is then in \(X\) and, not covered by \(M_1\), not in \(A\). Taking \(M_2\)'s, the only vertex left uncovered is an endpoint covered by \(M_1\) alone; it is not in \(X\), for a path from an \(X\)-endpoint with an \(M_1\) edge to a \(Y\)-endpoint with an \(M_2\) edge alternates from \(M_1\) to \(M_2\), so has an even number of edges and both endpoints on one side; so it is in \(Y\) and, not covered by \(M_2\), not in \(B\). So the matching \(M\) built covers \(A\cup B\). It has at least \(|A|=\nu(G)\) edges, so it is maximum, its \(X\)-cover is exactly \(A\) and its \(Y\)-cover exactly \(B\). The criterion: a maximum matching's leftover is a pair \((U_X,U_Y)\), every pair occurs, and the matching \(L_k\) uses only leftover vertices. The particular case: a pair spanning no edge of \(G_{k+1}\) has \(\nu=0<m_k-m_{k+1}\).

(b). Windows \(W_i=[iW,(i+1)W)\), \(i<w=\lfloor n/W\rfloor\), and \(o_i=iW+c\). \(E_i\): exactly two points of \(X\) in \(W_i\), one within \(\delta\) of \(o_i\) and one within \(\delta\) of \(o_i+2a\), and exactly two of \(Y\), one within \(\delta\) of \(o_i+a\) and one within \(\delta\) of \(o_i+2a+b\). On \(E_i\) each distance moves by less than \(2\delta\) from its value at the centres: \(x_1y_1,x_2y_1<a+2\delta<r_1\), \(r_1<x_2y_2<r_2\), \(x_1y_2>2a+b-2\delta>r_2\); so the edges among the four points are \(x_1y_1,x_2y_1\) in \(G_1\), and also \(x_2y_2\) in \(G_2\). The four points lie in \([o_i-\delta,o_i+2a+b+\delta]\), more than \(r_2\) from the window's ends (\(c-\delta>r_2\), \(W-c-2a-b-\delta>r_2\)), so they form a component \(Q\) of \(G_2\) and a union of components of \(G_1\) (\(y_2\) isolated there). Take a maximum matching \(M_1\) of \(G_1\) containing \(x_2y_1\), which exists since \(\{x_1,x_2,y_1\}\) is a component of \(G_1\) with matching number \(1\). For a matching \(L\) of \(G_2\) inside \(M_1\)'s leftover and each component \(Q'\) of \(G_2\), \((M_1\cup L)\cap Q'\) is a matching of \(G_2[Q']\), and \(M_1\cap Q'\) is a maximum matching of \(G_1[Q']\) (the components of \(G_1\) lie inside those of \(G_2\)), so \(|L\cap Q'|\) is at most the drop \(\nu(G_2[Q'])-\nu(G_1[Q'])\); the drops sum to \(m_1-m_2\). In \(Q\) the leftover is \(\{x_1,y_2\}\), not joined in \(G_2\), so \(|L\cap Q|=0\) against a drop of \(1\), and \(|L|\le m_1-m_2-1\): the universal form fails. Probability: \(P(E_i)=p_n\) as stated. For \(i\ne j\) the ratio \(P(E_i\cap E_j)/(P(E_i)P(E_j))\) is the square of \(\frac{(n-2)(n-3)}{n(n-1)}\big(\frac{1-2W/n}{(1-W/n)^2}\big)^{n-4}(1-W/n)^{-4}\), and \(\frac{1-2W/n}{(1-W/n)^2}=1-\frac{W^2}{(n-W)^2}\) (the reviewer's exact factor), so its logarithm is at most \(-(n-4)\frac{W^2}{(n-W)^2}+\frac{4W}{n-W}\le\frac{W}{n-W}(4-W)<0\) for \(W>4\) and \(n>2W\) (using \(-\log(1-x)\le x/(1-x)\) and \((n-4)/(n-W)\ge1\)): the window events are negatively correlated (at \(W=10\), \(0.877\) at \(n=10^3\), research/results/ultimate_matching_universal_completion_20261017/second-moment.txt). So \(Z=\sum_i1_{E_i}\) has \(\operatorname{Var}Z\le\mathbb EZ=wp_n\), and Chebyshev gives \(P(Z=0)\le1/(wp_n)\to0\).

(c). \(H\) is bipartite, so a vertex of a component with at most four vertices has at most three neighbours, all in the other sample, and every point of the other sample within \(s\) of it in both coordinates is a neighbour: it has at most three points of the other sample in its box of half-side \(s\). For a point \(z\), that box, cut to \([0,1]^2\), has area \(q\ge s^2\), and \(q=4s^2\) when \(z\) is at least \(s\) from the boundary; the \(N\) points of the other sample fall in it independently. \(P(\le3\text{ of them})\le\sum_{i\le3}\binom Niq^i(1-q)^{N-i}\le4\mu^3e^{-q(N-3)}\) for \(\mu=Nq\ge1\), and \(\mu^3e^{-\mu}\) decreases for \(\mu\ge3\), so a lower bound on \(\mu\) of at least \(3\) bounds the term. For points at least \(s\) from the boundary \(\mu=4L^2\log N\); for the others \(\mu\ge L^2\log N\), and their expected number is at most \(2N\cdot4s=8L\sqrt{N\log N}\). The expectation is at most \(2N\cdot4\mu^3N^{-4L^2(1-o(1))}+8L\sqrt{N\log N}\cdot4\mu^3N^{-L^2(1-o(1))}\): the first term is \(N^{1-4L^2+o(1)}\), the second \(N^{1/2-L^2+o(1)}\), and both tend to \(0\) when \(L>1/\sqrt2\) (the first already for \(L>1/2\)). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. (a): bipartiteness, in the parity step; finiteness. Readings of the item

(1) "Level counts at one scale" read as one level \(t\) of the condition: proved for every pair on and above the curve by thm:per-level-count-matchings (statement read this cycle), with no flow; read as the implication at one cell scale, it is (2). (2) The sufficient direction, a \(\psi_4\) load bound on a flow at one cell scale giving the matching: the recorded flow bound, lem:hopf-lax-matching-bound with Fenchel's inequality \(\nabla g\cdot\theta\le\lambda C^*(\nabla g)+\lambda C(\theta/\lambda)\), bounds the matching cost by the flow's Orlicz cost plus the grid error \(2hN\sum_j\Psi_j(\delta/h)\), \(\Psi_j(x)=\psi_4(x/s)\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\). At [C5]'s scale \(\delta\approx K(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), the item's scale, \(\delta/(hs)=K(\log N)^{1/4}/(Lh)\) and the error is \(2hN\big(N^{(K/(Lh))^4}-1\big)\) per coordinate (the reviewer's computation, checked), not of order \(N\) for any fixed \(L\): no flow on that grid gives the \((4,4)\) matching through the flow bound, whatever its tails, a failure of the method at the coarse scale. At the conjecture's own grid, side \(1/\lceil32/s\rceil\), where lem:grid-flow-duality (read this cycle) makes the cheapest flow the discrete functional of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy, a flow with \(\psi_4\) loads is that conjecture in flow form, not a new route. (3) An Orlicz version of [C5]'s Lemma 2.10 at one scale: the lemma below, which ties its counts to the electrical flow's within a window of levels. (4) The sum over dyadic scales: not reached, since (3) stops at one scale.

Setting

[C5]'s Lemma 2.10, read this cycle in the held copy (private/references), with its Lemma 2.9 and the use at (2.31)–(2.33): \(G=\{1,\dots,m\}^2\) the grid graph, \(f\) and \(h\) real flows on \(G\) with \(\operatorname{div}f=\operatorname{div}h\) and \(\|h\|_\infty\le U\); its proof writes \(c=f-h=\nabla^\perp\psi\) for a function \(\psi\) on the dual vertices, the dual edge fields \(p\), \(q\) of \(f\), \(h\) with \(D\psi=p-q\), \(a_p(x)=\sum_{e\ni x}|p(e)|\), \(B=\{x:Ma_p(x)>U\}\) (\(M\) a maximal function), the McShane extension \(\tilde\psi\) of \(\psi\) restricted to \(A=D^c\cup(D\setminus B)\), and \(g=h+\nabla^\perp\tilde\psi\); [C5] proves \(\|g\|_\infty\le LU\), \(\|g\|_1\le\|f\|_1+L\|f\|_2^2/U\) (its (2.29)) and, at (2.28), \(U^2|B|\le L\sum_e|p(e)|^2=L\|f\|_2^2\).

Lemma (interpolation locality)

Statement. The flow \(g\) of the real version of [C5]'s Lemma 2.10, as its proof builds it, agrees with \(f\) on every edge outside a set \(E_B\) of at most \(4|B|\le4L\|f\|_2^2/U^2\) edges. Hence for every \(u\ge0\), \(\big|\#\{e:|g_e|>u\}-\#\{e:|f_e|>u\}\big|\le4L\|f\|_2^2/U^2\), and for every \(\Phi\ge0\), \(\sum_e\Phi(|g_e|)\ge\sum_{e\notin E_B}\Phi(|f_e|)\). In [C5]'s setting, with probability tending to one (its (2.16) \(\|f\|_2^2\le LN\log N\) and Lemma 2.5's \(U=LNRs\) hold so), with (2.3), \(|E_B|=O(N/(K^2(\log N)^2))\) against \(|E|\) of order \(N/(K^2(\log N)^{3/2})\) edges: a fraction \(O((\log N)^{-1/2})\). The counts compare both ways inside a window and neither way above it: with the \(\psi_4\) allowance \(2|E|e^{-t}\) and \(|E_B|=o(|E|e^{-t})\) at levels \(t\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)\log\log N\), a failure of \(f\) by a factor \(1+\delta\) transfers to \(g\), and \(f\) within its allowance gives \(g\) within it up to a factor \(1+o(1)\); above the window, on \(E_B\) only \(\|g\|_\infty\le LU\) is known, and every edge with \(|f_e|>U\) lies in \(E_B\). Only the Orlicz-sum inequality is one-sided.

Proof. \(g-f=h+\nabla^\perp\tilde\psi-f=\nabla^\perp(\tilde\psi-\psi)\), since \(f-h=\nabla^\perp\psi\). [C5]'s proof of Lemma 2.9: "Since \(\tilde\psi=\psi\) away from \(B\), the gradients differ only on edges incident to \(B\). There are at most \(4|B|\) such edges." Each primal edge crosses one dual edge, and \(\nabla^\perp\) reads the dual gradient on it, so \(g_e\ne f_e\) only for the at most \(4|B|\) primal edges crossing dual edges incident to \(B\); with (2.28), \(4|B|\le4L\|f\|_2^2/U^2\). The counts: changing a flow on a set of edges moves each count by at most that set's size. The Orlicz cost: \(\Phi\ge0\), so dropping the terms of \(E_B\) lowers \(g\)'s sum, and off \(E_B\) its terms are \(f\)'s. The window: the counts of \(f\) and \(g\) above any level differ by at most \(|E_B|\), and \(|E_B|/|E|\le C(\log N)^{-1/2}\) is \(o(e^{-t})\) when \(t\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)\log\log N\), since then \(e^{-t}\ge(\log N)^{-1/2+\varepsilon}\); so a count of \(f\) above \((1+\delta)2|E|e^{-t}\) leaves \(g\)'s above \(2|E|e^{-t}\) for large \(N\), and a count of \(f\) at most \(2|E|e^{-t}\) leaves \(g\)'s at most \((1+o(1))2|E|e^{-t}\). The heavy edges: [C5]'s centered maximal function takes the supremum over \(r\ge0\), so \(Ma_p(x)\ge a_p(x)\ge|p(e)|\) for each dual edge \(e\) at \(x\), and an edge with \(|f_e|=|p(e)|>U\) has an endpoint in \(B\). The size in [C5]'s setting: \(U^2=L^2N^2R^2s^2\) with \(R=L_{LS}(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) and \(s\ge K(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) gives \(U^2\ge L^2L_{LS}^2K^2(\log N)^3\), so \(4L\|f\|_2^2/U^2\le4L\cdot LN\log N/(L^2L_{LS}^2K^2(\log N)^3)=O(N/(K^2(\log N)^2))\); \(|E|=2m(m-1)\) with \(m=\lfloor\sqrt N/(K(\log N)^{3/4})\rfloor\), of order \(N/(K^2(\log N)^{3/2})\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The construction of [C5]'s proof (the McShane extension of \(\psi\) restricted to \(A\)), in the agreement off \(E_B\); (2.28), in the size bound; \(\Phi\ge0\), in the Orlicz inequality (the first statement written asked \(\Phi\) nondecreasing, unused, dropped: more general); [C5]'s (2.3), (2.6) and (2.16), with their probability tending to one, only for the size in its setting. The class: the real flow \(g\) of Lemma 2.10 as built in its proof, for every \(f\), \(h\), \(U\); not the integral flow of (2.30), an optimal vertex of a linear program, which the proof does not tie to \(f\) edge by edge.

Degenerate cases. \(f=h\): \(c=0\) and \(\psi=0\), but the McShane extension is \(\tilde\psi(x)=\Lambda\operatorname{dist}_\infty(x,A)>0\) on \(B\), and \(B\) can be nonempty (\(a_p\le4U\) while \(Ma_p\) exceeds \(U\)), so \(g\ne f\) on the edges at \(B\): the construction is not idempotent, and \(g=f\) is guaranteed only when \(B=\emptyset\) (the first draft's "\(g=h=f\)" was false, the reviewer's correction). \(U\) small: \(E_B\) may be every edge, and the lemma says nothing, its bound exceeding \(|E|\). The integral version: not covered.

[C5]'s own (2.29), \(\|g\|_1\le\|f\|_1+L\|f\|_2^2/U\), bounds only \(g\)'s total, by Markov a count \(\|g\|_1/u\) above each \(u\), never an exponential tail; the lemma adds the comparison level by level.

An edge's current is a weighted sum of independent cell excesses, each of variance about \(2\lambda\), with weights the Green's gradient \(|\nabla G(e,Q)|\approx1/(2\pi r)\) at cell distance \(r\), so its variance is about \(2\lambda\sum_Q|\nabla G|^2\approx2\lambda\int_1^m\frac{2\pi r\,dr}{(2\pi r)^2}=\frac\lambda\pi\ln m\), with \(\ln m\approx\frac12\ln N\): a Gaussian of variance about \(\lambda\ln N/(2\pi)\); the normalized argument \(\theta/(32\lambda)\) then has standard deviation \(\sqrt{\lambda\ln N/(2\pi)}/(32\lambda)=\sqrt{1024/(2\pi L^2)}/32=1/(L\sqrt{2\pi})\), the same ratio as at [C5]'s scale with its normalization \(L\sqrt{\lambda\log N}\), so the tail above \(t^{1/4}\) is about \(e^{-\pi L^2\sqrt t}\), above the \(\psi_4\) allowance \(e^{-t}\) once \(t>\pi^2L^4\), inside \([1,\log N]\) for large \(N\). Meta. Both habits come from reading a cited result or a construction for what it is about rather than running it on the case: the lemma was "about flows on a grid", so it was taken to decide a question about flows on another grid. The change is in how a citation is used: a result is cited to decide something only after its hypotheses are written out with the instance's numbers, as AGENTS.md's order of work already asks of a cited lemma "applied through its proof as well as its statement"; the queued build makes that a row of the append's form.

The electrical flow fails above exponent two

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; the electrical flow on grids of side at most a negative power of N, with an imported Berry–Esseen bound · Position-aware exits. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: Its clause that divisible sandpiles of one reversible rule, in any number of stages, give only the electrical flow stays exact; the flow obstructions listed there are of the same kind as this cycle's, which the next review consolidates.

It must beat thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, which excludes the dyadic flow only, and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, whose hypothesis (steps with the dyadic step's square means) is not shown for the electrical flow.

Setting

As in lem:grid-flow-duality (c): \(L>0\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), a grid of \(k\times k\) square cells of side \(\delta=1/k\) (the reduction's grids have \(\delta\le s/32\) and \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\); the theorem asks only \(\delta\le N^{-\varepsilon}\) and \(N\delta^2\ge1\)); \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform, \(n_Q\) the count of cell \(Q\), \(\bar n=N\delta^2\). The electrical flow \(\theta\) is the least-squares edge flow on the cell graph (unit conductances) with outflow \(n_Q-\bar n\) at each cell: with \(B\) the cell–edge incidence matrix, \(\Delta=BB^{\mathsf T}\) the free-boundary grid Laplacian, \(b_e\) the column of edge \(e\) and \(w_e=\Delta^+b_e\), \(\theta_e=b_e^{\mathsf T}\Delta^+(n-\bar n\mathbf 1)=\sum_Qw_e(Q)\,n_Q\), since \(\Delta^+\) maps into the mean-zero vectors. For a coordinate \(j\), \(\lambda'>0\) and \(\alpha_j\in(2,\infty]\), its coordinate-\(j\) flow-bound value is \(V_j=\lambda'\delta^2\sum_{e:\,d(e)=j}\psi_{\alpha_j}\big(|\theta_e|/(\delta\lambda's)\big)\), \(d(e)\) the coordinate of the flux edge \(e\) carries.

Theorem (electrical flow obstruction)

Statement. For every \(L>0\), \(K'\ge1\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12]\), coordinate \(j\) with \(\alpha_j\in(2,\infty]\), or with \(\alpha_j=2\) when \(L<\sqrt\varepsilon/(\pi^2K')\), every grid of side \(\delta=1/k\) with \(\delta\le N^{-\varepsilon}\) and \(N\delta^2\ge1\) (the grids above among them, for every \(\varepsilon<\frac12\) and large \(N\)), every \(\lambda'\in[N/K',K'N]\), and every \(C>0\), there is \(c=c(C,L,K',\varepsilon,\alpha_j)>0\) with \(P(V_j>CN)\ge c\) for all large \(N\) (logarithms natural). So the electrical flow's flow-bound value is not \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one, at every pair of the curve (each has an exponent above \(2\)); the same holds for the net flow of every finite sequence of divisible-sandpile stages with equal splitting on the cell graph carrying the counts to \(\bar n\), which is this flow by lem:idle-slack-sandpile (a) and lem:balanced-sandpile-flow.

Proof. The current as an i.i.d. sum. \(\theta_e=\sum_{i\le N}g_e(X_i)\) with \(g_e(x)=w_e(Q(x))\), i.i.d. terms with \(\mathbb Eg_e=\delta^2\sum_Qw_e(Q)=0\) and \(\mathbb Eg_e^2=\delta^2M_e\), \(M_e=\|w_e\|^2\). Since \(w_e(Q)=b_e^{\mathsf T}\Delta^+(\mathbf 1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf 1)\) is the current on \(e\) of the electrical flow with outflow \(\mathbf 1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf 1\), a potential flow, hence acyclic, it decomposes into paths of total mass \(1-k^{-2}\), so \(|w_e(Q)|\le1\) and \(\mathbb E|g_e|^3\le\delta^2M_e\).

The spectral sum. The free-boundary Laplacian of the path on \(k\) vertices has the unit eigenvectors \(u_a(i)=c_a\cos(\pi a(i-\frac12)/k)\), \(c_0^2=1/k\), \(c_a^2=2/k\), eigenvalues \(4\sin^2\alpha_a\), \(\alpha_a=\pi a/(2k)\), \(a=0,\dots,k-1\); the grid's are \(\varphi_{ab}=u_a\otimes u_b\) with \(\mu_{ab}=4\sin^2\alpha_a+4\sin^2\alpha_b\). For a horizontal edge \(e\) between \((i,j)\) and \((i+1,j)\) (coordinate \(1\); coordinate \(2\) is symmetric), \(b_e\perp\mathbf 1\) and \(M_e=\sum_{(a,b)\ne(0,0)}(b_e\cdot\varphi_{ab})^2/\mu_{ab}^2\), \(b_e\cdot\varphi_{ab}=(u_a(i+1)-u_a(i))u_b(j)=-2c_a\sin(\pi ai/k)\sin\alpha_a\,u_b(j)\). Mean. Summed over the \(k(k-1)\) horizontal edges, \((b_e\cdot\varphi_{ab})^2\) gives the horizontal energy of \(\varphi_{ab}\), \(4\sin^2\alpha_a\), so \(\sum_eM_e=\sum_{(a,b)\ne0}\sin^2\alpha_a/(4(\sin^2\alpha_a+\sin^2\alpha_b)^2)\). With \(\sin x\ge2x/\pi\) on \([0,\pi/2]\) and \(\sin x\le x\), each term with \(a\ge1\) is at least \(\alpha_a^2/(\pi^2(\alpha_a^2+\alpha_b^2)^2)=\frac{4k^2}{\pi^4}\frac{a^2}{(a^2+b^2)^2}\), at least \(\frac{4k^2}{\pi^4}\frac1{4a^2}\) when \(1\le b\le a\); summing over \(1\le b\le a\le k-1\), \(\sum_eM_e\ge\frac{k^2}{\pi^4}H_{k-1}\), so the mean \(\bar M\) over the horizontal edges is at least \(H_{k-1}/\pi^4\ge\ln k/\pi^4\). Maximum. \((b_e\cdot\varphi_{ab})^2\le4c_a^2c_b^2\sin^2\alpha_a\le\frac{16}{k^2}\sin^2\alpha_a\), zero for \(a=0\); with \(\sin^2\alpha_a+\sin^2\alpha_b\ge\frac4{\pi^2}(\alpha_a^2+\alpha_b^2)\) each term is at most \(\frac{\pi^2}4\frac{a^2}{(a^2+b^2)^2}\); for fixed \(a\ge1\) the \(b=0\) term is \(\frac{\pi^2}{4a^2}\) and, \(y\mapsto a^2/(a^2+y^2)^2\) decreasing, the rest at most \(\frac{\pi^2}4\int_0^\infty\frac{a^2\,dy}{(a^2+y^2)^2}=\frac{\pi^3}{16a}\); so \(M_e\le\frac{\pi^4}{24}+\frac{\pi^3}{16}H_{k-1}\le\frac{\pi^3}{16}\ln k+6.0=:U\). Good edges. Let \(G\) be the horizontal edges with \(M_e\ge\bar M/2\); from \(\sum M_e\le|G|U+(k(k-1)-|G|)\bar M/2\), \(|G|\ge k(k-1)\bar M/(2U)\ge k(k-1)\frac{\ln k/\pi^4}{2(\frac{\pi^3}{16}\ln k+6)}=k(k-1)p_k\), \(p_k\to8/\pi^7\), and every \(e\in G\) has \(M_e\ge\ln k/(2\pi^4)\).

One edge's tail. Let \(a_e=\theta_e/(\delta\lambda's)\), of standard deviation \(\sigma_e=\sqrt{\bar nM_e}/(\delta\lambda's)=N\sqrt{M_e}/(\lambda'L\sqrt{\log N})\ge\sqrt{M_e}/(K'L\sqrt{\log N})\). From \(k\ge N^\varepsilon\), \(\ln k\ge\varepsilon\ln N\), so on \(G\), \(\sigma_e\ge\sigma_\varepsilon:=\sqrt{\varepsilon/(2\pi^4)}/(K'L)\); on the grids above, \(k\ge32/s\) gives \(\ln k\ge\frac12\ln N-\frac12\ln\ln N+\ln(32/L)\), so there \(\liminf\) of the bound is \(1/(2\pi^2K'L)\), the case \(\varepsilon\to\frac12\). The Berry–Esseen theorem for i.i.d. sums (imported: \(\sup_x|P(\sum g_e(X_i)>x\sigma\sqrt N)-\bar\Phi(x)|\le C_0\mathbb E|g|^3/(\sigma^3\sqrt N)\) with an absolute \(C_0\), \(\sigma^2=\mathbb Eg^2\)) gives, with \(\mathbb E|g_e|^3/((\mathbb Eg_e^2)^{3/2}\sqrt N)\le1/\sqrt{\bar nM_e}\le\big(\varepsilon\ln N/(2\pi^4)\big)^{-1/2}=:\eta_N\to0\) (using \(\bar n\ge1\)), for every \(u>0\) and \(e\in G\): \(P(|a_e|>u)\ge2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_e)-2C_0\eta_N\ge2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_\varepsilon)-2C_0\eta_N\).

A bounded fraction with bounded probability. Let \(F=|\{e\in G:|a_e|>u\}|/|G|\in[0,1]\) and \(q_N=2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_\varepsilon)-2C_0\eta_N\le\mathbb EF\). Since \(\mathbb EF\le P(F\ge x)+x\) for \(x\in[0,1]\), \(P(F\ge q_N/2)\ge q_N/2\). On that event, \(\psi_{\alpha_j}\) being nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\), \(V_j\ge\lambda'\delta^2|G|\frac{q_N}2\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\ge\frac N{K'}\,\delta^2k(k-1)\,p_k\,\frac{q_N}2\,\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\), with \(\delta^2k(k-1)=1-\delta\to1\). As \(N\to\infty\), \(q_N\to q(u)=2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_\varepsilon)>0\) and \(p_k\to8/\pi^7\). Choice of \(u\). For \(\alpha_j\in(2,\infty)\): \(\bar\Phi(x)\ge\frac{x}{1+x^2}\frac{e^{-x^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\), so \(q(u)\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\ge c'u^{-1}e^{-u^2/(2\sigma_\varepsilon^2)}(e^{u^{\alpha_j}}-1)\to\infty\) as \(u\to\infty\), since \(\alpha_j>2\); for \(\alpha_j=2\) the same bound is \(c'u^{-1}e^{u^2(1-1/(2\sigma_\varepsilon^2))}(1-e^{-u^2})\), which tends to infinity exactly when \(1/(2\sigma_\varepsilon^2)=\pi^4K'^2L^2/\varepsilon<1\), that is \(L<\sqrt\varepsilon/(\pi^2K')\); take \(u\) with \(\frac{4}{\pi^7K'}q(u)\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)>4C\); then for large \(N\), \(V_j>CN\) on an event of probability at least \(q(u)/4=:c\). For \(\alpha_j=\infty\), \(\psi_\infty(u)=N(u-1)_+\): at \(u=2\), \(V_j\ge\frac{N}{K'}\cdot\frac{8}{\pi^7}\cdot\frac{q(2)}{4}\cdot N(1-o(1))\), above \(CN\) for large \(N\), with probability at least \(q(2)/4\). The sandpile clause: lem:idle-slack-sandpile (a), "the net flow of every finite sequence of divisible-sandpile stages with this one rule ... carrying eta to eta', is the electrical flow from eta to eta' with conductances c", and lem:balanced-sandpile-flow, "With equal splitting on the grid of cells and uniform thresholds, the sandpile odometer flow is the electrical flow": equal splitting has \(c(x,y)=\pi(x)/\deg x\), constant, so the conductances are the unit ones above. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(\alpha_j>2\): in the choice of \(u\), where the Gaussian tail must lose to \(e^{u^{\alpha_j}}\). At \(\alpha_j=2\), per case: for \(L<\sqrt\varepsilon/(\pi^2K')\) the same step works, and the statement covers it (more general, off the reduction's \(L\ge128\)); for \(L\ge\sqrt\varepsilon/(\pi^2K')\), the reduction's \(L\) among them, the product stays bounded or tends to \(0\) and the argument gives nothing (the first correction stated only this case, for every \(L\), which the widening to free \(L\) made false). \(\lambda'\le K'N\): in \(\sigma_e\)'s lower bound; \(\lambda'\ge N/K'\): in the prefactor of \(V_j\). \(\delta\le N^{-\varepsilon}\): only through \(\ln k\ge\varepsilon\ln N\), which keeps \(\sigma_e\) bounded below (the first draft asked \(\delta\le s/32\) and \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\), the grids of lem:grid-flow-duality (c); both widened at the reviewer's remark, more general, those grids still covered). \(N\delta^2\ge1\): only in \(\eta_N\to0\), with \(M_e\to\infty\). Independence of the \(X_i\): in Berry–Esseen; their being identically uniform: in \(\mathbb Eg_e=0\); the evenly spread \(Y\) enters only as the target \(\bar n\) per cell. The class: the electrical flow of the cell counts on every such grid, and the sandpile sequences named; a statement with probability bounded below, weaker than the probability tending to one of thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, and enough, since the flow route needs success with probability tending to one.

Degenerate cases. \(k=1\): no edge, \(V_j=0\); excluded for large \(N\) since \(k\ge N^\varepsilon\to\infty\). \(\alpha_j=2\): covered only for \(L<\sqrt\varepsilon/(\pi^2K')\) (see Hypotheses). \(N\) small: the statement is asymptotic; the Berry–Esseen error \(2C_0\eta_N\) must fall below \(q(u)\), which at the instance below, \(q(u)\approx e^{-2.95\cdot10^{15}}\), needs \(\bar nM_e\) beyond \(e^{5.9\cdot10^{15}}\).

Nonvacuity. Ninth review: a linear-flow lemma by hand

17 October 2026 · Goal-level route review, reviewed in two stages; no statement registered · Ninth route review. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Six research entries since the eighth review: two on two-choice-routing (adapted partitions, split-matched transports), two on local-completion-hall (local completion masking, universal completion), and two on position-aware-exits (interpolation locality, electrical flow). The period proves that hierarchical rank-cut transports fail above exponent \(2\), that per-level completion glues only in its universal form, which fails on random lines, and that the electrical flow, and every equal-splitting sandpile sequence, fails the flow route at every pair of the curve.

Open statements. ultimate-matching (the full target) and conjugate-class-discrepancy (sufficient) open; shor-exponential and grid-discrepancy open and untouched in the period. The line's open-item count is \(4\), as at the review twelve research entries back, so this review is goal-level.

The line's general claim. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy on the curve in its discrete form: by lem:grid-flow-duality (c) the discrete \(X\)-term class bound on grids with \(\delta\le s/32\) and \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\) gives the conclusion of cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction, and by its (d) the class supremum is the minimal edge flow cost.

What the goal needs. That discrete bound at every pair of the curve, or a matching built directly; equivalently a flow carrying the cell counts to the background at flow-bound cost of order \(N\), with one universal \(L\).

The six entries

Adapted partitions (thm:adapted-partition-obstruction): matchings following an equal-count hierarchical partition fail above exponent \(2\). Split-matched transports (thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction): so do transports cutting through a ranked point with targets steered within \(A/\sqrt{n_C}\) of the count split, which covers steering up to \(n^{3/4}\) points per cut. Local completion masking (thm:local-completion-dichotomy): per-level Hall conditions with completion do not glue at constant \(C>1\), at \(C=1\) or in the cover form; completion for every maximum matching glues. Universal completion (thm:universal-completion-criterion): that form holds iff every pair of co-bases spans the deficiency drop one level up, and fails on random lines between any two radii; at the goal's box scale components of at most four vertices are absent. Interpolation locality (lem:interpolation-locality): [C5]'s interpolated flow agrees with the electrical flow off a vanishing fraction of edges; the entry's reading (2), not a registered statement, computes that at [C5]'s cell scale the flow bound's grid error alone is \(2hN(N^{(K/(Lh))^4}-1)\) per coordinate, so no flow on that grid serves the route through the flow bound. Electrical flow (thm:electrical-flow-obstruction): the electrical flow's flow-bound value exceeds every \(CN\) with probability bounded below, on every grid of side at most \(N^{-\varepsilon}\).

Falsification attempt. Does the electrical obstruction reach the cheapest flow? Write a flow rule linear in the counts as \(\theta=W\rho\), \(\rho_Q=n_Q-\bar n\), with \(\operatorname{div}W\rho=\rho\) for every mean-zero \(\rho\), and \(W_e(Q)=(W(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1))_e\). Then \(\theta_e=\sum_iW_e(Q(X_i))\), an i.i.d. sum of mean zero, as in the electrical proof. Each column \(W(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1)\) is a unit flow from \(Q\) to the uniform sink, so by Thomson's principle its energy is at least the electrical one, and \(\sum_e\|W_e\|^2\ge\sum_e\|w_e\|^2\ge2k(k-1)\ln k/\pi^4\) by thm:electrical-flow-obstruction's spectral sum. Two steps of that proof change. The Berry–Esseen ratio needs no kernel bound: \(\max_Q|W_e(Q)|\le\|W_e\|_2\), so \(\mathbb E|g|^3/(\sigma^3\sqrt N)\le\|W_e\|\delta^2\|W_e\|^2/(\delta^3\|W_e\|^3\sqrt N)=1/\sqrt{\bar n}\to0\) on the reduction's grids. And the good-edge count is replaced by weights: in a coordinate \(j\) whose edges carry at least half the total, let \(E'\) be its edges with \(\|W_e\|^2\ge\ln k/(2\pi^4)\), which carry at least \(k(k-1)\ln k/(2\pi^4)\) of it; with \(r_e=\sigma_e^2/\sigma_*^2\ge1\) and thresholds \(u_e=u\sqrt{r_e}\), every \(e\in E'\) has \(P(|a_e|>u_e)\ge2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_*)-2C_0/\sqrt{\bar n}=:q\), and \(\psi_\alpha(u\sqrt r)\ge r\,\psi_\alpha(u)\) for \(r\ge1\) and finite \(\alpha\ge2\); the weighted fraction \(\sum_{E'}\psi(u_e)\mathbf1\{|a_e|>u_e\}/\sum_{E'}\psi(u_e)\le1\) has mean at least \(q\), so with probability at least \(q/2\) the cost is at least \(\lambda'\delta^2\frac q2\psi_\alpha(u)\sum_{E'}r_e\ge\frac q2\psi_\alpha(u)\lambda'\delta^2k(k-1)\), which exceeds \(CN\) for \(u\) large when \(\alpha_j>2\), as in the electrical proof. So, by hand, checked step by step by the stage-two reviewer, and not registered: for every linear rule \(W\) fixed before the points are drawn and defined on every mean-zero \(\rho\), on grids of side at most \(N^{-\varepsilon}\) with \(\bar n\to\infty\), the flow-bound value exceeds every \(CN\) with probability bounded below, at every pair of the curve whose exponents both exceed \(2\) (the coordinate carrying the energy is the rule's choice, so at the endpoints \((2,\infty)\) and \((\infty,2)\) a rule may put it on the exponent-\(2\) side, and the argument gives nothing there). The attempt therefore does not falsify the line; it gives a conditional: if some flow has flow-bound value \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one at such a pair, no linear rule attains it, and in particular the \(\psi_4\)-minimal flow is then not given by a linear rule. The blind stage proposed the same lemma independently (below).

Assessment of this line. The period closed two more classes on the primal side, hierarchical rank-cut transports and the electrical flow with the sandpiles that carry it, and the falsification attempt extends the second, by hand and not registered, to every linear rule at pairs with both exponents above \(2\), with probability bounded below; on the dual side it supplied no new bound, and the gluing question of local-completion-hall ended in a criterion that decides nothing at the goal's levels. The evidence now points to one property a cheap flow must have, nonlinearity in the counts together with corrections across scales (the eighth review's restoring drift), and every construction the record has built lacks it. The line is not refuted, and its core statement keeps its evidence: the forced order (lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound), the class lower bounds, the partial dual bounds.

Obstacle

On the primal side the line is stuck at a mechanism no construction has: a flow nonlinear in the counts whose fine levels correct the coarse ones, so that the per-edge loads have tails lighter than the Gaussian tails that, by the falsification attempt's unregistered hand derivation, every linear rule produces at pairs with both exponents above \(2\), across the boundaries of fine dyadic squares (the eighth review's boundary identity). On the dual side it is stuck where the seventh review put it: class functions with gradients over many levels, chains longer than \(e^{\lambda\sqrt{\log N}}\) in the strict both-high instance.

Across the goal

  • ultimate-matching (the full target): unchanged since the eighth review, the last goal-level one; six cycles through its sufficient statement's primal side and the gluing question, none on it directly.
  • conjugate-class-discrepancy: unchanged; four cycles on its primal form and two on the gluing route to its matching; its primal side is restricted, by the registered obstructions, to flows other than the electrical, dyadic, square-mean and rank-cut ones, and, by the review's unregistered hand derivation, to flows nonlinear in the counts at pairs with both exponents above \(2\).
  • shor-exponential: unchanged; no cycle.
  • grid-discrepancy: unchanged; no cycle.

record-audit lists no open gap that no later entry took up ("0 open gaps no later entry links").

Architecture review

Necessary target. The weakest endpoint: at every pair of the curve, with probability tending to one, one matching with \(\sum_i\exp[(|X^j_i-Y^j_{\pi(i)}|/s)^{\alpha_j}]\le2N\) for both \(j\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L\) universal; evenly spread \(Y\) suffice by lem:two-sample-matching-transfer. Downstream. Linear flow rules fail when both exponents exceed two

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; flow rules linear in the counts, both exponents finite, with an imported Berry–Esseen bound · Position-aware exits. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. The ninth review's Decision: prove, lemma-first, its falsification attempt's extension of thm:electrical-flow-obstruction to every flow linear in the counts.

Chosen. position-aware-exits, not the head local-completion-hall, because the review's Decision names this lemma as the next entry on that item (its electrical-flow route generalized), bearing on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy in its flow form.

Best outcome. At the goal's own parameters, every pair of the curve with both exponents above \(2\), it excludes every linear transport rule from the flow route, so a flow of flow-bound value \(O(N)\), if one exists there, is not given by a linear rule; it decides nothing about the cheapest flow. It must beat thm:electrical-flow-obstruction, which excludes one linear rule.

Target form. The goal's flow form: a flow on the grid of lem:grid-flow-duality (c) with flow-bound value \(\lambda'\delta^2\sum_e\Psi_{d(e)}(|\theta_e|/(\delta\lambda'))\), \(\Psi_j=\psi_{\alpha_j}(\cdot/s)\), of order \(N\) with probability tending to one.

Architecture test. Not decided. The ninth review's retained test (the gap-charged bound for nested chains, outcomes (A), (B), (C)) did not occur: none of its outcomes was reached, since this entry proves the lemma that review's Decision put first, and the test's cycle, the dual side on mixed-level-counts, is scheduled after it, behind the user's pick restoring-drift-construction.

Owed attempt. The electrical flow entry named the exit matching's distance from the transport of thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction; it is not made here, and another attempt came first because of the mathematics: the linear lemma decides a whole class, every linear rule, in a few lines from recorded results (the electrical spectral sum, Thomson's principle), and so fixes which of the item's routes remain before the narrower exit question, which needs the split-matched proof's tolerance read, is spent on; it stays the item's next attempt. The item's earlier entries: the interpolation locality entry, read, whose Follow-up asked to "prove that the electrical flow of the cell excesses fails", which the electrical entry did and this one extends; and the electrical entry above.

Review. The stand-in review of the previous checkpoint raised five objections. (1) A Smallest case miscounted (eight points staying, written as five) answered with "no check for that is built": right; nothing mechanical catches a miscount of a construction's objects, and the prevention is the Spin self-review step of PROMPTS.md committed in that turn (commit "PROMPTS.md: constructions are run on a numeric instance before they are described"), which asks every object's fate set down; no check is in force. (2) "Its first slip this session, so no check is added yet", for a clause left after a widening: right that the reply named no change; the same commit's step asks that "a widened hypothesis is followed by a reread of every clause that used the narrower one", which the reply should have named. (3) A Meta citing a rule written in the same turn as the slip: right that the rule did not stop the slip; that commit was the change, and the third pass found the slip in a sentence written before it. (4) The guard fix's Meta reusing an earlier commit: right; this entry's Meta paragraph answers it below. (5) The electrical theorem's spectral bounds called checked numerically at \(k=8\) to \(128\): wrong about the status (the bounds are proved for every \(k\) by the spectral sum in the entry's proof, the numerical check being a control), right that the reply's sentence read as if the check carried them.

Setting

As in thm:electrical-flow-obstruction: \(L>0\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), logarithms natural, a \(k\times k\) grid of cells of side \(\delta=1/k\), \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform, counts \(n_Q\), \(\bar n=N\delta^2\), \(\rho_Q=n_Q-\bar n\); \(V\) the mean-zero vectors on the cells. A linear flow rule is a linear map \(W\) from \(V\) to edge flows with \(\operatorname{div}W\rho=\rho\) for every \(\rho\in V\), fixed before the points are drawn; its flow is \(\theta=W\rho\), and \(W_e(Q)=(W(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1))_e\). The coordinate-\(j\) flow-bound value is \(V_j=\lambda'\delta^2\sum_{e:\,d(e)=j}\psi_{\alpha_j}(|\theta_e|/(\delta\lambda's))\).

Theorem (linear flow obstruction)

Statement. For every \(L>0\), \(K'\ge1\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,\frac12)\), exponents \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in(2,\infty)\), grids with \(\delta\le N^{-\varepsilon}\) and \(N\delta^2\to\infty\) (the reduction's grids among them), \(\lambda'\in[N/K',K'N]\), every linear flow rule \(W\) (which may depend on \(N\) and the grid) and every \(C>0\), there is \(c=c(C,L,K',\varepsilon,\alpha_1,\alpha_2)>0\) with \(P(V_1+V_2>CN)\ge c\) for all \(N\) beyond a threshold depending only on the grid sequence and these constants, both \(c\) and the threshold uniform in \(W\). So no linear flow rule has flow-bound value \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one at any pair of the curve other than its endpoints; the electrical flow, the equal-splitting sandpile sequences, every rule adding to the electrical flow a circulation linear in the counts, and, on grids with \(k\) a power of two and dyadic depth at least \(\log_2k\), the dyadic flow written as grid fluxes (linear in the count excesses by lem:sequential-rules-dyadic (a); its finer squares' tent fields vanish on their own boundaries, so only those levels carry flux across cell edges) are among them.

Proof. The current as an i.i.d. sum. Since \(\sum_Q\rho_Q=0\), \(W\rho=\sum_Q\rho_QW(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1)\), so \(\theta_e=\sum_QW_e(Q)n_Q-\bar n\sum_QW_e(Q)\); and \(\sum_QW_e(Q)=(W(\sum_Q(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1)))_e=(W0)_e=0\). Hence \(\theta_e=\sum_{i\le N}g_e(X_i)\), \(g_e(x)=W_e(Q(x))\), i.i.d. with \(\mathbb Eg_e=\delta^2\sum_QW_e(Q)=0\) and \(\mathbb Eg_e^2=\delta^2M_e\), \(M_e=\|W_e\|^2=\sum_QW_e(Q)^2\). Energy. Each column \(W(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1)\) is a flow with outflow \(\mathbf1_Q-k^{-2}\mathbf1\); by Thomson's principle its energy \(\sum_eW_e(Q)^2\) is at least that of the electrical flow with that outflow, \(\sum_ew_e(Q)^2\), \(w_e=\Delta^+b_e\). Summing over \(Q\), \(\sum_eM_e\ge\sum_e\|w_e\|^2\ge2k(k-1)\ln k/\pi^4\), by thm:electrical-flow-obstruction's spectral sum (its mean bound \(H_{k-1}/\pi^4\ge\ln k/\pi^4\) over the \(k(k-1)\) edges of each coordinate). Fix a coordinate \(j\) whose edges carry at least half: \(\sum_{d(e)=j}M_e\ge k(k-1)\ln k/\pi^4\); its edges with \(M_e<\tau:=\ln k/(2\pi^4)\) carry less than \(k(k-1)\tau\), so \(E'=\{e:d(e)=j,\,M_e\ge\tau\}\) has \(\sum_{E'}M_e\ge k(k-1)\tau\). One edge's tail. \(a_e=\theta_e/(\delta\lambda's)\) has standard deviation \(\sigma_e=\sqrt{\bar nM_e}/(\delta\lambda's)=N\sqrt{M_e}/(\lambda'L\sqrt{\ln N})\); put \(\sigma_*=N\sqrt\tau/(\lambda'L\sqrt{\ln N})\ge\sqrt{\tau}/(K'L\sqrt{\ln N})\ge\sigma_\varepsilon:=\sqrt{\varepsilon/(2\pi^4)}/(K'L)\), using \(\ln k\ge\varepsilon\ln N\), and \(r_e=\sigma_e^2/\sigma_*^2=M_e/\tau\ge1\) on \(E'\). Since \(\max_Q|W_e(Q)|\le\|W_e\|\), \(\mathbb E|g_e|^3\le\|W_e\|\delta^2M_e\), and the Berry–Esseen ratio is \(\mathbb E|g_e|^3/((\mathbb Eg_e^2)^{3/2}\sqrt N)\le1/(\delta\sqrt N)=1/\sqrt{\bar n}\), whatever \(W\); so by the Berry–Esseen theorem (imported: \(\sup_x|P(\sum g(X_i)>x\sigma\sqrt N)-\bar\Phi(x)|\le C_0\mathbb E|g|^3/(\sigma^3\sqrt N)\), \(C_0\) absolute), with \(u_e=u\sqrt{r_e}\), \(P(|a_e|>u_e)=P(|a_e|>(u/\sigma_*)\sigma_e)\ge2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_*)-2C_0/\sqrt{\bar n}\ge q_N:=2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_\varepsilon)-2C_0/\sqrt{\bar n}\) for every \(e\in E'\). Weights. For \(r\ge1\) and \(\alpha\ge2\), \(\psi_\alpha(u\sqrt r)=e^{u^\alpha r^{\alpha/2}}-1\ge e^{u^\alpha r}-1\ge r(e^{u^\alpha}-1)=r\psi_\alpha(u)\), the last by convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{x}-1\) through \(0\). Let \(F=\sum_{E'}\psi_{\alpha_j}(u_e)\mathbf1\{|a_e|>u_e\}/\sum_{E'}\psi_{\alpha_j}(u_e)\in[0,1]\); \(\mathbb EF\ge q_N\), and \(\mathbb EF\le P(F\ge x)+x\) for \(x\in[0,1]\), so \(P(F\ge q_N/2)\ge q_N/2\). On that event \(V_j\ge\lambda'\delta^2\frac{q_N}2\sum_{E'}\psi_{\alpha_j}(u_e)\ge\lambda'\delta^2\frac{q_N}2\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\sum_{E'}r_e\ge\frac N{K'}\delta^2k(k-1)\frac{q_N}2\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\), as \(\sum_{E'}r_e=\sum_{E'}M_e/\tau\ge k(k-1)\). Choice of \(u\). As \(N\to\infty\), \(q_N\to q(u)=2\bar\Phi(u/\sigma_\varepsilon)\) and \(\delta^2k(k-1)=1-\delta\to1\); \(\bar\Phi(x)\ge\frac{x}{1+x^2}\frac{e^{-x^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\) gives \(q(u)\psi_{\alpha}(u)\ge c'u^{-1}e^{-u^2/(2\sigma_\varepsilon^2)}(e^{u^\alpha}-1)\to\infty\) for \(\alpha>2\); with \(\alpha_{\min}=\min(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)\), take \(u\ge1\) with \(\frac1{K'}q(u)\psi_{\alpha_{\min}}(u)>8C\) (both \(\psi_{\alpha_j}(u)\ge\psi_{\alpha_{\min}}(u)\) for \(u\ge1\)), so \(u\) and \(c=q(u)/4\) depend on \(C,L,K',\varepsilon,\alpha_1,\alpha_2\) and not on \(W\) or \(j\); then for large \(N\), \(V_1+V_2\ge V_j>CN\) with probability at least \(c\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Linearity of \(W\) on \(V\) with \(\operatorname{div}W\rho=\rho\): in the i.i.d. form and in Thomson's principle per column. \(W\) fixed before the points: in the independence of the \(g_e(X_i)\). A paired restoring drift amplifies tails

17 October 2026 · Two working proofs and a finite check, reviewed; the construction's prediction failed at J = 6, 7 · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Lemma (restoring drift tail)

Statement. Let \(\alpha\ge1\), \(\kappa>0\), \(\sigma>0\), \(d\) with \(d(r)\) between \(0\) and \(r\) and \(|d(r)|\ge\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) (for instance \(d(r)=\operatorname{sign}(r)\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\)), and \(R_{n+1}=R_n-d(R_n)+\xi_{n+1}\) adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_n)\), \(R_0=0\), with \(\mathbb E[e^{t\xi_{n+1}}\mid\mathcal F_n]\le e^{\sigma^2t^2/2}\) for every real \(t\). Then for every \(n\ge1\) and \(u>0\): (a) \(P(|R_n|\ge u)\le2e^{-u^2/(2n\sigma^2)}\); (b) \(P(|R_n|\ge u)\le2n\exp\big(-\min(\kappa(u/2)^\alpha,(u/2)^2/2)/\sigma^2\big)\). In particular, with \(n\sigma^2=s^2\) fixed and \(\kappa=c\sigma^2\ln n\), \(n\ge2\): for \(u\) with \(c(u/2)^\alpha\ge2\) and \(c\ln n\,(u/2)^{\alpha-2}\le n/(2s^2)\), (b) gives \(P(|R_n|\ge u)\le2\exp(-\frac c2\ln n\,(u/2)^\alpha)\), a \(\psi_\alpha\)-type tail with constants independent of \(n\) on a window of \(u\) that grows like \((n/\ln n)^{1/(\alpha-2)}\) for \(\alpha>2\).

Proof. (a) With \(y=R_n-d(R_n)\), \(|y|\le|R_n|\) (\(d(r)\) lies between \(0\) and \(r\)), and \(\mathbb E[\cosh(t(y+\xi_{n+1}))\mid\mathcal F_n]=\frac12(e^{ty}\mathbb Ee^{t\xi}+e^{-ty}\mathbb Ee^{-t\xi})\le\cosh(ty)e^{\sigma^2t^2/2}\le\cosh(tR_n)e^{\sigma^2t^2/2}\); by induction \(\mathbb E\cosh(tR_n)\le e^{n\sigma^2t^2/2}\), and \(P(|R_n|\ge u)\le\mathbb E\cosh(tR_n)/\cosh(tu)\le2e^{n\sigma^2t^2/2-tu}\), at \(t=u/(n\sigma^2)\) the bound. (b) Put \(a=u/2\), \(\mu=\min(\kappa a^{\alpha-1},a/2)\), \(\theta=2\mu/\sigma^2\). For \(r\ge a\), \(d(r)\ge\min(\kappa r^{\alpha-1},r)\ge\min(\kappa a^{\alpha-1},a)\ge\mu\) (\(\alpha\ge1\)). Hence on \(\{R_k\ge a\}\), \(\mathbb E[e^{\theta R_{k+1}}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le e^{\theta R_k-\theta\mu+\theta^2\sigma^2/2}=e^{\theta R_k}\); on \(\{R_k<a\}\), \(R_k-d(R_k)<a\) (it lies between \(0\) and \(R_k\)), so \(\mathbb E[e^{\theta R_{k+1}}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le e^{\theta a+\theta^2\sigma^2/2}\). Last exit: since \(R_0=0<a\), on \(\{R_n\ge u\}\) there is a last \(m<n\) with \(R_m<a\), and then \(R_k\ge a\) for \(m<k\le n\). For fixed \(m\) put \(Z_k=e^{\theta R_k}\prod_{m<i<k}\mathbf 1\{R_i\ge a\}\) for \(k>m\); then \(\mathbb E[Z_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le Z_k\mathbf 1\{R_k\ge a\}\le Z_k\), so \(\mathbb E[Z_n\mathbf 1\{R_m<a\}]\le\mathbb E[Z_{m+1}\mathbf 1\{R_m<a\}]\le e^{\theta a+\theta^2\sigma^2/2}\), while \(Z_n\ge e^{\theta u}\) on the event of that \(m\). Summing over \(m\), \(P(R_n\ge u)\le n\,e^{-\theta(u-a)+\theta^2\sigma^2/2}=n\,e^{-(2\mu/\sigma^2)(a-\mu)}\le n\,e^{-\mu a/\sigma^2}\), since \(\mu\le a/2\); and \(\mu a=\min(\kappa a^\alpha,a^2/2)\). The lower tail is the same for \(-R_n\), which follows the same recursion with \(\tilde d(r)=-d(-r)\), again between \(0\) and \(r\) with the same size bound, and \(-\xi\), with the same conditional bound. For the particular case: the condition \(c\ln n\,a^{\alpha-2}\le n/(2s^2)\) is \(\kappa a^\alpha\le a^2/2\), so the minimum is \(\kappa a^\alpha\) and \(2n\,e^{-c\ln n\,a^\alpha}=2e^{\ln n(1-ca^\alpha)}\le2e^{-\frac c2\ln n\,a^\alpha}\) when \(ca^\alpha\ge2\). \(\square\)

Lemma (sibling exchange leg)

Statement. Let \(B\) be a closed rectangle and \(\Gamma\subset\partial B\) a segment of its top side, of length \(\ell\), and let \(w\) be a piecewise continuously differentiable vector field near \(B\) with continuous normal components across its pieces' boundaries, \(\operatorname{div}w=0\) on each piece, and \(w\cdot n=0\) on \(\partial B\setminus\Gamma\). Then \(\int_Bw_1=\int_\Gamma(x-c)\,w_2\,dx\) for every real \(c\), so \(|\int_Bw_1|\le\frac\ell2\int_\Gamma|w_2|\,dx\). In particular, a divergence-free correction on two stacked squares of side \(\rho\) with zero normal flux on their outer boundary, which shifts the lower square's horizontal mean by \(m\) (\(\int_Bw_1=m\rho^2\)), has \(\frac1\rho\int_\Gamma|w_2|\ge2|m|\) on their shared side \(\Gamma\): its vertical leg is on average at least twice the shift. The same with the coordinates exchanged.

Proof. \(\operatorname{div}(x\,w)=w_1+x\operatorname{div}w=w_1\) on each piece, and the continuity of the normal components lets the divergence theorem be summed over the pieces: \(\int_Bw_1=\int_{\partial B}x\,w\cdot n=\int_\Gamma x\,w_2\,dx\), the outward normal on \(\Gamma\) being \(e_2\). Likewise \(\int_\Gamma w_2\,dx=\int_B\operatorname{div}w=0\), so \(c\int_\Gamma w_2=0\) may be subtracted, and with \(c\) the midpoint of \(\Gamma\)'s projection, \(|x-c|\le\ell/2\) on \(\Gamma\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Restoring drift tail: \(\alpha\ge1\) in \(\min(\kappa r^{\alpha-1},r)\ge\min(\kappa a^{\alpha-1},a)\) for \(r\ge a\); of \(d\) only that it lies between \(0\) and \(r\) (\(|y|\le|R_n|\) in (a), \(R_k-d(R_k)<a\) below \(a\) in (b)) and is at least \(\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) in size (\(d\ge\mu\) above \(a\)); the conditional sub-Gaussian bound in both parts, for \(t=\pm\theta\) and \(t=\pm u/(n\sigma^2)\); \(R_0=0\) in the existence of a last exit (\(|R_0|<u/2\) suffices for the two-sided form). No condition on \(u\) and no independence of the \(\xi\) beyond the conditional bound is used; the window in the particular case is where the minimum in (b) is its first term. Sibling exchange leg: \(\operatorname{div}w=0\) and the vanishing normal flux off \(\Gamma\) in both identities; piecewise smoothness with continuous normal components for the divergence theorem. Conclusions: (a) and (b) for every adapted chain of the stated form; the leg bound for every such field.

Degenerate cases. lem:restoring-drift-tail: \(\kappa\to0\): (b) tends to \(2n\), empty, and (a) remains, the Gaussian tail. \(u\) with \(c(u/2)^\alpha<2\): the particular case does not apply; (a) and (b) do. \(\alpha=2\): the exponent in (b) is \(\min(\kappa,\frac12)u^2/(4\sigma^2)\), a Gaussian-type tail of variance \(2\sigma^2/\min(\kappa,\frac12)\), the stationary scale of a linear drift up to constants. \(n=1\): \(R_1=\xi_1\) and both bounds hold trivially. lem:sibling-exchange-leg: \(m=0\) gives nothing; \(\Gamma=\partial B\) entire is outside the statement.

Nonvacuity. At the curve's pair \((4,4)\): \(\alpha=4\), \(n=J=7\) levels, per-level proxy \(\sigma^2=1/7\) (total \(s^2=1\)), \(c=2\), so \(\kappa=c\sigma^2\ln n=0.556\); (b) holds for every \(u\), and the particular case's window \(2\le u\le\sqrt{2/\kappa}\) (its two conditions at \(\alpha=4\)) is empty at \(n=7\) (upper end \(1.90\)) and nonempty exactly when \(\kappa\le\frac12\), first at \(n=9\) (\(\kappa=0.488\), upper end \(2.02\); research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_drift_20261017/window.txt), its upper end growing like \(\sqrt{n/\ln n}\). Leg lemma: the continuum field the test's script samples, \(w_1=2m(y)\,\mathrm{tent}(x_{\rm loc})\) with \(m\) constant on each child and \(w_2=-(2/\rho)\,\mathrm{tent}'(x_{\rm loc})\int_{y_0}^ym\), is piecewise \(C^1\) with continuous normal components (\(w_1\) continuous in \(x\), \(w_2\) continuous in \(y\)) and divergence-free on each piece, with zero normal flux on the parent's boundary; the script's grid values sample it. Plainest bound. For (b), the plainest bound is (a), Hoeffding's tail for the sum without drift, Gaussian; what (b) adds is the exponent \(\alpha\) in a window growing with \(n\). For the leg, none bounds the leg from below; the shift alone is bounded by the field's supremum.

Baseline. Without a drift the chain is a martingale and its tail is Gaussian at scale \(\sqrt n\sigma\) (part (a)); a drift that cancels the running value outright (\(\kappa\) large, \(d(r)=r\)) makes \(R_n=\xi_n\), with Gaussian tail at scale \(\sigma\) only, which is the trivial optimum of the one-dimensional model and is not available to a flow, whose running loads are forced in part by the divergence (lem:straight-cut-forced-flux) and whose corrections have legs (the second lemma). What the lemma adds over these: a drift of order \(\sigma^2\ln n\,r^{\alpha-1}\) per step, below the noise for \(r\ll(\sigma\ln n)^{-1/(\alpha-1)}\), already gives the \(\psi_\alpha\) tail on its window.

The paired restoring drift and its test

Construction. The dyadic flow built level by level (level_step of the simultaneous rule's script, unchanged), and after the step of level \(j\): for coordinate \(1\), the two vertically stacked children of each level-\(j\) square in each \(x\)-half, running means \(R_b,R_t\), normalized by the dyadic flow's analytic per-position standard deviation, get mean shifts \(\mp(D_b-D_t)/2\), \(D=\sigma d(R/\sigma)\), \(\alpha=4\), \(\kappa=c\ln J/J\), carried by \(2m\,\mathrm{tent}\) on each child and a vertical return leg inside the parent; coordinate \(2\) alike with horizontally adjacent children. The script is research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_drift_20261017/drift_test.py, its Prediction, controls and baseline committed before the run.

Result. \(N=16\cdot4^J\), \(J=6,7\), \(64\) seeds each (research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_drift_20261017/results.json). Controls passed: \(\kappa=0\) gives the dyadic field exactly (relative difference \(0.0\)); global averages agree (largest difference at most \(10^{-9}\) of the scale); the dyadic fractions are Gaussian within the factor \(1.5\) (at \(J=7\): \(0.0106\), \(0.00209\), \(0.00032\) in coordinate \(1\) against \(0.0124\), \(0.00270\), \(0.000465\)); the planted lighter law is seen (ratios \(0.12\), \(0.021\), \(0.0\) at \(J=7\)). The Prediction failed in every coordinate and size: the ratios of the drift flow's exceedance fractions to the dyadic flow's at \(t=2.5,3.0,3.5\) are at \(J=7\) \(2.67,9.24,45.6\) and \(3.94,12.8,58.0\) for \(c=0.5\), \(23.7,103.9,607\) and \(26.5,120,661\) for \(c=2\), and larger for \(c=8\); variance ratios at \(J=7\) \(2.24\) and \(4.62\) at \(c=0.5\), \(133\) and \(238\) at \(c=2\), and growing from \(J=6\) to \(J=7\) at \(c=2\) (\(51.6\) to \(133\), \(163\) to \(238\)) and at \(c=8\) in coordinate \(2\) (\(389\) to \(2490\)). The drift makes the tails heavier, not lighter, and more so at the larger size.

What the record says of it. The correction after level \(j\) stays inside the level-\(j\) squares with zero normal flux and zero divergence, so with it counted in the step of level \(j\) (still measurable with respect to the counts of levels at most \(j+1\), and local) every step keeps the dyadic means on its own level's squares, and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction covers the paired drift, whose statement says so: "(as has every flow whose level steps stay in the level-\(j\) squares with zero normal flux ...)". That theorem gives the divergence of the \(\psi_\alpha\) cost at scale \(L\sqrt{N\log N}\) with probability tending to one; it says nothing about tails heavier than the dyadic flow's at \(2.5\) to \(3.5\) standard deviations, and it covers the dyadic flow equally. Withdrawn from the script's docstring, committed before the run: the sentence "the correction changes the means of the level-(j+1) squares, so the step means are not the dyadic ones and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's hypothesis fails for it" (wrong: the theorem constrains each step on its own level's squares only); the Record checked line's "none decides the fractions of a rule that changes square means" (it rests on the same misreading); and the position counts "262,144 at J = 6, 1,048,576 at J = 7" with their Poisson spreads (results.json gives \(1{,}048{,}576\) and \(4{,}194{,}304\), \(64\) seeds of \(4^{J+1}\) positions).

Mechanism, an untested hypothesis. Each exchange of a mean \(m\) puts a leg of average at least \(2|m|\) into the other coordinate (the second lemma). In the construction that leg is \(\pm(4/\rho)\int m\,dy\) on the two halves of each child (\(\rho\) the child's side), so it has zero mean on the child but means of opposite sign on the level-\((j+2)\) squares, which the other coordinate's drift at the next level sees and exchanges in turn: plausibly a cascade between the coordinates, which the growth of the variance ratios with \(J\) points to. The run does not separate the legs' share from the shifts'.

Meta. Lagged restoring flow: lighter tails below 3.5σ

17 October 2026 · Finite check, reviewed; lighter per-point tails at J = 6, 7 below 3.5 standard deviations · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. Does the lagged greedy restoring flow, the repaired candidate the restoring drift entry names, have per-point tails lighter than the dyadic flow's?

Shortest route. The most direct step the record names is a flow nonlinear in the counts whose fine levels correct the coarse ones, tested for lighter tails (the ninth review's Obstacle; the restoring drift entry's next attempt); this entry builds the lagged candidate and tests it.

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Create one, maybe?? Does that make sense???? Have you tried??????", on the record having no nonlinear flow whose fine levels correct the coarse ones.

Target form. The goal's flow form: a flow on the grid of lem:grid-flow-duality (c) whose flow-bound value is of order \(N\) with probability tending to one; here its first necessary property, per-point loads whose tails are lighter than Gaussian.

Architecture test. Not decided. The ninth review's retained test (the gap-charged bound for nested chains, outcomes (A), (B), (C)) did not occur: none of its outcomes was reached, since this entry develops the user's pick, which defers the test without clearing it.

Owed attempt. The restoring drift entry named "a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level \(j\) is a circulation straddling the shared side of two sibling level-\(j\) squares", then "first the push-probability measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on it, then the exceedance test at \(J=6,7\)". The construction and the exceedance test were made (below). The push measurement was not: the exceedance test answers the construction's own question (are its tails lighter), while the push measurement only decides whether one recorded lemma covers it, which matters once the tails are lighter; it is the next entry's first step.

Review. The stand-in review of the previous checkpoint (research/logs/stand-in-review/20261017T142731.json) raised five objections. (1) A commit check's refusal answered by a retry "because the check has now seen the text", without first quoting the refusal's rule line: right; in this cycle each refusal's line was quoted in the reply before its retry ("a Python computation allowed more than 120 s needs --kernel-reason", "may not nest loops 3 deep in its script or local imports", "already ran with 4 different argument lists in this session", the last not retried). (2) A commit "went out with a stale message carrying an old figure": wrong; the attempt that carried the old text was refused by the commit check ("the message reports a passing suite run, \"1398 tests in 9.4 s\", that is not the last passing run of the whole suite"), so no commit carries it; the reply's sentence "the commit used the old text with 9.4 s" described that refused attempt, and the commit made after (the route judge's) carries "1398 tests in 9.2s", from the whole-suite run saved in research/provenance/framework/route-judge-suite-20261017.txt. (3) The route judge's false refusals never counted over the past record: right; one history replay, run in this turn, showed the judge naming the goal itself as the shortest step when the record named none, which would refuse exploration the user allowed; the prompt now says a restated goal is not a named step (commit "route_judge: a restated goal is not a named step"), and the full history replay is queued as route-judge-history-replay with its partial check. (4) The judge fails open on an outage, yet was reported as enforcement: right that it fails open; that is its design, stated in its docstring and its commit (an outage must not block work), and the reply said so; the paragraph requirement, which does not depend on the judge, does not fail open.
