The lagged greedy restoring flow and its test

Construction. The dyadic flow built level by level (level_step of the simultaneous rule's script, unchanged). After the step of level \(j\ge1\), which uses the counts of level \(j+1\), the level-\(j\) squares are paired inside their level-\((j-1)\) parents: in coordinate \(1\) the two vertically stacked level-\(j\) squares of each column of a parent, in coordinate \(2\) the two horizontally adjacent ones of each row. Each pair receives the unit circulation of the restoring drift entry's script at the parent's level (a mean shift \(+1\) on one square and \(-1\) on the other, carried by \(2\,\mathrm{tent}\) profiles and the return leg \(4S\,(Cs)\)) times an amplitude chosen by damped Newton descent on the quartic cost \(\sum(F_1+a\phi_1)^4+(F_2+a\phi_2)^4\) of the running field over the pair's positions, both coordinates, so the leg of lem:sibling-exchange-leg is paid for in the choice; coordinate \(1\)'s pairs first, then coordinate \(2\)'s on the corrected field. The cost is a quartic polynomial in the amplitude, its five coefficients summed once over the positions. The correction changes the means of the level-\(j\) squares; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction asks that "every step \(\Phi_j\) with \(j\ge j_1\) has on every level-\(j\) square \(S\) the mean of the dyadic step", which the correction breaks when assigned to step \(j\), and assigned to step \(j-1\) it would use the counts of level \(j+1\), which that step may not; other decompositions into steps are not excluded. Script: research/results/ultimate_matching_lagged_restoring_20261017/lagged_test.py, its Prediction, controls and baseline committed before the run.

Hand case. The restoring drift entry's hand case, two stacked siblings with normalized running horizontal means \(3\) and \(-1\) and a leg modelled on one child's area: the quartic descent moves the amplitude to \(0.852\) and lowers the cost from \(82\) to \(29.7\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_drift_20261017/smallest_case.txt); the script at \(J=3\), \(28\) seeds, ran its controls end to end before the full run (dry_run_J3.txt).

Result. \(N=16\cdot4^J\), \(J=6,7\), \(512\) seeds each (research/results/ultimate_matching_lagged_restoring_20261017/results.json; run_output.txt). Controls passed: amplitude forced to \(0\) gives the dyadic field exactly (relative difference \(0.0\)); no pair's quartic cost rose (largest relative rise \(0.0\)); global averages agree (differences \(1.3\cdot10^{-16}\) and \(2.1\cdot10^{-16}\) of the scale); the planted lighter law is seen (analytic ratios \(0.129\) to \(0.147\), \(0.026\) to \(0.041\), \(0.0016\) to \(0.0062\)). A control the script lacked, added after the review and committed before its run (divergence_check.py, divergence_check.txt): the correction's weak divergence, \(|\sum w\cdot\nabla g|/\sum|w_1\partial_xg|+|w_2\partial_yg|\) over five test functions \(g\), is \(0.0\) for both seeds tried, so the correction is divergence-free with zero normal flux to the sampling's precision; its positive control, the coordinate-\(2\) leg negated, gives \(0.066\) to \(0.100\) on the three functions that can see it, below the committed threshold \(0.2\), so that positive control failed as committed; read post hoc, the separation from \(0.0\) suggests the check sees a misoriented leg. The Prediction held in every coordinate, size and normalization. Per-position standardization over the \(512\) seeds (the normalization of ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances; the dyadic fractions \(0.0275\) to \(0.0280\) at \(2.2\) and \(0.0009\) to \(0.0011\) at \(3.3\), against Gaussian \(0.0278\) and \(0.000967\)): the lagged flow's ratios to the dyadic flow at \(2.2\) and \(3.3\) are \(0.566\), \(0.115\) (\(J=6\)) and \(0.563\), \(0.128\) (\(J=7\)) in coordinate \(1\), \(0.481\), \(0.089\) and \(0.460\), \(0.070\) in coordinate \(2\), with spreads over seed halves at \(3.3\) of \(0.005\) and \(0.014\) in coordinate \(1\), \(0.008\) and \(0.005\) in coordinate \(2\). Analytic normalization at \(2.5\), \(3.0\), \(3.5\): \(0.120\), \(0.046\), \(0.044\) and \(0.115\), \(0.039\), \(0.014\) in coordinate \(1\); \(0.881\), \(0.557\), \(0.349\) and \(0.859\), \(0.597\), \(0.391\) in coordinate \(2\). Variance ratios to the dyadic flow \(0.78\) in coordinate \(1\) and \(1.23\) in coordinate \(2\) at both sizes.

What the run does not show. Two sizes give a difference, not a trend: the per-position ratio at \(3.3\) moved from \(0.115\) to \(0.128\) in coordinate \(1\) (within the combined half-split spread, \(0.015\)) and from \(0.089\) to \(0.070\) in coordinate \(2\); the analytic ratios carry no spread, so their change between the sizes is not read. Coordinate \(2\)'s variance is \(1.23\) times the dyadic flow's and its analytic ratios, which measure absolute loads, are much closer to \(1\) than its per-position ones; that the legs of coordinate \(1\)'s exchanges move variance into it is an untested hypothesis (the order of the coordinates and dyadic_sigma's factor \(2\) between them are alternatives). Coordinate \(1\)'s variance ratio is \(0.78\) at both sizes; a constant-fraction restoring drift on per-point values would make it fall with \(J\), and why it does not is open. Thresholds stop at \(3.5\) standard deviations, below the \(\sqrt{\log N}\) scale where thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction acts, and nothing here bounds the flow-bound value. A third size, \(J=8\), was refused by the launcher (a fifth argument list for the script in the session) and not run.

Plainest bound. The variance alone: a Gaussian field whose variance is \(v\) times the dyadic flow's has analytic fraction ratios \(\mathrm{erfc}(t/\sqrt{2v})/\mathrm{erfc}(t/\sqrt2)\), which at \(t=2.5,3.0,3.5\) are \(0.374\), \(0.253\), \(0.159\) for coordinate \(1\)'s \(v=0.78\) and \(1.95\), \(2.53\), \(3.44\) for coordinate \(2\)'s \(v=1.23\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_lagged_restoring_20261017/hand_checks.txt), against the measured \(0.115\) to \(0.120\), \(0.039\) to \(0.046\), \(0.014\) to \(0.044\) and \(0.86\) to \(0.88\), \(0.56\) to \(0.60\), \(0.35\) to \(0.39\): in both coordinates the measured tails are lighter than the variance explains, more so farther out, and the per-position standardization removes the variance altogether, so the lightness is in the shape.

Nonvacuity. The test's instances lie at the curve's pair \((4,4)\) in the sense that its cost is quartic and its question is the per-point tail that thm:linear-flow-obstruction forces Gaussian for linear rules; the lagged flow is nonlinear in the counts, additivity failing in the counts themselves: for two random count arrays \(c_1,c_2\) at \(J=3\), the lagged field has \(\max|L(c_1+c_2)-L(c_1)-L(c_2)|/\max|L(c_1+c_2)|=0.438\), while the dyadic field, linear in the counts, has \(0.0\) (additivity_witness.py, additivity_witness.txt); as a map of the running field one exchange with the script's own unit shapes already fails additivity (child means \((2,-2)\), \((1,1)\) and their sum \((3,-1)\) give amplitudes \(-0.404\), \(0\), \(-0.508\), gradients at most \(7\cdot10^{-7}\), so minimizers), so that theorem does not cover it, and under the natural assignment of steps neither does thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction.

Baseline. The dyadic flow (ratio \(1\)); a variance change alone (the Plainest bound); the record's simultaneous rule, keeping square means, at \(0.245\) to \(0.364\) at \(3.3\) in the same per-position normalization with \(512\) seeds (ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances; ex:exceedance-curve-slopes measured it again at \(J=5,6\)); the paired restoring drift at \(45.6\) and above at \(3.5\) (ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails). The lagged flow's \(0.070\) to \(0.128\) at \(3.3\) is two to five times lighter than the simultaneous rule's at the same threshold and normalization.

Record comparison. From the record's side: ex:greedy-circulation-tails (a greedy circulation per square, keeping square means) and ex:simultaneous-rule-tails, ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances, ex:exceedance-curve-slopes (the simultaneous rule) are the record's earlier nonlinear rules, all inside thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction; ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails exchanges sibling means inside their own parents and amplifies; the lagged flow exchanges the means of the squares whose information it uses. New here: the lagged construction and its test.

General statement. The all-parameter statement this test bears on is lem:restoring-drift-tail (the one-dimensional mechanism), whose hypothesis, a drift of size at least \(\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) at each point, is what the lagged flow would have to be shown to realize; ex:lagged-restoring-tails records the test.

New mathematics. ex:lagged-restoring-tails: the dyadic flow corrected after each level by circulations exchanging the means of sibling level-\(j\) squares inside their level-\((j-1)\) parents, amplitudes by quartic descent on both coordinates, has per-point exceedance fractions at \(3.3\) standard deviations \(0.070\) to \(0.128\) of the dyadic flow's (per-position standardization, \(512\) seeds, \(J=6,7\)), lighter than the simultaneous rule's \(0.245\) to \(0.364\) in the same normalization, with its controls passing (the divergence control's positive control failing its committed threshold); a difference at two sizes below \(3.5\) standard deviations, its change with \(J\) undecided. In a two-value model of one exchange (child means \(P\pm R\), the other coordinate's load \(B\) where the leg lands, the leg on one child's area) the cost-optimal exchange is \(m=(R-B)/3\) at \(P=0\) for every strictly convex even cost, a linear rule, and nonlinear in \(P\) for the quartic.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; a finite check at two sizes. Bearing. At the goal's own parameters it gives nothing yet: the test stops at \(3.5\) standard deviations and \(J=7\); the cycle was spent on it because the construction is the direct route the record names, and its lighter tails are the first evidence for a flow outside thm:linear-flow-obstruction and, under the natural assignment of steps, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction (whether lem:conditional-push-obstruction covers it is open).

One exchange in a two-value model. One parent, two children with running horizontal means \(P+R\) and \(P-R\), a load \(B\) of the other coordinate where the leg lands, and the leg of size \(2m\) spread flat over one child's area (the modelling choice: lem:sibling-exchange-leg gives an average of at least \(2|m|\) on the shared side, here spread over one child of the two the shift covers; the script's leg is instead a profile over the whole parent with twice that mass, so the model's coefficients are the model's, not the script's). With \(u=R-m\), the cost per child area \(\psi(P+u)+\psi(P-u)+\psi(B+2m)\) is stationary where \(\psi'(P+u)-\psi'(P-u)=2\psi'(B+2m)\). At \(P=0\) and any strictly convex even \(\psi\) (evenness is used: it makes \(\psi'(u)-\psi'(-u)=2\psi'(u)\)) this is \(\psi'(u)=\psi'(B+2m)\), so \(m=(R-B)/3\), a linear rule; the computed minimizers at \(R=1\), \(\psi(x)=x^4\) are \(0.556\), \(0.333\), \(0.111\), \(1\), \(-1/3\) at \(B=-2/3,0,2/3,-2,2\) (exchange_with_load.txt), and at \(R=0.5,1,1.5\), \(B=0\), \(m=R/3\) also for \(\psi(x)=e^{x^4}-1\) (hand_checks.txt). At \(P\ne0\) and \(\psi(x)=x^4\) the stationarity is \((B+2m)^3=u^3+3P^2u\), nonlinear in \(P\): the hand case's means \(3\) and \(-1\) (\(P=1\), \(R=2\), \(B=0\)) give \(m=0.852\), not \(2/3\) (smallest_case.txt). So the exchange is nonlinear through the common parent mean as well as through the spread inside the children (the Smallest case below). By Thomson's principle applied to each realization, every flow with the cells' outflows has \(\sum_e\theta_e^2\) at least the electrical flow's; that bounds the total from below, not each coordinate's nor against the dyadic flow, and it applies to the lagged field because the divergence control shows the correction divergence-free with zero normal flux, to the sampling's precision.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow, since it tells at small sizes whether lem:conditional-push-obstruction's push hypothesis holds for it, which would put the flow under a recorded obstruction; then the lightness as a function of the threshold \(t\) at fixed \(J\), larger \(t\) reached with more seeds, since the exchange's model is scale-invariant (running values and their spread scale together) and so predicts a lightness that changes with \(t\) in units of the spread, not with \(J\); and the regression of the amplitudes on the square-mean rule \((R-B)/3\), the parent mean \(P\) and the spread \(\delta\), which names the nonlinear terms a general statement would use. Smallest case. Children with two positions each, running values \(R\pm\delta\) and \(-R\pm\delta\), a uniform shift \(m\), the leg on one child's area, \(B=0\): the quartic optimum against the linear rule's \(R/3\) is \(m/(R/3)=1\) at \(\delta=0\), \(2.65\) and \(2.89\) at \(R=0.25\) with \(\delta=1,2\), \(1.68\) and \(2.21\) at \(R=1\), \(1.28\) and \(1.68\) at \(R=2\) (exchange_with_spread.txt): its stationarity is \(u^3+3\delta^2u=8m^3\), so \(m\approx(3\delta^2R/8)^{1/3}\) for \(R\ll\delta\) and \(m\to R/3\) for \(R\gg\delta\), a stronger pull at the centre that returns to linear at large values in units of the spread; the model depends on \(R/\delta\) only, so it predicts that the lightness fades at large thresholds, which the attempt's dependence on \(t\) is to test. Nontrivial because: the quartic of the running values inside a square gains the term \(6(R-m)^2\delta^2\), which the descent weighs and the two-value model drops. Plainest bound. lem:sibling-exchange-leg: every exchange costs a leg of average at least \(2|m|\); in the two-value model at \(P=0\) the exchange is exactly \((R-B)/3\). Own statements. lem:restoring-drift-tail asks a drift of at least \(\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\), which a linear drift \(r/3\) meets wherever \(\kappa r^2\le1/3\), most of the lemma's window, so the lemma does not exclude a linear drift; what excludes linear rules is thm:linear-flow-obstruction's second-moment bound, which does not apply to this flow, nonlinear in the counts by the additivity witness in Nonvacuity; lem:sibling-exchange-leg prices each exchange; ex:lagged-restoring-tails says the shape is lighter at \(J=6,7\) below \(3.5\) standard deviations and decides nothing at large \(N\); thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction does not cover the flow under the natural assignment of steps; whether lem:conditional-push-obstruction does is open, the measurement's question; ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails, the same circulations chosen by a cubic rule inside their own level's squares, amplified, so a push measurement or a threshold sweep on the lagged flow decides nothing about it and it decides nothing about them; thm:adapted-partition-obstruction (read this cycle) decides matchings following rank-cut transports steered within \(A/\sqrt n\) of their count splits, and the lagged flow is no such transport, so it decides nothing about the next attempt. Record search. "restoring drift running field cubic correction Lyapunov exponential quartic tail Markov chain levels" and "circulation straddling sibling squares child means later level information measurable", which returned ex:greedy-circulation-tails, ex:simultaneous-rule-tails, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction and ex:rule-conditional-pushes; the reviewer's "greedy circulation quartic descent per square tails linear rule" returned ex:greedy-circulation-tails, ex:simultaneous-rule-tails and lem:conditional-push-obstruction.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read: the registered statements of thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, thm:linear-flow-obstruction, lem:restoring-drift-tail, lem:sibling-exchange-leg, ex:simultaneous-rule-exceedances, ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails and ex:rule-conditional-pushes. One medium reviewer (record: research/results/ultimate_matching_lagged_restoring_20261017/review.txt), strength count \(3\): it checked the script's reshapes and their inverses, its unit shapes against the restoring drift script's, the continuum divergence of the correction in both coordinates, the quartic coefficients, the figures against results.json, the variance baseline against hand_checks.txt, the Smallest case against exchange_with_spread.txt, and the square-mean theorem's exclusion under the natural assignment (locality holding, only the mean condition failing). Required, all made: the planted ratios corrected; a divergence control (added and run, its positive control failing its committed threshold, as reported); the dry run's output saved; the two-value model's \(m=(R-B)/3\) stated at \(P=0\) only (less general: the step \(\psi'(P+u)-\psi'(P-u)=2\psi'(u)\) needs \(P=0\); at other \(P\) it is false) and its "can come only from" conclusion withdrawn as false wherever written (the model is nonlinear in \(P\), as the hand case showed); nonlinearity shown by additivity failing, not by cubic equations; the reading of a linear drift against lem:restoring-drift-tail corrected (a linear drift meets its hypothesis on most of its window; linear rules are excluded by thm:linear-flow-obstruction's second-moment bound); the Thomson sentence's "only the shape can change" withdrawn as false (Thomson bounds the total, not each coordinate nor against the dyadic flow), and the sentence now made for a field shown divergence-correct (less general: Thomson's step needs the flow's outflows); the variance-moving sentence labelled an untested hypothesis; the analytic ratios' change not read; the next attempt's variable changed from \(J\) to the threshold \(t\) (the model is scale-invariant) and the push measurement put first; the Review answers given their quotes and sources. The reviewer's claim that evenness of \(\psi\) is unused does not hold in the model as written: with child means \(\pm R\) the two children's terms combine as \(\psi'(u)-\psi'(-u)=2\psi'(u)\) only for even \(\psi\), and the entry says so; its follow-up agreed and withdrew the objection. That follow-up checked the divergence control's report, the two-value model, the Follow-up and the Review answers, and required, all made: "post hoc" for the positive control's separation; the additivity witness computed with the script's own unit shapes (additivity_witness.py) rather than the model's; the check's single refusal named a false refusal and its appositive gap named in the Prevention; the spec's "first ... clearly" replaced by the comparison made; "to the sampling's precision" in the Thomson sentence. Its third check found the witness a map of the running field, not of the counts (constant child fields are no counts' image); the witness was then computed in the counts (additivity defect \(0.438\) against the dyadic field's \(0.0\)), with the exchange's stationarity residuals printed. Process audit. The reviewer found the title "A lagged restoring flow lightens tails" stronger than the body (it dropped "at J = 6, 7, below 3.5σ", while the Follow-up doubts the effect persists; now "Lagged restoring flow: lighter tails below 3.5σ"), "lighter than every rule the record tested" and "a flow outside every recorded obstruction" stronger than the comparisons made (both now say only what was compared: less general, the comparison step covering the simultaneous rule and two theorems only), the Hand case read without its quantity beside the model's conclusion it contradicted, the constant variance ratio across \(J\) not asked about (now stated), and no orbiting.

Process assessment. The stand-in review's right objections (1), (3), (5) share one fault: a check or a rule called in force before its effect was measured on the case that needed it (a judge reported before its false refusals were counted; a prevention promised for a later commit; a refusal retried before its rule line was read). Prevention. For (3), the route judge's prompt fixed after the history replay that exposed it (commit "route_judge: a restated goal is not a named step") and the full replay queued with its partial check (route-judge-history-replay); for (1) and (5), the rules exist and were followed in this cycle (each refusal's rule line quoted before its retry), and nothing mechanical can tell from a command whether its reply quoted the refusal, so no check is added. The reviewer's findings of this cycle: a model's conclusion drawn at one parameter (\(P=0\)) while the entry's own hand case, at another, contradicted it; a nonlinearity asserted from the form of equations; a script without the control its construction most needed. For the second, notebook-append now refuses a sentence asserting that a rule is (not linear | nonlinear) in the counts without an additivity witness (commit "notebook-append: a nonlinearity claim names its additivity witness"; replayed over 2546 articles it refuses 1, research/provenance/framework/nonlinearity-witness-replay-20261017.txt, a sentence true in content refused for its missing witness, which the reviewer counts a false refusal), since this is the class's second slip; its limit, that the appositive form pinned to one object ("this flow, nonlinear in the counts") passed it while this entry's own Own statements used that form, was closed in this turn (commit "notebook-append: the nonlinearity check reads the appositive form pinned to one object"; it refuses the draft's sentence and still 1 of 2546 articles, nonlinearity-witness-replay2-20261017.txt); a witness computed on inputs the object never receives (constant child fields) was offered for a property in the counts, which AGENTS.md now addresses (below); for the first and third the rules exist (a statement drawn from one worked construction is checked on the construction most unlike it; a control is chosen for what the construction can get wrong), the reviewer caught both, and no check can tell a model's parameters from its prose.

Meta. The way of working behind the stand-in review's right objections: counting a check as done when it is written, not when its run on the case that needed it and on the record's past has been read; it shows also in the restoring drift entry's docstring, written before the theorem it dismissed was applied. The change in how the work is done is in the reviewer's audit (commit "medium-reviewer: a check called in force is shown with its run and its losses", .claude/agents/medium-reviewer.md): every reviewed entry now has a reader who asks, of each check it calls in force, for that run and that count. The same habit, one level up, is behind this cycle's reviewer findings: a model's formula was trusted where it was computed (\(P=0\)) and read as the model's whole behaviour, and a control was chosen for what was easy to compute (the global average) rather than for what the construction could get wrong (its leg's orientation); the durable change is in COMPUTATION_RULES.md (commit "COMPUTATION_RULES.md: controls are chosen for what the construction can get wrong"): a script lists its construction's failure modes and gives each a control with a planted positive control, and a script building a flow checks its divergence in weak form with a flipped leg as positive control, the pattern of divergence_check.py. Wider still, the reviewer's later reports show the habit of taking a stand-in for the object: a two-value model, then fields no counts produce, offered for a property of the flow in the counts; AGENTS.md now asks that evidence for a property of the object be computed on that object in its own variables, a model's result written as the model's (commit "AGENTS.md: evidence for a property is computed on the object, in its own variables").

Mixed-level chains with up to \(e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\) layers

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; nested chains at \((4,4)\) on dyadic grids with at most \(\exp((\log N)^{2/3}\Lambda_B^{1/3})\) large layers · Mixed-level counts. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Question. The ninth review's first step on the dual side: does lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c)–(d), proved for nested chains at one level \(y\), extend to chains whose layers sit at different levels, with a bound linear in each layer's cost?

Shortest route. The most direct step the record names is the restoring-drift construction (a flow nonlinear in the counts whose fine levels correct the coarse ones, the lagged restoring flow its latest candidate). Not taken in this entry: compute.sh start printed "REFUSED IN ADVANCE: on route side-ultimate-matching the last two research entries developed restoring-drift-construction and declared no bearing; the finisher refuses the next entry on that route that develops it", and the construction's named next attempt, the push measurement, is a finite check, while it also printed "Another finite-check-only research entry on this route will be rejected; this cycle must attempt a proof or refutation of the General statement". On the dual side the direct path is the gap-charged bound for chains of many layers, which the cut-cell variance entry names; this entry makes the ninth review's first step toward it, and its Follow-up names the gap charge next.

Chosen. mixed-level-counts, not the head local-completion-hall, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy directly (its dual side bounds the discrete class itself) and the ninth review scheduled this step on it with its retained test.

Target form. The goal's discrete form: the bound \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\) for the \(X\)-term \(D(g)=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\) over grid functions of discrete cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\), on dyadic grids of side between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\); this entry bounds the nested chains at mixed levels, which by the layer cake are the grid functions with separated values.

Architecture test. Not decided. The ninth review's retained test (the gap-charged bound for nested chains, outcomes (A), (B), (C)): none of its outcomes was reached; this entry makes the step its Decision put first, the multi-level corollary, which covers chains at mixed levels with up to \(\exp((\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3})\) layers of perimeter at least \(1\), and leaves the test's instance, chains of more such layers.

Owed attempt. The item's latest entry, bounded chain values, named "bound the length of an optimal chain, through the range of an optimal integral dual potential"; not made here, because the multi-level corollary bounds the discrete class itself, the form of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy, while that attempt bounds the matching side's chain values at one pair of levels, a consequence of the class bound; this is its first deferral (lead_queue.py history printed beside that entry "[no later entry has an Owed attempt paragraph]"), and it stays the item's next attempt. The item's earlier entries, read: low-level mixed counts ("a high second level remain, and a refutation there would refute the conjecture"), windowed mixed counts ("the mixed counts at every pair of levels, proved now"), column crossing ("this entry excludes every repair keeping both-box pairs off a fine family of vertical lines"), two-graph chain duality ("now exactly the bound \(2Ne^{-t_2}\) on chain values, proved for length at most one"), and the bounded chain values entry ("the bound on every chain's value, now proved for chains of length up to").

Setting

As in lem:cut-cell-variance-bound: \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), \(\ell_1\) the Leighton–Shor scale, \(\kappa>0\) fixed, a dyadic mesh \(\delta_0\) with \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), \(D(g)=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\) for \(g\) constant on the cells, \(P(A)\) the inner perimeter of a union of cells, the discrete cost \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\), \(C_b\) the constant of part (b) of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound and \(L_f\) that of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor. A nested chain at mixed levels is \(g=\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}y_k1_{A_k}\) with \(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\) unions of cells and heights \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\), otherwise arbitrary; \(P_k=P(A_k)\), \(\Lambda_k=\log(y_k/2)\). Its layers split into the high ones \(H=\{k:y_k\ge N^{1/3}\}\), the small ones \(S=\{k\notin H:P_k<1\}\) and the large ones \(B=\{k\notin H:P_k\ge1\}\); \(y_B=\min_{k\in B}y_k\).

Lemma (multi-level chain bound)

Statement. On the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, which has probability tending to one, at \((4,4)\), for every such \(\delta_0\), every fixed \(M\in[1,2e^{16}]\) and every nested chain at mixed levels with discrete cost at most \(M\) (the goal's class has \(M=2\)): (a) with \(c_k=\delta_0P_k\psi_4^*(y_k/2)\), \(\sum_kc_k\le M\) and \(y_k\delta_0P_k\le4c_k\Lambda_k^{-1/4}\); (b) for \(N\) large, if \(|S|\le N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) and \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\) (no condition on \(B\) when it is empty, none on \(H\)), then \(|D(g)|\le(17MC_b+1+6ML_f)\sqrt{N\log N}\); in particular when \(K\le N^{1/7}\) and \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(\min_ky_k/2))^{1/3}\). (c) Consequently every grid function whose distinct values \(v_0<\dots<v_K\) satisfy \(v_k-v_{k-1}\ge2e^{16}\delta_0\), of discrete cost at most \(M\), whose chain \(A_k=\{g\ge v_k\}\), \(y_k=(v_k-v_{k-1})/\delta_0\) meets the conditions of (b), has the same bound; in particular when \(K\le e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\).

Proof. (a) Across an inner edge \(e\) the increments of the nested sets \(1_{A_k}\) have one sign, so \(|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0=\sum_{k:\,e\in\partial A_k}y_k\); \(\psi_4^*\) is convex with \(\psi_4^*(0)=0\), hence superadditive on \([0,\infty)\), so \(\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\ge\sum_{k:\,e\in\partial A_k}\psi_4^*(y_k/2)\), and summing \(\delta_0^2\) times this over the edges, each \(\partial A_k\) having \(P_k/\delta_0\) of them, the cost is at least \(\sum_kc_k\). For \(t=y_k/2\ge e^{16}\), \(\psi_4^*(t)\ge t(\log t)^{1/4}-e^{\log t}+1\) at \(s=(\log t)^{1/4}\) in \(\psi_4^*(t)=\sup_s(ts-e^{s^4}+1)\), that is \(\psi_4^*(t)\ge t((\log t)^{1/4}-1)+1\ge\frac t2(\log t)^{1/4}\), as \((\log t)^{1/4}\ge2\); so \(c_k\ge\frac14y_k\delta_0P_k\Lambda_k^{1/4}\). (b) Write \(g=g_H+g_S+g_B\) by the split of the Setting; \(D\) is linear. High layers. By nesting \(\mathrm{TV}(g_H)=\sum_{k\in H}y_k\delta_0P_k\le\sum_{k\in H}4c_k\Lambda_k^{-1/4}\le4M(\log(N^{1/3}/2))^{-1/4}\) by (a), so lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) gives \(|D(g_H)|\le4ML_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\frac13\log N-\log2)^{-1/4}\le6ML_f\sqrt{N\log N}\) for \(N\) large (\(4\cdot3^{1/4}<5.3\)); at \(M=2\) lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) gives the same with \(8\sqrt3L_f\). Small layers. By lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), \(|D(g_S)|\le L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\sum_{k\in S}y_k\delta_0P_k\le L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}|S|N^{1/3}\delta_0\le2L_f|S|(\log N)^{3/2}N^{1/3}\), as \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}<2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\); for \(|S|\le N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) this is at most \(2L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{-1/2}\le\sqrt{N\log N}\) once \(\log N\ge2L_f\). Large layers. For \(k\in B\), part (b) of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound with \(u(P)=2\log_2(c_0/P)+5\), \(c_0=4/\delta_0\) (so \(u(P)\ge2\log_2\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)+5\), as \(4/\delta_0\ge2^{\ell_1}\) and \(P<2/\delta_0\), as in that lemma's proof of (c)), gives \(|D(1_{A_k})|\le C_b\sqrt N\,P_k(u(P_k)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\). With \(x_k=y_k\delta_0P_k\), \(c_0/P_k=4y_k/x_k\), so \(y_k\delta_0|D(1_{A_k})|\le C_b\sqrt N(f_k(x_k)+x_k\sqrt{\log N})\), \(f_k(x)=x(2\log_2(4y_k/x)+5)^{3/4}\), increasing on \((0,2y_k]\) (its derivative is \(u^{-1/4}(u-\frac3{2\ln2})>0\) for \(u\ge5\)). Both \(x_k\) (as \(P_k<2/\delta_0\)) and \(\xi_k=4c_k\Lambda_k^{-1/4}\le2M\le2y_k\) (as \(M\le2e^{16}\le y_k\)) lie in that interval, and \(x_k\le\xi_k\) by (a), so \(f_k(x_k)\le f_k(\xi_k)=4c_k\Lambda_k^{-1/4}\big(2\log_2(y_k\Lambda_k^{1/4}/c_k)+5\big)^{3/4}\). Here \(2\log_2(y_k\Lambda_k^{1/4}/c_k)+5=7+2\Lambda_k/\ln2+\frac12\log_2\Lambda_k+2\log_2(1/c_k)\le3.49\Lambda_k+2\log_2(1/c_k)\) for \(\Lambda_k\ge16\), and with \((a+b)^{3/4}\le a^{3/4}+b_+^{3/4}\) (\(a>0\), \(a+b>0\)) and \(3.49^{3/4}\le2.56\), \(f_k(\xi_k)\le10.24\,c_k\Lambda_k^{1/2}+4\Lambda_B^{-1/4}\varphi(c_k)\), \(\Lambda_B=\log(y_B/2)\), \(\varphi(c)=c\,(2\log_2(1/c))_+^{3/4}\). First, \(\sum_{k\in B}10.24\,c_k\Lambda_k^{1/2}\le10.24M(\log N/3)^{1/2}\le5.92M\sqrt{\log N}\), as \(y_k<N^{1/3}\). Second, \(\varphi\) is concave on \((0,1)\) (with \(s=\ln(1/c)\), \(\varphi'\propto s^{3/4}-\frac34s^{-1/4}\), whose derivative in \(c\) is \(-\frac1c(\frac34s^{-1/4}+\frac3{16}s^{-5/4})<0\)) and vanishes on \([1,\infty)\); over the \(K'\le|B|\) layers of \(B\) with \(c_k<1\), of total \(S'\le M\), Jensen gives \(\sum\varphi(c_k)\le K'\varphi(S'/K')=S'(2\log_2(K'/S'))^{3/4}\), increasing in \(S'\) while \(S'/K'<e^{-3/4}\); so when \(K'>e^{3/4}M\) it is at most \(M(2\log_2(K'/M))^{3/4}\le M(2\log_2|B|)^{3/4}\) (\(M\ge1\)), and otherwise at most \(K'\max\varphi\le0.843(2.12M+1)\) (the maximum of \(\varphi\) is at \(c=e^{-3/4}\), \(0.8428\)). Third, \(\sum_{k\in B}x_k\sqrt{\log N}\le\sqrt{\log N}\sum_k\xi_k\le\sqrt{\log N}\cdot4\cdot16^{-1/4}M=2M\sqrt{\log N}\). Hence \(|D(g_B)|\le C_b\sqrt N\big(7.92M\sqrt{\log N}+4\Lambda_B^{-1/4}(M(2\log_2|B|)^{3/4}+0.843(2.12M+1))\big)\); with \((2\log_2|B|)^{3/4}\le2.22(\log|B|)^{3/4}\le2.22(\log N)^{1/2}\Lambda_B^{1/4}\) under the condition on \(|B|\), and \(4\Lambda_B^{-1/4}\le2\), \(|D(g_B)|\le C_b\sqrt N(7.92+8.88)M\sqrt{\log N}+1.69(2.12M+1)C_b\sqrt N\le17MC_b\sqrt{N\log N}\) for \(N\) large (at \(M=2\): \(15.9+17.8\le34\), the reviewed draft's figures). Adding the three parts gives (b). The particular case: \(|S|\le K\le N^{1/7}\le N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) for \(N\) large, and \(|B|\le K\), \(y_B\ge\min_ky_k\). (c) With \(A_k=\{g\ge v_k\}\), nested unions of cells, \(g-v_0=\sum_{k\le K}(v_k-v_{k-1})1_{A_k}\), a nested chain at mixed levels with \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\), and \(D(g)=D(g-v_0)\); for \(K\le e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\), \(K\le N^{1/7}\) for \(N\) large and \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}\le(\log N)^{2/3}16^{1/3}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Nesting: the one-signed increments, which give both the superadditive cost split in (a) and the high part's increments at least \(N^{1/3}\); for layers that are not nested the cost does not split and the lemma says nothing. Heights \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\): \((\log t)^{1/4}\ge2\) in the lower bound on \(\psi_4^*\), and \(\Lambda_k\ge16\) in \(7+\frac12\log_2\Lambda_k\le0.6\Lambda_k\) and in \(16^{-1/4}\). Cost at most \(M\), any fixed \(M\in[1,2e^{16}]\): \(\sum c_k\le M\) in the three parts, the constants linear in \(M\); the reviewed draft fixed \(M=2\) with a wrong reason (that lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), stated at cost \(2\), was needed), and the high part now uses its (b) with (a), so the statement is more general; \(M\ge1\) only in \(M(2\log_2(K'/M))^{3/4}\le M(2\log_2|B|)^{3/4}\), and \(M\le2e^{16}\) only in \(\xi_k\le2y_k\), the interval where \(f_k\) increases (a larger fixed \(M\) would need the interval widened, which the proof does not do). \((4,4)\): the conjugate \(\psi_4^*\). \(|S|\le N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\): the small layers only; \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}\Lambda_B^{1/3}\): the Jensen term only, with the minimum height over \(B\) only; the high layers need neither (so the lemma includes the high case of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) without a condition on \(K\)); the split at \(N^{1/3}\) is a choice, as in (d). Dyadic \(\delta_0\) between \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \(2^{-\ell_1}\): the cited lemmas' events. \(N\) large: the absorption of \(1.69(2.12M+1)C_b\sqrt N\), of the small layers and of \((\frac13\log N-\log2)^{-1/4}\) against \((\log N/3)^{-1/4}\). What the lemma adds over the record is uniformity in a growing number of layers at mixed heights (see Baseline). Conclusion for every nested chain at mixed levels on such grids, and in (c) for every grid function with values separated by \(2e^{16}\delta_0\). The hypotheses moved from the reviewed draft's \(K\le N^{1/7}\) and \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(\min_ky_k/2))^{1/3}\) to these weaker ones, so the statement is more general; the earlier form is its particular case.

Degenerate cases. lem:multilevel-chain-bound with all heights equal recovers lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), at \(M=2\) with the constant \(34C_b+1+12L_f\) where that lemma has \(\max(55C_b+1,8\sqrt3L_f)\); with \(K=1\) a single layer at any level \(y\ge2e^{16}\); with \(K=0\), \(g=0\); a chain all of whose layers are high, only the high part, by (a) and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), for any number of layers; all of whose layers have perimeter below \(1\), only the small-layer bound. A function with two values closer than \(2e^{16}\delta_0\) is outside (c), even when every increment across an edge is large (values never adjacent); lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) covers it with its factor.

Nonvacuity. On the curve's pair \((4,4)\), with lem:cut-cell-variance-bound's witness grid, \(\kappa=1\), \(\delta_0=2^{-\ell_1-1}\), \(\log N\ge4096\) and \(N\) large: let \(K_N=\lfloor\sqrt{\log N}\rfloor\), and for \(k\le K_N\) let \(A_k\) be the cells whose centre \((x,y)\) has \(y\le h_k(x)=\frac12-\frac k{4K_N}+\frac1{16}\sin2\pi x\), at height \(y_k=2^{k+1}e^{16}\); then \(A_{K_N+1}=[0,\frac18]^2\) at height \(2e^{16}\) and \(A_{K_N+2}=[0,\delta_0]^2\) at height \(\sqrt N\). Nesting: \(h_k\) decreases in \(k\), and \(h_{K_N}\ge\frac3{16}\), so \([0,\frac18]^2\subseteq A_{K_N}\). Each \(A_k\), \(k\le K_N\), is bounded by a staircase of horizontal length \(1\) and vertical length at most the variation \(\frac14\) of \(h_k\) plus \(\delta_0\) per column, so \(1\le P_k\le3\); between neighbouring columns a staircase steps by at most \(\frac{2\pi}{16}\delta_0+\delta_0<1.4\delta_0\), far below the gap \(\frac1{4K_N}\) to the next curve, so the boundaries are disjoint (multiplicity \(1\)); \(P_{K_N+1}=\frac14\), \(P_{K_N+2}=2\delta_0\). So \(B=\{1,\dots,K_N\}\), \(S=\{K_N+1\}\), \(H=\{K_N+2\}\), \(y_B=4e^{16}\), \(\log|B|\le\log\log N\le(\log N)^{2/3}16^{1/3}\); the heights in \(B\) take \(K_N\) distinct dyadic values, the largest \(2^{K_N+1}e^{16}\le e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\) for \(N\) large. Cost: \(\sum_kc_k\le3K_N\delta_0\big(\frac{y}2(2\log\frac y2)^{1/4}+1\big)|_{y=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}}+\frac14\delta_0\psi_4^*(e^{16})+2\delta_0^2\big(\frac{\sqrt N}2(\log N)^{1/4}+1\big)\to0\) (with \(\psi_4^*(t)\le t(2\log t)^{1/4}+1\), recorded in lem:cut-cell-variance-bound's entry, \(\delta_0e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\sqrt{\log N}\to0\) and \(\delta_0^2\sqrt N\le(\log N)^{3/2}/\sqrt N\)), so at most \(2\) for \(N\) large. The witness exercises each branch of (b): the large layers, with \(K'=K_N\ge5\) in the Jensen step, the small layer and the high layer. What the recorded statements give on it, composed as the Baseline describes: per layer by lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) at \(K=1\), \((K_N+2)C_d\sqrt{N\log N}\); per dyadic height group by that lemma's proof (one layer per group here), the same; lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), applicable as \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\) once \(\log N\ge4096\), with the high layer split off to lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), on the rest, whose increments lie in \(\{0\}\cup[2e^{16},e^{\sqrt{\log N}}]\) at multiplicity \(1\): \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\min\{1+(\log N)^{1/8},(\log N/16)^{1/4}\}\); the hybrids tried here, a split at one height \(Y^*\) and the top \(t\) layers taken singly by (i) with the rest by (iii), give at best order \((\log N)^{1/8}\) (the first, as the Baseline computes; the second, \(tC_d+C((K_N-t)\ln2+16)^{1/4}\), is at least of order \(\min(K_N/2,(K_N/2)^{1/4})\)); the lemma gives \(C'\sqrt{N\log N}\). Plainest bound. Every fixed witness is decided by one function: Bernstein's inequality for \(D(g)\), with variance at most \(N\int g^2\le N(2\delta_0e^{\sqrt{\log N}})^2+N^2\delta_0^4\) and \(\|g\|_\infty\le\delta_0(\sqrt N+2e^{\sqrt{\log N}})\le(\log N)^{3/4}\) up to constants, gives, at the deviation level \(t=\log N\) (failure probability \(2/N\)), \(|D(g)|\le\sqrt{2N\int g^2\,\log N}+\frac13\|g\|_\infty\log N=O((\log N)^{5/4}e^{\sqrt{\log N}}+(\log N)^2)\), far below \(\sqrt{N\log N}\). The plainest uniform bound over the lemma's family, a union over all \(2^{\delta_0^{-2}}\) unions of cells with Bernstein's inequality, gives \(|D(1_A)|\le\sqrt{2N\lambda(A)\delta_0^{-2}\ln2}+\dots\), of order \(N(\log N)^{-3/4}\): vacuous; over a polynomial family fixed in advance lem:guided-chain-bound (b) is that union bound. The lemma's content is the uniformity over every nested chain of arbitrary unions of cells with up to \(\exp((\log N)^{2/3}\Lambda_B^{1/3})\) large layers at mixed heights.

Baseline. Three compositions of the record need no idea. Composed. (i) Per layer: by (a) each layer alone has cost \(c_k\le2\), so lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) at \(K=1\) and linearity give \(KC_d\sqrt{N\log N}\), the goal's order for bounded \(K\). (ii) Per dyadic height group: the proof of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c)–(d), run on a nested chain whose heights lie in \([y,2y]\), keeps \(\sum_kP_k\le T(y)/(y\delta_0)\) (its \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\ge y\delta_0\sum_kP_k\) and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) need only increments at least \(y\)) and loses the factor \(2\) in \(\delta_0\sum_ky_k|D(1_{A_k})|\le2y\delta_0\sum_k|D(1_{A_k})|\); so a chain with \(G\) dyadic height groups, each within (d)'s conditions, has \(|D(g)|\le2GC_d\sqrt{N\log N}\), the goal's order for boundedly many groups (this step is the entry's reading of that proof, which the reviewer's follow-up checked step by step against it). (iii) By lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), which needs \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\) (so on grids with \(\kappa\ge4\); below, the record has only (i)–(ii)), with a free split height \(Y^*\in[2e^{16},\infty)\): the layers below \(Y^*\) form a nested chain whose increments lie in \([2e^{16},mY^*]\), \(m\) the largest number of their boundaries through one edge, and those at or above \(Y^*\) one with increments at least \(Y^*\), each of cost at most \(2\); this gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\big((1+(\log mY^*)^{1/4})+(\log N/\log(Y^*/2))^{1/4}\big)\), whose two terms balance near \(\log Y^*=\sqrt{\log N}\) at order \((\log N)^{1/8}\) when \(\log m\le\sqrt{\log N}\); at the endpoints, \(Y^*\) above every height empties the high part and gives that lemma's first clause on the whole chain, \(1+(\log mY_{\max})^{1/4}\) with \(Y_{\max}\) the largest height, and \(Y^*=2e^{16}\) empties the low part and gives its second clause, \((\log N/16)^{1/4}\); so (iii) gives at best order \(\min\{1+(\log mY_{\max})^{1/4},(\log N)^{1/8}\}\), the second when \(\log m\le\sqrt{\log N}\). So these compositions give the goal's order for chains with boundedly many layers, boundedly many height groups or bounded \(\log(mY_{\max})\); otherwise their factor grows with the number \(G\) of dyadic height groups, at least of order \(\min\{(G\ln2)^{1/4},(\log N)^{1/8}\}\) (as \(Y_{\max}\ge2^{G-1}\cdot2e^{16}\) and (ii) gives \(2G\)), or with the number of layers once a group exceeds (d)'s conditions; the lemma removes that factor for up to \(\exp((\log N)^{2/3}\Lambda_B^{1/3})\) large layers, by charging each layer through its own cost.

Suggestion checked. The lead's first instance, \(K\) nested translates by \(\delta_0,2\delta_0,\dots\) (downward) of the cells under one staircase graph of slope at most \(s\), at one height \(y\): each horizontal boundary edge lies on exactly one translate, and a vertical edge between two columns lies on as many translates as that column step has rows, at most \(s+2\); so the multiplicity is at most \(s+2\), and the nested-chain clause of lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) bounds the chain at \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log((s+2)y))^{1/4})\), the goal's order for bounded slope and \(y\). The first instance is decided by the record; the lead bears only where the multiplicity grows (steep or long vertical pieces, or bundles of coinciding boundaries), which the next attempt takes.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: the gap-charged bound for chains with more than \(\exp((\log N)^{2/3}\Lambda_B^{1/3})\) large layers at growing multiplicity, charging each bundle of layers sharing a tube by its spread as lem:band-family-discrepancy (c) does for continuous bands along graphs of bounded slope (the reviewer's ramp lead, its first instance decided above); then the item's owed attempt, to bound the length of an optimal chain. Smallest case. At one level \(y=2e^{16}\) the open instance needs a multiplicity that grows: with every boundary edge on at most \(m\) layers, the nested-chain clause of lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(my))^{1/4})\), the goal's order for bounded \(m\), and a chain whose boundaries all coincide is one layer at height \(Ky\), which lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) at \(K=1\) decides. The lemma's proof, without its condition on \(|B|\), bounds the large layers by \(C_b\sqrt N\big(8M\sqrt{\log N}+4\Lambda^{-1/4}S'(2\log_2(K'/S'))^{3/4}+O(M)\big)\), \(S'\) their total own cost, so the open case also needs \(S'\) of order \(1\). The cost on bundled edges: an edge carrying \(m\) boundaries costs \(\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(my/2)\), which is at most \(m\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y/2)\) times \(\bar\rho=(2\sqrt{\log N}+33)^{1/4}\), about \(1.19(\log N)^{1/8}\), at \(y/2=e^{16}\) and \(m=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\): by the bounds recorded in lem:cut-cell-variance-bound's entry and in (a), \(\psi_4^*(my/2)\le\frac{my}2(2\log\frac{my}2)^{1/4}+1\) and \(\psi_4^*(y/2)\ge\frac y2((\log\frac y2)^{1/4}-1)+1\ge\frac y2\), and \(2\log(my/2)=2\sqrt{\log N}+32\); bundling a fraction \(\varepsilon\) of every boundary multiplies the cost by at most \(1-\varepsilon+\varepsilon\bar\rho\). So the smallest open case is \(K=e^{(\log N)^{3/4}}\) layers at \(y=2e^{16}\) with equal own costs, \(S'=\sum_kc_k=1\), whose boundaries coincide in bundles of \(m=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\) on a fraction \(\varepsilon=1/\bar\rho\), about \(0.84(\log N)^{-1/8}\), of their length and are disjoint elsewhere: its cost is at most \(1\cdot(1+1)=2\) (the computation is the reviewer's correction of an estimate written from \(\psi_4^*\)'s shape); its existence as nested unions of cells with these perimeters and bundles is unchecked here (length and area allow it: \(\sum_kP_k\approx e^{-16}/\delta_0\), against \(2/\delta_0\) edges); the proof's Jensen term is \(4\Lambda^{-1/4}(2\log_2K)^{3/4}\le4.5(\log N)^{9/16}\), above \(\sqrt{\log N}\) by \((\log N)^{1/16}\); the nested clause gives order \((\log N)^{1/8}\), charging every edge at the largest multiplicity although the bundles carry a fraction \(\varepsilon\) of the length, which may be a loss of its bookkeeping rather than of the object (the reviewer's second suggestion below, unverified). With bundles on a constant fraction of the length the cost forces \(S'\) down by \(\rho\), the Jensen term to order \((\log N)^{7/16}\), and the proof decides the chain (the reviewer's observation, checked here by the same computation). It is the single-level open case of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), not one specific to mixed levels, and whether \(D(g)\) itself exceeds \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\) there is the question. Nontrivial because: both recorded mechanisms charge a bundle by its count (Jensen) or its height (the flow), and the ramp lead charges it by its spread. Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b): \(L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\le4L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\), as \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=\sum_ky_k\delta_0P_k\le\sum_k\xi_k\le4\cdot16^{-1/4}\cdot2=4\) by (a); lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(my))^{1/4})\), \((\log N)^{1/8}\) at \(m=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\). Tried. On the instance: lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \(4L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\); the nested-chain clause of lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), order \((\log N)^{1/8}\sqrt{N\log N}\); the per-layer composition (Baseline (i)), \(KC_d\sqrt{N\log N}\); and this entry's own proof steps used alone: the large-layer step with Jensen, \(4.5C_b(\log N)^{9/16}\sqrt N\) beside \(8M\sqrt{N\log N}\), the high and small steps empty on it; each exceeds \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\), so none decides it. On the item's owed attempt, the matching side: thm:bounded-length-chains (read this cycle) bounds every chain of lem:two-graph-chain-duality of length \(\ell\) by \((\ell+1)2Ne^{-t'}\), so "chains of length up to \(e^{t'-t_2}\) have value at most \(2Ne^{-t_2}\)", and at \((4,4)\), \(t_1=\log N\), \(t_2=\sqrt{\log N}\), a refutation "needs a chain longer than \(e^{\lambda\sqrt{\log N}}\)": the owed attempt is exactly the chains beyond that length, which it does not decide; cor:short-chains-per-level (read this cycle) is its case of length at most one; thm:per-level-count-matchings (read this cycle) gives the per-level matchings these bounds start from and no chain bound. Coarse-mean flow obstruction; the lagged flow fails

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed; every pair with an exponent in \((2,\infty]\) · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Create one, maybe?? Does that make sense???? Have you tried??????", on the record having no nonlinear flow whose fine levels correct the coarse ones.

Question. The lagged restoring flow, the item's construction, was said to escape thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction "under the natural assignment of steps", a choice the stand-in review found undersupported. Does any recorded obstruction cover it, and if so, what must a construction do that it does not? The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through a flow whose cost stays bounded at exponents above \(2\); this cycle tests the item's one candidate against the obstruction's mechanism.

Shortest route. The direct route on the primal side is to build the flow nonlinear in the counts whose fine levels correct the coarse ones, the user's pick. Not taken in this entry, which builds no flow: the item's one candidate, the lagged restoring flow, had to be tested first, since building the next candidate on the same design would repeat its failure if it were covered; the test decided that it is covered at every amplitude, and that the next construction must change the means of squares unboundedly many levels coarser, which the next entry builds. The dual-side step the ninth review named, the multi-level corollary of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, was made in the mixed-level chains entry.

Target form. The goal's primal form through the flow bound: a field \(\Phi\) whose cost \(I_k=\int\psi_\alpha(4|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) stays bounded at the curve's pairs; this entry's statements are sufficient conditions for that cost to diverge.

Owed attempt. The lagged restoring flow entry named "first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow"; not made, and dropped: it waits on nothing, because this entry decides the flow by proof (cor:lagged-flow-obstruction), which a measurement at small sizes could not. The item's two entries, read: restoring drift ("Next attempt: a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level") and the lagged restoring flow ("first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow").

Setting

As in thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction (read this cycle, statement and proof): \(N\) i.i.d. uniform points in \([0,1]^2\), depth \(J\) with \(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\), level-\(j\) squares of side \(\rho_j=2^{-j}\), \(\mathcal F_j\) the counts of the squares of levels at most \(j\), \(j_1=J-m\), \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\), a coordinate \(k\), \(E_k(S)=n^{\rm low}_{S,k}-n_S/2\) for a level-\(j\) square \(S\) (the points of its lower half in coordinate \(k\), a level-\((j+1)\) count), a square good when it holds at least half its mean count, \(p_0=2^{-768}\) from lem:block-lower-tail at \(x=1\). A level-by-level field is \(\Phi=\sum_{j<J}\Phi_j\), each step \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable; it is local at level \(j_1\) when for every level-\(j_1\) square \(T\) and \(j\ge j_1\), \(\Phi_j\) on \(T\) is a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points in \(T\).

Theorem (coarse-mean flow obstruction)

Statement. Fix an integer \(r\ge0\) and \(0<\theta<\min(1/1542,\kappa/6160)\). Let \(\Phi\) be a level-by-level field, local at level \(j_1-r\) (for every level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T'\) and every \(j\ge j_1\), \(\Phi_j\) on \(T'\) is a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points in \(T'\); at \(r=0\) this is the locality of the Setting), such that for every \(j_1\le j<J\) and every level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\), \[\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\,dx=\sum_{S\subseteq P,\ S\text{ of level }j}\frac{\rho_j}2\,\epsilon_S\,E_k(S),\] with signs \(\epsilon_S\in\{-1,1\}\) that are \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable; the steps \(j<j_1\) are unrestricted beyond measurability. Then for every \(L>0\), \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\) and \(M\), with probability tending to one, \(I_k\ge M\). At \(r=0\) this is thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction; for every \(r\) the condition holds when \(\Phi_j=\Phi^0_j+\Psi_j\) with \(\Phi^0_j\) a step meeting that theorem's mean condition on the level-\(j\) squares (the dyadic step among them) and \(\Psi_j\) any \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable correction, local at level \(j_1-r\), with \(\int_P\Psi_{j,k}=0\) on every level-\((j-r)\) square, for instance one divergence-free on each level-\((j-r)\) square with zero normal flux on its boundary (piecewise \(C^1\) with continuous normal components), whatever it does to the means of the finer squares.

Proof. It is the proof of thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction run on squares \(r\) levels coarser; each step is written out where it changes. The push of a coarse mean. For a level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\), \(j\ge j_1\), let \(\xi_P=|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}=X_P/(2\cdot4^r\rho_j)\) with \(X_P=\sum_{S\subseteq P}\epsilon_SE_k(S)=\sum_{z\in P}\epsilon_{S(z)}(1\{z\text{ in the lower half of }S(z)\}-\frac12)\), \(S(z)\) the level-\(j\) square of \(z\), as \(|P|=4^r\rho_j^2\). Given \(\mathcal F_j\) the counts \(n_S\) are fixed and the points of each \(S\) are i.i.d. uniform in \(S\), independent across the \(S\); each term is \(\pm\frac12\) with probability \(\frac12\) each, whatever \(\epsilon_{S(z)}\), so \(X_P\) is a sum of \(n_P\) i.i.d. terms of mean \(0\), variance \(\frac14\) and size \(\frac12\), standard deviation \(s=\sqrt{n_P}/2\). If \(P\) is good, \(n_P\ge N|P|/2\) and \(s\ge2^r\rho_j\sqrt{N/8}\). With \(\sigma_P\) an \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable sign, lem:block-lower-tail at \(x=1\) on the terms times \(\sigma_P\) (it needs \(n_P\ge256\), true for large \(N\) since \(n_P\ge\kappa\log N\,4^{J-j+r}/2\)) gives \(P(\sigma_PX_P\ge s\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p_0\), so \(P(\sigma_P\xi_P\ge h_r\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p_0\) with \(h_r=2^{-r}\sqrt{N/32}\le s/(2\cdot4^r\rho_j)\). The walk and the chain. For a level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\) let \(U_j(P)=|P|^{-1}\int_PR_j\), \(R_j=\sum_{i<j}\Phi_{i,k}\), \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable; for each of its four children \(P'\) (level \(j-r+1\), equal areas) put \(\delta_{P'}=U_{j+1}(P')-U_j(P)-\xi_P\), \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable, with \(\sum_{P'}\delta_{P'}=0\) since the mean of \(R_{j+1}=R_j+\Phi_{j,k}\) over \(P\) is the average of its means over the children. With \(\sigma_P=\operatorname{sign}U_j(P)\) (\(+1\) at \(0\)) and \(P'_*\) the first child with \(\sigma_P\delta_{P'}\ge0\), \(|U_{j+1}(P'_*)|\ge|U_j(P)|+\sigma_P\xi_P\). The chain starts at the good level-\((j_1-r)\) squares all of whose ancestors are good, at step \(j=j_1\), and runs through steps \(j_1\le j<J\), keeping \(P'_*\) when \(\sigma_P\xi_P\ge h_r\) and \(P'_*\) is good; its squares at step \(j\) have level \(j-r\ge j_1-r\), so each lies inside one level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T'\), and by induction \(|U_j(P)|\ge(j-j_1)h_r\). With \(m'=m\) steps, the area \(W\) of the chain's last squares (level \(J-r\)) has, as in the theorem, \(\mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge(p_0/4)^{m'}W_{j_1}-Y\), \(Y\) the expected area of bad squares, \(\mathbb EY\le2N^{-\kappa/8}\) by the exceptional counts; \(\mu=(p_0/4)^{m'}\ge N^{-\theta\log_2(4/p_0)}\), so \(\mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge\mu/4\) with probability tending to one when \(\theta\log_2(4/p_0)<\kappa/8\). Many squares. \(W=\sum_{T'}W(T')\) over the level-\((j_1-r)\) squares, each \(W(T')\) a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points of \(T'\) (the chain inside \(T'\) uses \(\Phi_i\) on \(T'\), local at level \(j_1-r\), and \(\Phi_i\), \(i<j_1\), \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\)-measurable), conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) (the point sets of distinct level-\((j_1-r)\) squares are independent given their counts), with variance at most \(\sum_{T'}|T'|^2/4=4^{r-j_1}/4\); Chebyshev gives \(P(W<\mu/8\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\le16\cdot4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2\theta\log_2(4/p_0)}\to0\) for fixed \(r\). Cost. On a last square \(Q\) (level \(J-r\)), \(U_J(Q)\) is the mean of \(\Phi_k\) over \(Q\) and \(|U_J(Q)|\ge m'h_r\); by Jensen for the convex \(z\mapsto\psi_\alpha(4|z|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\), \(I_k\ge W\psi_\alpha(u_N)\), \(u_N=4mh_r/(L\sqrt{N\log N})=2^{-r}m/(\sqrt2L\sqrt{\log N})\ge\frac{2^{-r}\theta}{\sqrt2L}\sqrt{\log N}\), as \(m\ge\theta\log_2N-1\ge\theta\ln N\) for large \(N\) (logarithms natural where not marked; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's proof writes \(m\ge\frac12\theta\log N\) for the same constant, a harmless slip not copied here). For finite \(\alpha>2\), \(u_N^\alpha\) grows like \((\log N)^{\alpha/2}\), faster than \(\theta\log_2(4/p_0)\log N\), so \(I_k\to\infty\); for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(u_N\ge2\) for large \(N\) and \(I_k\ge N^{1-\theta\log_2(4/p_0)}/8\to\infty\). The conditions on \(\theta\) are the theorem's (\(\log_2(4/p_0)=770\)); the factor \(4^r\) is a constant. The particular case: \(\int_P\Phi^0_{j,k}=\sum_{S\subseteq P}\int_S\Phi^0_{j,k}\) gives the sum, and a correction divergence-free on \(P\) with zero normal flux has \(\int_P\Psi_{j,k}=\int_{\partial P}x_k\Psi_j\cdot n-\int_Px_k\operatorname{div}\Psi_j=0\). \(\square\)

Corollary (lagged flow obstruction)

Statement. The lagged restoring flow of ex:lagged-restoring-tails, in its continuous form (the dyadic flow, and after the step of each level \(j\ge1\) the correction \(a\,(\text{main},\text{other})\) on each pair of sibling level-\(j\) squares inside their level-\(j-1\) parent, main \(=\pm2\,\mathrm{tent}\) on the two children in the exchanged coordinate and other \(=4C(y)S(x)\) in the other coordinate, then the same with the coordinates exchanged), with any amplitudes \(a\) that are \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable and, for \(j\ge j_1\), functions of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points in the level-\((j_1-1)\) square containing the pair (the script's damped Newton descent on the pair's quartic cost among them), has \(I_k\to\infty\) in probability for both \(k\), every \(L>0\) and every \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\).

Proof. The theorem with \(r=1\). Count the correction after level \(j\) in step \(j\): it reads the counts of level \(j+1\) (its script's docstring: "After the step of level j >= 1 (which uses the counts of level j+1)"), so the step is \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable; it is local at level \(j_1-1\): at step \(j\ge j_1\) the correction lives on a parent of level \(j-1\ge j_1-1\), inside one level-\((j_1-1)\) square \(T'\), and the descent reads the running field on its pair only, which on \(T'\) is a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) (the steps before \(j_1\)) and the points of \(T'\) (the steps from \(j_1\) on, by induction); at \(j=j_1\) the pair's two level-\(j_1\) squares are distinct, which is why the theorem's locality is taken at level \(j_1-r\) and not \(j_1\). Its mean on each level-\((j-1)\) parent \(P\) vanishes in both coordinates, for every amplitude: quoted from lagged_test.py's unit_shapes, "main = 2.0 * np.concatenate([np.ones(m), -np.ones(m)])[:, None] * T[None, :]" is \(+2T\) on one child and \(-2T\) on the other, summing to zero over the pair, and "other = 4.0 * c[:, None] * S[None, :]" with "S = np.where(u < 0.5, -2.0, 2.0)" sums to zero over each row of a child, \(S\) taking \(-2\) and \(+2\) on equal halves (the child side \(m=G\gg j\) is a power of two at least \(4\) for \(j<J\)); in the continuous form the same integrals vanish, \(\int(\pm2\,\mathrm{tent})=0\) over the pair and \(\int_0^1S=0\). The coordinate-\(2\) exchange is the same with the axes exchanged. The dyadic step meets thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's mean condition on the level-\(j\) squares (that theorem's statement), so step \(j\) meets the theorem's condition at \(r=1\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Theorem: \(r\) fixed: \(h_r=2^{-r}\sqrt{N/32}\), \(u_N\ge2^{-r}\theta\sqrt{\log N}/(\sqrt2L)\) and the factor \(4^r\) in Chebyshev; the proof seems to reach \(r\) growing with \(N\) as long as \(2^{-r}(\log N)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\to\infty\) for finite \(\alpha\) and \(2^{-r}\sqrt{\log N}\to\infty\) at \(\alpha=\infty\) (with \(4^r\) kept below \(N^{1-2\theta-1540\theta}\)), which the statement does not claim. A shift \(r_j\le r_0\) varying with \(j\) is covered at \(r=r_0\): a zero mean on the level-\((j-r_j)\) squares gives a zero mean on the coarser level-\((j-r_0)\) squares, and the dyadic condition sums likewise. The coarse mean condition: the push of a coarse mean, and only there; it asks nothing of a step's means on the finer squares. \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs: the terms \(\epsilon_{S(z)}(\cdot)\) stay i.i.d. given \(\mathcal F_j\). \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurability: \(U_j(P)\), \(\sigma_P\in\mathcal F_j\). Locality at level \(j_1-r\) and the start at step \(j_1\) on the level-\((j_1-r)\) squares: many squares (the chain inside one such square depends on its points only); locality at level \(j_1\) implies it, so the statement is more general than with locality at \(j_1\). The depth bounds and \(\theta\): exceptional counts and Chebyshev, as in the theorem. Not used: that \(\Phi\) is a flow, any bound on a step, any property of a correction beyond its coarse means. Corollary: the correction's zero means on the parents (quoted shapes) and the amplitudes' measurability and locality; nothing about their size or rule.

Degenerate cases. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at \(r=0\) is thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction; at \(r\ge1\) with \(\Psi\equiv0\) it is that theorem again, the condition summed over children; a step with zero mean on every level-\((j-r)\) square violates it (\(X_P\) is not zero) as \(\Phi\equiv0\) must; the condition needs \(j-r\ge0\) at \(j=j_1\), true for fixed \(r\) and large \(N\). cor:lagged-flow-obstruction at amplitude \(0\) is the dyadic flow, covered at \(r=0\) already; at every amplitude it is covered at \(r=1\). The flow of ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails is already covered at \(r=0\), as its registered statement says: "The construction is covered by thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, its corrections staying in the level-j squares".

Nonvacuity. At the curve's pair \((4,4)\), with the dyadic flow of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential at depth \(L_0=260\) (\(\kappa\approx16.5\)) and \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\), as in thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's Nonvacuity (\(\theta<1/1542\approx6.49\cdot10^{-4}\), \(770\theta=0.462<\kappa/8\approx2.06\)): the lagged restoring flow with the script's descent amplitudes, \(r=1\), \(k=1\). Its step \(j\), counted with its correction, changes the means of the level-\(j\) squares by \(\pm a\) times the mean of main over a child, \(2\int_0^1\mathrm{tent}\neq0\) (the tent is nonnegative and not zero), whenever \(a\neq0\), so it then breaks thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's condition at \(r=0\) under that assignment, and counted in step \(j-1\) it is not \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable; whether some other decomposition brings it under \(r=0\) is open (the reviewer's sketch: it would need the amplitudes to be \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable up to a multiple of \(E_k(S)/\rho_j\)), and the theorem at \(r=1\) covers it with no decomposition. Plainest bound. Tried on the witness: thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction under the construction's assignment of steps does not apply (above); a single level's forced mean, \(|\xi_P|\) of order \(\sqrt N\), gives an argument of order \(1/\sqrt{\log N}\) and nothing, as the theorem's own Plainest bound says, since no single-level bound sees the chain of squares; ex:lagged-restoring-tails is a finite check at \(J=6,7\) and decides nothing at large \(N\). The plainest uniform bound over the witness's family, a union over its rules, is not available, the rules ranging over every measurable local amplitude; the theorem's content is the chain of coarse squares, shared by every rule meeting the coarse mean condition.

Baseline. thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, the case \(r=0\). Composed. thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction applied to the lagged flow with each assignment of its correction separately: in step \(j\) it does not apply (the level-\(j\) means change), in step \(j-1\) it does not apply (measurability), and with the correction regrouped it covers the corrections with zero means on the squares one level coarser than the counts they read, which the lagged correction is not; applied through its own proof on squares one level coarser it gives the theorem at \(r=1\), the step this entry adds. lem:conditional-push-obstruction, applied pointwise along a run, needs a push at every state the run reaches, which a restoring correction may break at large \(|R_j|\), so it does not apply without a bound this entry does not have.

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction (read this cycle, statement and full proof) is the case \(r=0\); its proof's steps are reused, the push now taken over the \(n_P\) points of a coarse square, with the \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs absorbed because each term is symmetric. Its Hypotheses paragraph: "The mean condition: the push of a square mean, and only there". The coarse version is not stated in the record; the search "coarse square mean shifted levels parent square dyadic mean descendants chain push obstruction lagged" returned thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, ex:rule-conditional-pushes, lem:conditional-push-obstruction, ex:lagged-restoring-tails and ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails. lem:conditional-push-obstruction (read this cycle) is the pointwise form, neither more general than the theorem nor a special case of it. The restoring drift entry's design note said of the lagged correction "other decompositions are not excluded"; this entry does not exclude them, and needs none. New here: the theorem for every fixed \(r\), and the corollary that the lagged restoring flow fails at every exponent above \(2\).

Refinement checked. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at \(r=0\) against thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction: the same depth conditions (\(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\)), the same \(\theta\) range (\(0<\theta<\min(1/1542,\kappa/6160)\)), the same mean condition (\(\int_S\Phi_{j,k}=\frac{\rho_j}2\epsilon_SE_k(S)\) on every level-\(j\) square, \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs, \(j_1\le j<J\)), the same measurability, and locality at level \(j_1-0=j_1\), the theorem's own; the conclusion, \(I_k\) exceeding every constant with probability tending to one at every \(L>0\) and \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\), is the same. So the new statement at \(r=0\) implies the old, and for \(r\ge1\) it covers fields the old does not state.

General statement. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, for every fixed \(r\ge0\), every field meeting its coarse mean condition, every \(L>0\) and every \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\); cor:lagged-flow-obstruction for every measurable, local amplitude rule.

New mathematics. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction: a level-by-level field, local at level \(j_1-r\), whose step \(j\) has on every square \(r\) levels coarser the sum of the dyadic means of its level-\(j\) descendants (signs \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable), \(r\) fixed, has cost exceeding every constant with probability tending to one at every \(L>0\) and every \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\); so does every dyadic-based field whose corrections, counted in the step whose counts they read, have zero mean on the squares a fixed number of levels coarser. cor:lagged-flow-obstruction: the lagged restoring flow, with any measurable local amplitudes, is such a field at \(r=1\); its lighter tails at \(J=6,7\) (ex:lagged-restoring-tails) are not those of a flow with bounded cost.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy; the item's one candidate construction is excluded. Bearing.
