Coarse restoration: where the cost moves

17 October 2026 · Attempt, no result proved; hand analysis labelled untested · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The attempt proved no statement; the living sections already state the obstructions it rests on and the next step names the route review.

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Create one, maybe?? Does that make sense???? Have you tried??????", on the record having no nonlinear flow whose fine levels correct the coarse ones.

Question. The coarse-mean obstruction entry showed that a construction must change the means of squares unboundedly many levels coarser than the counts it reads. Can a coarse-restoring correction, after each step exchanging sibling means at every coarser level, keep its own cost bounded? The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through a flow of bounded cost at exponents above \(2\).

Shortest route. The direct route on the primal side is to build the flow nonlinear in the counts whose fine levels correct the coarse ones, the user's pick; this entry takes it, as an attempt by hand on the construction's smallest instance before any script, and stops where the hand analysis shows the construction's free choice to be the goal's own minimization.

Target form. The goal's primal form through the flow bound: a field \(\Phi\) with \(\int\psi_\alpha(4|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) bounded at the curve's pairs.

Owed attempt. The coarse-mean obstruction entry named "a coarse-restoring construction, a correction after each level \(j\) that shifts the means of squares \(r_j\) levels coarser with \(r_j\) unbounded"; made here by hand, with the outcome below; no script was written, because the hand analysis decided what the script would have measured (the free choice is the leg's placement, below). The item's earlier entries, read: restoring drift ("Next attempt: a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level"), lagged restoring flow ("first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow") and the coarse-mean obstruction entry above.

Attempt

Where the coarse pushes can be cancelled. A square's mean changes only through flux across its boundary (the moment identity \(\int_Q\Phi_k=\int_{\partial Q}(x_k-c_k)\Phi\cdot n-\int_Q(x_k-c_k)\operatorname{div}\Phi\), the integration by parts of thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction's proof). An exchange between sibling level-\(i\) squares moves flux across their shared side, so exchanges at every level \(i\le j\) after step \(j\) can change the mean of every square except the root's: no square mean is invariant under the construction, and thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, which needs a fixed shift, does not apply to it. The push of step \(j\) on a level-\(i\) square has standard deviation of order \(2^{-(j-i)}\sqrt N\) (the coarse push of that theorem's proof at \(r=j-i\)), so cancelling all of them needs exchange amplitudes that decay geometrically in \(j-i\), and per step a geometric sum of order \(\sqrt N\) (by hand; the legs' sizes are below).

Where the cost moves. An exchange in coordinate \(1\) on a stacked pair has a leg in coordinate \(2\): by lem:sibling-exchange-leg, shifting the lower square's coordinate-\(1\) mean by \(\mu\) needs \((1/\rho)\int|w_2|\ge2|\mu|\) on the shared side. In the lagged script's shapes the leg is "other = 4.0 * c[:, None] * S[None, :]", with zero coordinate-\(2\) mean over each pair, so the coordinate-\(2\) square means do not see it, while pointwise its values are of order \(|\mu|\). At a point, the legs of all levels \(i\) add in coordinate \(2\), with signs set by the coordinate-\(1\) mean differences of the pairs containing it. Untested hypothesis: with fixed-shape legs and those signs independent across levels, the coordinate-\(2\) field at a point is a sum of about \(m\) terms of order \(\sqrt N\) that align with probability \(p^m=N^{-a}\), the pointwise mechanism of lem:conditional-push-obstruction in the other coordinate, so the cost diverges. If the amplitudes are linear in the running field (an exact equalizer), the whole flow is linear in the counts and thm:linear-flow-obstruction already covers it at every pair with both exponents finite and above \(2\) (its statement: "every linear flow rule W ... fixed before the points").

The free choice. lem:sibling-exchange-leg fixes only first moments: for each horizontal line in the pair, \(\int(x-c)w_2\,dx\) equals \(F(y)=\int_{B_y}w_1\). The leg's placement along each line is free, so a leg can be routed where the running coordinate-\(2\) field \(R_2\) has the opposite sign. Smallest case, one pair, minimizing the coordinate-\(2\) quartic alone: with the total \(T=R_2+w_2\) on a line and the constraint \(\int(x-c)T=F(y)+\int(x-c)R_2\), Lagrange's condition \(4T^3=\lambda(x-c)\) gives \(T=\kappa(x-c)^{1/3}\): the leg absorbs \(R_2\) entirely except its first moment, so \(w_2=T-R_2\) has the size of \(R_2\) itself, and its partner \(w_1=-\int\partial_2w_2\,dx\) (zero flux at the pair's side) is as large as \(R_2\)'s variation across lines. Minimizing one coordinate moves the cost to the other; the placement must minimize both coordinates' costs jointly. Made fully joint over all pairs and levels, that minimization is the minimum-cost flow, whose value lem:grid-flow-duality identifies with the penalized discrete functional: "the cheapest flow on the cells costs exactly the penalized discrete functional" (this notebook's Where we stand, from that lemma), the dual of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy's discrete form. So the construction's free choice, made optimally, is the goal's own minimization, and a construction must instead fix a restricted rule whose cost it can bound.

Plainest bound. On the smallest case, one exchange of amplitude \(\mu\): the correction alone costs at least \((\rho^2/2)\psi(c|\mu|)\) (the coarse-mean obstruction entry's Smallest case); the one-coordinate placement above has no bound beyond the size of \(R_2\). A computation of the minimum-cost flow at reachable sizes would decide nothing: at \((4,4)\) the record's losses are powers of \(\log N\) such as \((\log N)^{1/8}\), which change by about \(7\%\) over \(\log N\) from \(10\) to \(17\) (\((17/10)^{1/8}=1.069\)), and COMPUTATION_RULES.md says "a series whose predicted difference is a power of \(\log N\) over a few units of \(\log N\) decides nothing".

General statement. The cycle tests whether thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, proved for every fixed shift \(r\) (a field local at level \(j_1-r\) whose step \(j\) has on every level-\((j-r)\) square the sum of the dyadic means of its level-\(j\) descendants, with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs, has cost exceeding every constant at every \(L>0\) and \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\)), extends to corrections at unbounded shifts; no extension or counterexample was proved.

New mathematics. No result was proved. By hand, unreviewed: coarse exchanges at every level can move every square mean except the root's, so no fixed-shift obstruction covers them; their cost moves to the other coordinate's legs, invisible to the square means; a leg's placement is free up to its first moments, and placing it to minimize one coordinate moves the cost to the other, while the fully joint placement is the goal's own minimum-cost flow.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy. Bearing. At the goal's own parameters it gives nothing: no statement was proved. The cycle was spent on the construction the user picked because a coarse-restoring correction was the one design the coarse-mean obstruction left open; it could have given a candidate outside every recorded obstruction, and it shows instead that the design's free choice must be a restricted rule, since optimizing it fully is the goal itself.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: a restricted leg rule with a provable cost, legs placed by a fixed nonlinear rule of the running field in the other coordinate (for instance on the half of the side where \(R_2\) has the opposite sign), so that lem:restoring-drift-tail can be applied to the pointwise coordinate-\(2\) sum, its drift supplied by the legs; first prove the leg rule's drift bound on one pair. Smallest case. One pair and one leg on the half of the shared side where \(R_2\) has the opposite sign of the leg: the leg then reduces \(|R_2|\) on that half by its own size, of order \(|\mu|\), and leaves the other half; the drift at a point is of order \(|\mu|\) when the point lies on the chosen half and \(0\) otherwise, so the drift lemma's condition \(|d(r)|\ge\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) holds only on half the points, and whether a point lies on the chosen half is decided by the coarser field, not by the point's own \(R_2\). Nontrivial because: the drift must act on each point's own running value, while a leg acts on a half-side at once. Plainest bound. lem:restoring-drift-tail applies only when every step has the drift at the point; with a drift on half the points at each step, a point escapes the drift at about half the steps, and the lemma gives nothing as stated. Own statements. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction covers bounded shifts only and decides nothing about the leg rule; cor:lagged-flow-obstruction excludes the lagged design; lem:sibling-exchange-leg fixes the legs' first moments and nothing else; lem:conditional-push-obstruction would cover the leg rule if its pointwise pushes keep a fixed probability at every state, which the rule is designed to break; thm:linear-flow-obstruction covers linear amplitude rules only; lem:restoring-drift-tail is the target bound; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction is the case \(r=0\) of the coarse-mean theorem and covers the rule's level-\(j\) steps only when they keep the dyadic means, which the coarse exchanges do not; ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails is a design inside the level-\(j\) squares, already covered, and decides nothing about legs at coarse sides; thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction (read this cycle) concerns hierarchical transports whose targets follow their count splits, not dyadic-based flows, so it does not decide the leg rule, though its common push of cell means is again the mechanism the rule must escape. Record search. "flow sup norm lower bound Leighton Shor every flow maximum field equalize square means all levels both coordinates dipole moment boundary", "leg placement position aware routing flux crossing side chosen where running field opposite sign two choice exits first moment constraint" and "minimum cost flow convex optimal numerical cost growth N psi_4 grid optimizer computed min-cost penalized functional value", which returned thm:per-level-count-matchings, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, lem:flow-coarea-level-bound, lem:discrete-flow-bound, ex:lagged-restoring-tails, ex:greedy-circulation-tails, ex:simultaneous-rule-tails, ex:rule-conditional-pushes, lem:sibling-exchange-leg, lem:grid-flow-duality, lem:straight-cut-forced-flux, lem:flow-matching-bound, lem:hopf-lax-matching-bound and lem:band-overlap-penalty; none computes a minimum-cost flow; ex:simultaneous-rule-tails chooses each square's crossing profiles "by Newton's method to minimize the quartic load of both coordinates given the coarser field", at the square's own level, a rule thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction covers, and ex:greedy-circulation-tails adds a circulation per square, also inside the square; none places the legs of coarse exchanges by the running field.

  • The lagged flow's divergence control, whose flipped-leg positive control gave 0.066 to 0.100 against a committed threshold of 0.2: not attempted in this cycle; the lagged design is excluded by cor:lagged-flow-obstruction, so the check now bears only on whether ex:lagged-restoring-tails' statement that the correction is divergence-free was shown at the committed sensitivity, a record question that waits for a cycle on that check. Follow-up. Continuing.

Where we stand. Six research entries since the ninth review: linear flows (thm:linear-flow-obstruction), restoring drift (ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails, lem:restoring-drift-tail, lem:sibling-exchange-leg), the lagged restoring flow (ex:lagged-restoring-tails), mixed-level chains (lem:multilevel-chain-bound), the coarse-mean obstruction (thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, cor:lagged-flow-obstruction) and coarse restoration (an attempt, no statement). The period proves: no flow rule linear in the counts, fixed before the points, has flow-bound value \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one at pairs with both exponents finite and above \(2\); a level-by-level field, \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable at step \(j\) and local at level \(j_1-r\), whose step \(j\) has on every square \(r\) levels coarser the sum of the dyadic means of its level-\(j\) descendants with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs, has cost exceeding every constant with probability tending to one at every exponent in \((2,\infty]\), for each fixed \(r\), the lagged restoring flow among them; and, on the dual side at \((4,4)\), the class bound for nested chains at mixed heights under lem:multilevel-chain-bound's conditions on its small and large layers (at most \(N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) small layers and large layers \(B\) with \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\)).

Open statements. ultimate-matching and conjugate-class-discrepancy open; shor-exponential and grid-discrepancy open and untouched. The line's open-item count is \(4\), as at the review twelve research entries back, so this review is goal-level.

The line's general claim. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy on the curve in its discrete form, which by lem:grid-flow-duality (c), (d) is a bound on the minimal edge flow cost.

What the goal needs. That discrete bound at every pair of the curve, or a matching built directly; equivalently a flow carrying the cell counts to the background at flow-bound cost of order \(N\), with one universal \(L\).

The six entries

Linear flows: no rule linear in the counts, fixed before the points, has flow-bound value \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one at any pair with both exponents finite and above \(2\). Restoring drift: a pointwise restoring drift \(d(r)\ge\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) gives \(\psi_\alpha\)-type tails to a running sum (lem:restoring-drift-tail), and an exchange between siblings costs a leg of at least twice its shift (lem:sibling-exchange-leg); the paired drift tested amplified the tails. Lagged restoring flow: lighter per-point tails at \(J=6,7\) below \(3.5\) standard deviations, a finite check. Mixed-level chains: lem:multilevel-chain-bound, at \((4,4)\), the class bound at the goal's order for nested chains at mixed heights \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\) with large layers \(B\) under \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\). Coarse-mean obstruction: thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction for every fixed shift \(r\), and the lagged flow is its case \(r=1\) (cor:lagged-flow-obstruction). Coarse restoration: by hand, exchanges at every level can move every square mean but the root's, their cost moves to the other coordinate's legs, and the fully joint leg placement is the minimum-cost flow itself.

Falsification attempt. Can the chain of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction refute the core statement through a class function? The discrepancy \(\int G\,d(\mu_X-\mu_Y)=\int\nabla G\cdot\Phi\) is the same for every flow \(\Phi\) and every Lipschitz \(G\); the chain, though, is chosen from one flow's own running means, so a field \(c\,e_k\) on the chain's last squares is a statement about that flow and is not a gradient, and a \(G\) built on the chain's squares must be fixed before any flow. Such a \(G\), rising across the chain's nested squares, has nested superlevel sets; the stage-two reviewer observes (unverified in detail) that with few steep, well-separated values lem:multilevel-chain-bound (c) bounds its discrepancy by \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\) at \((4,4)\). I checked its layer-count conditions only: \(K\approx\theta\log N\) layers are fewer than \(N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) and than \(e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\); its height condition \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\) restricts which chain functions it covers. The attempt stops there; the line is not refuted.

Assessment of this line. The primal side has narrowed, this period, to two properties of a flow with flow-bound value \(O(N)\): at pairs with both exponents finite and above \(2\) it is not given by a rule linear in the counts (thm:linear-flow-obstruction), and if it is level-by-level, adapted and local it must change the means of squares at a shift \(r\) beyond the reach of the coarse-mean proof, which by this review's Attempt and its reviewer reaches every \(r\le r^*-c_0\), \(r^*=(\frac12-\frac1\alpha)\log_2\log N\), \(c_0\) a constant (\(10.92\) levels at \(\alpha=4\), \(L=1\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\)). At \((4,4)\) squares \(r^*\) levels above the finest have the Leighton–Shor side \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\); at another pair, coordinate \(k\) gives side \((\log N)^{1-1/\alpha_k}/\sqrt N\), which matches the curve's box there only at \(\alpha_k=4\). The coarse restoration attempt showed that optimizing such corrections jointly is the goal's own minimization, and the stage-two reviewer observed that the legs of all levels coarser than the cells are the edge fluxes of a flow on the cells: a construction must fix a coarse rule on the Leighton–Shor cells. The dual side added the multi-level chain bound and leaves chains of many layers at growing multiplicity. The core statement keeps its evidence.

Obstacle

On the primal side, at \((4,4)\), the line is stuck at a flow on the cells of side about \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) (shift \(r\ge r^*-c_0\)) whose per-point displacement has \(\psi_4\) tails at scale \(s\): thm:linear-flow-obstruction shows that no linear rule there has flow-bound value \(O(N)\) with probability tending to one, thm:position-blind-cell-exits exits blind to position, thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction hierarchical rank-cut transports; no construction exists, and no lemma yet says that such a coarse flow, composed with a flow inside the cells, gives the goal. On the dual side it is stuck where the seventh review put it: chains of many layers, now at growing multiplicity of coinciding boundaries.

  • conjugate-class-discrepancy: unchanged; five cycles on its primal form, one on its dual (lem:multilevel-chain-bound).
  • shor-exponential: unchanged; no cycle.
  • grid-discrepancy: unchanged; no cycle.

Architecture review

Necessary target. At every pair of the curve, with probability tending to one, one matching with \(\sum_i\exp[(|X^j_i-Y^j_{\pi(i)}|/s)^{\alpha_j}]\le2N\) for both \(j\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L\) universal; evenly spread \(Y\) suffice by lem:two-sample-matching-transfer. Downstream. Through lem:grid-flow-duality (c) the discrete class bound on grids of side \(\delta\le s/32\) gives that endpoint at every pair with \(\alpha\in[1,\infty]^2\); through its (d) it is a minimal flow cost; thm:linear-flow-obstruction, thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction (with thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction its case \(r=0\)) and cor:lagged-flow-obstruction show that linear rules and the adapted local fields they describe have flow-bound value not \(O(N)\) above exponent \(2\); lem:multilevel-chain-bound gives the class bound on a subclass at \((4,4)\); thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential gives the endpoint at \((2,2)\), off the curve; weaker than the goal.

Extra requirements. The route demands one flow where the goal needs one matching, justified up to tube density (lem:grid-flow-duality (d), lem:tube-density-converse), and it demands that flow on cells of side at most \(s/32\), a demand of lem:grid-flow-duality (c)'s smearing error, not of the goal: a matching may be composed from a flow on coarser cells and matchings inside them. The period's constructions added two demands the goal does not make: corrections at bounded shift (the lagged flow, the paired drift), excluded by thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, and corrections whose legs are optimized jointly, which is the goal itself (the coarse restoration attempt); both are dropped, and the fine-cell demand is weakened: the next entry replaces the smearing error by the cost of a matching inside cells of the Leighton–Shor side.

Independent alternative. Stage one (blind report; brief and the thread's 75 registered statements in blind/ beside it; stage two's record), given the goal and the registered statements only. Its answers: the hardness is that every per-coordinate consequence holds alone while the constructions on record add about \(\log N\) independent level contributions, Gaussian at variance \(N\log N\); the obstructions leave open nonlinear routing not hierarchical at a fixed lag, matchings far from every flow, and refutations by long chains; its architecture is a two-scale matching, a Leighton–Shor-type matching between coarse cells of side \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) by a nonlinear, position-aware rule that cancels coarse means, then a dyadic flow inside each cell over about \(\frac14\log_2\log N\) levels, whose Gaussian part has variance \(N\log\log N\) (its estimate, unverified); its first lemma, the coarse-mean obstruction rerun with \(r(N)\) free; its most informative weaker statement, the discrete class bound at \((4,4)\). Comparison with the route: its architecture is the route's next construction, placed by a threshold the route had marked "not claimed" (the coarse-mean entry's Hypotheses: "the proof seems to reach \(r\) growing with \(N\) as long as \(2^{-r}(\log N)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\to\infty\)") and never named as a next step; its process audit names that as orbiting, rightly (Process assessment). Stage two (research/results/ultimate_matching_tenth_review_20261017/review.txt) placed its first lemma inside this review's Attempt and moved the open step to the composition of the two scales.

Rank normalization. Does not apply: no step of the line compares dimensions or ranks; its quantities are costs and discrepancies.

Decision. Core: conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy stays the core statement, in its discrete form, and the line is retained. The next research entry, on restoring-drift-construction, the user's pick, proves lemma-first the two-scale composition at \((4,4)\) that the stage-two reviewer sketched (unverified until that entry): the matching cost bounded, at constant \(3\) in \(L\) by convexity of \(\psi_4\), by the inner transports \(X\to\nu_X\) and \(\nu_Y\to Y\) inside cells of side about \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\) and a flow between the cell-smeared measures, glued into one plan between the two \(N\)-point measures, a permutation then costing no more by Birkhoff's theorem; the inner term bounded in expectation by an annealed per-point tail (Bernstein inside a cell) and in probability by Markov's inequality, the cells being conditionally independent given their counts, with no uniformity over cells. It registers, as a corollary, the extension of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction to shifts \(r\le r^*-c_0\), which this review's Attempt gives (reviewer: scheduling it first would be one more exclusion). The construction the entries after it build and test: a flow on the grid of those cells, nonlinear in the cell counts, whose edge fluxes are the legs of every coarser exchange (the stage-two reviewer's observation), first the cells' dyadic flow corrected at every coarser level by a restoring drift of lem:restoring-drift-tail's form on the cell means, its test the tails of its normalized per-edge loads against \(\psi_4\) at scale \(s\), with thm:linear-flow-obstruction's linear rules as the baseline it must beat; on the dual side the retained test below at mesh \(2^{-l_1}\). No order the user set for the goal's statements is changed. A branch's artefact: \(r^*\le3.4\) for \(\log N\le10^4\), and the coarse-mean proof's cost step is in force only for \(\ln N>1.4\cdot10^{13}\) at \(\alpha=4\), \(L=1\), a threshold of the proof's bookkeeping (\(p_0=2^{-768}\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\)) and not of the obstruction (instance_check.txt), so no computation at reachable sizes bears on the shift threshold; the decision rests on proofs.

Decisive test. Test disposition. Retained exploratory: the seventh review's test, the gap-charged bound for nested chains of many layers fitted to the points, with its outcomes (A) the bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\); retained by the eighth and ninth reviews; no new mechanism is claimed. Its open instance moves: lem:multilevel-chain-bound now covers nested chains at \((4,4)\) with heights \(y_k\ge2e^{16}\), at most \(N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2\) small layers and large layers \(B\) with \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\), so the open instance is chains with more large layers than that, or with small layers beyond that count; and the composition of the Decision makes its mesh \(2^{-l_1}\) the one that decides the goal at \((4,4)\). Two tests this review first posed are answered or made lemmas: the extension of the coarse-mean proof to growing shifts (Attempt below), and the two-scale composition, whose outcomes the stage-two reviewer found decided in a few lines by gluing with Birkhoff's theorem and by an annealed Bernstein bound (unverified until the next entry). "coarse square mean shifted levels parent square dyadic mean descendants chain push obstruction lagged growing shift" returned cor:lagged-flow-obstruction, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, ex:rule-conditional-pushes, ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails, thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction and lem:conditional-push-obstruction, none at a growing shift (the coarse-mean entry's Hypotheses paragraph names the range unclaimed); "two scale matching Leighton Shor cells coarse matching nonlinear position aware dyadic inside cells log log N levels" returned lem:local-factor-discrepancy, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, lem:guided-chain-bound, lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor and lem:anisotropic-leighton-shor-bound: the Leighton–Shor scale is the dual side's recorded mesh, and none builds a matching or flow in two scales; the stage-two reviewer's "coarse grid flow cells fine matching inside cells composition smearing error Leighton-Shor mesh" found no composition lemma. Trivial cases. A chain of one layer is lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d)'s single set; a chain whose layers coincide is one layer of summed height; relabelling the layers or adding an empty one changes neither the cost nor the discrepancy; the instance's own system has no degree-one structure that decides it. Power. lem:multilevel-chain-bound decides chains under its conditions; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) decides, at \((4,4)\) and mesh at most \(2^{-l_1}\), grid functions whose increments are \(0\) or of slope at least \(y\ge N^c\), with discrepancy at most \(8\cdot3^{1/4}c^{-1/4}L\sqrt{N\log N}\); lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) gives nested chains \(y\delta_0\sum_k1_{A_k}\) of one height \(y\), each inner edge on at most \(m\) boundaries and cost at most \(2\), the bound \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(my))^{1/4})\), which is outcome (C) wherever \(my\le(\log N)^K\), so the open instance is chains with \(my\) beyond every power of \(\log N\) or with heights of mixed size; the test's instance lies within the goal's parameter window, the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve at every large \(N\), and no computation reaches the sizes where these counts separate. Instance check. At \(\ln N=100\): lem:multilevel-chain-bound allows \(\log|B|\le(\ln N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\), at least \(21.5\cdot16^{1/3}=21.5\cdot2.52\) since \(y_B\ge2e^{16}\), and at most \(N^{1/6}/(\log N)^2=e^{16.7}/10^4\approx e^{7.5}\) small layers, against the seventh review's \(N^{1/7}=e^{14.3}\) layers; \((\ln N)^{2/3}<\ln N/7\) once \(\ln N>343\), the factor \(2.52\) moving that crossing to larger \(N\); a chain of cost at most \(2\) whose layers each have at least one cell's perimeter has at most about \(1/\delta_0^2\le N/(\kappa^2\log N)\) layers. For the composition, at \(\ln N=100\) and \(L=1\): \(\ell/s=3.16\) and \((\ell/s)^4=100=\ln N/L^4\), so a smearing term \(\psi_4(\ell/s)\) per point would be \(e^{100}\), which is why the inner transport replaces it (instance_check.txt). Attempt. On the retained test, lem:multilevel-chain-bound's proof was read at the open instance from its registered assessment: it runs on the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, which holds for every union of cells at once, splits a chain by layer through the superadditivity of \(\psi^*_4\), bounds each large layer by that event's per-layer bound with its own logarithmic factor, and sums by "Jensen for the concave \(c(2\log_2(1/c))^{3/4}\) over the costs"; the sum is about \((\log|B|)^{3/4}(\log y)^{-1/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\), and requiring it at most \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) times a constant is the condition on \(B\). It stops there because each layer is charged separately, correlations between layers discarded; probability plays no part (stage-two reviewer, checked against the assessment). On the composition, the reviewer's gluing and annealed bound are taken to the next entry. On the coarse-mean extension, every step of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's proof holds for \(r=r(N)\) (the push \(h_r\), \(n_P\ge256\), \(\mu\) independent of \(r\), Chebyshev's \(4^r\) allowed up to almost a power of \(N\)), and the cost step, \(u_N^\alpha-a\ln N=\ln N\,(C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}-a)\) with \(C=(\theta/(\sqrt2L))^\alpha\), \(a=770\theta\), diverges when \(r\le r^*-c_0-\varepsilon\), \(c_0=\log_2(a/C)/\alpha\) (\(10.92\) levels at \(\alpha=4\), \(L=1\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\)), and at \(\alpha=\infty\) when \(r\le\frac12\log_2\ln N-\log_2(2\sqrt2L/\theta)-\varepsilon\); beyond that this proof stops, which does not show that a construction escapes. A few lines decide it, so it is the next entry's corollary, not a test.

Process assessment. Two habits, each met twice in this review: calling a condition exact, or a step open, from the shape of a result before working its plain tools (the growth condition, the inner-stage uniformity, the coupling outcome), and naming a recorded proof's mechanism from memory of its kind instead of its registered assessment (the multilevel bound's stop). Prevention. For the first, a check: tools/draft_claim_sentences.py now asks a "converse:" answer of every summing-up or test sentence that calls a condition exact, and tools/notebook-append.py refuses the draft without it (commit "draft_claim_sentences.py: a condition called exact is answered on a "converse:" line"; it flags both exposing sentences, and 119 sentences in 108 of 2550 past articles, research/provenance/framework/converse-rows-replay-20261017.txt); and a rule, AGENTS.md's Order of work, that a step called open first meets the plainest tools of its kind, their outcome written. For the second, the rule that a cited lemma is applied through its proof already covers it and was not followed; the Attempt's sentence is rewritten from the registered assessment.

Meta. Both habits close a step on a picture of it, the shape of a condition or the kind of a proof, and leave the working to the reviewer, so that four review rounds did what a draft read against its sources would have done in one. The same habit gave the earlier entries' "no decomposition covers it" and the corollary checked everywhere but its boundary. The change in how I work is in AGENTS.md's Order of work (commit "AGENTS.md: a step called open first meets the plainest tools of its kind"): before a stop, an exactness or an outcome is written, the plainest tools of its kind are run on it and the outcome written beside it. The stand-in review's right objections (1), (2) and (5) come from the same habit at the level of replies and tools: a refusal answered from its quoted surface, and a reply's claim written before its check; their changes are the two tool commits named in the Review paragraph.

Flows on coarse cells suffice at finite exponents

17 October 2026 · Working proofs, reviewed in two rounds; a reduction, goal unchanged · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The reduction leaves the living sections' statements true; Where we stand is at its word limit and the entry is linked from the next step

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Create one, maybe?? Does that make sense???? Have you tried??????", on the record having no nonlinear flow whose fine levels correct the coarse ones.

Question. The tenth review decided that this entry prove lemma-first a two-scale composition: does a flow between measures smeared over cells of side about \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), with what happens inside the cells, give the goal at \((4,4)\)? The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at the curve's pairs through a flow of bounded cost; the composition would let a construction work on cells and ignore the finest levels. The item's earlier entries, read: restoring drift ("Next attempt: a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level"), lagged restoring flow ("first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow"), coarse means ("a coarse-restoring construction, a correction after each level") and coarse restoration.

Shortest route. The review named it: the composition lemma, then a nonlinear flow on the cells. This entry takes the first step and finds it shorter than the review's sketch: no gluing and no Birkhoff step are needed, because the recorded flow bound applies to the sum of the inner dyadic flow and any coarse flow, and the inner part costs nothing in the limit by the recorded dyadic proof's own tail estimate, run on the inner levels with a cap that its event \(E_1\) gives.

Target form. The goal's primal form through the flow bound: a field \(\Phi\) carrying the smeared configuration to the uniform measure with \(\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(c|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) bounded, at pairs of the curve with finite exponents.

Owed attempt. The item's latest follow-up (coarse restoration) named "a restricted leg rule with a provable cost, legs placed by a fixed nonlinear rule of the running field in the other coordinate"; another came first: the tenth review's Decision, after its reviewer observed that the legs of all levels coarser than the cells are the edge fluxes of a flow on the cells, scheduled the composition first, so that the leg rule is posed on the cells this entry fixes; it is the Follow-up's next attempt below.

Architecture test. Not decided. The tenth review retained the seventh review's chain test (outcomes (A) the bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\)); none of them occurred in this entry, which took the review's Decision first, the composition, and does not touch nested chains.

General statement. thm:cell-scale-reduction: for exponents \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in[2,\infty)\), a fixed \(\beta\ge\frac12\) with \((\beta-\frac12)(\max_k\alpha_k-2)<1\), \(L\ge260\) and dyadic cell sides \(\ell\le(\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\), with probability tending to one the minimal matching cost is at most \(\frac N8\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(8|\Phi_{c,k}|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))+0.03N\) for every bounded field \(\Phi_c\) carrying the cell-smeared \(X\) to \(N\) times Lebesgue measure; so the goal at such a pair follows from such a \(\Phi_c\) with that integral at most \(7\).

Setting. As in thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's proof (read this cycle): \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \(\Omega=[0,1]^2\), \(Y\) evenly spread, \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\) (natural logarithms), \(\psi_\alpha(u)=e^{u^\alpha}-1\), \(C(z)=\sum_k\psi_{\alpha_k}(|z_k|/s)\), \(h=\frac14\); \(J\) the least integer with \(\delta=2^{-J}\le s/32\), so \(\delta\ge s/64\); \(\rho_j=2^{-j}\); \(m(S)\) the number of \(X_i\) in a dyadic square \(S\); \(E_1\): every dyadic square of level \(j\le J\) has \(N|S|/2\le m(S)\le2N|S|\), \(P(E_1)\to1\) for \(L\ge260\); \(\nu^{\rho}_X\): each \(X_i\) smeared uniformly over its dyadic square of side \(\rho\); \(\nu_Y=N\,\mathrm{Leb}\), each \(Y_j\) smeared over its rectangle (within \(20/\sqrt N\)); \(\Phi_j=\sum_S\Phi^S\) the dyadic square flows of that proof, \(\Phi^S\) built from the child excesses \(e_c=m(S_c)-m(S)/4\) of a level-\(j\) square \(S\).

Theorem (cell-scale reduction). Let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in[2,\infty)\), \(\beta\ge\frac12\) fixed (independent of \(N\)) with \((\beta-\frac12)(\max_k\alpha_k-2)<1\), \(L\ge260\), and for each \(N\) let \(j_c\le J\) with \(\ell=2^{-j_c}\le(\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\). With probability tending to one: for every bounded field \(\Phi_c\) on \(\Omega\) with \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi_c=\int g\,d(\nu^{\ell}_X-\nu_Y)\) for every Lipschitz \(g\), \[\min_\pi\sum_{i\le N}\sum_k\psi_{\alpha_k}\Big(\frac{|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|}s\Big)\le\frac N8\sum_k\int_\Omega\psi_{\alpha_k}\Big(\frac{8|\Phi_{c,k}|}{L\sqrt{N\log N}}\Big)dx+0.03N.\] In particular, if with probability tending to one such a \(\Phi_c\) exists with \(\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(8|\Phi_{c,k}|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\le7\), the conclusion of conj:ultimate-matching holds at \(\alpha\) with the constant \(L\) (each coordinate's sum of \(\psi\) at most \(0.905N\), its sum of exponentials at most \(2N\)). At \((4,4)\) the condition is \(\beta<1\): cells of side \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), the Leighton–Shor side, and coarser ones up to \((\log N)^{1-\varepsilon}/\sqrt N\) are allowed.

Proof. The inner flow. Put \(m'=J-j_c\) and \(\Phi_{\rm in}=\sum_{j_c\le j<J}\Phi_j\). The telescoping identity of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's proof, run over the levels \(j_c\le j<J\) only, gives \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi_{\rm in}=\int g\,d(\nu^{\delta}_X-\nu^{\ell}_X)\): each level moves the smearing of the points from their level-\(j\) squares to their level-\((j+1)\) squares. So \(\Phi=\Phi_{\rm in}+\Phi_c\) satisfies \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi=\int g\,d(\nu^\delta_X-\nu_Y)\). The flow bound. On \(E_1\) the density of \(\nu^\delta_X\) is at least \(N/2\); lem:flow-matching-bound (2) with \(\lambda=N/2\), \(\lambda'=N/4\), \(h=\frac14\), \(\delta_X=\delta\), \(\delta_Y=20/\sqrt N\) gives cost at most \(\frac N4\int C(4\Phi/N)+\frac N4\sum_k[\psi_{\alpha_k}(4\delta/s)+\psi_{\alpha_k}(80/(L\sqrt{\log N}))]\); with \(4\delta/s\le\frac18\) and \(\alpha_k\ge2\), \(\psi_{\alpha_k}(1/8)\le e^{1/64}-1<0.02\), and the \(Y\) term tends to \(0\), so the error is at most \(0.02N\) for large \(N\), as in that proof. Each \(z\mapsto\psi_{\alpha_k}(|z_k|/s)\) is convex, so \(C(4(\Phi_{\rm in}+\Phi_c)/N)\le\frac12C(8\Phi_{\rm in}/N)+\frac12C(8\Phi_c/N)\), and \(Ns=L\sqrt{N\log N}\): the cost is at most \(\frac N8(I_{\rm in}+I_c)+0.02N\), with \(I_\bullet=\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(8|\Phi_{\bullet,k}|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\). It remains to show \(I_{\rm in}\le0.08\) with probability tending to one. The tail. Fix \(x\) and a coordinate \(k\), and put \(U=8|\Phi_{{\rm in},k}(x)|/(L\sqrt{N\log N})\). The supermartingale step of that proof, started at level \(j_c\) instead of \(j_0\) (given \(\mathcal F_j\) each coordinate of \(\Phi_j(x)\) is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy \(4m(S_j(x))/\rho_j^2\le8N\) on \(E_1\), by Hoeffding's lemma), gives \(P(|\Phi_{{\rm in},k}(x)|\ge t,E_1)\le2e^{-t^2/(16Nm')}\), that is \(P(U\ge u,E_1)\le2e^{-Au^2}\) with \(A=L^2\log N/(1024m')\). The cap. The square-flow lemma of the flow-bound entry gives \(|\Phi^S|\le6\max_c|e_c|/\rho_j\), and on \(E_1\) \(|e_c|\le m(S)\le2N\rho_j^2\), so \(|\Phi_j(x)|\le12N\rho_j\) and \(|\Phi_{{\rm in},k}(x)|\le12N\sum_{j\ge j_c}\rho_j\le24N\ell\); hence on \(E_1\), \(U\le u_{\max}=192\sqrt N\ell/(L\sqrt{\log N})\). The integral. \(\mathbb E[\psi_\alpha(U)1_{E_1}]=\int_0^{u_{\max}}\alpha u^{\alpha-1}e^{u^\alpha}P(U>u,E_1)\,du\le\int_0^{u_{\max}}2\alpha u^{\alpha-1}e^{u^\alpha-Au^2}du\). If \(u_{\max}^{\alpha-2}\le A/2\), then \(u^\alpha\le u^2A/2\) on \([0,u_{\max}]\) and the integral is at most \(\int_0^\infty2\alpha u^{\alpha-1}e^{-Au^2/2}du=\alpha\Gamma(\alpha/2)(2/A)^{\alpha/2}\). The condition. \(m'=\log_2(\ell/\delta)\le\log_2(64(\log N)^{\beta-1/2}/L)\le(\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N\) for \(L\ge64\); \(u_{\max}\le(192/L)(\log N)^{\beta-1/2}\le(\log N)^{\beta-1/2}\) for \(L\ge192\); so \(u_{\max}^{\alpha-2}\le(\log N)^{(\beta-1/2)(\alpha-2)}\), while \(A/2\ge L^2\log N/(2048(\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N)\) (for \(m'\ge1\); \(m'=0\) is the degenerate case below); the ratio of the first to the second tends to \(0\) when \((\beta-\frac12)(\alpha-2)<1\), so the condition holds for large \(N\), for both coordinates since \(\alpha_k\le\max\alpha\). Markov. Then \(\mathbb E[I_{\rm in}1_{E_1}]\le\eta_N=\sum_k\alpha_k\Gamma(\alpha_k/2)(2/A)^{\alpha_k/2}\to0\) as \(A\to\infty\), and \(P(I_{\rm in}>0.08,E_1)\le\eta_N/0.08\to0\). On \(E_1\cap\{I_{\rm in}\le0.08\}\) the cost is at most \(\frac N8I_c+0.01N+0.02N\). The particular case: \(I_c\le7\) gives cost at most \(0.905N\), so each coordinate's \(\sum_i\psi_{\alpha_k}\le0.905N\) and \(\sum_i\exp[(|X^k_i-Y^k_{\pi(i)}|/s)^{\alpha_k}]\le1.905N\le2N\). At \((4,4)\), \((\beta-\frac12)\cdot2<1\) is \(\beta<1\). \(\square\)

Corollary (coarse means at growing shifts). thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction holds with the fixed shift \(r\) replaced by a sequence of integers \(r=r(N)\ge0\) with \(j_1-r\ge0\) and \(r\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\) such that, with \(C=(\theta/(\sqrt2L))^\alpha\), \(a=770\theta\) and \(r^*=(\frac12-\frac1\alpha)\log_2\ln N\): for finite \(\alpha\in(2,\infty)\), \(\liminf_N(C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}-a)>0\), which holds in particular when \(r\le r^*-c_0-\varepsilon\) for a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), \(c_0=\log_2(a/C)/\alpha\); for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(2^{-r}\theta\sqrt{\ln N}/(\sqrt2L)\ge2\) for all large \(N\). Its other hypotheses (depth, \(\theta\), locality at level \(j_1-r\), the coarse mean condition with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs) are the theorem's.

Proof. The theorem's proof, as written in the coarse-mean entry, at \(r=r(N)\); the steps that involve \(r\): the push \(h_r=2^{-r}\sqrt{N/32}\) and its probability \(p_0\) hold for every \(r\); \(n_P\ge\kappa\log N\,4^{J-j+r}/2\ge256\) eases as \(r\) grows; \(\mu=(p_0/4)^{m}\) does not depend on \(r\); the chain starts at the good level-\((j_1-r)\) squares, which exist as \(j_1-r\ge0\); Chebyshev's factor \(16\cdot4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+1540\theta}\le16K(\log N)^2N^{1542\theta-1}\to0\) as \(4^r\le\ln N\) and \(\theta<1/1542\). The cost step: \(I_k\ge W\psi_\alpha(u_N)\) with \(W\ge\mu/8\ge N^{-770\theta}/8\) and \(u_N\ge2^{-r}\theta\sqrt{\ln N}/(\sqrt2L)\), so for finite \(\alpha\), \(\ln(8I_k)\ge u_N^\alpha-770\theta\ln N+O(1)\ge\ln N\,(C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}-a)+O(1)\to\infty\) under the condition, since \(2^{-r\alpha}(\ln N)^{\alpha/2}=(\ln N)\,2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}\); for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(u_N\ge2\) gives \(I_k\ge W\,N(u_N-1)\ge N^{1-770\theta}/8\to\infty\). A fixed \(r\) meets the condition for large \(N\), since \(r^*\to\infty\). \(\square\)

Refinement checked. cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift beside thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction: the same depth conditions (\(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\)), the same \(\theta\) range (\(0<\theta<\min(1/1542,\kappa/6160)\)), the same field class (level-by-level, \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-measurable steps, locality at level \(j_1-r\), the coarse mean condition with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs) and the same conclusion (\(I_k\) exceeding every constant with probability tending to one, every \(L>0\), \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\)); the corollary's shift is a sequence \(r(N)\) under its stated conditions, and the theorem's fixed integer \(r\) is the constant sequence, which for large \(N\) has \(j_1-r\ge0\), \(r\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\), \(C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}-a\to\infty\) and, at \(\alpha=\infty\), \(2^{-r}\theta\sqrt{\ln N}/(\sqrt2L)\ge2\); so the corollary implies the theorem.

Hypotheses, each with its step. Theorem: \(\alpha_k\ge2\): the error bound \(\psi_{\alpha_k}(1/8)<0.02\) (for \(\alpha_k<2\), \((1/8)^{\alpha_k}\) is larger but still below \(1/8\), so the error is at most \(\frac N4\cdot2\cdot0.14\); not needed here), and the integral step, where \(u^{\alpha-2}\le u_{\max}^{\alpha-2}\) on \([0,u_{\max}]\) needs \(\alpha\ge2\) (for \(\alpha<2\) it fails near \(0\)); \(\beta\) fixed: \(A\to\infty\) needs \(m'=o(\log N)\); \(\beta\ge\frac12\) is automatic from \(\delta\le\ell\) for large \(N\); \(\alpha_k<\infty\): the integral \(\Gamma(\alpha/2)\) and the cap condition, which at \(\alpha=\infty\) would need \(u_{\max}\le1\), false for \(\beta>\frac12\) and large \(N\); \((\beta-\frac12)(\max\alpha-2)<1\): the cap condition, the weakest form being \(u_{\max}^{\alpha_k-2}\le A/2\) for each \(k\) at the given \(N\); \(L\ge260\): the registered statement of thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's constant, whose proof uses \(L\ge256\) for \(E_1\) (\(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\)); this proof needs \(L\ge256\) there and \(L\ge192\) in the cap; \(\ell\) dyadic with \(\delta\le\ell\): the telescoping over whole levels; \(\Phi_c\) bounded with the stated identity: lem:flow-matching-bound (2); \(X\) i.i.d. uniform: \(E_1\) and Hoeffding given \(\mathcal F_j\); \(Y\) evenly spread: \(\nu_Y=N\,\mathrm{Leb}\) and \(\delta_Y\). The conclusion holds for every such \(\Phi_c\) at once on one event. Corollary: each hypothesis is the theorem's with its step there; the new ones, \(r\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\) (Chebyshev, \(4^r\le\ln N\)) and the liminf condition (the cost step), are used where stated; \(j_1-r\ge0\) for the chain's start.

Degenerate cases. Theorem: \(\ell=\delta\) (\(m'=0\)): \(\Phi_{\rm in}=0\) and the statement is lem:flow-matching-bound (2) at the fine smearing, with \(I_{\rm in}=0\). \(X=Y\)-like configurations: the counts are random, so the event, not the configuration, is the degenerate input; on \(E_1\) the bound holds for every \(\Phi_c\). \(\Phi_c=0\) is admissible only when \(\nu^\ell_X=\nu_Y\), which fails for i.i.d. points (cells of \((\log N)^{2\beta}\) points have random counts). \(\ell=1\): excluded, also at \(\max\alpha=2\): there \(m'=J\) and \(A=L^2\ln2/512\), about \(91.5\) at \(L=260\), stays bounded, so Markov's bound \(\eta_N\) does not tend to \(0\); the dyadic proof's split at a coarse level would be needed (reviewer's computation, checked: \(260^2\cdot0.693/512=91.5\)). Corollary: \(r(N)=0\) is thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction; \(r(N)\) beyond \(r^*\): the condition fails and the corollary says nothing.

Nonvacuity. At \((4,4)\) on the curve's parameters: \(\beta=\frac34\), \(L=260\), \(\ell\) the dyadic side nearest below \((\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), so \(\ell>(\log N)^{3/4}/(2\sqrt N)\), and \(\delta\le s/32\): \((\frac34-\frac12)(4-2)=\frac12<1\); \(\ell/\delta\ge16(\log N)^{1/4}/L\), so \(m'=\log_2(\ell/\delta)\ge1\) once \((\log N)^{1/4}\ge33\), so the inner levels are used, which the recorded flow bound at smearing \(\ell\) does not cover (its error \(\frac N4\psi_4(4\ell/s)\), Plainest bound below). Corollary: \(\alpha=4\), \(L=1\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\): \(c_0=10.92\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_tenth_review_20261017/instance_check.txt); \(r(N)=\max(0,\lfloor r^*-12\rfloor)\), positive once \(\log_2\ln N\ge48\) and growing without bound, meets \(r\le r^*-c_0-1\). Plainest bound. On the theorem's instance the flow bound smeared directly at \(\ell\) has error \(\frac N4\cdot2(N^{256/L^4}-1)\), unbounded in \(N\), so it does not decide the instance; on the corollary's, the recorded theorem covers each fixed \(r\) and not a growing \(r(N)\). A fixed \(r\) is the recorded theorem.

Plainest bound. The recorded flow bound with the points smeared directly over the cells of side \(\ell\) (lem:flow-matching-bound with \(\delta_X=\ell\)): its error is \(\frac N4\sum_k\psi_{\alpha_k}(4\ell/s)\), and at \((4,4)\) with \(\ell=(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), \(4\ell/s=4(\log N)^{1/4}/L\) and \(\psi_4(4\ell/s)=N^{256/L^4}-1\), which tends to infinity for every fixed \(L\): the plainest bound fails for every cell side above \(c\,s\), \(\beta>\frac12\). The theorem's own steps used alone: the convexity split with \(\Phi_c\) alone needs \(\Phi_{\rm in}\), and the inner tail alone without the cap gives \(\int_0^\infty e^{u^4-Au^2}du=\infty\): the cap is the step that decides it.

Baseline. thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's flow at all levels, the obvious witness: at \(\alpha=2\) it gives the pair \((2,2)\), and at exponents above \(2\) thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction excludes it, since its variance \(8NJ\) is of order \(N\log N\). The theorem uses that flow on the inner \(m'\le(\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N\) levels only, where the variance \(8Nm'\) is of order \(N\log\log N\), and leaves the coarse levels to \(\Phi_c\). Composed. thm:dyadic-flow-square-exponential's supermartingale tail combined with the square-flow lemma's cap on \(E_1\) and with lem:flow-matching-bound (2) applied to the summed field gives the theorem; its proof's split into coarse and fine levels at \(j_0=\lfloor(\log N)^{1/4}\rfloor\) is the same split at another level, used there for \(\psi_2\) without a cap. thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, composed with the split, says the full dyadic flow fails above exponent \(2\), and applied to \(\Phi_{\rm in}\) alone it does not apply: its proof needs the Gaussian lower tail over about \(\frac12\log_2N\) levels, while \(\Phi_{\rm in}\) spans \(m'\le(\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N\) levels, which is why the inner part escapes it.

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:grid-flow-duality (c) reduces the goal to the discrete class on grids of side at most \(s/32\), whose smearing error needs \(\delta\le s/32\); lem:flow-matching-bound allows any smearing at the error \(hN\Psi(\delta/h)\), which fails above \(c\,s\) (Plainest bound); lem:discrete-flow-bound (b) is the dual neighbour: functions whose increments are at most \(Y\delta_0\) lose \((\log Y)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\) through the full dyadic flow at \(\psi_2\). lem:flow-coarea-level-bound (the registry's nearest claim, read this cycle) is a dual bound through the full dyadic flow at \(\psi_2\), its (d) giving \(C_K\sqrt{N\log N}(\log\log N)^{1/4}\) for class functions with partials at most \((\log N)^K\); it is neither a more general version of the theorem nor a special case: it bounds discrepancies over a class, the theorem bounds matching costs by flows. None states that the finest \((\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N\) levels cost nothing at exponents above \(2\). The registry's other resembling claims, read this cycle: cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction reduces the goal to a class discrepancy bound on the grid of side \(1/\lceil32/s\rceil\), a dual reduction at the finest mesh, neither more general than the theorem nor a special case (the theorem is a primal reduction at a coarser mesh); conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is the open statement whose primal form the theorem moves to coarser cells, not a version of it; lem:smeared-y-term compares the cell-smeared \(Y\) with Lebesgue measure on fine grids, a step of the dual reduction the theorem does not use; lem:cut-cell-variance-bound bounds discrepancies of unions of cells, a dual tool, neither more general nor a special case. The steps of the proof are inside cited proofs (the tail, the square-flow bound, the flow bound); what the entry adds is running the tail on the inner levels with the cap that \(E_1\) gives, and the condition on \(\beta\) that makes the \(\psi_\alpha\) integral finite. The corollary is the coarse-mean theorem's proof read at a growing shift; the tenth review computed it by hand and its reviewer corrected the condition to a fixed offset.

New mathematics. thm:cell-scale-reduction: at pairs with exponents in \([2,\infty)\), a flow between the points smeared over dyadic cells of side up to \((\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\), \((\beta-\frac12)(\max\alpha-2)<1\), and the uniform measure, of bounded \(\psi_\alpha\) cost, gives the goal; at \((4,4)\) every \(\beta<1\), coarser than the Leighton–Shor cells. cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift: the coarse-mean obstruction at shifts up to \(r^*-c_0\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: the reduction asks a flow at a coarser scale, and the converse appears to hold up to replacing \(L\) by \(L/4\) (given a fine flow \(\Phi\), \(\Phi_c=\Phi-\Phi_{\rm in}\) has \(I_c\) at constant \(8\) at most half of \(\Phi\)'s at \(16\) plus half of \(\Phi_{\rm in}\)'s at \(16\), since \(\psi_\alpha(2u)\) is not \(O(\psi_\alpha(u))\)); that converse is sketched, not proved, so the entry does not rest a decision on it: no necessary implication changed, since the theorem asks a flow of the same kind on a coarser grid, which no recorded statement gives. Bearing. At the goal's own parameters, on the curve's parameters at \((4,4)\): a construction may now treat the finest \((\beta-\frac12)\log_2\log N\) levels, almost \(\frac12\log_2\log N\) of them, by the plain dyadic flow and work on cells of \((\log N)^{2\beta}\) points; the reduction does not lift what the corollary asks of the coarse flow: if it is level-by-level, adapted and local, some step \(j\ge j_1\) must still fail the mean condition at every shift within \(r^*-c_0\), since a field meeting it at all such steps at one shift within that reach has cost exceeding every constant. Not covered. Heuristic: restoring exchanges stall the mean chain; the cost is in the legs

17 October 2026 · Attempt by hand, heuristic; no statement proved · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Where we stand. Unchanged: The attempt proved no statement; the living sections already state the obstructions it rests on and the next step names the leg sum

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Create one, maybe?? Does that make sense???? Have you tried??????", on the record having no nonlinear flow whose fine levels correct the coarse ones.

Question. Does the chain of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction survive an added mean term \(c_P\) from restoring exchanges at shifts at least \(r_0=\lceil r^*-c_0\rceil+1\), beyond cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's reach? The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through a flow of bounded cost; a chain that survives would exclude the restoring design on the cells of thm:cell-scale-reduction. The item's earlier entries, read: restoring drift ("Next attempt: a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level"), lagged restoring flow ("first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow"), coarse means ("a coarse-restoring construction, a correction after each level"), coarse restoration ("a restricted leg rule with a provable cost, legs placed by") and cell scale ("the stage-two reviewer's test before any construction (unverified until made)").

Shortest route. The cell-scale entry named it: test the obstruction against the restoring design before building, then build. This entry makes that test by hand and finds the design escapes the mean chain, which moves the route to its legs; it does not build the flow, because the hand test shows the legs, not the means, decide its cost. Building the restoring flow on the cells: Not taken in this cycle, because its first step, the composition lemma, is proved (thm:cell-scale-reduction) and its second, the flow, needs a leg placement rule that this entry's computation shows is where the cost lies; a flow built with the default fixed-shape legs would repeat the lagged flow's design, which cor:lagged-flow-obstruction excludes at shift \(1\) and whose legs the saturation computation shows to be of the dyadic flow's size at any shift.

Target form. The goal's primal form through the flow bound: a field \(\Phi\) carrying the smeared configuration to the uniform measure with \(\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(c|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) bounded, at the curve's pairs with finite exponents, at \((4,4)\) first.

Owed attempt. The cell-scale entry named "the stage-two reviewer's test before any construction (unverified until made)": made here by hand, with the outcome below.

Architecture test. Not decided. The tenth review's retained chain test (outcomes (A) the bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\)) was not worked; none of them occurred. This entry continued the user's pick on the primal side.

General statement. The cycle tests whether cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's mechanism (a level-by-level field, local at level \(j_1-r\), meeting the coarse mean condition at shift \(r\le r^*-c_0-\varepsilon\) at every step, with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs, has cost exceeding every constant) survives an added mean term from exchanges at shifts beyond its reach; no statement was proved.

Attempt

The chain with the added term. As the cell-scale entry derived and its reviewer confirmed, the chain step becomes \(|U_{j+1}(P'_*)|\ge|U_j(P)|+\sigma_P\xi_P+\sigma_Pc_P\), with \(c_P\) the mean over \(P\) of the exchanges. Saturation, by hand and heuristic: let the exchange at shift \(r_0\) restore the mean difference \(R\) of the sibling pair whose square \(Q\) contains \(P\), with a drift at least linear for large \(|R|\) (full restoration \(d(R)=R\) there, the most lem:restoring-drift-tail's form allows). \(P\) is one of about \(4^{r_0-r}\) squares of its level in \(Q\); if the others are typical, \(R\) carries about \(4^{-(r_0-r)}U(P)\), and the exchange lowers \(P\)'s mean by about that amount times the exchange profile's value over \(P\), of order \(1\). The running mean then follows a walk with pushes \(h_r\) and reversion at rate about \(4^{-(r_0-r)}\), which saturates near \(U^*\approx4^{r_0-r}h_r\) up to a constant. Normalized as in the cost step, \(u^*=4U^*/(L\sqrt{N\log N})\approx4^{r_0}2^{-r}/(\sqrt2L\sqrt{\ln N})\) up to a constant; at \((4,4)\), where \(4^{r^*}=\sqrt{\ln N}\), and \(r_0\le r^*+O(1)\), it stays bounded, while the cost step needs \(u_N\) of order \((\ln N)^{1/4}\). So, heuristically, the chain stalls and cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's mechanism does not reach a field with such exchanges; the threshold at which saturation and the cost step balance is \(r^*\) itself, a consistency check, not a proof.

Where the cost goes. The exchanges at shift \(r_0\) after step \(j\) act on level-\((j-r_0)\) squares, and every level is that level for some later step: over the run, the means of the squares of every level are restored. By lem:sibling-exchange-leg, shifting a square's mean by \(\mu\) needs a leg with \((1/\rho)\int|w_2|\ge2|\mu|\) on the shared side, so the legs carry pointwise values of the order of the means they restore. The mean of a level-\(i\) square before its restoration is a sum of pushes at shifts below \(r_0\), dominated by its own push \(h_0\) of order \(\sqrt N\); so each level adds legs of order \(\sqrt N\), as many levels as the dyadic flow has. The pointwise sum of the legs is then of the dyadic flow's size, about \(\frac12\log_2N\) terms of order \(\sqrt N\): whether its tails are lighter than Gaussian is the leg placement question of the coarse restoration entry, now posed with the means known to saturate. For rules linear in the counts thm:linear-flow-obstruction answers it negatively at pairs with both exponents finite and above \(2\) (its grid form); the saturation computation, which ignored the legs, cannot by itself contradict that theorem, and does not.

Plainest bound. Without the exchanges, the chain's mean grows by \(h_r\) per step (the coarse-mean proof); with full restoration at shift \(r_0\) the reversion at rate \(4^{-(r_0-r)}\) bounds the walk's stationary size by \(4^{r_0-r}h_r\) times a constant, the plainest estimate of a linear mean-reverting walk; the legs' plainest bound is lem:sibling-exchange-leg's \(2|\mu|\) per restored mean.

New mathematics. No statement proved. By hand, heuristic: restoring exchanges at shift \(r_0\le r^*+O(1)\), with a drift at least linear for large mean differences, make the chain means of the coarse-mean proof saturate at a normalized size bounded in \(N\) at \((4,4)\), below the \((\ln N)^{1/4}\) the cost step needs, so that obstruction's mechanism does not reach them; the legs of the restorations, by lem:sibling-exchange-leg, carry pointwise values of the size of the means restored, about \(\sqrt N\) per level, so the design's cost is decided by the leg placement.

Goal progress. Unchanged: no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is proved. Bearing. None at the goal's own parameters: no statement was proved. The cycle was spent on the test the cell-scale entry named before building, because a surviving chain would have closed the restoring design at once; it could have excluded the design, and found instead that the obstruction's mean chain likely does not reach it, moving the decision to the legs.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: the legs' pointwise sum under a fixed placement rule, at \((4,4)\) on the cells of thm:cell-scale-reduction: the legs of the restorations of all levels at one point, each of order \(\sqrt N\) with a sign set by the restored mean difference, placed on the half of the shared side where the running field of the other coordinate has the opposite sign; first the conditional push of lem:conditional-push-obstruction for that sum, whether each level's leg still pushes the point's running value along its sign with a probability bounded below. Smallest case. One point and two levels: the point lies on the shared sides of the level-\(i\) pair and of the level-\((i+1)\) pair containing it; each restoration adds a leg of size about the restored difference, \(\pm\) of order \(\sqrt N\); with the placement rule the second leg falls on the point only if its sign opposes the point's running value after the first, so the two legs cannot align at the point, while without the rule they align with probability about \(\frac12\). Nontrivial because: the placement rule reads the running value of the other coordinate at the point and chooses where the leg crosses, which is the nonlinear choice that lem:conditional-push-obstruction's fixed push probability does not allow. Plainest bound. lem:sibling-exchange-leg fixes only each leg's first moment along each line, so a leg can be put where the running field opposes it; the plainest bound on the sum is the sum of the legs' sizes, of order \(\sqrt N\log N\), which decides nothing. Own statements. lem:conditional-push-obstruction covers the leg sum if its pushes keep a fixed probability at every state, which the placement rule is designed to break; thm:linear-flow-obstruction excludes linear rules, so the placement rule must be nonlinear; cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift is, by the saturation above, heuristically escaped; thm:cell-scale-reduction lets the attempt stop at the cells; the coarse restoration entry found that a fully joint placement is the goal's own minimization, so the rule is fixed; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction is the case \(r=0\) of the corollary, escaped the same way; ex:simultaneous-rule-tails is a rule inside each square that keeps square means, covered by that theorem, and decides nothing about legs at coarse sides; thm:adapted-partition-obstruction concerns hierarchical rank-cut matchings and does not bear; ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails measured a drift on sibling means at shift \(0\), whose tails it amplified, a design inside each square that cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's case \(r=0\) covers, and it decides nothing about legs placed at coarse sides; thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction concerns transports whose targets follow their count splits within \(A/\sqrt n\), not flows with placed legs, and its common push of cell means is the mechanism the saturation above escapes. "pointwise Gaussian lower tail fine levels conditional on coarse counts sign absorbed corrections coarse measurable dyadic obstruction rerun" returned thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction, cor:lagged-flow-obstruction and thm:cell-scale-reduction; the coarse restoration entry's "leg placement position aware routing flux crossing side chosen where running field opposite sign two choice exits first moment constraint" returned no placement rule; none states the leg sum's tail.

General statement. The cycle tests whether lem:conditional-push-obstruction (a level-by-level field, local at level \(j_1\), whose step increments at the points of a set of measure at least \(N^{-\gamma}\) push along the running sum's sign by \(h=c\sqrt N\) with conditional probability at least \(p\), has cost exceeding every constant) applies to restoring designs whose corrections read only square means; no statement was proved.

Attempt

The decomposition, read from the record. The square-flow lemma of the flow-bound entry builds the vertical part from \(E_b=e_{0,b}+e_{1,b}\) alone, "\(v(y)=-\int_0^yr\), \(r=E_b/(\rho^2/2)\) on the half \(b\)", and the horizontal parts from \(d_{a,b}=e_{a,b}-E_b/2\), "\(k_b(x)=-\int_0^x\frac{d_{a(x'),b}}{\rho^2/4}dx'\)". The four child excesses have three degrees of freedom (\(\sum e=0\)): \(E_0\), and \(d_{0,0}\), \(d_{0,1}\). In this split order the coordinate-2 field is a function of \(E_0\) alone, and so is its mean over the square; the coordinate-1 field's mean over the square is a function of \(d_{0,0}+d_{0,1}\), while \(d_{0,0}-d_{0,1}\), the diagonal excess, enters it with opposite signs on the two halves \(b\), zero mean over the square and over each of its sibling halves' unions with the other square, and nonzero values pointwise. So each step's coordinate-1 increment at a point is a square-mean part plus an oscillation part carried by the diagonal excess, which no square mean of its own level sees. Which coordinate carries the diagonal is a choice of the split order, not of the square: lem:equalized-flow-separable (read this cycle) routes the same \(d_0-d_1\) through a vertical profile, "\(\Phi(t_1)=-(d_0-d_1)\,\mathrm{tent}(t_1)/(2\rho)\)", and finds it is "the dyadic flow with its splits transposed"; lem:sequential-rules-dyadic shows that rules choosing profiles by crossing maps or by separate convex costs of each coordinate reproduce the dyadic flow exactly. In either order, one coordinate carries the diagonal oscillation; what follows holds in that coordinate.

What restoration sees. A restoring exchange after step \(j\), at any shift, reads the means of squares at levels at most \(j\) (the mean-term entry's design, the lagged flow, the coarse restoration attempts). The oscillation part of step \(j\) contributes zero to every square mean of level at most \(j\), and its contribution to finer squares' means is fixed by the square-flow lemma's profiles; heuristically, conditional on all square means of levels at most \(j\), the diagonal excess still has conditional spread of order \(\sqrt{n_S}\) (a multinomial contrast orthogonal to the two conditioned ones), so the oscillation part at a point keeps a push of order \(\sqrt N\) along any prescribed sign with probability bounded below. A chain of points whose coordinate-1 running value grows by such pushes is then invisible to every restoration, the exchanges' corrections at those points stay of the size of typical square means, and lem:conditional-push-obstruction's hypothesis holds for the corrected field in coordinate 1, at every shift. So, heuristically, every restoring design whose corrections read only square means fails in coordinate 1, the pointwise version of cor:lagged-flow-obstruction at every shift.

What escaping needs. A construction must also steer the oscillation parts, choosing the within-square profiles against the running value, as the simultaneous rule does (ex:simultaneous-rule-tails), while restoring the square means, which that rule keeps and which thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction then excludes; each recorded obstruction excludes one half of that combination, and the mean-term entry's saturation estimate suggests the restoration half escapes its obstruction. The combination, steered within-square profiles together with mean restoration at shift \(r_0\), is the design no record excludes.

Plainest bound. lem:conditional-push-obstruction's own nonvacuity witness, "the dyadic flow plus a local circulation bounded by half the push", already excludes every correction bounded by half the push; the attempt's addition is that corrections reading square means are of that size along the oscillation chain, because the chain is invisible to them.

New mathematics. No statement proved. Read from the square-flow lemma's proof: the coordinate-2 part of each dyadic square flow is a function of its square's vertical excess alone, while the coordinate-1 part carries, besides its mean, the diagonal excess, with zero mean over the square. By hand, heuristic: restorations that read square means cannot see the diagonal oscillations, so the pointwise chain of lem:conditional-push-obstruction survives them in coordinate 1; a construction must steer within-square profiles and restore means together.

Next attempt: the oscillation-chain theorem: for the dyadic flow plus corrections that are, at each step \(j\), local and measurable with respect to the counts of levels at most \(j\) together with the square means of level \(j\) (both coordinates), prove lem:conditional-push-obstruction's hypothesis in coordinate 1 from the conditional lower tail of the diagonal excess given those means, as thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction's proof uses lem:block-lower-tail conditionally on coarse counts. Smallest case. One square \(S\) at level \(j\) with \(n_S\) points and its four children: given \(E_0\) and \(d_{0,0}+d_{0,1}\), the diagonal \(\Delta=d_{0,0}-d_{0,1}\) is \(e_{0,0}-e_{1,0}-e_{0,1}+e_{1,1}\) halved, a sum of \(n_S\) terms \(\pm\frac12\) under the conditional law, which is no longer i.i.d. (the conditioning fixes two other contrasts); at a point of the lower half, the coordinate-1 oscillation is \(\Delta\) times the profile \(k\)'s coefficient, at most \(1/\rho\) in size by the square-flow lemma. Nontrivial because: the conditioning on the two mean contrasts is what the corrections read, and the diagonal's conditional spread under it decides whether the oscillation still pushes. Plainest bound. Without conditioning, \(\Delta\) has variance \(n_S/4\) and lem:block-lower-tail gives a push of order \(\sqrt{n_S}/\rho\sim\sqrt N\) with probability at least \(p_0\); with the two contrasts fixed, the multinomial's three contrasts are uncorrelated (orthogonal \(\pm1\) patterns on four equally likely children), so a central limit gives a conditional spread of the same order when the conditioned contrasts are typical, and the theorem must handle atypical ones. Own statements. lem:conditional-push-obstruction is the theorem the attempt feeds; its nonvacuity witness covers corrections bounded by half the push and not corrections that read means; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction and cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift exclude keeping means, the other half; ex:simultaneous-rule-tails steers profiles and keeps means; ex:rule-conditional-pushes measured that rule's pushes bounded below; thm:linear-flow-obstruction excludes linear rules; thm:cell-scale-reduction lets every attempt stop at the cells; cor:lagged-flow-obstruction is the mean version at shift \(1\); ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails and thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction concern designs inside squares and rank-cut transports, deciding nothing about the diagonal; thm:adapted-partition-obstruction concerns rank-cut matchings and does not bear; lem:equalized-flow-separable and lem:sequential-rules-dyadic say which coordinate the diagonal enters under each split order and that sequential rules of separate costs reproduce the dyadic flow, so the theorem is stated for the coordinate carrying the diagonal.
