General statement. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound, for every grid function on a dyadic grid of side at least \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\), at every pair in \([2,\infty]^2\), with nested chains of any heights as its case (b).

Lemma (cost-weighted slope bound)

Statement. In the setting of lem:discrete-flow-bound (\(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), one dyadic sequence \(\delta_0=2^{-J}\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(D(g)=\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta_0^2)g_Q\), \(\Delta_eg\) the increment across an inner edge \(e\) of direction \(d(e)\)), write \(v_e=|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0\) and, for a pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\), \(w_e=\delta_0^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(v_e/2)\). On the event of lem:discrete-flow-bound (a), which has probability tending to one: (a) for every pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\) and every \(g\) with \(\sum_ew_e\le2\), \[|D(g)|\le\tfrac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\Big(46+6W\Big),\qquad W=\sum_{e:\,v_e\ge2e^{16}}w_e(\log v_e)^{1/2-1/\alpha_{d(e)}};\] (b) at \((4,4)\), every nested chain \(g=\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}y_k1_{A_k}\) (\(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\) unions of cells, heights \(y_k>0\), \(K\) arbitrary) with \(\sum_ew_e\le2\) has \(v_e=\sum_{k:\,e\in\partial A_k}y_k\), so (a) applies with these increments; at one height \(y\), with \(m_e\) the number of boundaries \(\partial A_k\) through \(e\) and any \(M\ge1\), if the edges with \(m_e>M\) carry cost at most \(\eta\), then \(|D(g)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(46+12(\log\max\{My,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}+6\eta(\log\max\{m_{\max}y,2e^{16}\})^{1/4})\).

Proof. (a) On the event, lem:discrete-flow-bound (a) gives \(|D(g)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_2^*(v_e))\) for every \(g\). Its proof of (b) bounds \(\psi_2^*(v)\) edge by edge, quoted from the discrete flow entry: "If \(v/2\ge e^{16}\): \(\psi_2^*(v)\le v\sqrt{\log(1+v)}\) (lem:flow-coarea-level-bound (b)) and \(\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)\ge\frac{v/2}{2\sqrt2}(\log(v/2))^{1/\alpha}\) (same, for \(\alpha=\infty\) with exponent \(0\))", and "If \(v/2<e^{16}\): … \(\psi_2^*(v)\le8.2\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)+14.2\)". In the first case, \(\log(1+v)=\log(v/2)+\log2+\log(1+1/v)\le\log(v/2)+0.70\le1.044\log(v/2)\) since \(\log(v/2)\ge16\), so \(\psi_2^*(v)\le4\sqrt2\sqrt{1.044}\,(\log(v/2))^{1/2-1/\alpha}\psi_\alpha^*(v/2)\le5.8\,(\log v)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\psi^*_\alpha(v/2)\), the exponent \(\frac12-\frac1\alpha\) being nonnegative for \(\alpha\ge2\) and \(\log(v/2)\le\log v\). The entry's proof then replaced \(\log v\) by \(\log\max\{Y,2e^{16}\}\); keeping it per edge, with \(\alpha=\alpha_{d(e)}\), \[\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi_2^*(v_e)\le5.8W+8.2\sum_ew_e+14.2\sum_e\delta_0^2,\] and \(\sum_ew_e\le2\), \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\le2\) (at most \(2\cdot2^J(2^J-1)\) inner edges) give at most \(5.8W+16.4+28.4\); with the \(1\) of (a), \(45.8+5.8W\le46+6W\). (b) As in that entry's proof of (c): "\(\Delta_e\sum_k1_{A_k}\) counts, with one sign (the sets being nested), the boundaries \(\partial A_k\) through \(e\)"; with weights, the same one-signed count gives \(|\Delta_eg|=\delta_0\sum_{k:\,e\in\partial A_k}y_k\). At one height \(y\), \(v_e=m_ey\); in \(W\) at the exponent \(\frac14\), the edges with \(m_e\le M\) contribute at most \(\sum_ew_e(\log\max\{My,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}\le2(\log\max\{My,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}\), the others at most \(\eta(\log\max\{m_{\max}y,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The dyadic sequence \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and the points i.i.d. uniform: only through the event of lem:discrete-flow-bound (a), its flow's event. The pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\): the exponent \(\frac12-\frac1\alpha\ge0\), used to replace \(\log(v/2)\) by \(\log v\), and the recorded lower bound of \(\psi^*_\alpha\). The cost \(\sum_ew_e\le2\): the two sums of the small edges and the normalization of \(W\); without it (a) holds with \(46\) replaced by \(1+14.2\sum_e\delta_0^2+8.2\sum_ew_e\). The threshold \(2e^{16}\): the recorded per-edge bounds, which are stated with it; any larger threshold also works. In (b): nesting, so that increments add the heights with one sign; no condition on the heights, on \(K\) or on \(m_e\); \(M\ge1\) only to name a split. Conclusions: (a) for the discrete class at every pair; (b) for nested chains at \((4,4)\) with any heights and any number of layers; both for the \(X\)-term only.

Degenerate cases. \(g\) constant: every \(v_e=0\), \(W=0\), and \(D(g)=0\) by \(\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta_0^2)=0\); the bound gives \(46\cdot\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\). No edge above the threshold: \(W=0\), the conjectured order, as the record's (b) gives at \(Y<2e^{16}\). Every edge at one value \(v\ge2e^{16}\): \(W=(\log v)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\sum w_e\), the record's (b) with \(Y=v\). \(\alpha=(2,2)\): the exponent is \(0\) and \(W\le2\), the record's \((2,2)\) bound. A chain with \(K=1\): one layer, \(m_e\le1\), \(W\le2(\log\max\{y,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}\).

Nonvacuity. On the curve's parameters at the pair \((4,4)\), take \(\delta_0\) the dyadic number in \([4\sqrt{\log N/N},8\sqrt{\log N/N})\), \(A\) the union of the cells in \([0,\frac12]^2\), \(Q\) a cell of \(A\) none of whose neighbours lies outside \(A\) or on the unit square's boundary, \(y=2e^{16}\), \(m=\lceil e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\rceil\), and the nested chain \(A_1=A\), \(A_2=\dots=A_{m+1}=Q\) at height \(y\): \(g=y\delta_01_A+my\delta_01_Q\), with \(m_e=1\) on \(A\)'s boundary and \(m_e=m\) on \(Q\)'s four inner edges. Cost: \(A\)'s boundary has \(1/\delta_0\) inner edges, each \(w=\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(e^{16})\le\delta_0^2(e^{16}(32)^{1/4}+1)\le2.4e^{16}\delta_0^2\) by the recorded bound \(\psi_4^*(x)\le x(2\log x)^{1/4}+1\), in all at most \(2.4e^{16}\delta_0\), at most \(1\) once \(\delta_0\le e^{-16}/2.4\); \(Q\)'s four edges cost at most \(4\delta_0^2((my/2)(2\log(my/2))^{1/4}+1)\), which tends to \(0\) since \(\delta_0^2my=O(e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\log N/N)\). So \(\sum w_e\le2\) for \(N\) large. The record's lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) nested clause and its (b) with \(Y=my\) give \(47+12(\log(my))^{1/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{1/8}\); (b) here, with \(M=1\) and \(\eta\) the cost of \(Q\)'s edges, gives \(46+12(\log(2e^{16}))^{1/4}+6\eta(\log(my))^{1/4}\), and \(\eta(\log(my))^{1/4}\to0\), so \(|D(g)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(46+12\cdot17^{1/4}+o(1))\); both the chain clause and (a) are used. Plainest bound. On this witness the triangle inequality decides it too: \(|D(my\delta_01_Q)|\le my\delta_0(n_Q+N\delta_0^2)\), with \(n_Q\le4N\delta_0^2\) for every cell with probability tending to one (Chernoff and a union over the at most \(N\) cells, \(N\delta_0^2\ge16\log N\)), at most \(5myN\delta_0^3=O(e^{\sqrt{\log N}}(\log N)^{3/2}/\sqrt N)=o(\sqrt{N\log N})\), and \(y\delta_01_A\) is the record's (b) at \(Y=y\). The lemma's gain on it is that no split is chosen.

Baseline. The plainest recorded bounds: lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\); lem:discrete-flow-bound (b), with loss \((\log Y)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\) at the largest increment; for chains its nested clause, \((\log(m_{\max}y))^{1/4}\); and lem:multilevel-chain-bound, conditions on the number of large layers. The lemma replaces the largest increment's logarithm by its average weighted by cost; at the pair \((2,2)\), and wherever \(W\) is bounded, it gives the conjectured order at every number of layers; for chains at one height \(y\) with \(\log y\) bounded, that is when the edges of multiplicity above a fixed \(M\) carry cost \(\eta\) with \(\eta(\log(m_{\max}y))^{1/4}\) bounded. At a single value of the increments it is the record's (b). Composed. lem:discrete-flow-bound (b) applied to the whole class, its free \(Y\) at the largest increment, gives \(47+12(\log Y)^{1/2-1/\alpha}\); split by linearity into a chain's layers, it charges each layer \(47\) and so grows with \(K\); a split into a part of small increments and a part of large ones is not available in general, the increments of each part having to be a gradient, so the composed record bound keeps the maximum. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) applied to each part alone gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}\), larger by \((\log N)^{1/4}\) on every class. lem:multilevel-chain-bound applied to the chain parts decides chains under its condition on the number of large layers, at every multiplicity, and nothing beyond it; composed with the triangle inequality over the \(K/m\) groups of the open instance, its constant is paid per group.

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:discrete-flow-bound's proof bounds \(\psi_2^*\) edge by edge and sums with the maximum; this lemma is that proof with the maximum taken after the sum, a refinement of that lemma with no new step; its chain clause is the record's nested clause with the multiplicity averaged and the heights mixed. lem:flow-coarea-level-bound supplies the per-edge conjugate bounds. lem:multilevel-chain-bound decides many-layer chains by sets, not by a flow, and its condition on \(|B|\) is untouched here. lem:cut-cell-variance-bound is neither more general nor a special case: it bounds sets and coarse averages through cut cells (its (b) per set with a logarithm of the set's own perimeter, its (d) chains under a count of layers), while this lemma bounds every grid function through the dyadic flow, with no count of layers and a logarithm of the increments; on single layers both apply and neither implies the other's constants.

Refinement checked. lem:discrete-flow-bound (b), in its words, "for every pair \(\alpha\in[2,\infty]^2\) and every \(g\) with \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(|\Delta_eg|/(2\delta_0))\le2\) and \(|\Delta_eg|\le Y\delta_0\) on every edge, \(|D(g)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}\,(47+12\max_j(\log\max\{Y,2e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j})\)": under its hypotheses every \(v_e\le Y\), so \(W\le2\max_j(\log\max\{Y,2e^{16}\})^{1/2-1/\alpha_j}\), and (a) here gives \(46+12\max_j(\cdots)\), below the record's bound with its own constants; the converse fails on the Nonvacuity witness. So lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound implies lem:discrete-flow-bound (b), under the same hypotheses on \(\delta_0\) and the same event.

The restoring flow built: excluded by the record, Gaussian per point at stable gains

17 October 2026 · Finite check, J = 6 to 8; prediction refuted as written · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Picked. The user, 17 October 2026: "Build it. What if you are wrong.....", choosing to build the restoring flow as an existence check over testing it by proof alone.

Best outcome. The record already decides this construction in the limit (Plainest bound): thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at \(r=r_0+1\) gives it unbounded cost at every gain. So the best outcome of the build at \(J\le8\) was a finding about the construction at reachable sizes that no entry had predicted, which the record's theorem does not give: whether it is stable, and what its per-point law looks like; at the goal's own parameters it gives nothing, and the result it would have had to beat is that theorem.

Question. What does the restoring flow, the dyadic flow corrected after each level by exchanges restoring sibling means at shift \(r_0\), do at the sizes reachable: is it stable, and is its per-point law lighter than Gaussian, as the tenth review's construction hoped, or Gaussian in the coordinate carrying the diagonal oscillation, as the oscillation entry's heuristic predicts? The missing implication is conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy through a flow of bounded cost. Item history, read: restoring drift ("Next attempt: a lagged greedy restoring flow, whose correction after the step of level"), lagged restoring flow ("first the push measurement of ex:rule-conditional-pushes on the lagged flow"), coarse restoration ("a restricted leg rule with a provable cost, legs placed by"), cell scale ("the stage-two reviewer's test before any construction (unverified until made)"), mean term ("the legs' pointwise sum under a fixed placement rule, at") and the oscillation entry ("the oscillation-chain theorem: for the dyadic flow plus corrections").

Shortest route. The user's choice is the step taken: build the construction the tenth review named and run it (research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_flow_20261017/, the full run measured at 159 s). The direct route on this item, read after the review: the oscillation chain is open only for corrections that move the means of coarser squares at every shift, crossing parent boundaries, since thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction decides every design whose corrections keep the parents' means; the next attempt names that class.

Target form. The goal's primal form through the flow bound: a field \(\Phi\) carrying the smeared configuration to the uniform measure with \(\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(c|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) bounded, at \((4,4)\) first.

Owed attempt. The oscillation entry named "the oscillation-chain theorem: for the dyadic flow plus corrections" that read square means: not made; the user's pick came first, and the review found that for this construction thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction decides it; the attempt is renamed, below, to the class that theorem leaves open.

Architecture test. Not decided. The tenth review's retained chain test, outcomes (A) the bound holds, (B) a full-budget chain violates it, (C) it holds up to \((\log\log N)^c\): none occurred here; this entry builds the review's primal construction, which, as its reviewer found, the review's own registered corollary family already excludes in the limit.

General statement. The construction falls under thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction (a level-by-level field whose steps are a step meeting the square-mean condition "plus a correction, F_(j+1)-measurable and local, with zero coordinate-k mean on every level-(j-r) square", local at level \(j_1-r\), at a fixed integer \(r\), has unbounded cost); the registered claim is the finite check ex:restoring-flow-tails.

Construction

research/results/ultimate_matching_restoring_flow_20261017/restoring_flow_test.py: the dyadic flow of the simultaneous rule script's level step (rule off), and after the step of level \(j\), for \(i=j-r_0\ge1\), every pair of sibling level-\(i\) squares inside its level-\((i-1)\) parent gets the lagged flow's unit circulation (mean \(+1\) on one square, \(-1\) on the other, its leg in the other coordinate) times \(a=-\gamma R/2\), \(R\) the difference of the pair's running means in the exchanged coordinate, so that \(R\) becomes \((1-\gamma)R\); coordinate 1's pairs first, then coordinate 2's. Gain \(\gamma=1\) is full restoration, the drift \(d(R)=R\) of lem:restoring-drift-tail's form; the amplitudes read only the running field. Controls (all passed, results.json): gain \(0\) reproduces the dyadic field exactly (largest relative difference \(0\)); the correction is divergence-free in weak form (ratios at most \(8.3\cdot10^{-8}\) against five smooth \(g\), at gain \(1\), \(J=6\)) while flipped legs give up to \(0.172\); restoration leaves residual differences of \(0\) at gain \(1\); the planted lighter law has analytic ratios falling from about \(0.13\) to \(0\).

Findings

Full restoration is unstable. At gain \(1\), \(J=6\), shift \(1\), seed \(1\), the restored field's coordinate-1 spread is \(170\), \(430\), \(667\), \(2069\) after the restorations of levels \(1\) to \(4\), against the dyadic flow's \(177\) to \(248\), ratios \(2.5\), \(1.55\), \(3.1\) from level to level (gain1_levels.txt); over \(J\), its spread ratio to the dyadic flow is \(8.3\), \(12.6\), \(23.4\) in coordinate 1 and \(8.2\), \(27.4\), \(47.0\) in coordinate 2 at \(J=6,7,8\) (gain_growth.txt). The seeding, computed for one pair: restoring a unit mean difference on one sibling pair seeds mean differences \(1\), \(1\), \(3\), \(3\) on four pairs one level finer, in the other coordinate, at levels \(2\), \(3\), \(4\) and from either coordinate, an L2 gain of \(\sqrt{20}\approx4.47\) per unit (feedback_factor.txt). A one-chain model following the largest seed, \(R_{i+1}=\text{noise}+3\gamma R_i\), predicts growth above \(\gamma=\frac13\) at rate \(3\gamma\) per level (the seeds scale by \(\gamma\), since \(R\) is linear in the field); it is a model, not the level-to-level map: each finer pair receives its seed from exactly one coarser pair, so seeds never overlap, and only the next dyadic step's own differences can offset one; the measurements do not show its rates: at gain \(1\) the coordinate-1 spread ratio grows by \(1.5\) and \(1.9\) per \(J\), below \(3\) per level, and at gains \(0.4\) and \(0.5\) the ratios (coordinate 2: \(1.13\), \(1.30\), \(1.18\) and \(1.37\), \(1.83\), \(1.69\); coordinate 1 at \(0.4\): \(0.955\), \(1.024\), \(1.005\); one seed each, gain_growth.txt) are near or above \(1\) but not shown growing with \(J\). So the seeding stands for one pair, each restoration seeding finer differences of up to three times its size through its leg, and the threshold \(\frac13\) is the model's prediction, unverified; gains \(0.1\) and \(0.25\) are stable (spread ratios between \(0.90\) and \(1.06\) at every \(J\)).

Tails at gains 0.1 and 0.25, \(J=6,7,8\), 512 seeds. Per-position standardized (each flow by its own spread): the restored flows' exceedance ratios to the dyadic flow's are between \(0.97\) and \(1.02\) at \(2.2\) and \(3.3\) and between \(0.95\) and \(1.10\) at \(3.8\) (bootstrap spreads up to \(0.15\) at \(J=6\), \(0.06\) at \(J=8\)), in both coordinates, every configuration and level, and the standardized fourth moments are \(2.98\) to \(3.04\) for every flow, the dyadic one included (results.json): Gaussian in shape per position at both gains. Coordinate 1's variance is \(0.855\) to \(0.942\) of the dyadic flow's; coordinate 2's falls at gain \(0.1\) and rises to about \(1.05\) at gain \(0.25\) (results.json). In the dyadic flow's analytic normalization the coordinate-1 ratios at \(4.0\) are \(0.44\) to \(0.66\), below the committed floor \(0.7\), so the prediction as written is refuted; beside a Gaussian scaled by one spatially averaged spread (variance_baseline.txt) they match it at gain \(0.1\) (\(J=8\), shift \(1\): observed \(0.46\pm0.02\), baseline \(0.45\)) and exceed it at gain \(0.25\) (\(0.46\pm0.05\) against \(0.24\); coordinate 2, \(2.25\pm0.22\) against \(1.52\)), while the per-position ratios there show no heavier shape (\(J=8\), gain \(0.25\), at \(3.8\): coordinate 1 \(1.06\pm0.04\), \(1.07\pm0.04\); coordinate 2 \(0.98\pm0.06\), \(0.96\pm0.06\)); the excess is consistent with a variance change that varies across positions, which a single averaged spread cannot follow (the reviewer's reading, unverified: the per-position variance ratios were not saved).

What it does not show. Nothing at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) standard deviations or in the limit, which thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction decides; the check's thresholds stop at \(4\). A variance reduction by a fixed factor changes the cost only through the constant \(L\), not the Gaussian tail class that thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction excludes.

Plainest bound. The record decides the limit before any run. The correction after step \(j\) is the lagged flow's unit circulation on level-\((j-r_0)\) pairs, whose shapes, in cor:lagged-flow-obstruction's assessment, have "zero sum over each sibling pair in both coordinates (quoted from the script's unit_shapes), so its mean on each level-(j-1) parent vanishes for every amplitude"; here the parents are of level \(j-r_0-1\). thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's statement: "the condition holds when each step is a step meeting that theorem's mean condition plus a correction, F_(j+1)-measurable and local, with zero coordinate-k mean on every level-(j-r) square (for instance divergence-free there with zero normal flux), whatever it does to finer means". With \(r=r_0+1\): the dyadic step meets the mean condition (that assessment: "the dyadic step meets the r = 0 condition"), the amplitudes read the field after step \(j\), which uses the counts of levels at most \(j+1\), and the correction is local to its parent; so for every fixed \(r_0\ge0\) (\(r_0=0\) is cor:lagged-flow-obstruction; the runs are at \(r_0=1,2\)), every gain, both coordinates, every \(L>0\) and every \(\alpha\in(2,\infty]\), the cost exceeds every constant with probability tending to one (the reviewer's application, checked here against the two quoted sentences).

One level-\(j\) square with \(n_S\) points and its four children, the row and column contrasts \(A\), \(B\) fixed: the top-left count \(n_1\) then determines the diagonal contrast \(D=4n_1+\mathrm{const}\), and, the four cells being equally likely, \(n_1\) given \(A\), \(B\) is central hypergeometric with variance \(ab(n-a)(n-b)/(n^2(n-1))\), \(a=(n_S+A)/2\), \(b=(n_S+B)/2\), of order \(n_S\) whenever \(|A|,|B|\le(1-\varepsilon)n_S\) (the reviewer's computation; the variance formula checked here at \(A=B=0\): \(n_S/16\cdot n_S/(n_S-1)\), the multinomial's \(n_S\cdot\frac14\cdot\frac34\) less the two conditioned contrasts' shares); a hypergeometric is a sum of independent Bernoullis, so Paley–Zygmund gives a lower tail \(P(D-\mathbb ED\le-c\sqrt{n_S})\ge c'\) uniformly there (the reviewer's, unverified). The obstruction is elsewhere: given \(A\), \(B\) and the coarser counts, the field at a point is a correction term plus a multiple of \(D-\mathbb ED\), and a correction of order \(\sqrt{n_S}\) opposing the running sign defeats a push along it. Coarse push obstruction, partial restoration and the boundary flux of a mean shift

17 October 2026 · Working proof; a member beyond the recorded theorems not shown · Restoring drift construction. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

The restoring flow entry named "find what such a correction must do across parent boundaries, through the general form of lem:sibling-exchange-leg": made below; the coarse push lemma says what a step must avoid at each shift, the flux lemma what moving a square's mean costs across its sides.

General statement. lem:coarse-push-obstruction, for every shift \(r\) fixed or \(r(N)\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\), every push size \(c_N>0\) and probability \(p\) within its conditions; cor:partial-restoration-obstruction, its consequence for corrections restoring a part of the dyadic push; lem:boundary-flux-mean-shift for every rectangle and piecewise \(C^1\) field.

Lemma (coarse push obstruction)

Setting of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction: \(N\) i.i.d. uniform points in \([0,1]^2\), depth \(J\) with \(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\), \(j_1=J-\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\), \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\), a shift \(r\ge0\) (fixed, or \(r=r(N)\) with \(j_1-r\ge0\) and \(r\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\)), a coordinate \(k\), and a level-by-level field \(\Phi=\sum_{j<J}\Phi_j\), \(\Phi_j\) measurable with respect to the counts of levels at most \(j+1\), local at level \(j_1-r\) (for every level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T'\) and \(j\ge j_1\), \(\Phi_j\) on \(T'\) a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points of \(T'\)). Call a level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\) good if it holds at least half its mean count, and reachable if it and its ancestors down to level \(j_1-r\) are good. Suppose that for every \(j_1\le j<J\) and every reachable level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\), \(P\big(\sigma_P\,|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\ge c_Nh_r\mid\mathcal F_j\big)\ge p\), where \(\sigma_P\) is the sign of the running mean \(U_j(P)=|P|^{-1}\int_P\sum_{i<j}\Phi_{i,k}\) (\(+1\) at \(0\)), \(h_r=2^{-r}\sqrt{N/32}\), \(c_N>0\) and \(p\in(0,1]\) with \(b=\theta\log_2(4/p)\), \(b<\kappa/8\) and \(2\theta+2b<1\). Then for \(L>0\), with \(u_N=4mh_r/(L\sqrt{N\log N})\), \(\int\psi_\alpha(4|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) exceeds every constant with probability tending to one when \(\alpha\in(2,\infty)\) and \((c_Nu_N)^\alpha-b\ln N\to\infty\), or \(\alpha=\infty\) and \(c_Nu_N\ge2\) for all large \(N\).

Proof. The proof of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, quoted in the coarse-mean entry, with its push step replaced by the hypothesis. The walk: for a reachable \(P\) at step \(j\), put \(\xi'_P=|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\) and, for its four children \(P'\), \(\delta_{P'}=U_{j+1}(P')-U_j(P)-\xi'_P\), which sum to \(0\) since the mean of \(\sum_{i\le j}\Phi_{i,k}\) over \(P\) is the average of its means over the children; the first child \(P'_*\) with \(\sigma_P\delta_{P'_*}\ge0\) has \(|U_{j+1}(P'_*)|\ge|U_j(P)|+\sigma_P\xi'_P\). The chain starts at the reachable level-\((j_1-r)\) squares at step \(j_1\) and keeps \(P'_*\) when \(\sigma_P\xi'_P\ge c_Nh_r\) and \(P'_*\) is good, so \(|U_j(P)|\ge(j-j_1)c_Nh_r\) on its squares; the event kept on has conditional probability at least \(p\) given \(\mathcal F_j\) by hypothesis. Locality: \(\xi'_P\), \(U_j(P)\), \(U_{j+1}(P')\) and so the kept event and \(P'_*\) are functions of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points of the level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T'\) containing \(P\), by the locality of \(\Phi_i\) for \(i\ge j_1\) and the \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\)-measurability of \(\Phi_i\), \(i<j_1\). The area \(W\) of the chain's last squares then has, as in the theorem, \(\mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge(p/4)^mW_{j_1}-Y\), \(Y\) the area of bad squares, \(\mathbb EY\le2N^{-\kappa/8}\), and \(\mu=(p/4)^m\ge N^{-b}\), so \(\mathbb E[W\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge\mu/4\) with probability tending to one by \(b<\kappa/8\). \(W=\sum_{T'}W(T')\) with \(W(T')\) a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points of \(T'\), conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\), variance at most \(4^{r-j_1}/4\); Chebyshev gives \(P(W<\mu/8\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\le16\cdot4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2b}\to0\), using \(2\theta+2b<1\) and \(4^r\le\ln N\). Cost: on a last square \(Q\), \(|U_J(Q)|\ge mc_Nh_r\), and Jensen for the convex \(z\mapsto\psi_\alpha(4|z|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) gives \(I_k\ge W\psi_\alpha(c_Nu_N)\ge\frac{\mu}8\psi_\alpha(c_Nu_N)\); for finite \(\alpha\), \(\frac\mu8\psi_\alpha(c_Nu_N)\ge\frac18(e^{(c_Nu_N)^\alpha-b\ln N}-N^{-b})\to\infty\); for \(\alpha=\infty\), \(\psi_\infty(c_Nu_N)\ge N\) and \(I_k\ge N^{1-b}/8\to\infty\), as \(b<\frac12\). \(\square\)

Corollary (partial restoration obstruction)

Let \(\Phi\) satisfy the hypotheses of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at shift \(r\) (fixed, or \(r(N)\) as in the lemma) except its mean condition, and let \(\xi_P=|P|^{-1}\sum_{S\subseteq P}\frac{\rho_j}2\epsilon_SE_k(S)\) with \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable signs \(\epsilon_S\), the dyadic coarse mean. Suppose that for every \(j_1\le j<J\), on every reachable level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\) and on the event \(\sigma_P\xi_P\ge h_r\), \(\sigma_P|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\ge(1-\lambda_N)h_r\), with \(\lambda_N\in[0,1)\). Then the conclusion of the lemma holds with \(c_N=1-\lambda_N\), \(p=p_0\), \(b=770\theta\), under \(\theta<\min(1/1542,\kappa/6160)\): for finite \(\alpha>2\) when \(((1-\lambda_N)u_N)^\alpha-770\theta\ln N\to\infty\), in particular for every fixed \(\lambda<1\) at a fixed \(r\), and at \(r(N)\) when cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's condition holds with \(C\) replaced by \((1-\lambda)^\alpha C\), that is \(c_0\) by \(c_0+\log_2\frac1{1-\lambda}\); for \(\alpha=\infty\) when \((1-\lambda_N)u_N\ge2\). It covers every step whose coarse mean differs from the dyadic one by \(\Delta_j(P)\) with \(\sigma_P\Delta_j(P)\ge-\lambda h_r\), and steps restoring a fixed fraction of the actual push, \(\Delta_j(P)=-\lambda\xi_P\).

Proof. The theorem's push step, quoted: given \(\mathcal F_j\), \(X_P=\sum_{z\in P}\epsilon_{S(z)}(1\{z\text{ in the lower half of }S(z)\}-\frac12)\) is a sum of \(n_P\) i.i.d. terms \(\pm\frac12\), so lem:block-lower-tail gives \(P(\sigma_P\xi_P\ge h_r\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p_0\) on good \(P\); this uses only the \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurability of \(\epsilon_S\) and \(\sigma_P\), not their locality. On that event the hypothesis gives \(\sigma_P|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\ge(1-\lambda_N)h_r\), so the lemma's hypothesis holds with \(c_N=1-\lambda_N\) and \(p=p_0\); its conditions are the theorem's, \(b=\theta\log_2(4/p_0)=770\theta\). The two cases: \(\sigma_P\xi_P\ge h_r\) and \(\sigma_P\Delta\ge-\lambda h_r\) give \(\sigma_P(\xi_P+\Delta)\ge(1-\lambda)h_r\); \(\Delta=-\lambda\xi_P\) gives \(\sigma_P(1-\lambda)\xi_P\ge(1-\lambda)h_r\). The growing shift: \(((1-\lambda)u_N)^\alpha\ge(1-\lambda)^\alpha C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}\ln N\) by cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift's bound on \(u_N\). \(\square\)

Lemma (boundary flux of a mean shift)

Let \(B=[x_0,x_0+a]\times[y_0,y_0+b]\) and \(w\) a piecewise \(C^1\) field near \(B\) with continuous normal components across the pieces' interfaces. Then for every real \(c\), \(\int_Bw_1=\int_{\partial B}(x-c)\,w\cdot n-\int_B(x-c)\operatorname{div}w\), so \(|\int_Bw_1|\le\frac a2\big(\int_{\partial B}|w\cdot n|+\int_B|\operatorname{div}w|\big)\); the same holds for \(w_2\) with \(b\) and \(y\). In particular a divergence-free \(w\) whose mean of \(w_1\) over \(B\) is \(m\) has \(\int_{\partial B}|w\cdot n|\ge2|m|b\), \(2|m|\rho\) on a square of side \(\rho\).

Proof. On each piece \(\operatorname{div}((x-c)w)=w_1+(x-c)\operatorname{div}w\); the divergence theorem on each piece, summed, cancels the interface terms by the continuity of the normal components. With \(c=x_0+a/2\), \(|x-c|\le a/2\) on \(B\) and \(\partial B\). For divergence-free \(w\), \(\int_Bw_1=mab\le\frac a2\int_{\partial B}|w\cdot n|\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Coarse push lemma: the push hypothesis on reachable squares only, in the walk; locality of \(\Phi\) at level \(j_1-r\), in the many-squares step, through the kept event's being a function of \(\Phi_j\)'s mean over \(P\) (the theorem's push event used the signs \(\epsilon_S\), whose locality the theorem never needed because its mean condition made the two events equal); \(b<\kappa/8\), the area bound against bad squares; \(2\theta+2b<1\) and \(4^r\le\ln N\), Chebyshev; \(b<\frac12\), at \(\alpha=\infty\) only, implied by \(2\theta+2b<1\). Not used: that \(\Phi\) is a flow, any bound on \(\Phi_j\), anything on finer squares. \(c_N\) and \(p\) may depend on \(N\) within the conditions; \(p\) fixed is the case used. Corollary: the hypothesis only on the push event and on reachable squares; \(\lambda_N\) may depend on \(N\), \(j\) and \(P\) as long as it is at most a \(\lambda_N\) satisfying the cost condition. Flux lemma: piecewise \(C^1\) with continuous normal components, the divergence theorem; the rectangle, \(|x-c|\le a/2\) (on any bounded \(B\), \(a\) the width of its projection). The lemma and the corollary hold in each coordinate \(k\) separately, for every field of their class.

Degenerate cases. lem:coarse-push-obstruction at \(c_N=1\), \(p=p_0\) contains thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, whose steps meet it by the push step; at \(r=0\) thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction. At \(p\to0\) or \(c_N\to0\) faster than its conditions allow it says nothing. The corollary at \(\lambda_N\to1\) with \((1-\lambda_N)u_N\) bounded says nothing, and a step with \(\Delta_j(P)=-\xi_P\) on the push event (full restoration of the actual push) does not meet the corollary's hypothesis; whether it meets the lemma's depends on the step off that event, which the lemma's hypothesis also counts. lem:boundary-flux-mean-shift at \(w=0\) gives \(0\le0\); at a divergence-free \(w\) with zero normal flux on \(\partial B\) it gives \(\int_Bw_1=0\), the identity written in thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's proof, "\(\int_P\Psi_{j,k}=\int_{\partial P}x_k\Psi_j\cdot n-\int_Px_k\operatorname{div}\Psi_j=0\)".

Nonvacuity. Both statements have members: the dyadic flow meets the lemma's hypothesis at \(c_N=1\), \(p=p_0\) by the theorem's push step, and the corollary's at \(\lambda_N=0\). A member that no recorded statement covers is not shown. The candidate tried, and refuted as such by the reviewer: the dyadic flow plus, after each step \(j\ge j_1\), the deterministic field \(w_j=\eta_j(\partial_yb,-\partial_xb)\), \(b(x,y)=\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y)\), with \(\eta_j=\lambda h_r/\pi\) at \(\lambda=\frac12\), for the \(k=1\) coordinate. It is divergence-free with zero normal flux on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) (\(b\) vanishes there), so the sum is a flow between the same measures; it is deterministic, hence measurable and local. Its mean over a square \(P\) of side \(\rho\) is \(\Delta=\frac{\eta_j}{\rho^2}\int(b(x,y_{\rm top})-b(x,y_{\rm bot}))dx\), with \(|\Delta|\le\pi\eta_j=\lambda h_r\), so \(\sigma_P\Delta\ge-\lambda h_r\) and the corollary applies. thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at any shift \(r'\), and cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift, demand \(|P|\xi'_P=\sum_S\frac{\rho_j}2\epsilon_SE_k(S)\), a number in \(\frac{\rho_j}4\mathbb Z\) since \(E_k(S)\in\frac12\mathbb Z\); the dyadic part already is one, so they demand \(|P|\Delta\in\frac{\rho_j}4\mathbb Z\), which fails for every square whose \(|P|\Delta\) is not such a multiple, all but countably many choices of \(\eta_j\) at each square not symmetric about \(y=\frac12\). That excludes only the construction's own assignment of steps: the correction is deterministic, the recorded theorems leave the steps before \(j_1\) unrestricted beyond measurability, and the conclusion concerns only \(\Phi\), so the whole correction regrouped into step \(j_1-1\) leaves the steps \(j\ge j_1\) dyadic, and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction covers the flow. A member escaping every regrouping needs corrections that read data of the steps \(j\ge j_1\), such as running signs; the reviewer's candidate of that kind is listed below, unverified. The lemma is therefore proved, implies the recorded theorems, and is not shown to cover more. On the curve parameters at \((4,4)\), \(r=1\), \(\lambda=\frac12\): \((1-\lambda)u_N\ge\frac{\theta}{4\sqrt2L}\sqrt{\ln N}\), and \(((1-\lambda)u_N)^4-770\theta\ln N\ge\ln N\,((\frac\theta{4\sqrt2L})^4\ln N-770\theta)\to\infty\); the bracket turns positive at \(\ln N>770\theta(4\sqrt2L/\theta)^4\), about \(1.7\cdot10^{25}\) at \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\), \(L=260\), an astronomically large threshold set by the proof's bookkeeping, not by the field. Flux lemma: \(w=(1,0)\) on \(B=[0,1]^2\), \(\int_Bw_1=1\), \(\int_{\partial B}|w\cdot n|=2\), equality; lem:sibling-exchange-leg does not cover it, its field having flux off the top side. Plainest bound. For the lemma and the corollary, thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction itself, which decides steps whose coarse means equal the dyadic ones, and through the regrouping above also the deterministic candidate. For the flux question on a level-\((j-r)\) square \(P\): restoring its mean by \(\lambda h_r\) costs \(\int_{\partial P}|w\cdot n|\ge2\lambda h_r\rho_P=2\lambda\rho_j\sqrt{N/32}\), a mean normal flux density at least \(\lambda h_r/2\) on \(\partial P\).

Baseline. The construction needing no idea is the dyadic flow, decided by thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction; the bound needing no idea is thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction. The coarse push lemma replaces its mean condition by a conditional push of the step's own coarse mean, local by construction; the corollary adds steps restoring part of the dyadic push; the flux lemma adds fields with flux through every side, where lem:sibling-exchange-leg needs zero flux off one segment. Composed. thm:dyadic-flow-obstruction decides the dyadic flow alone and nothing about a corrected step, since a correction is not a dyadic step; thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, applied to the dyadic part and to the correction separately, gives nothing on the sum, its conclusion being a cost lower bound for one field, which a correction can cancel, so it decides the lemma's class only where the correction's coarse means vanish (its own case) or regroup away (the deterministic candidate); lem:sibling-exchange-leg, applied to each side of a rectangle in turn, needs zero flux off that side's segment, which a field with flux through two sides breaks, so composing it over sides does not give the flux lemma's bound.

Bearing on the open class

By the lemma's contrapositive, a field local at level \(j_1-r\) whose cost stays bounded with probability bounded below along a sequence of \(N\) fails its hypothesis there, for every admissible \(c_N\) and \(p\): at some step \(j\) and some reachable square \(P\), \(P(\sigma_P|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\ge c_Nh_r\mid\mathcal F_j)<p\). That is all it gives: one square at one step; a stronger form, that the failures must carry a positive share of the chain's area, is not proved. By the corollary the same holds of the restoration: on some reachable square at some step, on the push event, the step's coarse mean is below \((1-\lambda_N)h_r\). The flux lemma prices such a restoration by boundary flux of density at least about \(h_r/2\) on \(\partial P\); summed over shifts these densities are \(O(\sqrt N)\), averages over different curves, a heuristic; it does not by itself exclude such corrections, nor permit them, since a per-step \(O(\sqrt N)\) aligned with the sign over \(m\) steps is what lem:conditional-push-obstruction shows fatal.

Record comparison. From the record's side: thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's proof (coarse-mean entry) states its mean condition's use as "the push of a coarse mean, and only there"; the reviewer found a second, hidden use, that the condition makes the push event equal an event on the step's own mean and so local, which the lemma makes explicit. Its walk, area bound, many-squares step, Chebyshev and cost step are the theorem's, cited; what is new is the hypothesis, a conditional coarse push of the step itself, not shown to admit a field the recorded theorems miss (Nonvacuity), which contains the theorem, thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction (\(r=0\)), cor:lagged-flow-obstruction (\(\Delta=0\) at \(r=1\)) and cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift as cases. lem:conditional-push-obstruction is its pointwise counterpart; neither implies the other. The flux lemma's identity at \(c=0\) is in the theorem's proof, quoted in Degenerate cases; the bound \(|x-c|\le a/2\) and the absence of a zero-flux hypothesis are new; lem:sibling-exchange-leg has the sharper constant \(\ell/2\) when the flux crosses one segment of length \(\ell<a\), and neither implies the other.

Refinement checked. lem:coarse-push-obstruction implies thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction: same depth, \(\theta\) and locality at level \(j_1-r\); the theorem's mean condition gives, by its push step, \(P(\sigma_P|P|^{-1}\int_P\Phi_{j,k}\ge h_r\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p_0\) on good \(P\), the lemma's hypothesis at \(c_N=1\), \(p=p_0\), \(b=\theta\log_2(4/p_0)=770\theta\); the theorem's \(\theta<\min(1/1542,\kappa/6160)\) gives \(b<\kappa/8\) and \(2\theta+2b=1542\theta<1\); the cost conditions then read \(u_N^\alpha-770\theta\ln N\to\infty\), which the theorem's \(u_N\ge\frac{2^{-r}\theta}{\sqrt2L}\sqrt{\ln N}\) gives at fixed \(r\) and finite \(\alpha>2\), and \(u_N\ge2\) at \(\alpha=\infty\). It implies cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift at the same \(c_N=1\), \(p=p_0\): that corollary's \(r(N)\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\) is the lemma's range, and its condition \(\liminf(C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}-a)>0\), with \(u_N^\alpha\ge C2^{\alpha(r^*-r)}\ln N\), gives \(u_N^\alpha-a\ln N\to\infty\), \(a=770\theta=b\). It implies thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction at \(r=0\): that theorem's steps have on each level-\(j\) square "the mean of the dyadic step", its locality is at level \(j_1\), the lemma's at \(r=0\). cor:partial-restoration-obstruction implies thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at \(\lambda_N=0\): the theorem's mean condition makes the step's coarse mean equal \(\xi_P\), at least \(h_r\) along \(\sigma_P\) on the push event, its constants unchanged.

New mathematics. lem:coarse-push-obstruction: a level-by-level field, local at level \(j_1-r\), whose step pushes the running mean of every reachable level-\((j-r)\) square along its sign by \(c_Nh_r\) with conditional probability at least \(p\) has unbounded cost, at fixed and growing shifts, under conditions on \(c_N\), \(p\) and \(\theta\); it implies thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction and cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift, and no field it covers beyond them is exhibited. cor:partial-restoration-obstruction: so has every field whose step keeps at least \((1-\lambda_N)h_r\) of the dyadic coarse push on its push event. lem:boundary-flux-mean-shift: a mean shift \(m\) of \(w_1\) over a rectangle of height \(b\) needs boundary flux plus divergence mass at least \(2|m|b\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: these are obstructions with a cost identity; no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is proved. Bearing. At \((4,4)\) and every \(L\) (curve parameters): a flow of bounded cost, local at level \(j_1-r\), must at some step and some reachable square fail to push that square's coarse mean along its sign by \(c_Nh_r\) with conditional probability \(p\), for every admissible \(c_N\), \(p\), and at every shift up to \(r^*-O(1)\) by the growing-shift form; the price of such a failure in boundary flux is of one dyadic step's order, which does not by itself exclude it. Not covered. Shifts beyond the growing-shift condition; whether failures must carry a positive share of the chain's area; the pointwise accumulation of the restoring legs, which the flux lemma does not locate.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: build the construction the Shortest route names, the multi-shift restoring flow: after each step \(j\), for every shift \(1\le s\le R_N\) with \(R_N\ge r^*-c_0\), sibling exchanges between the level-\((j-s)\) squares inside their parents, amplitude restoring a gain \(\gamma\) of the running coarse difference, so that coarse means move at every shift the growing-shift corollary covers; ex:restoring-flow-tails built these exchanges at the single shifts \(r_0=1,2\). Since cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift decides, at each \(L\), every construction with \(R_N+1\le r^*-c_0(L)-\varepsilon\), a cost bounded at \(L\) needs \(R_N\ge r^*-c_0(L)-1\), \(c_0\) depending on \(L\). The mechanism the construction relies on: a restoration proportional to the running coarse mean, \(\Delta=-\gamma U_j(P)\), has \(\sigma_P\Delta=-\gamma|U_j(P)|\), growing with \(|U_j(P)|\), so it leaves the corollary's hypothesis and, at large \(|U_j(P)|\), the lemma's. First written as a proof object: its legs' pointwise sum at one point and the seeding factor of ex:restoring-flow-tails across shifts. Smallest case. At \((4,4)\), \(r^*=\frac14\log_2\ln N\), \(0.87\), \(0.91\), \(0.95\) at \(J=6,7,8\) (\(N=16\cdot4^J\)), and \(c_0=10.92\) at \(L=1\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\) (about \(18.9\) at \(L=260\), the reviewer's figure), so \(r^*-c_0<0\) at every reachable size: every fixed \(R\) is decided by thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction at shift \(R+1\), and the construction differs from a recorded one only through \(R_N\to\infty\), which no run reaches; the smallest instance that tests it is the proof at one point \(x\) with two shifts, where the exchanges at shifts \(1\) and \(2\) both move flux across sides near \(x\) only if \(x\) lies near those sides, which the flux lemma does not decide since it bounds the flux's total on \(\partial P\), not its place. Nontrivial because: two shifts' exchanges act on squares containing \(x\), and whether their legs at \(x\) align is the pointwise question the construction must settle. Plainest bound. The flux lemma gives on \(\partial P\) at each shift a mean density at least \(\lambda h_s/2\), lower bounds; on the two shifts' boundaries together at least \(\lambda(h_1+h_2)/2=\frac38\lambda\sqrt{N/32}\), with no value at \(x\). Own statements. lem:coarse-push-obstruction says the construction must make "P(sigma_P mean_P Phi_j >= c_N h_r | F_j) >= p" fail at every shift up to \(r^*-O(1)\); cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift decides every \(R\) with "r <= r* - c_0 - eps" unrestored; lem:boundary-flux-mean-shift gives "\(\int_{\partial B}|w\cdot n|\ge2|m|b\)" per square, not per point; ex:restoring-flow-tails's seeding, differences "1, 1, 3, 3" one level finer per restored unit, applies to each shift's exchanges; lem:conditional-push-obstruction decides the construction if its legs push points along a sign with probability bounded below; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction asks each step to have "the mean of the dyadic step" on its own level-\(j\) squares, which the construction's exchanges at shift \(1\) change, so it does not decide it; thm:adapted-partition-obstruction concerns matchings following "an adapted partition cutting each cell alternately", not flows, and does not bear on the construction. Record search. "coarse mean push partial restoration correction opposing running sign half push chain survives" returned thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction, ex:rule-conditional-pushes, lem:conditional-push-obstruction, thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, ex:restoring-flow-tails, thm:adapted-partition-obstruction, cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift and thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction; none states a coarse push form.

  • The lagged flow's divergence control, which asks to "find which part of the leg the weak-form test functions miss": deferred in the restoring flow entry and here, the second deferral; this entry's question is the coarse-mean proof's. Follow-up. Continuing: the weak-form response to a flipped leg per exchange coordinate and per test function, made or dropped with its reason in the next entry on this item.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  1. For a flow step with \(\operatorname{div}\Phi_j\) the change of smeared counts and \(\epsilon_S=+1\), \(|P|\Delta_j(P)=\int_{\partial P}(x_k-c_P)\Phi_j\cdot n\): the corollary's hypothesis is then a statement on the first moment of flux across coarse sides, and the flux lemma's price exact bookkeeping. Record. The reviewer's search "square mean conditional push probability chain coarse square sign running mean" found no such identity; lem:boundary-flux-mean-shift and thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction bear on it.
  2. A way to decide the pointwise question: flux across a side shared by \(P\) and a neighbour \(\tilde P\) adds the same sign to both squares' moments, so where their running signs conflict a leg restoring \(P\) pushes points of \(\tilde P\) near the side along \(\tilde P\)'s sign; with \(G_N\) the points within \(\delta\rho_{j-r}\) of the level-\((j-r)\) grid lines at every level, of measure about \((c\delta)^m=N^{-\gamma}\), lem:conditional-push-obstruction might apply; a counterexample design restores only through sides whose neighbour agrees in sign. Record. "restoring flow gain instability legs feedback" and the entry's search returned lem:sibling-exchange-leg and lem:conditional-push-obstruction, none on side sign patterns.
  3. A witness that resists regrouping: at each step \(j\ge j_1+1\), the curl of a bump centred on a midline of the level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T'\), amplitude a small multiple of \(h_r\) times a running sign read at step \(j\), straddling squares of every finer level; local, divergence-free, zero flux on \(\partial T'\), means nonzero at every shift and at most \(\lambda h_r\), and not movable before \(j_1\) since it reads running data. The reviewer's second search, "coarse exchanges every level sibling restoring legs move every square mean except root multi-shift", returned ex:restoring-flow-tails, ex:paired-restoring-drift-tails, cor:lagged-flow-obstruction, lem:sibling-exchange-leg, ex:lagged-restoring-tails and lem:sequential-rules-dyadic, none such a witness.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read: thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's proof in the coarse-mean entry (line by line), the registered statements of cor:coarse-mean-growing-shift, lem:conditional-push-obstruction, lem:sibling-exchange-leg, cor:lagged-flow-obstruction and thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction. One medium reviewer, two passes (research/results/ultimate_matching_partial_restoration_20261017/review.txt). Pass one: both proofs work after one repair; the first draft's many-squares step was not local, its push event using signs whose locality the theorem never needed, which the coarse push lemma repairs by keeping on the step's own coarse mean; the contrapositive overstated; the witness checked against a lemma's witness, not its hypothesis; the flux lemma correct. Pass two: the lemma's proof and conditions, the corollary through it, the three refines edges and the flux lemma check; the deterministic witness is covered by the record through regrouping, so the strict extension is not shown, which the entry now says; the spec rationales, the full-restoration sentence and the follow-up's dependence on \(c_0(L)\) corrected in the reviewer's wording, not sent back. Not reviewed: the Baseline's Composed sentence and the Shortest route's last two sentences, added at the append's request after pass two. Scope moved: cor:partial-restoration-obstruction's hypothesis is weaker than the first draft's (on the push event only, \(\lambda_N\) allowed to vary), so more general; the lemma is new and more general than the theorem. Process audit. Title against body: the reviewer found the title matches the body in both passes; the status line now carries that no member beyond the recorded theorems is shown. It found, in pass one, an unasked locality question, an overstated contrapositive, an unsupported negative and orbiting (the mechanism named, no build); in pass two, an overstated witness claim and a rationale written the wrong way; strength count \(6\), then \(4\).

Process assessment. The first draft reran thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's proof trusting that record's own sentence that its mean condition is used "only there", in the push, and lost the locality the condition also supplied; it read the contrapositive as "restores nearly the whole push at every shift" where it gives one square at one step; and it checked its witness against lem:conditional-push-obstruction's witness, not its hypothesis; the second draft's witness escaped the recorded theorems only under its own assignment of steps, the regrouping the coarse-mean entry had raised for the lagged flow left untried. Prevention. AGENTS.md, Order of work: a proof rerun with one hypothesis replaced lists every step the hypothesis serves, read from the steps rather than from the record's sentence on where it is used, indirect services included. The contrapositive and the witness are covered by the existing rules on summaries ("names the class its hypotheses cover") and on witnesses escaping the recorded statement; both were applied after the review, not before, and no check reads either; the regrouping is the existing rule that a question unchanged under another presentation of its object is tried on each presentation, which the witness skipped.

Meta. The habit common to the four: a description stood in for the thing described (a record's sentence on its proof, the mechanism's picture of a contrapositive, a witness's name for a hypothesis, one assignment of steps for the field it decomposes). .claude/agents/medium-reviewer.md now asks every reviewer to check a record's description of itself against its own steps, so the stage that sees the record checks the wider class, beside the drafting rule in AGENTS.md.

Eleventh review: the multi-shift restoring flow lemma-first, then the dual residual class

17 October 2026 · Route review, goal-level · Restoring drift construction and the class bound. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, default).

Where we stand. Unchanged: a route review proves no statement and changes no result that Where we stand summarizes

Where we stand. The goal is open. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is sufficient at every pair of the curve by cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction; its primal form asks for a flow of bounded cost (lem:flow-matching-bound), and on the cells of thm:cell-scale-reduction a flow suffices at finite exponents. No flow of bounded cost above exponent \(2\) is known; the dual side has chain bounds that leave open chains with many layers in bundles.

Falsification attempt. The line's claim is false if every field of the class a flow on cells can take has unbounded cost. Tried: a field restoring at every shift \(1\le s\le R_N\), after each step, in proportion to the coarse mean after the step, \(U_j(P)+\xi_P\), gain \(\gamma\). Its legs at a point \(x\), summed over shifts, are its pointwise correction. Four cases, by how the correction relates to the running value \(R_j(x)\) and to the step's own pointwise push \(D_j(x)\). Legs aligned with \(R_j(x)\) along a run reach about \(m\sqrt N\) over the \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\) finest levels, \((\theta/\ln2)(\ln N)^{1/4}\) times the budget's scale \(\sqrt{N\ln N}(\ln N)^{1/4}\) (about \(0.0017\) at \(\ln N=13.86\), \(\theta=6\cdot10^{-4}\), growing): lem:conditional-push-obstruction's mechanism. Legs independent of both \(R_j(x)\) and \(D_j(x)\) add to a sum of \(m\) independent pushes of about \(\sqrt N\), the dyadic flow's own mechanism, whose lower tail lem:block-lower-tail bounds below (\(P(S\ge xs)\ge e^{-540x^2}\) while \(m\ge128x^2\)), so its \(\psi_4\) cost diverges (the second stage reviewer's correction of this draft, which had called this case below the budget). A drift, a part known before the step that opposes \(R_j(x)\) with a size comparable to the push once \(|R_j(x)|\) is large, escapes the push obstructions: once it exceeds the push, the step no longer pushes along the sign with probability \(p\). Bounded cost by lem:restoring-drift-tail needs more: that lemma is about a scalar walk \(R_{n+1}=R_n-d(R_n)+\xi_{n+1}\) with \(d\) a function of \(R_n\) between \(0\) and \(r\), \(|d(r)|\ge\min(\kappa|r|^{\alpha-1},|r|)\) and sub-Gaussian \(\xi\), and gives \(\psi_\alpha\)-type tails only for a drift growing like \(|r|^{\alpha-1}\), cubic at \(\alpha=4\), up to full restoration; the design's drift is a function of coarse means, not of \(R_j(x)\), so the lemma would apply only in a pathwise form with an adapted \(d_n\), neither stated nor proved, and a push-sized drift meets only its case \(\alpha=1\), exponential tails (the fourth check's reading). A cancellation, a part anti-correlated with \(D_j(x)\), escapes too. The attempt stops there: whether a correction reading coarse means supplies a pointwise drift or a cancellation of the push's size is decided by no recorded statement (the third check of this review corrected an earlier draft that, following the second stage, kept only the cancellation). No falsification.

The eleventh review's test, outcome (A) (the flow meets the extended lemma's hypothesis at small gain, and is excluded) or (B) (its complement): neither occurred; the entry proves the extended lemma the test needs and bounds the step part of the correction, and whether the pre-step part stays small along runs, which decides between (A) and (B), is open.

General statement. lem:local-event-push-obstruction, for every level-by-level field local at a level \(j_1-r\) meeting the Chebyshev condition and every family of events \(A_j(x)\in\mathcal F_j\), local or not; lem:restoring-step-part-tail, for every number of shifts, gain and shape bound.

Lemma (push obstruction on local events)

Setting of lem:conditional-push-obstruction: \(N\) i.i.d. uniform points in \([0,1]^2\), depth \(J\) with \(\kappa\log N\le N4^{-J}\le K\log N\), \(j_1=J-m\), \(m=\lfloor\theta\log_2N\rfloor\), a level-by-level field \(\Phi=\sum_{j<J}\Phi_j\), \(\Phi_j\) measurable with respect to the counts of levels at most \(j+1\), local at level \(j_1-r\) for some \(r\ge0\) with \(j_1-r\ge0\) (for every level-\((j_1-r)\) square \(T\) and \(j\ge j_1\), \(\Phi_j\) on \(T\) a function of \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\) and the points in \(T\)), a coordinate \(k\), \(B_j(x)\) the event that the squares \(S_i(x)\), \(i\le j\), hold at least half their mean counts, \(R_j=\sum_{i<j}\Phi_{i,k}\), \(\sigma_j(x)\) its sign at \(x\), \(+1\) where \(R_j(x)=0\). Let \(G_N\) be a set of measure at least \(N^{-\gamma}\) and, for \(x\in G_N\) and \(j_1\le j\le J\), \(A_j(x)\in\mathcal F_j\) events, jointly measurable in \((x,\omega)\), not necessarily local. Suppose that for every \(x\in G_N\) and \(j_1\le j<J\), on \(A_j(x)\cap B_j(x)\), \(P(\{\sigma_j(x)\Phi_{j,k}(x)\ge h\}\cap A_{j+1}(x)\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p\), and that with probability tending to one \(\lambda\{x\in G_N:A_{j_1}(x)\text{ fails}\}\le\lambda(G_N)/4\). With \(a=\theta\log_2(1/p)+\gamma\), \(\theta\log_2(1/p)<\kappa/8\) and \(4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2a}\to0\) (at \(r=0\), or \(4^r=N^{o(1)}\), this is \(2a<1-2\theta\)), the conclusion of lem:conditional-push-obstruction holds: with \(u_N=4mh/(L\sqrt{N\log N})\), \(\int\psi_\alpha(4|\Phi_k|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\) exceeds every constant with probability tending to one when \(\alpha\) is finite above \(2\) and \(u_N^\alpha-a\ln N\to\infty\), or \(\alpha=\infty\) and \(u_N\ge2\).

Proof. The proof of lem:conditional-push-obstruction, quoted in its entry, with its run's events carrying \(A_j\). Write \(P_j=\{\sigma_j(x)\Phi_{j,k}(x)\ge h\}\in\mathcal F_{j+1}\). On \(P_j\), \(|R_{j+1}(x)|\ge|R_j(x)|+h\), so on \(\bigcap_jP_j\), \(|\Phi_k(x)|\ge mh\). Put \(H_{j_1}=A_{j_1}(x)\cap B_{j_1}(x)\) and \(H_{j+1}=H_j\cap P_j\cap A_{j+1}(x)\cap B_{j+1}(x)\). Since \(H_j\in\mathcal F_j\) and \(H_j\subseteq A_j(x)\cap B_j(x)\), \(P(H_j\cap P_j\cap A_{j+1}(x)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})=\mathbb E[1_{H_j}P(P_j\cap A_{j+1}(x)\mid\mathcal F_j)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge p\,P(H_j\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\), and removing \(B_{j+1}(x)\) costs at most \(P(B_j(x)\setminus B_{j+1}(x)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\): the theorem's recursion, the joint event in place of \(P_j\). Iterating, \(P(|\Phi_k(x)|\ge mh\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\ge p^m1_{A_{j_1}(x)\cap B_{j_1}(x)}-P(B_{j_1}(x)\setminus B_J(x)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\). Exceptional counts: \(\mu=p^m\lambda(G_N)\ge N^{-a}\); \(Y\) and \(Z\) as there, with \(P(Y\ge\mu/8)\le16N^{\theta\log_2(1/p)-\kappa/8}\to0\) and \(P(Z\ge\lambda(G_N)/2)\le4N^{-\kappa/8}\), and \(Z_A=\lambda\{x\in G_N:A_{j_1}(x)\text{ fails}\}\le\lambda(G_N)/4\) with probability tending to one by hypothesis. Many points: \(D=\{x:|\Phi_k(x)|\ge mh\}\) has \(\mathbb E[\lambda(D)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\ge p^m(\lambda(G_N)-Z-Z_A)-Y\ge\mu/4-\mu/8=\mu/8\) outside those events; \(\lambda(D\cap T)\) over the level-\((j_1-r)\) squares \(T\) are conditionally independent given \(\mathcal F_{j_1}\), since \(D\) is defined by \(\Phi\) alone and \(\Phi_j\) for \(j\ge j_1\) is local at level \(j_1-r\) (the events \(A_j\) enter only the conditional expectation above), with \(4^{j_1-r}\) terms of variance at most \(|T|^2/4\), in all at most \(4^{r-j_1}/4\); Chebyshev gives \(P(\lambda(D)<\mu/16\mid\mathcal F_{j_1})\le64\cdot4^{r-j_1}\mu^{-2}\le64\cdot4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2a}\to0\), using \(4^{-j_1}=4^{m-J}\le N^{2\theta}K\log N/N\). Cost: on \(D\) the argument is at least \(u_N\), so \(I_k\ge\frac{N^{-a}}{16}(e^{u_N^\alpha}-1)\to\infty\) for finite \(\alpha\) when \(u_N^\alpha-a\ln N\to\infty\), and \(I_k\ge N^{1-a}/16\to\infty\) at \(\alpha=\infty\), \(a<\frac12\). \(\square\)

Lemma (step part tail)

Points \(N\) i.i.d. uniform in \([0,1]^2\), dyadic squares of side \(\rho_i=2^{-i}\), \(\mathcal F_j\) the counts of levels at most \(j\), a level \(j\), \(R\ge1\) shifts with \(R\le j\), a gain \(\gamma>0\), \(b>0\). For each \(1\le s\le R\) and coordinate \(c\in\{1,2\}\), let \(Q_{s,c}\) be a union of at most two level-\((j-s)\) squares, \(\epsilon_z\in\{-1,0,1\}\) for each point \(z\) of \(Q_{s,c}\), constant on the level-\(j\) squares and \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable, and \(\xi_{s,c}=(2\cdot4^s\rho_j)^{-1}\sum_{z\in Q_{s,c}}\epsilon_z(1\{z\text{ in the lower, for }c=1\text{, or left, for }c=2\text{, half of its level-}j\text{ square}\}-\frac12)\) (with \(\epsilon_z\) the dyadic step's signs and \(Q_{s,c}\) one square, its coarse push; with signs \(\pm\) on a sibling pair, their difference); and weights \(b_{s,c}\ge0\), any random variables (reading the step or not), with \(b_{s,1}+b_{s,2}\le b\). On the event that every level-\((j-s)\) square, \(s\le R\), holds at most twice its mean count, for every \(t>0\), \(P(\gamma\sum_{s\le R}\sum_cb_{s,c}|\xi_{s,c}|\ge t\mid\mathcal F_j)\le4R\exp(-2t^2/(\gamma^2b^2N))\). Hence, for every \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\)-event \(E\) with \(P(E\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p\), \(P(E,\ \gamma\sum_{s,c}b_{s,c}|\xi_{s,c}|\le h/4\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p-4Re^{-h^2/(8\gamma^2b^2N)}\), which is at least \(p/2\) when \(\gamma\le h/(b\sqrt{8N\ln(8R/p)})\).

Proof. Given \(\mathcal F_j\), the counts of the level-\(j\) squares are fixed and their points i.i.d. uniform in each, independent across squares, so each term \(\epsilon_z(1\{\cdot\}-\frac12)\) has mean \(0\) and lies in an interval of length \(1\) (of length \(0\) where \(\epsilon_z=0\)): the push step of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, whose terms are these with one square. \(Q_{s,c}\) holds at most \(n\le2\cdot2N4^s\rho_j^2\) points on the event, so Hoeffding gives \(P(|\xi_{s,c}|\ge v\mid\mathcal F_j)\le2\exp(-2(2\cdot4^s\rho_jv)^2/n)\le2\exp(-2\cdot4^sv^2/N)\). Split \(t\) as \(\sum_{s,c}t_{s,c}\), \(t_{s,c}=t2^{-s}b_{s,c}/b\), whose sum is at most \(t\sum_{s\ge1}2^{-s}\le t\): the sum reaching \(t\) forces, pointwise in \(\omega\), some \(\gamma b_{s,c}|\xi_{s,c}|\ge t_{s,c}\) with \(b_{s,c}>0\), that is \(|\xi_{s,c}|\ge t2^{-s}/(\gamma b)\), an event that does not involve the weights, of probability at most \(2\exp(-2\cdot4^s4^{-s}t^2/(\gamma^2b^2N))=2e^{-2t^2/(\gamma^2b^2N)}\); the union over the at most \(2R\) pairs \((s,c)\) gives the bound. With \(t=h/4\), \(P(E\cap B)\ge P(E)-P(B^c)\) gives the joint bound, whatever the correlation of \(E\) with the pushes, and \(4Re^{-h^2/(8\gamma^2b^2N)}\le p/2\) exactly when \(\gamma^2\le h^2/(8b^2N\ln(8R/p))\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Push obstruction on local events: \(A_j\in\mathcal F_j\), so that \(H_j\in\mathcal F_j\) in the chain rule; their joint measurability in \((x,\omega)\), the integrals \(Z_A\) and \(\mathbb E[\lambda(D)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\) (Fubini); the joint event \(P_j\cap A_{j+1}\), the recursion's next factor; \(A_{j_1}\) failing on at most a quarter of \(G_N\), the lower bound on \(\mathbb E[\lambda(D)\mid\mathcal F_{j_1}]\); the field's locality at level \(j_1-r\), the conditional independence of the \(\lambda(D\cap T)\) over \(4^{j_1-r}\) squares, whence the factor \(4^r\) in Chebyshev; the exponent conditions, the exceptional counts (\(\theta\log_2(1/p)<\kappa/8\)) and Chebyshev (\(4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2a}\to0\)), as in lem:conditional-push-obstruction at \(r=0\). Not used, so not assumed: that \(\Phi\) is a flow, that the events \(A_j\) are local (they enter only the conditional expectation, not \(D\)), anything about \(\Phi\) off \(G_N\). The conclusion holds for every level-by-level field local at a level \(j_1-r\) with \(4^r=N^{o(1)}\) and \(2a<1-2\theta\), or with the displayed condition at larger \(r\). Step part tail: the conditional independence and uniformity of points given \(\mathcal F_j\), Hoeffding; the count bound, the exponent; \(\epsilon_z\) \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable, so that the terms of each \(\xi_{s,c}\) stay independent given \(\mathcal F_j\); \(b_{s,1}+b_{s,2}\le b\) and \(\sum2^{-s}\le1\), the split of \(t\), which holds pointwise in \(\omega\), so the weights may be any random variables (the reviewer's correction: an earlier draft asked them \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable, a hypothesis copied from the flow and used by no step; the lemma is now more general); the union over the \(2R\) pairs. Not used: any bound on \(R\) beyond \(R\le j\) or on \(\gamma\) for the tail (the gain condition is for the joint bound only); any property of \(E\) beyond \(P(E\mid\mathcal F_j)\ge p\).

Degenerate cases. lem:local-event-push-obstruction with \(A_j\) the sure event is lem:conditional-push-obstruction (the joint event is then the push alone, \(Z_A=0\)), with \(\mu/16\) in place of \(\mu/8\) in its count; with \(A_{j_1}\) empty its initial hypothesis fails and it says nothing; at \(p\) with \(\theta\log_2(1/p)\ge\kappa/8\) the exceptional counts are not controlled and it says nothing, as lem:conditional-push-obstruction. lem:restoring-step-part-tail as \(\gamma\to0\) gives probability tending to \(0\) for the step part and the joint bound \(p\); with all \(\epsilon_z=0\) or all \(b_{s,c}=0\) the sum is \(0\) and the bound holds trivially; at \(t\) with \(4Re^{-2t^2/(\gamma^2b^2N)}\ge1\) it says nothing.

Nonvacuity. A field the push obstruction on local events covers and lem:conditional-push-obstruction covers at no \(p,h>0\): \(\Phi_j=0\) for \(j<j_1\), and for \(j_1\le j<J\), with \(S\) the level-\(j\) square of \(x\), \(s_j=\operatorname{sign}E_k(S)\) (\(0\) when \(E_k(S)=0\)), \(Z_j=1+|E_{k'}(S)|/\sqrt{n_S}\) (\(k'\) the other coordinate, \(Z_j=1\) when \(n_S=0\)) and \(h=c\sqrt N\), \(\Phi_{j,k}(x)=hs_jZ_j-\sigma_j(x)(|R_j(x)|+h(1+\sqrt{n_S}))1\{|R_j(x)|>3(j-j_1)h\}\) and \(\Phi_{j,k'}=0\), with \(A_j(x)=\{|R_j(x)|\le3(j-j_1)h\}\), \(G_N=[0,1]^2\) (so \(\gamma=0\)) and \(r=0\); \(A_j\) is jointly measurable, \(R_j(x)\) being constant on the level-\(j\) squares. Measurability: \(s_j,Z_j\) are functions of the counts of \(S\)'s children (level \(j+1\)), \(R_j(x)\) and \(n_S\) are \(\mathcal F_j\)-measurable, and every term depends only on \(x\)'s squares, so \(\Phi\) is local at level \(j_1\). Initial events: \(R_{j_1}=0\), so \(A_{j_1}\) holds everywhere. Joint hypothesis: on \(A_j\cap B_j\) the indicator vanishes and \(\Phi_{j,k}=hs_jZ_j\); when \(s_j=\sigma_j\) and \(Z_j\le3\), \(\sigma_j\Phi_{j,k}=hZ_j\ge h\) and \(|R_{j+1}|\le3(j-j_1)h+3h\), so \(A_{j+1}\) holds; given \(\mathcal F_j\) on \(B_j\) (so \(n_S\ge1\)), \(E_k(S)\) is a centred symmetric count with \(P(E_k(S)=0)\le\frac12\) (\(\binom{n}{n/2}2^{-n}\le\frac12\), computed for \(n\le60\) and decreasing in even \(n\)), so \(P(s_j=\sigma_j)\ge\frac14\), and Hoeffding on the \(n_S\) terms of \(E_{k'}(S)\) gives \(P(Z_j>3)\le2e^{-8}\); so the joint probability is at least \(\frac14-2e^{-8}=0.2493\), and \(p=\frac18\). Exponents: \(\theta\log_2(1/p)=3\theta<\kappa/8\) and \(2(3\theta+\gamma)<1-2\theta\) for small \(\theta,\gamma\); the cost conclusion applies at \((4,4)\) and every \(L\) on the curve parameters, \(u_N=4c\,m\sqrt N/(L\sqrt{N\log N})\ge(2c\theta/L)\sqrt{\log N}\) with \(m\ge\frac12\theta\log_2N\), so \(u_N^4-a\ln N\to\infty\). Outside the original lemma: off \(A_j\), \(\sigma_j\Phi_{j,k}\le hZ_j-|R_j|-h-h\sqrt{n_S}\le h(1+\sqrt{n_S}/2)-h-h\sqrt{n_S}<0\), using \(|E_{k'}(S)|\le n_S/2\); so \(P(\sigma_j\Phi_{j,k}\ge h'\mid\mathcal F_j)=0\) there for every \(h'>0\), and the event \(B_j(x)\setminus A_j(x)\) has positive probability at every \(x\) at \(j=j_1+1\), which suffices (a step \(Z_{j_1}>3\), possible once \(n_S\ge17\), which \(B_{j_1}\) gives for large \(N\), then \(|R_{j_1+1}|>3h\)): lem:conditional-push-obstruction's hypothesis, asked on all of \(B_j(x)\), fails at every \(x\), every \(p>0\) and every \(h'>0\). Step part tail: \(b=6\) (the lagged unit shapes' largest values, below \(2\) and \(4\) for the exchanged and the other coordinate at sides \(8\), \(32\), \(128\): \(1.75\), \(1.94\), \(1.98\) and \(3.75\), \(3.94\), \(3.98\), computed from research/results/ultimate_matching_lagged_restoring_20261017/lagged_test.py's unit_shapes), \(R=1\), \(p=p_0=2^{-768}\) (the coarse-mean proof's push probability) and, as an instance value, \(h=\sqrt{N/32}\) (that proof's \(h_0\)): the joint bound holds for \(\gamma\le\sqrt{1/32}/(6\sqrt{8\ln(8\cdot2^{768})})=0.000451\), an abstract instance of the lemma; the flow's figure, at the pointwise push \(\sqrt{N/128}\), is \(0.000225\) (Bearing). Plainest bound. For the local-event lemma, lem:conditional-push-obstruction itself, which fails on this witness at every \(p,h\); for the step part, Chebyshev with the conditional variance at most \(n/4\) gives \(P(|\xi_{s,c}|\ge v)\le N/(4\cdot4^sv^2)\), polynomial in \(N/v^2\), which at \(p_0=2^{-768}\) asks \(v\) of order \(2^{384}\sqrt N\), so the exponential bound is needed.

Baseline. The bound needing no idea is lem:conditional-push-obstruction, which asks the push on the whole half-full event; the local-event lemma lets the push hold only on local events, paid for by the joint probability with the next event. The step part's baseline is the Chebyshev bound above. Composed. lem:conditional-push-obstruction applied on each event \(A_j\) separately gives nothing, its hypothesis being uniform in the outcome; composed with a restriction of \(G_N\) to points where \(A_j\) holds, it fails because that set is random; so the run's events must enter the chain rule, as here. Hoeffding per shift with a union is the step part's proof itself.

Record comparison. From the record's side: the conditional push entry's proof is the chain rule over the run's events, and the local-event lemma reruns it with \(A_{j+1}\) carried in each factor; that is a citation of its steps, and what is new is the hypothesis's form. Its witness and lem:coarse-push-obstruction, the coarse analogue, do not carry events. The step part tail uses the push step of thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction, whose terms' conditional independence it quotes, and Hoeffding, imported; lem:block-lower-tail is its lower-tail counterpart; the search "upper tail coarse push Hoeffding sub-Gaussian sum of square mean increments conditional on counts" returned lem:band-family-discrepancy, whose (a) bounds count deviations of column-interval unions of cells given their parents by the same Hoeffding argument ("children counts multinomial given the parents, sub-Gaussian deviations, Hoeffding"), and thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction's push step, with the terms used here; lem:restoring-drift-tail (a) is a sub-Gaussian upper tail for a walk whose increments are already sub-Gaussian. None states the tail of the coarse pushes summed over shifts; the step-part tail is that Hoeffding argument applied to them, a citation of its mechanism. The registered statements nearest to the local-event lemma (claim_resemblance.py): lem:conditional-push-obstruction, a special case (the events sure); lem:coarse-push-obstruction, thm:coarse-mean-flow-obstruction and cor:partial-restoration-obstruction push coarse means, not points, and carry no events, so none is a more general version or a special case; thm:square-mean-flow-obstruction pushes level-\(j\) square means by its mean condition, a coarse-push case at shift \(0\), likewise unrelated by implication. Applied to the next attempt and its Smallest case: each decides a field whose push holds on the whole half-full event, which the restoring flow's step does not supply where its pre-step part exceeds the push, so none decides it; lem:restoring-step-part-tail's nearest, lem:conditional-push-obstruction, is an obstruction and gives no tail.

Refinement checked. lem:local-event-push-obstruction implies lem:conditional-push-obstruction: same depth, \(\theta\), locality at level \(j_1\), \(G_N\), \(p\), \(h\), exponents \(a=\theta\log_2(1/p)+\gamma\), \(2a<1-2\theta\), \(\theta\log_2(1/p)<\kappa/8\); with \(A_j\) sure, the joint hypothesis is the original push hypothesis on \(B_j(x)\) and \(A_{j_1}\) never fails; the conclusion is the same cost divergence.

New mathematics. lem:local-event-push-obstruction: a level-by-level field local at a level \(j_1-r\) (with \(4^rK\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2a}\to0\)) whose step pushes the running value at points along its sign jointly with keeping events of \(\mathcal F_{j+1}\), with conditional probability \(p\) on those events, has unbounded cost when the initial events hold on all but a quarter of a set of measure \(N^{-\gamma}\); the events need not be local; it implies lem:conditional-push-obstruction and covers fields that lemma covers at no \(p,h\). lem:restoring-step-part-tail: sums over \(R\) shifts and both coordinates of the coarse pushes at a point, with any random weights of total at most \(b\) per shift, have a sub-Gaussian conditional tail, \(4R\exp(-2t^2/(\gamma^2b^2N))\), so a correction's part reading the step stays below a quarter of a push \(h\) jointly with any event of conditional probability \(p\), at probability \(p/2\), for \(\gamma\le h/(b\sqrt{8N\ln(8R/p)})\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: these are an obstruction and a tail bound; no implication toward conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy is proved. Bearing. At \((4,4)\) and every \(L\) (curve parameters): the multi-shift restoring flow at gain \(\gamma\le h/(b\sqrt{8N\ln(8R_N/p_0)})\) has unbounded cost under three conditions the entry does not establish: its pre-step part stays below a quarter of the push along runs with the probability the local-event lemma asks; the step part tail's upper-count event is part of the events \(A_j\); and \(4^{R_N+1}K\log N\,N^{2\theta-1+2a}\to0\), since the flow's exchanges at shift \(s\) act on sibling pairs inside a level-\((j-s-1)\) parent, so it is local only at level \(j_1-R_N-1\) (for instance \(R_N\le\frac12\log_2\ln N\), as in lem:coarse-push-obstruction). The pointwise push on record is the conditional push witness's, \(\sigma\Phi^0_{j,2}\ge\sqrt{N/128}\) with probability \(p_0=2^{-768}\) on \(G_N\) of measure \((3/4)^m\), so \(\gamma=\theta\log_2(4/3)\) and \(p=p_0/2\) in the exponent conditions; at \(h=\sqrt{N/128}\), \(b=6\) the gain bound is \(0.000225\) at one shift, falling like \(1/\sqrt{\ln R_N}\) (the reviewer's correction: an earlier draft used the coarse-mean push \(\sqrt{N/32}\), giving \(0.000451\), which is not a pointwise push). Not covered. The pre-step part along runs; the upper-count event; locality at level \(j_1-R_N-1\) for growing \(R_N\) beyond \(4^{R_N}=N^{o(1)}\); gains above that bound, up to the gain-\(1\) instability; restoring designs other than the multi-shift exchanges; the cost of a design meeting outcome (B).

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: the pre-step part along runs: on a run of pushes at \(x\), the coarse running means \(U_j(P_s(x))\) receive from the pushes at \(x\) a share of about \(4^{-s}\) per level (the reviewer's share sketch, unverified) and from the rest of \(P_s\) a centred walk restored at gain \(\gamma\); bound \(P(A_{j+1}\mid P_j,A_j,\mathcal F_j)\), \(A_j=\{\gamma b\sum_s|U_j(P_s(x))|\le h/4\}\), from below, via lem:restoring-drift-tail on each coarse mean with the walk's increments sub-Gaussian by the step part tail. Smallest case. One shift, \(s=1\), two levels: \(U_{j+1}(P)=(1-\gamma)(U_j(P)+\xi_P)\) for the post-step restoration, so after a push at \(x\) the coarse mean moves by \((1-\gamma)\xi_P\), sub-Gaussian given \(\mathcal F_j\) with \(\sigma^2\le N/16\) for the restored pair's difference (twice the one-square bound \(N4^{-1}/8\) under Own statements, the count doubling) whatever the push at \(x\), the push at \(x\) entering \(\xi_P\) through one of the four level-\(j\) squares of \(P\), a quarter of its terms; so \(A_{j+1}\) fails only if \(\gamma b(1-\gamma)|U_j+\xi_P|>h/4\), which, when \(|U_j|\le h/(8\gamma b)\), asks \(\gamma b|\xi_P|>h/8\), with \(\xi_P\) the restored pair's difference (a union of two level-\((j-1)\) squares), of probability at most \(2\exp(-2\cdot4\,v^2/N)=2e^{-h^2/(8\gamma^2b^2N)}\) at \(v=h/(8\gamma b)\) by the Hoeffding step of the step part tail applied directly (its split over shifts would lose a factor \(4\) in the exponent). Nontrivial because: the push at \(x\) and \(\xi_P\) share the terms of \(x\)'s own square, so the next event is correlated with the push, which the joint hypothesis has to pay for. Plainest bound. The union bound \(P(P_j\cap A_{j+1})\ge P(P_j)-P(A_{j+1}^c)\) with the step part tail gives the joint probability \(p_0-2e^{-h^2/(8\gamma^2b^2N)}\) whenever \(U_j\) is at most \(h/(8\gamma b)\), at least \(p_0/2\) for \(\gamma\le h/(b\sqrt{8N\ln(4/p_0)})\); along a run, \(U_j\) itself is the open quantity, and so are two conditions the application needs (the reviewer's): the upper-count event of the step part tail, which \(B_j\) does not contain and which must be put into \(A_j\), and the flow's locality, only at level \(j_1-R_N-1\). The main parts: main is \(\pm2T\) on the two children of a pair, which share their positions along the exchange's axis, so against a gradient component that does not vary across the pair the two children cancel exactly: for the coordinate-1 exchange (children stacked in \(y\), main in \(w_1\)), \(\partial_xg=2x\) for \(x^2\) and \(0\) for \(y^3\); for the coordinate-2 exchange (children side by side in \(x\), main in \(w_2\)), \(\partial_yg=0\) for \(x^2\) and \(3y^2\) for \(y^3\); none varies across its pair, so the main parts give exactly \(0\) for both functions, at every amplitude. The other parts, flipped or not, are \(\mp a'\,4c(y)S(x)\) in \(w_2\) from each coordinate-1 exchange and \(\mp a'\,4c(x)S(y)\) in \(w_1\) from each coordinate-2 exchange, \(a'\) constant on each parent, with \(S=-2\) on one half of the child and \(+2\) on the other, odd about the child's centre line, so \(\sum S=0\) along every row (first) and every column (second) of every child. Process assessment. The cycle spent three review passes, mostly on sentences written from a picture of an object rather than its source: a script's comment for its code, a coarse mean's push for a point's, the flow's measurability for the lemma's need, a variance from a remembered factor. Prevention. AGENTS.md, Order of work: a script's record is its code, not a comment describing it, and a figure stood in for by a neighbouring one is a picture too (this cycle's commit). The closure check's masking and merge bypasses are now refused by tools/finish-turn.py's per-item scopes, with tests for each case. The hypothesis read off the proof, the unsupported negative and the unchecked figure are covered by existing rules applied at the review rather than at drafting; no new check, since none can tell a copied hypothesis from a used one.

Meta. The habit: drafting a sentence about an object from what I expect it to be, then checking the arithmetic but not the premise. It shows in figures (the push size), in readings of code (the flip) and in hypotheses (the weights). The change: for every property an entry uses of a recorded object, I open the object's source (code, statement or proof step) before writing the sentence, and quote it; AGENTS.md's Order of work now says so for scripts and stand-in figures.

Chains whose steep edges lie on separated straight bundles

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed · Mixed-level counts, the dual residual class. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).
