General statement. cor:fine-mesh-function-tube for every cell function at every fine mesh and tube scale; lem:separated-bundle-chains for every nested chain with heights in \([2e^{16},V]\), every number of layers and every family of separated straight bundles.

Corollary (fine-mesh function tube bound)

Statement. On the event of lem:guided-chain-bound (probability tending to one), for every dyadic \(\delta_0\) with \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), every dyadic \(W=2^{-k}\in[2^{-\ell_1},1]\) and every \(H\) constant on the cells of side \(\delta_0\), \[|D(H)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,\mathrm{TV}(H)+L\sqrt N\,\Phi_k\Big(\mathrm{TV}(H)+12W\sum_{Q\in\mathcal G_k}\big(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-\big)\Big),\] \(\Phi_k=(2(\ell_1-k)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\), \(\mathrm{TV}(H)=\sum_e\delta_0|\Delta_eH|\) over inner edges, \(\mathcal G_k\) the \(W\)-cells, \(D(H)=\sum_iH(X_i)-N\int H\).

Proof. \(H\) takes finitely many values, so \(H=\int_0^\infty1_{\{H>t\}}dt-\int_0^\infty1_{\{H<-t\}}dt\) and \(D\) is linear. Each \(\{H>t\}\) is a union \(A\) of cells; lem:guided-chain-bound (a) with \(S=\emptyset\) and \(T\) the \(W\)-cells meeting \(A\) gives \(|D(1_A)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}P(A)+L\sqrt N\Phi_k(P(A)+12W\#T)\). Integrate over \(t\): \(\int_0^\infty P(\{H>t\})dt+\int_0^\infty P(\{H<-t\})dt=\mathrm{TV}(H)\) (an inner edge with values \(u,v\) lies on \(\partial\{H>t\}\) or \(\partial\{H<-t\}\) for a set of \(t\) of length \(|u-v|\)), and a \(W\)-cell \(Q\) meets \(\{H>t\}\) exactly for \(t<\max_QH^+\). \(\square\)

Lemma (separated bundle chains)

Statement. On the intersection of the events of lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound and lem:guided-chain-bound at \(\kappa=4\), for every dyadic \(\delta_0\) with \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), at \((4,4)\): let \(g=\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}y_k1_{A_k}\) be a nested chain (\(A_1\supseteq\dots\supseteq A_K\) unions of cells, \(K\) arbitrary) with heights \(y_k\in[2e^{16},V]\), \(V\ge2e^{16}\), and discrete cost \(\sum_ew_e\le2\), \(w_e=\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\), \(v_e=\sum_{k:\,e\in\partial A_k}y_k\) the edge's increment over \(\delta_0\). Let \(\mathcal B\) be a family of bundles \(b\), each a straight run \(\Gamma_b\) of \(\ell_b/\delta_0\) collinear inner edges and a group \(t_b<k\le t_b+m_b\), with \(Y_b=\sum_{t_b<k\le t_b+m_b}y_k\), such that (B1) every edge of \(\Gamma_b\) lies on exactly the boundaries \(\partial A_k\), \(t_b<k\le t_b+m_b\); (B2) the strip \(S_b\) of the cells on the inner side of \(\Gamma_b\) at depth \(0,\dots,m_b\) (an \(\ell_b\times(m_b+1)\delta_0\) rectangle) lies in \(A_{t_b+m_b}\setminus A_{t_b+m_b+1}\); (B3) the strips are pairwise disjoint; (B4) \(\ell_b\ge\max\{2^{-\ell_1},\,2m_b\delta_0(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\}\). With \(\eta_W=\sum w_e(\log v_e)^{1/4}\) over the edges with \(v_e>V\) on no \(\Gamma_b\), \[|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\Big(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W\Big),\] \(C\) universal. At one height \(y\), \(V=My\) and \(v_e=m_ey\) give the bound with \((\log\max\{My,2e^{16}\})^{1/4}\) for the edges of multiplicity above \(M\) on no bundle.

Proof. Spread chain. For each \(b\) and \(k\) put \(d^b_k=0\) for \(k\le t_b\), \(d^b_k=k-t_b\) for \(t_b<k\le t_b+m_b\), \(d^b_k=m_b\) beyond, \(S_b(d)\) the cells of \(S_b\) at depth below \(d\), and \(A'_k=A_k\setminus\bigcup_bS_b(d^b_k)\). Since \(d^b_k\) is nondecreasing in \(k\), \(S_b(d)\) increasing in \(d\), and the \(A_k\) nested, the \(A'_k\) are nested; \(g'=\delta_0\sum_ky_k1_{A'_k}\). By (B2), \(A_k\supseteq S_b\) for \(k\le t_b+m_b\) and \(A_k\cap S_b=\emptyset\) beyond, so \(g\) is constant on \(S_b\). By (B2) and (B3) a cell \(Q\) at depth \(i<m_b\) of \(S_b\) leaves exactly the layers \(t_b+i<k\le t_b+m_b\), so \(g'(Q)=g(Q)-\delta_0R(Q)\) with \(R(Q)=\sum_{t_b+i<k\le t_b+m_b}y_k\le Y_b\), and \(R=0\) off the strips' depths below \(m_b\). Increments of \(g'\): on every edge \(e\) between \(Q\) and \(Q'\), \(v'_e\le v_e+\max\{R(Q),R(Q')\}\) and \(v'_e=|v_e\pm(R(Q)-R(Q'))|\). Three kinds of edge change. (i) The line between depths \(i-1\) and \(i\) of \(S_b\), \(1\le i\le m_b\) (depth \(m_b\) is in \(S_b\), with \(R=0\)): \(g\) is constant across it and \(v'_e=y_{t_b+i}\). (ii) An edge of \(\Gamma_b\): its inner cell \(Q\) has \(R(Q)=Y_b\) and by (B1) \(g(Q)-g(Q_{\rm out})=\delta_0Y_b\), so \(v'_e=R(Q_{\rm out})\), zero unless the outer cell lies in another strip \(S_{b'}\) (at depth below \(m_{b'}\)), and then the edge is a side edge of \(S_{b'}\) with \(v'_e\le Y_{b'}\). (iii) Every other edge with \(R(Q)\ne R(Q')\): let \(Q\) carry the larger \(R\), in \(S_b\) at depth \(i<m_b\); the edge lies on the perimeter of \(S_b\)'s first \(m_b\) rows and is neither on \(\Gamma_b\) (case (ii)) nor the line to depth \(m_b\) (case (i)), so it is one of the \(2m_b\) side edges of \(S_b\), with \(v'_e\le v_e+Y_b\). So every changed edge outside (i) is a side edge of exactly one strip, charged to it, at most \(2m_b\) for \(S_b\). Costs: \(\Gamma_b\)'s edges cost \(c_b=(\ell_b/\delta_0)\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)\) in \(g\); the depth lines cost \(\sum_{t_b<k\le t_b+m_b}(\ell_b/\delta_0)\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y_k/2)\le c_b\), \(\psi_4^*\) being convex with \(\psi_4^*(0)=0\), hence superadditive; a side edge of \(S_b\) costs at most \(\delta_0^2\psi_4^*((v_e+Y_b)/2)\le\frac12\delta_0^2(\psi_4^*(v_e)+\psi_4^*(Y_b))\le\frac72(w_e+\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2))\), by convexity and \(\psi_4^*(2t)\le7\psi_4^*(t)\) for \(t\ge e^{16}\) (from the recorded \(\frac t{2\sqrt2}(\log t)^{1/4}\le\psi_4^*(t)\le t(2\log t)^{1/4}+1\): the ratio is at most \(2\cdot2^{1/4}\cdot2\sqrt2(\log2t/\log t)^{1/4}+o(1)\le6.9\)), the case \(v_e=0\) included. With \(s_b\) the original cost of the side edges charged to \(S_b\) (each edge charged once, so \(\sum_bs_b\le2\)) and \(2m_b\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)=\frac{2m_b\delta_0}{\ell_b}c_b\le c_b(\log Y_b)^{-1/4}\le c_b/2\) by (B4), the cost of \(g'\) is at most \(2+E\), \(E=\frac72\sum_b(s_b+2m_b\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2))\le\frac72\cdot3=10.5\). With \(c=1+E/2\le6.25\), \(g''=g'/c\) has cost at most \(2\) (\(\psi_4^*(t/c)\le\psi_4^*(t)/c\) for \(c\ge1\)). lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) for \(g''\): its \(W\) is at most the sum over \(g'\)'s edges with \(v'_e\ge2e^{16}\) of \(w'_e(\log v'_e)^{1/4}\). The unchanged edges with \(v_e\le V\) give at most \(2(\log V)^{1/4}\), those with \(v_e>V\) at most \(\eta_W\) (no \(\Gamma_b\) edge is unchanged unless its \(v'_e=0\)); the depth lines, increments \(y_k\le V\), at most \(\sum_bc_b(\log V)^{1/4}\le2(\log V)^{1/4}\). A side edge of \(S_b\) has \(w'_e\le7\max\{w_e,\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)\}\) and \((\log v'_e)^{1/4}\le(\log(2\max\{v_e,Y_b\}))^{1/4}\le1.02(\log\max\{v_e,Y_b\})^{1/4}\); if \(v_e\ge Y_b\), it contributes at most \(7.2w_e(\log v_e)^{1/4}\), a term of \(\eta_W\) when \(v_e>V\), or of \(7.2\cdot2(\log V)^{1/4}\) in all otherwise, or, for an edge of another bundle's \(\Gamma_{b''}\) (case (ii) charged to \(S_b\)), at most \(7.2\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\) since then \(v'_e\le Y_b\); if \(v_e<Y_b\), it contributes at most \(7.2\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\). Over the at most \(2m_b\) side edges of \(S_b\) the last kind sums to at most \(7.2\frac{2m_b\delta_0}{\ell_b}(\log Y_b)^{1/4}c_b\le7.2c_b\) by (B4). So \(W\le C(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W)\) and \(|D(g')|=c|D(g'')|\le C_1\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W)\).

Remainder. \(H=g-g'=\sum_bH_b\), \(H_b=\delta_0R\) on \(S_b\), equal to \(\delta_0\sum_{t_b+i<k\le t_b+m_b}y_k\) at depth \(i<m_b\), nonincreasing in \(i\), at most \(\delta_0Y_b\), and \(0\) elsewhere. Its total variation: \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) across \(\Gamma_b\), \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) over the depth lines (the jumps telescope to \(\delta_0Y_b\) along each column), and at most \(2m_b\delta_0\cdot\delta_0Y_b\) on the sides, so \(\mathrm{TV}(H_b)\le2\ell_bY_b\delta_0+2m_bY_b\delta_0^2\le3\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) by (B4). Take \(W_b=2^{-k_b}\) the dyadic number in \([\max\{m_b\delta_0,2^{-\ell_1}\},2\max\{m_b\delta_0,2^{-\ell_1}\})\); by (B4), \(W_b<2\ell_b\) and \(m_b\delta_0\le W_b\), so the \(W_b\)-cells meeting the support of \(H_b\) lie in at most \(3\) rows and \(\ell_b/W_b+2\) columns, each with \(\max H_b^+\le Y_b\delta_0\) and \(H_b^-=0\): \(12W_b\sum_Q\max_QH_b^+\le36(\ell_b+2W_b)Y_b\delta_0\le180\,\ell_bY_b\delta_0\). cor:fine-mesh-function-tube gives \(|D(H_b)|\le(3c_4\sqrt{\log N}+183L\Phi_{k_b})\sqrt N\,\ell_bY_b\delta_0\), with \(\ell_1-k_b\le\log_2(2\max\{m_b\delta_02^{\ell_1},1\})\le\log_2(2m_b)\) (as \(\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\)), so \(\Phi_{k_b}\le(2\log_2(2m_b)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\). By the recorded lower bound at \(Y_b/2\ge e^{16}\), \(c_b\ge\ell_b\delta_0\frac{Y_b/2}{2\sqrt2}(\log(Y_b/2))^{1/4}\), so \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\le4\sqrt2\,c_b(\log(Y_b/2))^{-1/4}\). A single edge of \(\Gamma_b\) costs at most \(2\), and \(\psi_4^*(t)\ge\frac t{2\sqrt2}(\log t)^{1/4}\ge0.7t\), so \(Y_b\le6/\delta_0^2\le N\) (as \(\delta_0^2\ge16\log N/N\)), and \(m_b\le Y_b/(2e^{16})\); hence \((2\log_2(2m_b)+5)^{3/4}(\log(Y_b/2))^{-1/4}\le C\sqrt{\log N}\). Lemma (staircase bundle chains)

Statement. In the setting of lem:separated-bundle-chains (its events at \(\kappa=4\), \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\), \((4,4)\), a nested chain \(g=\delta_0\sum_{k\le K}y_k1_{A_k}\) with heights in \([2e^{16},V]\) and discrete cost at most \(2\), increments \(v_e\)), let \(\mathcal B\) be a family of bundles \(b\), each a monotone lattice path \(\Gamma_b\) of grid length \(\ell_b\), after a reflection of the square going up and to the right, its inner side above, \(\tau_b=(-\delta_0,\delta_0)\) in that frame, and a group \(t_b<k\le t_b+m_b\) of total height \(Y_b\). Band \(i\ge0\) of \(b\) is the set of cells whose centre is \(\gamma+(i+\frac12)\tau_b\) for a lattice point \(\gamma\) of \(\Gamma_b\), endpoints included. Suppose (B1) every edge of \(\Gamma_b\) lies on exactly the boundaries \(\partial A_k\), \(t_b<k\le t_b+m_b\); (B2) the strip \(S_b\), bands \(0,\dots,m_b\), lies in \(A_{t_b+m_b}\setminus A_{t_b+m_b+1}\); (B3) the strips are pairwise disjoint; (B4) \(\ell_b\ge\max\{2^{-\ell_1},\,4m_b\delta_0(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\}\). With \(\eta_W\) as there, \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W)\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. The proof of lem:separated-bundle-chains with the strip's depth rows replaced by bands; the changes, step by step. Bands. On a monotone path the points with an integer anti-diagonal coordinate \(u=(x+y)/\delta_0\) are lattice points, one for each \(u\) in \([u_p,u_q]\), \(p,q\) the endpoints; a cell centre \(c\) has integer \(u\), and the line \(c+s\tau_b\) keeps \(u\), so \(c\) is in at most one band, with its \(\gamma\) the lattice point of \(\Gamma_b\) at \(c\)'s \(u\) and \(i+\frac12\) the distance along \(\tau_b\). Neighbours: for cells with centres \(c\) and \(c+(\delta_0,0)\), \(c=\gamma+(i+\frac12)\tau_b\), the lattice point at \(u+1\) is \(\gamma'=\gamma+(\delta_0,0)\) or \(\gamma+(0,\delta_0)\), the next step of \(\Gamma_b\); in the first case both cells are in band \(i\) and the edge between them is on no translate; in the second \(c+(\delta_0,0)=\gamma'+(i-\frac12)\tau_b\) is in band \(i-1\), and the edge between them is the vertical edge of \(\Gamma_b+i\tau_b\) translated from \(\Gamma_b\)'s step \(\gamma\to\gamma'\). Vertical neighbours likewise, with the roles of the steps exchanged. So the translates \(\Gamma_b+i\tau_b\), \(i\ge1\), are edge-disjoint (each edge between a band-\((i-1)\) and a band-\(i\) cell), each edge of \(\Gamma_b+i\tau_b\) has a band-\((i-1)\) cell and a band-\(i\) cell on its two sides, and the inner cell of each edge of \(\Gamma_b\) is in band \(0\) (the case \(i=0\)). Depth lines. Cells of one band adjacent across an edge share their value of \(R\) (as there, a band-\(i\) cell, \(i<m_b\), leaves the layers \(t_b+i<k\le t_b+m_b\)). So the depth line \(\Gamma_b+i\tau_b\) has increment \(y_{t_b+i}\), \(1\le i\le m_b\), and the depth lines cost at most \(\sum_k(\ell_b/\delta_0)\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(y_k/2)\le c_b\), \(c_b=(\ell_b/\delta_0)\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)\) the cost of \(\Gamma_b\)'s edges, by superadditivity. Sides. The edges between a cell of bands \(0,\dots,m_b-1\) and a cell outside them, other than those of \(\Gamma_b\) and \(\Gamma_b+m_b\tau_b\), join cells whose \(u\) is \(u_p-1\) and \(u_p\), or \(u_q\) and \(u_q+1\) (by the neighbour analysis, inside \([u_p,u_q]\) every edge out of a band goes to the next or previous band): at each end the cells of the first \(m_b\) bands at \(u_p\) (or \(u_q\)) number \(m_b\), each with at most two such edges, so at most \(4m_b\) side edges in all, whichever way the path's end steps turn. The three kinds of changed edge are as there, case (iii) now on these \(4m_b\) edges; the contact cases (ii) as there, an edge lying on no two of \(\Gamma_b\), \(\Gamma_{b'}+m_{b'}\tau_{b'}\) by (B1), the inner sides and (B3). The cost and \(W\) accounting are unchanged with \(2m_b\) replaced by \(4m_b\): \(4m_b\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(Y_b/2)=\frac{4m_b\delta_0}{\ell_b}c_b\le c_b(\log Y_b)^{-1/4}\le c_b/2\) by (B4), so \(E\le10.5\) and the side lines' \(W\) at most \(7.2(2(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W+2)\) as there. Remainder. \(H_b=\delta_0R\) on bands \(0,\dots,m_b-1\), nonincreasing in the band index, at most \(\delta_0Y_b\); its total variation is \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) across \(\Gamma_b\), at most \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) over the translates (the jumps telescope to \(\delta_0Y_b\) across the bands), and at most \(4m_bY_b\delta_0^2\) on the sides, so \(\mathrm{TV}(H_b)\le3\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) by (B4). A band-\(i\) cell has its centre at \(\ell^\infty\)-distance \((i+\frac12)\delta_0\) from a lattice point of \(\Gamma_b\), so it lies within \(\ell^\infty\)-distance \((i+1)\delta_0\le m_b\delta_0\le W_b\) of \(\Gamma_b\) for \(i\le m_b-1\), \(W_b\) as there (\(m_b\delta_0\le W_b<2\ell_b\)). In half-open \(W\)-cells, a monotone path of grid length \(\ell=\Delta x+\Delta y\) meets at most \(\ell/W+3\) cells (it crosses at most \(\Delta x/W+1\) vertical and \(\Delta y/W+1\) horizontal lines of mesh \(W\), each crossing entering one new cell); the cells within \(\ell^\infty\)-distance \(W\) of those lie in their \(3\times3\) blocks, so the support meets at most \(9(\ell_b/W_b+3)\) \(W_b\)-cells, and \(12W_b\sum_Q\max_QH_b^+\le108(\ell_b+3W_b)Y_b\delta_0\le756\ell_bY_b\delta_0\) (\(W_b<2\ell_b\)). cor:fine-mesh-function-tube then gives \(|D(H_b)|\le(3c_4\sqrt{\log N}+759L\Phi_{k_b})\sqrt N\,\ell_bY_b\delta_0\), and the rest is as there: \(\ell_bY_b\delta_0\le4\sqrt2c_b(\log(Y_b/2))^{-1/4}\), \(\Phi_{k_b}\le(2\log_2(2m_b)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\), \(Y_b\le N\), \(\sum c_b\le2\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. As in lem:separated-bundle-chains, with: monotonicity of \(\Gamma_b\) (after a reflection, nondecreasing in both coordinates), for the one lattice point at each anti-diagonal coordinate, hence the band structure, the edge-disjoint translates and the side count, and for the count of \(W\)-cells met; \(\tau_b\) toward the inner side, so that the bands lie in the layers the group shares; (B4) with the factor \(4\), the \(4m_b\) side edges, and with \(2^{-\ell_1}\), for \(W_b<2\ell_b\). Not used: any bound on the number of turns of \(\Gamma_b\), its slope, or \(K\).

Degenerate cases. A straight horizontal \(\Gamma_b\) is a monotone path; the lemma then gives lem:separated-bundle-chains' conclusion with a slanted strip (its rows shifted one cell left per band) in place of the rectangle and (B4) with \(4\) for \(2\), neither implying the other's hypotheses. A path with one cell is excluded by (B4). \(\mathcal B\) empty: lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) for chains.

Nonvacuity. On the curve parameters at \((4,4)\), with \(\delta_0\), \(n\), \(y=2e^{16}\), \(m\), \(V=y\) as in the separated bundles witness, \(G=\lfloor n/(16ym(2\log(my))^{1/4})\rfloor\), \(K=Gm\): layer \(k=jm+i\) the cells \(\{(x,z):n/8+k\le x<7n/8-k,\ f_j(x)\le z<7n/8-k\}\), \(f_j(x)=b_j+\lfloor(x-n/8)/2\rfloor\), \(b_j=n/8+j(2m+2)\). Nested; the left, right and top sides of distinct layers are distinct lines, and no other layer's side meets \(\Gamma_j\)'s edges, later groups' sides starting above \(f_{j+1}\); group \(j\)'s bottoms follow the staircase \(f_j\), rising one row every two columns, with a turn every two cells, so no straight run of it is longer than \(2\delta_0\) and lem:separated-bundle-chains, whose (B4) asks \(2m\delta_0(\log(my))^{1/4}\), does not apply. \(\Gamma_j\) the staircase over the group's common columns less \(m+1\) columns at each end: monotone, multiplicity \(m\) (B1); a cell of bands \(0,\dots,m\) lies at most \(i+1\le m+1\) columns left of \(\Gamma_j\), so within the group's last layer's columns, and at most \(i+\lceil(i+1)/2\rceil\le1.5m+1\) rows above \(f_j\) over its column, below \(f_{j+1}=f_j+2m+2\) (B2); (B3); (B4) \(\ell_j\ge\frac12\). The cut-off ends, of multiplicity up to \(m\), are off-bundle high edges. Computed (research/results/ultimate_matching_staircase_bundles_20261017/witness_arithmetic.txt; a parameter evaluation testing no statement, run before its commit with the exploratory flag) at \(\ln N=80,140,200,400,700\): height used \(0.375n\) of \(\frac34n\), cost at most \(0.152\) (bundles at most \(0.047\), single sides at most \(0.105\), ends below \(10^{-12}\)), bundles' cost at least \(0.0046\), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\ge0.041\); \(\log K=15.6,45.4,75.2,174.9,324.6\) against lem:multilevel-chain-bound's \(46.8,67.9,86.2,136.8,198.7\), failing from \(\ln N=400\), and above lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d)'s \(\ln N/7\) at every size. The ends' \(\eta_W\to0\), and the lemma gives \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log(2e^{16}))^{1/4}+\eta_W)\). One function. The witness is one function fixed before the points, with \(\sup|g|\le Ky\delta_0<1\), so \(\mathrm{Var}\,D(g)\le N\) and Chebyshev gives \(|D(g)|=O_P(\sqrt N)\), below the lemma's bound; lem:guided-chain-bound (d), with its guide family the coarse roundings of the witness's own \(K\le\sqrt N\) layers, decides it too (the reviewer's application, not rerun here). The witness shows only that the class has members with many layers on turning bundles; what the lemma adds is the bound uniformly over its class, which has far more than \(N^c\) members, so the witness's own-guides argument does not extend to the class; a union over a coarser guide family, lem:guided-chain-bound (d) with guides of side about \(1/\log N\), fails that clause's condition on \(w\) by the reviewer's sketch (unverified), not tried here. Plainest bound. For the one function, Chebyshev, above. The plainest uniform bound, a union of one-function tails over the witness's family (the chains of the class), is the record's union over boundary curves by their length, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b): \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\), above \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) by a factor computed \(0.140,0.156,0.168,0.191\) (times \(L\)) at \(\ln N=80,140,200,400\) on the witness, of order \((\log N)^{1/8}\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) leaves \(6\eta(\log(my))^{1/4}\) with \(\eta\ge0.0046\), of order \((\log N)^{1/8}\). Tried. On this witness: Chebyshev on the one function, which decides it; uniformly: lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) on \(g\), factor computed above; lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b), \(\eta\ge0.0046\) computed; lem:separated-bundle-chains on the staircase's straight runs, excluded by its (B4) since runs have at most \(2\) cells against \(2m(\log(my))^{1/4}\); lem:multilevel-chain-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), their counts compared above; the band clauses, compared in the Baseline; the proof's own steps alone: the spread chain \(g'\) by lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) is bounded at the conjectured order, but \(g\) is not \(g'\), and the remainder alone by cor:fine-mesh-function-tube is bounded too, so the uniform bound rests on the two together, the proof itself.

Baseline. The bounds needing no idea: for one fixed function, Chebyshev, \(O_P(\sqrt N)\); uniformly, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b), the bundles charged their logarithm; lem:separated-bundle-chains, for straight bundles only. Composed. lem:separated-bundle-chains applied to the straight runs of a staircase treats each run of length \(s\delta_0\) as a bundle, which (B4) excludes once \(s<2m(\log Y)^{1/4}\), so on staircases turning every few cells it gives nothing; applied with the runs' high edges left in \(\eta_W\) it is lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound's charge. lem:multilevel-chain-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) need their counts of layers; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) applied to the spread chain and the remainder separately gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\) on each. lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (c) and (d), applied to each bundle alone, does not apply as stated: they bound "a band a phi(y - f(x)) with |f'| <= K, ramp width w >= 2^(-l_1)", and its (e), "a band with ramps w >= 6 sqrt(log N/N)", by "the plain per-cell count bound", likewise along such a graph; a bundle is a sharp jump of width \(\delta_0\) along a finite monotone path of any slope. lem:band-family-discrepancy, applied to each bundle alone, does not apply either: its (b) allows "any ramp width w > 0" and its (c) asks "disjoint bands inside the square along full-width graphs, slopes at most K, ramp gradients y_r >= e^16, any ramp widths, with class cost at most 2", while a group's layers are nested, not disjoint bands across the square; these clauses cover the class only where its layers are such full-width bands along graphs of bounded slope, a layer indicator being a band only in the limit \(w\to0\) that (b) allows, and give nothing on bundles that end inside the square or turn vertical; there the route is (b) per layer, summed by the triangle inequality, its total amplitude to be bounded through the cost (the reviewer's route, not checked here). The excerpts read do not define \(\varphi\) or a band's two sides; if a band has both sides along \(f\), the witness's layers, with horizontal tops and vertical sides, are not bands at all.

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:separated-bundle-chains' proof is reused step for step; what is new is the band structure along a monotone path (bands by cell centres, the edge-disjoint translates, the band on each side of each translate's edge, the side count at the ends, the count of \(W\)-cells met by a monotone path), which replaces straightness. Neither lemma implies the other: a straight run with a rectangle strip meets lem:separated-bundle-chains' (B2) and not necessarily this (B2), whose strip is slanted, and conversely staircases meet only this one. The band clauses of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and lem:band-family-discrepancy, compared in the Baseline, cover full-width bands along graphs of bounded slope, a different class. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound is neither more general nor a special case: it bounds every grid function with the loss \(W\), the cost-weighted \((\log v_e)^{1/4}\), which on the lemma's class charges each bundle \((\log Y_b)^{1/4}\) times its cost, while the lemma removes that charge on its class only; the lemma uses its (a) for the spread chain. lem:discrete-flow-bound, of which lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) is a refinement, stands in the same relation, its (b) and (c) charging the largest increment. The registered statements the search returned (lem:separated-bundle-chains, and unrelated records) carry no translate structure.

Refinement checked. No refines edge: neither statement implies the other, as compared above.

New mathematics. lem:staircase-bundle-chains: lem:separated-bundle-chains with straight runs replaced by monotone lattice paths and rectangle strips by bands of cells whose centres lie at half-integer diagonal distances from the path toward its inner side, (B4) with the factor \(4\): a nested chain with heights in \([2e^{16},V]\) and discrete cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\), any number of layers, whose edges of increment above \(V\) lie on such separated monotone bundles, up to off-bundle steep edges of cost-weighted log \(\eta_W\), has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W)\). Also, by a pigeonhole (Follow-up): inward spreading cannot lower the multiplicity of a stack of \(D\) lines of multiplicity \(m\) with \(r\) free rows behind it below \(mD/(D+r)\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy needs every grid function of cost at most \(2\); the lemma covers only a class of chains, those whose steep edges lie on separated monotone bundles. Bearing. At \((4,4)\), on the curve parameters: every chain of the lemma's class has discrepancy \(O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) at bounded \(V\) and \(\eta_W\), uniformly over the class, at every number of layers and every number of turns of its bundles; the class is not covered by the recorded uniform chain bounds (lem:multilevel-chain-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), their counts of layers; lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound and lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), their logarithm of the bundles' increments; lem:separated-bundle-chains, straight runs; lem:guided-chain-bound (d), guides from "a family F_N of at most N^c unions of cells of side 2^(-l_1) fixed before the points are drawn" and its condition on \(w\); the band clauses, full-width bands along graphs of bounded slope). Its witness, one fixed function, is decided by Chebyshev and serves only to show the class has such members. Not covered. Bundles along paths that are not monotone (a path turning back, such as a closed curve, is monotone only piecewise, each piece a bundle under (B4)); strips that meet a later layer (collisions), among them stacks of lines too close to spread; bundles shorter than \(4m_b\delta_0(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\); heights below \(2e^{16}\); grid functions that are not chains.

Follow-up. Continuing. Collisions, tried. The separated bundles entry's reviewer's lead (unverified there): when a later layer enters the strip at depth \(j<m_b\), cap the spread, \(d^b_k=\min(k-t_b,j)\), and leave a residual bundle on the collision line. Its smallest case, by hand: a straight bundle of \(m=2\) layers \(t+1,t+2\) on \(\Gamma\), \(A_{t+3}\) containing the strip's depth-\(1\) cells with its boundary on the line between depths \(0\) and \(1\). Nesting allows the spreads \((d_{t+1},d_{t+2})\in\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)\}\): \((0,0)\) leaves multiplicity \(2\) on \(\Gamma\); \((0,1)\) gives \(1\) on \(\Gamma\) and \(2\) on the depth-\(1\) line (layers \(t+2\), \(t+3\)); \((1,1)\), the lead's formula as written, gives \(0\) on \(\Gamma\) and \(3\) on the depth-\(1\) line. No spread lowers the maximum multiplicity below \(2\). In general (a pigeonhole, checked here): if \(D\) consecutive lines each carry \(m\) layers' boundaries along a common stretch and only \(r\) rows lie before the next layer, each column of the stretch crosses \(mD\) boundaries at at most \(D+r\) depths, so every inward spread (\(A_{\rm next}\subseteq A'_k\subseteq A_k\), the form the spread construction uses) leaves a multiplicity at least \(mD/(D+r)\); spreads moving boundaries outward into free rows before the stack are not counted: spreading, capped or recursed, does not end at bounded multiplicity on stacks with \(r\ll(m-1)D\). Such a stack is a steep ramp of slope \(my\) and width \(D\delta_0\). Next attempt: bound stacks as ramps, \(g=\)ramp\(+\)sawtooth on the stack's region: the linear ramp of amplitude \(mDy\delta_0\) through a band bound localized to a finite monotone path (lem:band-family-discrepancy (b) allows "any ramp width w > 0" but only along full-width graphs), and the sawtooth residue \(h\), \(|h|\le my\delta_0\), by per-cell counts. Smallest case. A stack of \(D\) straight horizontal lines of length \(\ell\), multiplicity \(m\), no room. The residue, by hand, for its cell-function part (the ramp taken as its cell averages, \(h\) constant on cells): with probability tending to one every cell has \(|n_Q-N\delta_0^2|\le C\sqrt{N\delta_0^2\log N}\) (Chernoff, \(N\delta_0^2\ge16\log N\), a union over the at most \(N\) cells), so \(|D(h)|\le\sum_Q|h_Q||n_Q-N\delta_0^2|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\,myA\), \(A=D\ell\delta_0\) the stack's area; the stack's \(D\ell/\delta_0\) edges cost at least \(D\ell\delta_0\frac{my/2}{2\sqrt2}(\log(my/2))^{1/4}\) by the recorded lower bound of \(\psi_4^*\), so \(myA\le4\sqrt2\,\mathrm{cost}\,(\log(my/2))^{-1/4}\) and that part is \(O(\sqrt{N\log N})\) uniformly. The band clauses are stated against Lebesgue measure for a continuous ramp, so the within-cell term, the continuous ramp less its cell averages, is not covered by this count; it is the mechanism of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (e), "Bernstein per cell and the cellwise remainder" (the reviewer's pointer), and goes with the ramp. Left: the ramp along a stretch of length \(\ell\) inside the square, which (b) covers only when the stretch spans the square, and its within-cell term. Nontrivial because: (b)'s band runs across the square, and its proof's column sums are what a finite stretch cuts. Plainest bound. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) charges the ramp's edges \((\log(my))^{1/4}\) times their cost. Own statements. lem:staircase-bundle-chains and lem:separated-bundle-chains need "(B2) the strip ... lies in A_{t_b+m_b} minus A_{t_b+m_b+1}" over its whole depth; in a stack with \(D\ge2\) every line but the deepest has the next line one row inside, so it is no bundle and stays an off-bundle high edge in \(\eta_W\), and the lemmas decide a stack only at \(D=1\) with at least \(m+1\) rows (bands \(0,\dots,m\)) inside the layer. lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) decides a chain consisting of one stack whenever its \(mD\) layers meet "K <= N^(1/7) and log K <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3)", for instance at \(m=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\), \(y=2e^{16}\) and \(D\le N^{1/8}\); in a chain with more layers it says nothing of the stack's share, so the attempt bears on stacks inside chains beyond that count. lem:guided-chain-bound (d) needs guides from "a family F_N of at most N^c unions of cells of side 2^(-l_1) fixed before the points are drawn", and a stack's lines are chosen with the chain, so it does not bear unless such guides are built. Record search. "ramp band stacked lines steep gradient finite path localized band discrepancy sawtooth staircase profile" returned lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and lem:band-family-discrepancy, both for bands along full-width graphs; "monotone lattice path staircase diagonal translate band ribbon edge disjoint nested chain bundle" returned lem:separated-bundle-chains; none localizes a band to a finite path.

Verification gate. Dependencies re-read: the registered statements of lem:separated-bundle-chains (with its full record), lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound, cor:fine-mesh-function-tube, lem:discrete-flow-bound, lem:multilevel-chain-bound, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, lem:guided-chain-bound, lem:tube-localized-discrepancy and lem:band-family-discrepancy. It required: the bands defined at the ends (the drafted "cells between translates" undefined there, a wrongly turned end staircase sharing an edge with \(\Gamma_b+\tau_b\)), now by cell centres, its form; the support's distance argument, false for end cells, replaced by the centre distance \((i+1)\delta_0\); half-open \(W\)-cells; the witness's TV figure, \(0.043\) where the output gives \(0.0410\) at \(\ln N=700\), now \(0.041\); the Bearing's "decided by none of the recorded chain bounds", false for the fixed witness (Chebyshev; lem:guided-chain-bound (d) with the witness's own layers as guides), now a sentence on the class's uniformity (the claim about the witness withdrawn, the class claim kept); and the Smallest case, which called one spread "the only nontrivial" and set it against the lead's words, now with the three spreads. At \((4,4)\), finer dyadic meshes reduce to the Leighton–Shor mesh

17 October 2026 · Working proof, reviewed · Mixed-level counts, the dual residual class. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry continues mixed-level-counts, the dual side of conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy, within the item's spell, by the staircase bundles entry's named next attempt.

Question. The staircase entry's next attempt asked for a band bound for stacks of bundled lines along a finite stretch, a ramp narrower or wider than the Leighton–Shor scale. Before building it: at which mesh does a stack's discrepancy live, and is the class's open part smaller than every grid function? The record's own Not covered lists, in the mixed-level chains entry, "Functions with values closer than \(2e^{16}\delta_0\)".

Shortest route. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) in its discrete dual form. Taken: reduce that form, on every dyadic mesh in range, to the single mesh \(2^{-\ell_1}\), each function presented there as a nested chain at one height. The direct path this shows: the problem on Leighton–Shor cells, which is, through lem:grid-flow-duality, the coarse-cell flow problem thm:cell-scale-reduction already reduces the primal side to; the next attempt takes the steep stacks of that problem on the dual side.

Target form. The goal's dual form through lem:grid-flow-duality: \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\) for every grid function \(g\) on a dyadic grid of side \(\delta_0\in[4\sqrt{\log N/N},2^{-\ell_1}]\) with discrete cost \(\sum_ew_e\le2\), \(w_e=\delta_0^2\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\), \(v_e=|\Delta_eg|/\delta_0\), at \((4,4)\).

Owed attempt. The staircase entry named "bound stacks as ramps", the ramp "through a band bound localized to a finite monotone path": not made here; the reductions below came first because they fix where that object lives (a stack narrower than \(2^{-\ell_1}\) averages into the coarse mesh), and the attempt is carried, at that mesh, as this entry's next attempt.

Architecture test. Not decided. The eleventh review's test concerns the multi-shift restoring flow, left at the pre-step part along runs; this entry, on the dual item, does not touch it.

General statement. thm:one-height-chain-reduction, for every dyadic mesh in \([4\sqrt{\log N/N},2^{-\ell_1}]\) and every grid function of discrete cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\); lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging and lem:one-height-rounding, for every cost bound \(M\).

Setting

\(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\); \(\ell_1\) the largest integer with \(2^{-\ell_1}\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), so \(2^{-\ell_1}<2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\); \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\). For a dyadic mesh \(\delta\), a grid function \(g\) is constant on its cells, \(D(g)=\sum_Q(n_Q-N\delta^2)g_Q=\sum_ig(X_i)-N\int g\), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=\sum_e\delta|\Delta_eg|\) over the inner edges, \(v_e=|\Delta_eg|/\delta\), and the discrete cost at \((4,4)\) is \(\sum_ew_e\), \(w_e=\delta^2\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\). \(E_Wg\) is the average of \(g\) on the cells of side \(W\). The count event \(\mathcal E_0\): for every dyadic mesh \(\delta\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\) every cell has \(|n_Q-N\delta^2|\le C_0\sqrt{N\delta^2\log N}\); it has probability tending to one, by Bernstein's inequality with \(t=3\sqrt{N\delta^2\log N}+3\log N\) and a union over the at most \(N\) cells of each of the at most \(\log_2N\) meshes, and \(\log N\le\frac14\sqrt{N\delta^2\log N}\) as \(N\delta^2\ge16\log N\), so \(C_0=\frac{15}4\) (the count event of lem:band-family-discrepancy's proof, there for meshes of side at least \(3\sqrt{\log N/N}\)). \(\psi_4^*\) is convex, nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\), with \(\psi_4^*(0)=0\), so \(\psi_4^*(t)/t\) is nondecreasing and \(\psi_4^*(t/c)\le\psi_4^*(t)/c\) for \(c\ge1\); \(\psi_4^*(1)=0.461650\) and, at \(Y=e^{22}\), \(\psi_4^*(Y/2)/Y\le1.2775\) by the recorded \(\psi_4^*(t)\le t(2\log t)^{1/4}+1\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_one_height_rounding_20261017/constants.txt). \(T(M)=4+2M/\psi_4^*(1)\).

Lemma (Leighton–Shor mesh averaging)

Statement. (a) Deterministically, for every mesh \(\delta\) with \(1/\delta\) an integer, every \(M>0\) and every grid function \(g\) on it with discrete cost at most \(M\) at \((4,4)\): \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(M)\). (c) Deterministically, for meshes \(\delta_0\le W\) with \(W/\delta_0\) and \(1/W\) integers, and any cost \(\sum_e\delta_0^2\psi^*(v_e/2)\) with \(\psi^*\) convex, nondecreasing on \([0,\infty)\) and zero at zero (one per direction): \(E_Wg\) has, on the mesh \(W\), cost at most that of \(g\). (b) For \(N\) large (so that \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\le W\)), on the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) at \(\kappa=4\), for every dyadic \(\delta_0\in[4\sqrt{\log N/N},W]\) and every \(g\) on it of cost at most \(M\) at \((4,4)\): \(|D(g)-D(E_Wg)|\le c_4T(M)\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(c_4\) the constant of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound.

Proof. (a) Edges with \(v_e<2\) give \(\delta_0|\Delta_eg|=\delta_0^2v_e<2\delta_0^2\), at most \(4\) over the at most \(2/\delta_0^2\) inner edges; an edge with \(v_e\ge2\) has \(\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\ge(v_e/2)\psi_4^*(1)\), \(\psi_4^*(t)/t\) being nondecreasing, so \(\delta_0^2v_e\le2w_e/\psi_4^*(1)\), at most \(2M/\psi_4^*(1)\) in all. (b) lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), whose hypotheses "square grids of sides \(\delta_0\le W\) with \(1/W\) and \(W/\delta_0\) integers, \(\delta_0\ge\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\) and \((W/\delta_0)^2\le\log N\)" hold: both are dyadic, \(\delta_0\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\), and \((W/\delta_0)^2<(2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N)^2/(16\log N/N)=\frac14\sqrt{\log N}\le\log N\); then (a). (c) Let \(r=W/\delta_0\), \(e'\) a horizontal coarse edge between coarse cells \(P\) (left) and \(P'\). For a fine cell \(Q\) of \(P\), \(g(Q+We_1)-g(Q)\) is the sum of the increments across the \(r\) horizontal fine edges \(e(Q,s)\), \(0\le s<r\), between \(Q+s\delta_0e_1\) and \(Q+(s+1)\delta_0e_1\); so \(|E_{P'}g-E_Pg|\le r^{-2}\sum_{Q\subset P}\sum_s\delta_0v_{e(Q,s)}\) and \(v'_{e'}=|\Delta_{e'}E_Wg|/W\le r^{-3}\sum_{Q,s}v_{e(Q,s)}\), an average over \(r^3\) instances. By monotonicity and convexity of \(\psi_4^*\), \(W^2\psi_4^*(v'_{e'}/2)\le W^2r^{-3}\sum_{Q,s}\psi_4^*(v_{e(Q,s)}/2)\). The instances are the horizontal fine edges inside \(P\cup P'\), the shared side included, those of a row at internal position \(c\in\{0,\dots,2r-2\}\) used \(\min(c+1,2r-1-c)\) times; with \(W^2r^{-3}=\delta_0^2r^{-1}\), \(W^2\psi_4^*(v'_{e'}/2)\le\sum_e\frac{\mu_{e'}(e)}r w_e\), \(\mu_{e'}(e)\) that multiplicity. A fine edge at column \(a\in\{0,\dots,r-2\}\) inside a coarse cell \(P\) has position \(a\) in the pair with \(P\) on the left and \(r+a\) in the pair with \(P\) on the right, weights \(\frac{a+1}r\) and \(\frac{r-1-a}r\), summing to \(1\); a fine edge on a coarse side has position \(r-1\) in its one pair, weight \(\frac rr=1\); pairs missing at the square's edge only lower the sum. So the horizontal coarse cost is at most the horizontal fine cost, and likewise vertically (the factor one: the reviewer's count, checked here; a first draft had the bound \(2M\) from counting each fine edge in two pairs at full weight). \(\square\)

Lemma (one-height rounding)

Statement. On \(\mathcal E_0\), for every dyadic \(\delta\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\), every \(M>0\), every \(Y\ge2e^{16}\) and every grid function \(h\) on mesh \(\delta\) with discrete cost at most \(M\) at \((4,4)\), there is \(\theta\in[0,1)\) such that \(r_Q=Y\delta(\lfloor h_Q/(Y\delta)+\theta\rfloor-\theta)\) satisfies (i) \(0\le h-r<Y\delta\); (ii) \(r-\min r=\delta\sum_kY1_{A_k}\), \(A_k=\{Q:\lfloor h_Q/(Y\delta)+\theta\rfloor\ge k+\min_Q\lfloor h_Q/(Y\delta)+\theta\rfloor\}\), \(k\ge1\), nested unions of cells: a nested chain at the one height \(Y\); (iii) the discrete cost of \(r\) is at most \(7M+\frac{\psi_4^*(Y/2)}{Y}T(M)\); (iv) \(|D(h)-D(r)|\le C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\).

Proof. (i), (ii): \(x+\theta-1<\lfloor x+\theta\rfloor\le x+\theta\); the superlevel sets of an integer-valued function are nested, and \(D\) of a constant is \(0\) since \(\sum_Qn_Q=N\). (iv): \(|D(h-r)|\le Y\delta\sum_Q|n_Q-N\delta^2|\le Y\delta\cdot\delta^{-2}\cdot C_0\sqrt{N\delta^2\log N}=C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\) on \(\mathcal E_0\). (iii): with \(a_Q=h_Q/(Y\delta)\), across an edge \(e\) between \(Q,Q'\), \(|a_Q-a_{Q'}|=v_e/Y\) and \(r\)'s increment over \(\delta\) is \(v^r_e=Y|\lfloor a_Q+\theta\rfloor-\lfloor a_{Q'}+\theta\rfloor|\). If \(v_e\ge Y\): the floors differ by at most \(v_e/Y+1\le2v_e/Y\), so \(v^r_e\le2v_e\) and \(\delta^2\psi_4^*(v^r_e/2)\le\delta^2\psi_4^*(v_e)\le7w_e\), by \(\psi_4^*(2t)\le7\psi_4^*(t)\) at \(t=v_e/2\ge e^{16}\) (the separated bundles entry, from the recorded bounds \(\frac t{2\sqrt2}(\log t)^{1/4}\le\psi_4^*(t)\le t(2\log t)^{1/4}+1\)). If \(v_e<Y\): \(v^r_e\in\{0,Y\}\), and \(v^r_e=Y\) exactly when an integer lies in the half-open interval between \(a_Q+\theta\) and \(a_{Q'}+\theta\), of length \(v_e/Y<1\), which for \(\theta\) uniform on \([0,1)\) has probability \(v_e/Y\); these edges' expected cost is \(\delta^2\psi_4^*(Y/2)\sum_{v_e<Y}v_e/Y\le\frac{\psi_4^*(Y/2)}Y\mathrm{TV}(h)\le\frac{\psi_4^*(Y/2)}YT(M)\) by the averaging lemma's (a), whose proof uses only the cost. Some \(\theta\) has total cost at most this mean plus \(7M\). \(\square\)

Theorem (one-height chain reduction)

Statement. Let \(Y=e^{22}\), \(C_1=14+\frac{\psi_4^*(Y/2)}YT(2)\le30.18\), \(c=C_1/2\) and \(y^*=Y/c\ge e^{19.28}\ge2e^{16}\) (constants.txt; any \(Y\) with \(Y/c(Y)\ge2e^{16}\) serves). If for some constant \(C_2\), with probability tending to one, every nested chain \(H=Wy^*\sum_k1_{A_k}\) at the one height \(y^*\) on the mesh \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) with discrete cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\) has \(|D(H)|\le C_2\sqrt{N\log N}\), then with probability tending to one, for every dyadic \(\delta_0\in[4\sqrt{\log N/N},W]\), every grid function \(g\) on mesh \(\delta_0\) with discrete cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\) has \(|D(g)|\le(c_4T(2)+C_0Y+cC_2)\sqrt{N\log N}\). Conversely those chains are such grid functions on the mesh \(W\), so the two statements are equivalent up to constants.

Proof. On the intersection of the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), \(\mathcal E_0\) and the hypothesis's event: the averaging lemma at \(M=2\) gives \(|D(g)-D(E_Wg)|\le c_4T(2)\sqrt{N\log N}\) and \(E_Wg\) of cost at most \(2\) on the mesh \(W\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\); the rounding lemma at \(\delta=W\), \(M=2\), \(Y=e^{22}\) gives \(r\) with \(|D(E_Wg)-D(r)|\le C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), cost at most \(C_1\), and \(r-\min r\) a nested chain at height \(Y\); \(H=(r-\min r)/c\) has cost at most \(C_1/c=2\) (\(c\ge1\)) and is a nested chain at the one height \(y^*\) on the mesh \(W\), so \(|D(r)|=c|D(H)|\le cC_2\sqrt{N\log N}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Averaging lemma, (a): only the cost bound \(M\) and that \(\psi_4^*\) is convex, nondecreasing and zero at zero (no event); (b): the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) at \(\kappa=4\), dyadic \(\delta_0\in[4\sqrt{\log N/N},W]\) for its integrality and ratio conditions, and (a); (c): only convexity and monotonicity of \(\psi_4^*\) and \(W/\delta_0\) an integer (no event). Rounding lemma, (i), (ii): none; (iii): \(Y\ge2e^{16}\) for the doubling, and the averaging lemma's (a) bound on \(\mathrm{TV}\); (iv): \(\mathcal E_0\) at the mesh \(\delta\). Points i.i.d. uniform: the events of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) and \(\mathcal E_0\). Dyadic \(\delta_0\in[4\sqrt{\log N/N},W]\): the integrality and ratio conditions of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), and \(\mathcal E_0\)'s range (also at the mesh \(W\)). The pair \((4,4)\): the doubling \(\psi_4^*(2t)\le7\psi_4^*(t)\) (finite exponent; at \(\alpha=\infty\) the conjugate is infinite beyond \(N\) and doubling fails) and the numerical constants; the averaging lemma's (a) and (c) use only that \(\psi_4^*\) is convex, nondecreasing and zero at zero, and hold for every such conjugate with its own \(\psi^*(1)\). The cost bound \(M\): \(\mathrm{TV}\) and the costs after averaging and rounding. \(Y\ge2e^{16}\): the doubling at \(t\ge e^{16}\); \(Y=e^{22}\) in the theorem, so that \(y^*\ge2e^{16}\), the height every chain lemma of the record asks. Conclusions: the lemmas for every \(M\) and every dyadic mesh in range (the rounding on every dyadic mesh of side at least \(4\sqrt{\log N/N}\)); the theorem for every dyadic \(\delta_0\) in range at cost \(2\).

Degenerate cases. lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging: \(g\) constant, \(\mathrm{TV}=0\) and \(E_Wg\) constant, both sides \(0\); \(\delta_0=W\), \(E_Wg=g\), (b) trivial and (c) an equality. lem:one-height-rounding: \(h\) constant, \(r\) constant; \(h\) with range below \(Y\delta\), \(r\) has at most one level line, possibly none, and the error (iv) carries all of \(D(h)\) up to \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\); \(h\) already a nested chain at the height \(Y\) with values in \(Y\delta\mathbb Z\), rounding with \(\theta=0\) returns it. thm:one-height-chain-reduction: \(g\) constant gives \(H=0\) and every term \(0\); \(g\) itself a one-height chain at height \(y^*\) on the mesh \(W\), values \(y^*Wk\), is averaged to itself and rounded on the lattice \(YW\mathbb Z\), \(k\mapsto\lfloor k/c+\theta\rfloor\): about \(c\) consecutive layers merge into one, a coarsening, not a scaling, and \(H\) is that coarsened chain over \(c\).

Nonvacuity. On the curve parameters at \((4,4)\), \(\delta_0\) the dyadic number in \([4\sqrt{\log N/N},8\sqrt{\log N/N})\), \(A=[\frac14,\frac34]^2\) (a union of cells of the mesh \(W\), \(N\) large), \(y'=e^{22}W/\delta_0\) and \(g_Q=\frac12x_1(Q)+y'\delta_01_A(Q)\), \(x_1(Q)\) the first coordinate of \(Q\)'s centre: horizontal edges have \(v_e=\frac12\) off \(\partial A\), the edges of \(\partial A\) have \(v_e=y'\) or \(y'\pm\frac12\); cost at most \(\psi_4^*(\frac14)+2\delta_0\psi_4^*(y')\), with \(\psi_4^*(\frac14)\le\psi_4^*(1)/4\) and \(\delta_0y'(2\log y')^{1/4}=e^{22}W(2\log y')^{1/4}\to0\), so at most \(2\) for \(N\) large. Averaging gives \(\frac12x_1+y'\delta_01_A\) on the mesh \(W\) with the first term's values moved to coarse centres; on the mesh \(W\) the edges of \(\partial A\) have \(v'=y'\delta_0/W=e^{22}=Y\) on its horizontal sides and \(Y\pm\frac12\) on its vertical ones, \(Y+\frac12\) at \(x_1=\frac14\) (the rounding's doubling branch) and \(Y-\frac12\) at \(x_1=\frac34\) (its crossing branch), and the linear part's edges, \(v'=\frac12<Y\), use the crossing branch, level lines every \(2YW\) in \(x_1\); scaled by \(1/c\), a nested chain at the one height \(y^*\) on the mesh \(W\). One function. This witness is one function fixed before the points, decided by Chebyshev (\(\mathrm{Var}\,D(g)\le N\sup g^2\le N\)); it shows each branch of the reduction in use; what the theorem adds is uniform over the class. Plainest bound. On the witness, lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) decides it uniformly over the class of such functions (its loss \(W\) here is the cost of \(\partial A\) times \((\log y')^{1/4}\), which tends to \(0\)); on the class, the plainest uniform bound, a union over the class's members, is the record's union over curves by length, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\le L\,T(2)\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\) by the averaging lemma's (a), larger than the goal by \((\log N)^{1/4}\).

Baseline. Uniformly over the class: lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), the loss \(W\), the cost-weighted \((\log v_e)^{1/4}\). The theorem bounds nothing by itself: it says where the class's difficulty lies. Composed. lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), applied to each \(g\) alone at \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), is the averaging lemma's (b), with the class's \(\mathrm{TV}\) bound; lem:multilevel-chain-bound (c), applied to each rounded function alone, decides every class function whose rounded chain meets its count, a consequence the rounding adds; lem:separated-bundle-chains and lem:staircase-bundle-chains, applied to each rounded chain alone at \(\delta_0=W\), decide every class function whose rounded coarse chain has its steep edges on separated straight or monotone bundles; lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b), applied to the rounded chain alone, decides it when its edges of multiplicity above a fixed \(M\) carry cost \(\eta\) with \(\eta(\log(m_{\max}y^*))^{1/4}\) bounded; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), applied to each part alone, gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\) on each.

Record comparison. From the record's side: the passage from a fine function to its coarse averages at \(2^{-\ell_1}\) at cost \(c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,\mathrm{TV}\) is lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), used by that lemma's (b) and by lem:guided-chain-bound (a) for sets, and named for a remainder in the cost-weighted slopes entry: the averaging lemma's (b) is that citation. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) bounds \(\mathrm{TV}\) when every increment is \(0\) or at least \(y\ge2e^{16}\); the averaging lemma's (a) bounds it for every class function. The averaging lemma's (c) is the discrete \(\psi^*\)-version of the corollary for cell averages in lem:mesh-function-discrepancy's record (cell pairs, "each point lies in at most two such pairs per direction"; the reviewer's pointer), which bounds their variation; the cost version with its weights summing to one is new here. Close values were never open: lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) bounds every class function uniformly, its loss coming only from edges with \(v_e\ge2e^{16}\); what the rounding lemma adds is the one-height chain form of every function at a given mesh, so that the record's chain lemmas apply to the steep part of any class function (the Composed clauses). On the primal side, thm:cell-scale-reduction ("flows on coarse cells suffice at finite exponents") reduces the goal to flows on cells of side up to \((\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\), \(\beta<1\) at \((4,4)\), the Leighton–Shor side among them; read on the dual side through lem:grid-flow-duality at that grid (the cell-scale entry's reviewer's suggestion, unverified there), it would pass from Lipschitz \(G\) to its coarse averages, whose cost the averaging lemma's (c) controls, with no cut-cell error, and so would reach the goal's own form, not only the dyadic proxy (on functions constant on the coarse cells the smeared measure and the point counts agree); the theorem here is the analogue for the dyadic proxy, passing from fine grid functions to their averages at the random error of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), a statement on a different class, and the rounding has no primal counterpart in the record. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound and lem:discrete-flow-bound are neither more general nor special cases: they bound every grid function with a loss, while the theorem reduces without bounding. lem:multilevel-chain-bound is neither more general nor a special case of the averaging or the rounding lemma: it bounds nested chains whose layers meet its count, on the same meshes, while the averaging lemma bounds \(\mathrm{TV}\) and coarse cost of every class function and the rounding lemma produces a one-height chain to which its (c) then applies (Composed).

Refinement checked. No refines edge: the theorem bounds nothing; it depends on lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), and lem:one-height-rounding uses the doubling recorded with lem:separated-bundle-chains.

Below exponent \(6\) the goal follows from a discrete bound on Leighton–Shor cells

18 October 2026 · Working proof of a conditional statement, reviewed · Mixed-level counts, the dual residual class. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall, a gluing question on the primal side whose last reviewer judged a failure at the goal's box levels likely (a heuristic, unverified); this entry takes mixed-level-counts for its fourth and last entry of the spell, to make the composition the mesh reduction left open; it changes no implication (Goal progress), and it was chosen as the cheapest step that fixes which statement on the coarse mesh is sufficient, by judgement.

Question. The mesh reduction moved the dyadic proxy to the Leighton–Shor mesh \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) and noted that thm:cell-scale-reduction does the same on the primal side; the cell-scale entry's reviewer suggested, unverified, composing that theorem with lem:grid-flow-duality (b) so that its (d) applies on the coarse grid. Does the goal itself, not only the dyadic proxy, follow from the discrete class on the mesh \(W\)?

Shortest route. conj:ultimate-matching at \((4,4)\) and at the pairs with both exponents in \([2,6)\). Taken: compose thm:cell-scale-reduction with lem:grid-flow-duality (b) and (d) at the mesh \(W\), so that the goal follows from one discrete statement on Leighton–Shor cells. Named, not taken in this entry: the converse, whether the goal implies that statement back, which would make it the goal up to constants; it is the item's next attempt.

Target form. The goal's own form at a pair \(\alpha\): with probability tending to one some matching has \(\sum_i\exp[(\frac{\sqrt N}{L\sqrt{\log N}}|X_i^j-Y^j_{\pi(i)}|)^{\alpha_j}]\le2N\) for \(j=1,2\), \(Y\) evenly spread.

The mesh reduction named "a stack on the mesh \(2^{-\ell_1}\) ... as a band clipped to the stretch", its clipped end the step: not made here; this composition came first, by judgement, and the reviewer counts the deferral as orbiting (Process audit); the attempt stays queued with the item, behind the converse.

General statement. cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency, (a) at every pair with both exponents in \([2,6)\), (b) at \((4,4)\), for every constant and every \(N\) large.

Corollary (coarse discrete sufficiency)

Statement. Let \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) be i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\), \(Y\) evenly spread, \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), \(n_Q\) the counts of the cells of side \(W\), \(D(G)=\sum_QG_Q(n_Q-NW^2)\), and, for a pair \(\alpha\), \(c_\alpha(G)=\sum_eW^2\psi^*_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(|\Delta_eG|/W)\) over the inner edges. (a) Let \(\alpha\in[2,6)^2\). If for some \(C\), with probability tending to one, every grid function \(G\) on the mesh \(W\) with \(c_\alpha(G)\le2\) has \(|D(G)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\), then conj:ultimate-matching holds at \(\alpha\) with the constant \(L=\max(260,4C)\). In particular at \((4,4)\) the hypothesis holds when it holds for the larger class \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eG|/(2W))\le2\). (b) At \((4,4)\): if for some \(C_2\), with probability tending to one, every nested chain \(Wy^*\sum_k1_{A_k}\) at the one height \(y^*\) of thm:one-height-chain-reduction on the mesh \(W\) with \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_e\cdot|/(2W))\le2\) has \(|D|\le C_2\sqrt{N\log N}\), the hypothesis of (a) holds with \(C=C_0e^{22}+\frac{C_1}2C_2\), so conj:ultimate-matching holds at \((4,4)\). Conditional: no instance of either hypothesis is known.

Proof. (a) thm:cell-scale-reduction, stated "For exponents alpha_1, alpha_2 in [2, infinity), a fixed beta >= 1/2 (independent of N) with (beta - 1/2)(max_k alpha_k - 2) < 1": for \(\max_k\alpha_k<6\) some fixed \(\beta\in(\frac34,1)\) has \((\beta-\frac12)(\max_k\alpha_k-2)<1\), and \(\ell=W<2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\le(\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\) and \(2^{-J}\le s/32\le W\) for \(N\) large (\(L\) fixed first); so the goal at \(\alpha\) with constant \(L\ge260\) follows when, with probability tending to one, there is a bounded field \(\Phi_c\) with \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi_c=\int g\,d(\nu^W_X-N\,\mathrm{Leb})\) for all Lipschitz \(g\) and \(\sum_k\int\psi_{\alpha_k}(8|\Phi_{c,k}|/(L\sqrt{N\log N}))\le7\). By lem:grid-flow-duality (b) on the \(k\times k\) grid of side \(W=1/k\), an edge flow \(\theta\) on the inner edges defines a bounded field \(\Phi\) with \(\int\nabla g\cdot\Phi=-\sum_Q(\mathrm{outflow}_Q/W^2)\int_Qg\) and \(\int\Psi_1(|\Phi_1|/\lambda)+\Psi_2(|\Phi_2|/\lambda)\le W^2\sum_e\Psi_{d(e)}(|\theta_e|/(W\lambda))\); \(\nu^W_X\) has density \(n_Q/W^2\) on \(Q\), so a flow with \(\operatorname{out}\theta_Q=NW^2-n_Q\) gives the divergence condition, and with \(\Psi_k=\psi_{\alpha_k}\), \(\lambda=L\sqrt{N\log N}/8\), the cost condition holds when \(W^2\sum_e\psi_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(8|\theta_e|/(WL\sqrt{N\log N}))\le7\). lem:grid-flow-duality (d), in its record "For every \(\lambda'>0\), with \(\Psi_j(t)=\psi_{\alpha_j}(t/s)\), \(\min\{\lambda'\delta^2\sum_e\Psi_{d(e)}(|\theta_e|/(\delta\lambda')):\operatorname{out}\theta_Q=N\delta^2-n_Q\}=\max_G[\frac1s\sum_QG_Q(n_Q-N\delta^2)-\lambda'I_\delta(G)]\)", a statement with no condition on the grid's side, at \(\delta=W\), \(s=L\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(\lambda'=N/8\) (so \(\lambda's=L\sqrt{N\log N}/8\)): the least \(\frac N8W^2\sum_e\psi_{\alpha_{d(e)}}(8|\theta_e|/(WL\sqrt{N\log N}))\) over flows with that outflow equals \(\max_G[\frac1sD(G)-\frac N8c_\alpha(G)]\), \(I_W=c_\alpha\); it is at most \(\frac78N\), and such a flow exists, exactly when \(D(G)\le\frac{sN}8(c_\alpha(G)+7)=\frac L8\sqrt{N\log N}(c_\alpha(G)+7)\) for every \(G\). Under (a)'s hypothesis: \(c_\alpha(G)\le2\) gives \(D(G)\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\); for \(c_\alpha(G)>2\), \(G'=2G/c_\alpha(G)\) has \(c_\alpha(G')\le2\) (\(\psi^*(t/u)\le\psi^*(t)/u\) for \(u\ge1\), each \(\psi^*_{\alpha_j}\) convex with \(\psi^*(0)=0\)), so \(D(G)=\frac{c_\alpha(G)}2D(G')\le\frac{c_\alpha(G)}2C\sqrt{N\log N}\). Both are at most \(\frac L8(c_\alpha(G)+7)\sqrt{N\log N}\) when \(C\le\frac78L\) and \(C\le\frac L4\cdot\frac{c+7}c\) for every \(c>2\), whose infimum is \(\frac L4\): \(L=\max(260,4C)\) gives both. The particular case: \(\psi_4^*(t/2)\le\psi_4^*(t)\), so \(\{c_{(4,4)}\le2\}\) lies inside the larger class. The events are those of thm:cell-scale-reduction and of (a)'s hypothesis. (b) By thm:one-height-chain-reduction's proof at \(\delta_0=W\) (the averaging step trivial there): lem:one-height-rounding at \(\delta=W\), \(M=2\), height \(e^{22}\), on its count event \(\mathcal E_0\) (probability tending to one, proved in the mesh reduction entry's Setting; \(W\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\) for \(N\) large), gives for every \(G\) of the larger class an \(r\) with \(|D(G)-D(r)|\le C_0e^{22}\sqrt{N\log N}\) and \((r-\min r)/c\), \(c=C_1/2\), a nested chain at the one height \(y^*\) of cost at most \(2\); \(D(r)=D(r-\min r)\) since \(D\) vanishes on constants, so \(|D(G)|\le(C_0e^{22}+cC_2)\sqrt{N\log N}\), and (a) at \((4,4)\) applies. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(Y\) evenly spread, \(L\ge260\), exponents finite and a fixed \(\beta>\frac34\) with \((\beta-\frac12)(\max_k\alpha_k-2)<1\), which exists exactly when \(\max_k\alpha_k<6\) (\(\beta=\frac34\) itself fails, \(W\) reaching \(2(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\)): thm:cell-scale-reduction. \(1/W\) an integer: lem:grid-flow-duality (b) and (d), and the counts \(n_Q\). \(N\) large: \(W\le(\log N)^\beta/\sqrt N\), \(2^{-J}\le W\), \(W\ge4\sqrt{\log N/N}\). Each \(\psi^*_{\alpha_j}\) convex with \(\psi^*(0)=0\): the scaling. (b): the pair \((4,4)\), for lem:one-height-rounding's doubling; \(\mathcal E_0\). On the curve, \(\max_k\alpha_k<6\) means both exponents in \((3,6)\); conclusions: (a) at every pair in \([2,6)^2\), (b) at \((4,4)\).

Degenerate cases. \(C=0\): \(L=260\), the theorem's least constant. A sample with every \(n_Q=NW^2\): \(D\equiv0\) and the zero flow carries the counts. \(c_\alpha(G)=0\) (\(G\) constant): \(D(G)=0\) since \(\sum_Qn_Q=N=\sum_QNW^2\). \(c_\alpha(G)=2\): \(G'=G\).

Nonvacuity. Conditional: no instance of either hypothesis is known. On the curve parameters at \((4,4)\), the plainest uniform bound on (a)'s class, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) at \(\delta_0=W\) with \(\mathrm{TV}\le T(2)\) (lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a)), gives \(L\,T(2)\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\), larger than the hypothesis by \((\log N)^{1/4}\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) at \(\delta_0=W\) gives \(\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(46+6\mathcal W)\), \(\mathcal W\) the cost-weighted \((\log v_e)^{1/4}\), so the hypothesis holds on the subclass with \(\mathcal W\) bounded, which is not the whole class. Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) on the class, larger than the hypothesis by \((\log N)^{1/4}\), and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), bounded only where \(\mathcal W\) is: neither gives the hypothesis.

Baseline. The bound needing no idea is thm:cell-scale-reduction itself, which asks a field on the coarse cells; the corollary replaces that field by a bound on grid functions on the same cells, through the duality the record proves. Composed. thm:cell-scale-reduction applied alone at \(\ell=W\) gives the goal from a coarse field; lem:grid-flow-duality (b) applied alone turns an edge flow into such a field; its (d) applied alone at \(\delta=W\) turns the flow's existence into the dual affine bound; lem:one-height-rounding applied alone at \(\delta=W\) turns the class into one-height chains; each part alone gives one link, and the corollary is their composition with the scaling of the class bound.

Record comparison. Universal completion at the box levels suffices; in samples it fails at \(L=\frac12\)

18 October 2026 · Working proof of a conditional statement and finite check, reviewed · Local completion. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Question. The item's first entry, local completion, found the universal form, "for every maximum matching, completion with \(C=1\), part (f), which glues at constant \(1\)"; the universal completion criterion entry named the next attempt: "decide the universal form at the goal's box levels through (a): at a level whose deficiency drops, find two co-bases with no edge of the next level between them, inside the deficient regions of the goal's box graphs, whose widths the record does not give, or show that every pair of co-bases is joined". What would the universal form give at the goal's box levels, and do random samples satisfy it there?

Target form. The goal's own form: a perfect matching with \(\sum_i\exp[(|X_i^j-Y^j_{\pi(i)}|/(Ls_1))^{\alpha_j}]\le2N\) for \(j=1,2\), \(s_1=\sqrt{\log N/N}\), obtained by gluing per-level maximum matchings of the box graphs.

Shortest route. conj:ultimate-matching at every pair of the curve. Taken: thm:local-completion-dichotomy (f) glues wherever universal completion holds, and the deficiency sum it then pays is at most \(N\) with probability tending to one by the per-level counts at a raised level, so the conjecture follows from universal completion at box levels of bounded ratio; this entry proves that, and tests the hypothesis on samples by a certificate of failure. The eleventh review's steps, "the multi-shift restoring flow lemma-first, then the dual residual class": Not taken here, because both were taken already in the entries after that review, the restoring flow's step lemma-first in the local event push entry (lem:local-event-push-obstruction, lem:restoring-step-part-tail), and the dual residual class developed through mixed-level-counts' spell, which reached its boundary with the coarse sufficiency entry; the queue drains, so this entry develops a queued item, its head.

Owed attempt. The last entry on the item named the attempt above. Made: the lemma below finds such a pair whenever a polynomial test passes (a maximum matching whose leftover spans no next-level edge), and at \((4,4)\) with \(Y\) evenly spread the test passes at the first level that drops in every computed sample at \(L=\frac12\); at \(L=1\) no level drops at the sizes computed. That every pair is joined, the other branch, is not shown anywhere.

Architecture test. Not decided. The eleventh review's test concerns the multi-shift restoring flow; this entry develops the queue's head, a primal gluing question, and does not touch it.

General statement. prop:universal-completion-sufficiency, for every pair with exponents in \([1,\infty]\) on or above the curve and every level sequence of bounded ratio; lem:completion-failure-certificate, for every pair of nested bipartite graphs.

Proposition (universal completion sufficiency)

Statement. Let \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in[1,\infty]\) with \(\frac1{\alpha_1}+\frac1{\alpha_2}\ge\frac12\), \(\beta_j=1/\alpha_j\), \(X\) and \(Y\) independent samples of \(N\) uniform points of \([0,1]^2\) (the setting of thm:per-level-count-matchings), \(s_1=\sqrt{\log N/N}\), \(L_1\) the constant of thm:per-level-count-matchings and \(K_0\) that of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold. Fix \(c\ge2\), integers \(1=k_1<k_2<\dots<k_I\) with \(k_{i+1}\le(c-1)k_i+1\) and \(k_I\ge\log N/(4c)\), a constant \(L''\ge\max(c^{\max_j\beta_j}L_1,(4c)^{\max_j\beta_j}K_0)\), and let \(G_i\) be the pairs with \(|X^j-Y^j|\le L''k_i^{\beta_j}s_1\) for \(j=1,2\) (side \(L''s_1\) in a coordinate with \(\alpha_j=\infty\)), \(G_{I+1}\) complete. If, with probability tending to one, universal completion with \(C=1\) holds at every level \(1\le i\le I\) (every maximum matching of \(G_i\) has a matching of \(G_{i+1}\) inside its leftover with \(m_i-m_{i+1}\) edges), then with probability tending to one some matching satisfies the conjecture's condition at \(\alpha\) with the constant \(2L''\) (for \(\alpha_j=\infty\), the maximum bound \(|\Delta^j|\le2L''s_1\)); on the curve this is conj:ultimate-matching at \(\alpha\). The integer levels \(k_i=i\) are the case \(c=2\).

Proof. Weights \(w_i=e^{k_{i+1}}-e^{k_i}\) (\(i<I\)) and \(w_I=1\), \(S=\sum_{i\le I}w_im_i\). (i) Top levels. On the event of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold (probability tending to one; it covers \(\alpha\in(0,\infty]^2\) with \(\frac1{\alpha_1}+\frac1{\alpha_2}\ge\frac12\)) some matching has \(|\Delta_i^j|\le K_0(\log N)^{\beta_j}s_1\) for all pairs; for \(k\ge\log N/(4c)\), \(L''k^{\beta_j}s_1\ge(4c)^{\beta_j}K_0(\log N/(4c))^{\beta_j}s_1=K_0(\log N)^{\beta_j}s_1\), so that matching lies in \(G_i\) and \(m_i=0\) at every level with \(k_i\ge\log N/(4c)\), in particular \(m_I=0\). (ii) Lower levels. For \(k_i<\log N/(4c)\), \(t=ck_i<\frac14\log N\), and \(L''k_i^{\beta_j}\ge L_1(ck_i)^{\beta_j}\), so \(G_i\) contains the box of level \(t\) of thm:per-level-count-matchings and \(m_i\le V_t\), the number of pairs outside that box in the matching its proof builds at \(t\) (each level may have its own matching; \(m_i\) does not depend on it). That proof gives, in the range \(t<\frac14\log N\) where it uses cells, "\(\mathbb EV/(2Ne^{-t})\le2\sqrt2/\log N+6e^t\Pr(\text{bad})^{1/2}\)", whose right side it shows tends to \(0\) uniformly in \(t\): \(\mathbb EV_t\le\delta_N2Ne^{-t}\), \(\delta_N\to0\). Then \(w_i\,\mathbb Em_i\le e^{k_{i+1}}\delta_N2Ne^{-ck_i}\le2e\delta_NNe^{-k_i}\), since \(k_{i+1}-ck_i\le1-k_i\), and summing over distinct integers \(k_i\ge1\), \(\mathbb E\sum_{k_i<\log N/(4c)}w_im_i\le2e\delta_NN/(e-1)\); by Markov this sum exceeds \(N\) with probability at most \(2e\delta_N/(e-1)\to0\). With (i), \(S\le N\) with probability tending to one. (iii) Gluing. On the intersection with the hypothesis' event, thm:local-completion-dichotomy (f), applied to \(G_1\subseteq\dots\subseteq G_{I+1}\), whose proof gives a perfect matching \(P\) with \(|P\setminus G_i|\le m_i\) at every level: \(|P\setminus G_I|\le m_I=0\), so every pair of \(P\) lies in \(G_I\). For a pair let \(i^*\) be the least index with the pair in \(G_{i^*}\); it is outside \(G_i\) for \(i<i^*\), so \(\sum_{i<i^*}w_i=e^{k_{i^*}}-e\), and summing over the pairs, \(\sum_{\text{pairs}}(e^{k_{i^*}}-e)\le\sum_iw_i|P\setminus G_i|\le S\le N\): \(\sum e^{k_{i^*}}\le(1+e)N\). In a coordinate with \(\alpha_j<\infty\), \(u^j=(|\Delta^j|/(L''s_1))^{\alpha_j}\le k_{i^*}\); with \(\alpha_j=\infty\), \(|\Delta^j|\le L''s_1\). (iv) Constant. With \(L=2L''\) and \(\alpha_j\ge1\), \(\exp[(|\Delta^j|/(Ls_1))^{\alpha_j}]=e^{u^j/2^{\alpha_j}}\le(e^{k_{i^*}})^{1/2}\), and by Jensen (concavity of \(x\mapsto x^{1/2}\)) the mean over the pairs is at most \((1+e)^{1/2}<1.93<2\), for each finite \(j\); an infinite coordinate has \(|\Delta^j|\le L''s_1\le Ls_1\). \(\square\)

Lemma (completion failure certificate)

Statement. For nested bipartite graphs \(G\subseteq G'\) on \(X\), \(Y\) with \(\nu(G')>\nu(G)\), let \(D_Y\) (\(D_X\)) be the \(Y\)- (\(X\)-)vertices missed by some maximum matching of \(G\), \(B_X\) the \(X\)-vertices with a \(G'\)-neighbour in \(D_Y\) and \(B_Y\) the \(Y\)-vertices with a \(G'\)-neighbour in \(D_X\). If \(B_X\) is matchable in \(G\), or \(B_Y\) is, then universal completion with \(C=1\) fails at \(G\): some maximum matching of \(G\) has a leftover spanning no edge of \(G'\). If \(\nu(G'[D_X\cup D_Y])<\nu(G')-\nu(G)\), completion with \(C=1\) fails for every maximum matching of \(G\), so its existential reading fails too.

Proof. The sets of \(X\)-vertices matchable in \(G\) are the independent sets of the transversal matroid of \(G\), whose bases are the \(X\)-covers of the maximum matchings. If \(B_X\) is matchable it extends to a basis: some maximum matching \(M\) covers \(B_X\). Its \(X\)-leftover avoids \(B_X\), and its \(Y\)-leftover lies in \(D_Y\) by definition, so no \(X\)-leftover vertex has a \(G'\)-neighbour in the \(Y\)-leftover: the largest matching of \(G'\) inside the leftover is empty, while completion asks \(\nu(G')-\nu(G)\ge1\) edges. Symmetrically for \(B_Y\). For the second test, every maximum matching's leftover lies in \(D_X\cup D_Y\), so the matching completion asks of it is at most \(\nu(G'[D_X\cup D_Y])\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Proposition: \(\frac1{\alpha_1}+\frac1{\alpha_2}\ge\frac12\), in (i) and (ii), the ranges of thm:maximum-displacement-curve-threshold and thm:per-level-count-matchings; two independent uniform samples, in (ii), the setting of the per-level counts; \(L''\ge c^{\beta}L_1\) in (ii) (the level-\(ck_i\) box inside \(G_i\)) and \(L''\ge(4c)^{\beta}K_0\) in (i); \(k_{i+1}\le(c-1)k_i+1\) in (ii), for the summable \(e^{-k_i}\); the hypothesis at every level \(1\le i\le I\), in (iii) through (f); \(\alpha_j\ge1\) in (iv), for \(2^{\alpha_j}\ge2\) (the exact need is \((1+e)^{2^{-\alpha_j}}\le2\), \(\alpha_j\ge0.93\)). The first draft stated the proposition at finite pairs on the curve with \(\alpha_j\ge2\) and integer levels; the review found that no step uses those restrictions, and the statement now covers pairs with exponents in \([1,\infty]\) on or above the curve, endpoints included, and level sequences of bounded ratio: more general. Lemma: \(G\subseteq G'\) and \(\nu(G')>\nu(G)\), so that completion asks at least one edge; finiteness, for the matroid. Conclusions: the proposition for two uniform samples; the lemma for every finite bipartite pair.

Degenerate cases. prop:universal-completion-sufficiency on a sample where \(G_1\) has a perfect matching: every \(m_i=0\), universal completion holds vacuously and \(S=0\) (the case of every computed sample at \(L=1\)). At an endpoint pair, say \((2,\infty)\): the second coordinate's box keeps side \(L''s_1\), the graphs stay nested, and (iii) puts every pair in \(G_I\). The lemma at \(\nu(G')=\nu(G)\): excluded, completion asking nothing; with \(B_X=\emptyset\): every vertex of \(D_Y\) is isolated in \(G'\), so \(\nu(G')\le n-|D_Y|\le n-m=\nu(G)\) and no drop is possible, so the case does not occur under the lemma's hypothesis.

Nonvacuity. On the curve parameters at \((4,4)\): the proposition is a conditional reduction whose hypothesis is not known to hold for any \(L''\), and the finite check points against it at small constants. Its hypothesis is not trivially true: by Leighton–Shor's lower bound every perfect matching has a pair at distance at least \(c'(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\), beyond \(\sqrt2L''\sqrt{\log N/N}\) once \((\log N)^{1/4}>\sqrt2L''/c'\), so \(m_1\ge1\) and a level drops. The lemma's hypothesis holds on the line gadget (box_controls.json: \(B_X\) of one vertex, matchable) and at the first drop level of all nine samples at \(L=\frac12\). Plainest bound. For \(S\) at the integer levels without raising them: the per-level proof's mean bound, with \(\delta_N=(2\sqrt2+o(1))/\log N\) (its \(\Pr(\text{bad})\) terms are \(o(1/\log N)\)), gives \(\mathbb ES\le2(e-1)\delta_NNK\), about \(1.2N\) at \(K=\log N/8\), bounded in mean but with no probability tending to one at a fixed margin; raising each level to \(ck_i\) makes the mean \(o(N)\) and Markov then gives \(S\le N\) with probability tending to one. For the samples: the deficiencies alone decide nothing on the quantifier, and thm:universal-completion-criterion (c) excludes only components of at most four vertices.

Finite check (box completion failures)

At \((4,4)\), \(X\) uniform and \(Y\) evenly spread (one uniform point per cell of the \(\sqrt N\times\sqrt N\) grid; the proposition takes two samples, so the check is of the evenly spread setting), box graphs \(G_k\) at \(Lk^{1/4}s_1\), levels \(k=1,\dots,60\), each sample stopped at its first level where the lemma's certificate or its second test fires, or at \(m=0\); three seeds at each of \(N=4096,16384,65536\) and \(L=\frac12,1\) (research/results/ultimate_matching_box_completion_20261018/: box_completion.py with its compiled Hopcroft–Karp kernel hk.cpp, outputs box_completion_4096.json and box_completion.json; controls box_controls.py and box_controls.json). The script and its expectations were committed before the runs ("Ultimate matching: box-level completion test script, expectations before its run"). Controls: on 1800 tiny line instances with every maximum matching enumerated, 1336 with a drop and 697 failing universal completion, the certificate fired 424 times and the second test 154 times, never where completion holds; the gadget certified; the kernel's matching size agreed with networkx on 200 of 200 random graphs. Twelfth review: piled one-height chains on Leighton–Shor cells

18 October 2026 · Route review, goal-level · The dual chain class and the gluing route. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: a route review proves no statement and changes no result that Where we stand summarizes

Where we stand. The goal is open. Three sufficient statements are on record: conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at every pair of the curve (cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction); the discrete class on Leighton–Shor cells at pairs with exponents in \([2,6)\), and at \((4,4)\) one-height chains there (cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency); and universal completion at box levels (prop:universal-completion-sufficiency). None has a known instance of its hypothesis.

Open statements. Four, unchanged: conj:ultimate-matching, conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy, Conjecture 5.5 and the grid discrepancy of Research Problem 17.2.2; this period advanced none of their implications.

The line's general claim. conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy holds at \((4,4)\), and the way to prove it is on the dual side: the class reduces to one-height nested chains on Leighton–Shor cells (thm:one-height-chain-reduction, cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)), whose discrepancy the chain lemmas bound piece by piece.

What the goal needs. At \((4,4)\): with probability tending to one, every nested chain \(Wy^*\sum_k1_{A_k}\) on the mesh \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) at the one height \(y^*\ge e^{19.28}\) with cost at most \(2\) has \(|D|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\); at the other pairs, the Lipschitz class bound or its discrete form with \(C\) uniform in the pair (the blind stage's remark: cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency gives \(L=\max(260,4C)\) per pair, one \(L\) only if \(C\) is uniform).

The six entries

Local event push: lem:local-event-push-obstruction and lem:restoring-step-part-tail, the eleventh review's lemma-first step, an obstruction on events and a tail bound; the restoring flow's pre-step part along runs, which decides it, stays open. Box-level completion: prop:universal-completion-sufficiency, the goal from universal completion at box levels, conditional, with lem:completion-failure-certificate and ex:box-completion-failures, which finds that completion failing at \(L=\frac12\) with \(Y\) evenly spread. One entry on the primal flows (an exclusion and a tail bound), three dual-side reductions or bounds, one gluing reduction with a finite check.

Falsification attempt. The line's claim is false if some one-height chain of cost at most \(2\) on the mesh \(W\) has discrepancy of larger order than \(\sqrt{N\log N}\). The plainest bound first: a chain whose layers' boundaries are distinct has every \(m_e\le1\), and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) with \(M=1\), \(\eta=0\) bounds it by \(\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(46+12(\log\max(y^*,2e^{16}))^{1/4})\), whatever the layers' shapes; so a stack of separate Leighton–Shor-extremal layers, the first draft's attempt here, is decided, and a violation must use piled edges, \(m_e>M\). Tried on piles, in the regime \(Wy^*\le1\) (\(N\) beyond \(10^{19.3}\) at the mesh of one_cell_threshold.txt), where layers of perimeter of order one fit (a layer of perimeter \(P\) costs about \(0.97PWy^*\)): the reviewer's curve-balanced pile (second stage, unverified), \(\Gamma\) a Leighton–Shor-extremal curve of length about \(c(\log N)^{-1/4}\), \(K\approx2/(Wy^*)\) vertical walls \(x_1>\dots>x_K\) and \(A_k\) the part below \(\Gamma\) left of \(x_k\), so \(g=Wy^*m(x)1_{\text{below }\Gamma}\) with \(m\) up to \(K\): walls cost about \(2\), \(\Gamma\)'s piled edges \(O(1)\), and if \(\Gamma\)'s gains are local along it, \(D(g)\) is of the order \(\sqrt{N\log N}\), the curve-balanced extremal of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound in chain form: of the target's order, not above it. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) gives \(\sqrt{N\log N}(\log N)^{1/4}\) on it, losing \((\log v_e)^{1/4}\) with \(v_e\) about \(\sqrt N\), and \(K\), of order \(\sqrt N\), is beyond lem:multilevel-chain-bound's layer counts: the instance is open for the record. No falsification.

Assessment of this line. Stronger than at the last review on reduction, unchanged on bounds. The period reduced the dual problem to one object, one-height chains on Leighton–Shor cells, and showed that object sufficient for the goal itself at \((4,4)\); it bounded two shapes of steep bundle, which (second stage, unverified) cannot cover the class's extremal in chain form; it proved no bound on the whole object. On the primal side, the gluing route reduced the goal to universal completion, and the computed samples at \(L=\frac12\) fail it at every level ratio tried, a finite check outside the reduction's constants; the flow side added an obstruction. Two entries, coarse sufficiency and box-level completion, were reductions whose reviewers called them orbiting or found the direct step unnamed.

Obstacle

The line is stuck on piled edges at middle multiplicities: lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) leaves a loss on edges of multiplicity above \(M\) carrying cost, and lem:separated-bundle-chains and lem:staircase-bundle-chains remove it only for separated straight bundles and monotone staircases meeting (B1) to (B4), whose (B4) asks a bundle length \(4mW(\log(my^*))^{1/4}\), about \((4/y^*)(\log N/2)^{1/4}\) on the curve-balanced pile, a length that does not shrink with \(N\), while almost all of a Leighton–Shor curve's length lies in wiggles below any fixed scale (the second stage's reading, unverified). Bundle geometry therefore cannot cover the class's own extremals; the clipped end of a stack (the mesh reduction's attempt) is one instance.
