Decisive test. Test disposition. New operation. Operation. For a one-height chain \(g=Wy^*\sum_k1_{A_k}\) on the mesh \(W\) with cost at most \(2\), group its edges by dyadic multiplicity, \(I_i=\{e:2^i\le m_e<2^{i+1}\}\), with \(c_i\) the cost on \(I_i\) and \(\ell_i\) the piled length of \(I_i\) (its number of edges times \(W\)). The test is one inequality on the whole chain, no share of the discrepancy being defined (multiplicity belongs to edges, and a chain does not split along its edge classes): is there \(C\) such that, with probability tending to one, every one-height chain \(g\) of cost at most \(2\) has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\,(1+\sum_{2^i>M}c_i)\)? Since \(\sum_ic_i\le2\), this is the one-height bound itself, cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)'s hypothesis, up to the factor \(3\), so (A) and (B) below are that hypothesis and its failure; what is new is only the operation, the class-by-class mesh charging. The operation tried for it: cor:fine-mesh-function-tube ("\(|D(H)|\le c_\kappa\sqrt{N\log N}\,\mathrm{TV}(H)+L\sqrt N\Phi_k(\mathrm{TV}(H)+12W\sum_Q(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-))\)", any dyadic \(W\in[2^{-\ell_1},1]\)) applied with the mesh chosen class by class, \(W_i'\) the dyadic nearest \(\min(1,1/\ell_i)\) (admissible: by the cost bound \(\ell_i\le2c_i/(W\psi_4^*(y^*/2))\), far below \(1/W\), and classes with \(\ell_i<1\) take \(W_i'=1\)), its covering term charged at each class's own height \(2^{i+1}Wy^*\), a variant of the corollary whose decomposition of \(g\) is the step. Prediction. Outcome (A): such a \(C\) exists; then the one-height bound holds and, through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b), the goal at \((4,4)\). Outcome (B), the exact negation: for every \(C\), along a subsequence of \(N\) depending on \(C\), with probability at least some \(p_C>0\), some chain of cost at most \(2\) has \(|D(g)|>C\sqrt{N\log N}\,(1+\sum_{2^i>M}c_i)\); then cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency's hypothesis fails and the route through it fails, and since no recorded statement transfers a large discrepancy of the class back to matchings, (B) bears on the route, not on the conjecture. A failure of the per-class charging alone decides neither outcome. Neither outcome is decided by a computation (Power). Extremal instance. The class cap: chains with only high piles are recorded, mixed chains are not

18 October 2026 · Attempt, no new statement, reviewed in four passes · Pile class cap. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Where we stand. Unchanged: an attempt with no new statement changes no result Where we stand summarizes

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry takes pile-class-cap, by the twelfth review's Decision, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b), the route's core statement, and is the review's Decisive test.

Question. The twelfth review's Decisive test: is there \(C\) such that, with probability tending to one, every one-height chain \(g\) of cost at most \(2\) on the mesh \(W\) has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+\sum_{2^i>M}c_i)\), through charging each dyadic multiplicity class at its own mesh?

Target form. The one-height bound of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) at \((4,4)\), equivalent to the review's inequality up to a factor \(3\).

Shortest route. conj:ultimate-matching at \((4,4)\) through the one-height bound. Taken: the review's test, from the record's plainest bounds first; the direct path the attempt arrives at, a uniform bound for one set cut by vertical half-planes (the reviewer's lead, unverified), is named as the next attempt.

Architecture test. Not decided. Of the twelfth review's outcomes, neither (A) nor (B) occurred: the review's operation, the class-by-class mesh charging, was not made (Owed attempt), and the recorded bounds decide only chains of one kind of edge.

Owed attempt. The class-by-class mesh charging through cor:fine-mesh-function-tube, from the twelfth review's operation, is not made because its step needs a split: cor:fine-mesh-function-tube bounds one cell function at one mesh \(W'\) by its total variation and its covering term at that mesh, so charging each class at its own mesh \(W_i'\) needs \(g\) written as a sum of functions each carrying one class, and \(g\) does not split along edge classes (a function with \(g\)'s increments on one class and none elsewhere need not exist, the review's fourth check); the inequality posed on the whole chain does not presuppose the split, but this route to it does; this entry instead reads what the recorded bounds give, and the reviewer's layer-cake reduction (below) replaces the decomposition for the curve-balanced pile's form.

General statement. None applies: the entry registers no claim; the statements it works with are lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound and lem:local-factor-discrepancy, recorded.

What the record already gives

lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c): "at (4,4), if every increment |jump|/delta_0 is 0 or at least y >= 2e^16 and sum_e delta_0^2 psi*_4(|jump|/(2 delta_0)) <= 2, then TV(g) <= 8 (log(y/2))^(-1/4), so for y >= N^c the discrepancy is at most 8 3^(1/4) c^(-1/4) L sqrt(N log N)". At \(\delta_0=W=2^{-\ell_1}\), the top of its range, it decides one-height chains whose every nonzero increment \(v_e=m_ey^*\) is at least \(N^c\), \(0<c\le1\): chains with only high piles, not the high classes inside a mixed chain, which do not split off. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) decides chains whose piled edges carry cost \(O((\log N)^{-1/4})\).

Two charges per edge

The total variation is a sum over edges, \(\mathrm{TV}(g)=\sum_eW|\Delta_eg|=\sum_eW^2v_e\), and every nonzero edge of a one-height chain has \(v_e\ge y^*\ge e^{19.28}\ge2e^{16}\) (thm:one-height-chain-reduction), so the lower bound \(\psi_4^*(u)\ge\frac12u(\log u)^{1/4}\), the one lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c)'s proof uses, gives \(W^2v_e\le4c_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\), \(c_e=W^2\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\), and with (b), \(|D(g)|\le4L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\sum_ec_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\): a per-edge sum at the rate \(r_1(v)=(\log N)^{3/4}(\log v)^{-1/4}\), in units of \(\sqrt N\) and up to constants. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) is a per-edge sum at the rate \(r_2(v)=(\log N)^{1/2}(\log v)^{1/4}\), with the constant term \(46\). The rates cross at \(\log v=(\log N)^{1/2}\), both \((\log N)^{5/8}\) there; up to constant factors, \(\min(r_1,r_2)\le(\log N)^{1/2}\) only where \(v\ge N^c\) (for \(r_1\)) or \(v\) is bounded (for \(r_2\)). Each bound is applied to the whole \(g\), so the per-edge minimum is not available; and that minimum would itself exceed the target by up to \((\log N)^{1/8}\), an excess of the two bounds, not shown to be one of the object. A chain with cost of order one on edges of both kinds escapes both.

Local charges. lem:local-factor-discrepancy (a), "for every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides 2^(-i), 1 <= i <= l_1 ..., and every H constant on its cells, |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N sum over inner edges e of length(e) |jump_e H| F(i(e))", \(F(i)=i^{3/4}+(2+\log_2i)\sqrt{\log\log N}\), applied to the coarsest such partition of \(g\) (the maximal dyadic squares of side at least \(W\) on which \(g\) is constant, disjoint by maximality, of levels \(1\) to \(\ell_1\) unless \(g\) is constant; a jump edge lies between two of them, its jump constant along their shared side), charges each mesh edge \(W|\Delta_eg|F(i(e))\), \(i(e)\) the level of the smaller maximal square beside \(e\): with the cost's lower bound, at the rate \(i(e)^{3/4}(\log v_e)^{-1/4}\) up to the \(\log\log N\) term, within the target where \(i(e)\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log v_e)^{1/3}\). A straight wall on the line \(x=kW\) has beside it dyadic squares of side at most \(2^{-\ell_1+v_2(k)}\), \(v_2(k)\) the power of \(2\) dividing \(k\) (the reviewer's correction): only walls at dyadically coarse positions are charged of order one, and a wall at an odd \(k\) is charged \(F(\ell_1)\), of order \((\log N)^{3/4}\).

The extremal, conditional. The curve-balanced pile of the twelfth review is its second stage's construction, unverified, whose cost this entry has not computed; the reviewer of this entry estimates (unverified) that it may break the cost bound, its walls lying under a curve of length about \((\log N)^{-1/4}\) or its curve's piled edges costing too much. So the statements here on it are conditional on the construction: if it is admissible, its walls, \(v=y^*\), are charged by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) at \((\log N)^{3/4}\), its curve by lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound at \((\log N)^{1/4}\) above the target, and its walls, \(y^*/2\) cells apart with \(y^*\) a constant (\(\log_2y^*\approx27.8\)), at level \(\ell_1-O(1)\) by the local charge.

Plainest bound. For the column function \(h\) alone (constant on columns, nonincreasing, total jump \(a=\max h\)): the one-dimensional Kolmogorov–Smirnov bound, \(|D(h)|\le a\sup_x|F_N(x)-Nx|\le a\,\omega_N\sqrt N\) with probability tending to one, for any \(\omega_N\to\infty\) (the reviewer's), below lem:guided-chain-bound (b)'s \(\sqrt{N\log N}\) on the half-planes; neither decides \(h\cdot1_B\).

New mathematics. No statement proved. The entry finds that lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) decides one-height chains whose every nonzero increment is at least \(N^c\); that the two recorded bounds are per-edge sums at the rates \((\log N)^{3/4}(\log v)^{-1/4}\) and \((\log N)^{1/2}(\log v)^{1/4}\), each applied to the whole chain, so mixed chains escape both; and that lem:local-factor-discrepancy (a) on the coarsest constant dyadic partition charges each edge at its local level, of order one only for walls at dyadically coarse positions.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: the layer-cake reduction (the reviewer's suggestion, unverified): for \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and nonincreasing in \(x\), \(\{h1_B>t\}=B\cap H_t\), \(H_t\) a vertical half-plane, so \(D(h1_B)=\int_0^aD(1_{B\cap H_t})\,dt\), the walls' number and spacing dropping out; the step is a uniform bound for one set cut by a vertical half-plane, \(|D(1_{B\cap H})|\le C\sqrt N((\log N)^{3/4}P(B)+(\log N)^{1/2}\ell(B\cap\partial H))\), the straight cut charged \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit length, over the at most \(1/W\) half-planes. Smallest case. One layer, \(g=Wy^*1_{B\cap H}\), the cut a single wall of jump \(Wy^*\): every increment is \(y^*\), multiplicity one, and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) with \(M=1\), \(\eta=0\) decides it at the target; the case the attempt adds is many layers with distinct cuts at one curve, the layer cake's integral. Nontrivial because: the mechanism acts on the cut's straightness, which a union bound over polynomially many positions covers, while lem:mesh-function-discrepancy's coarse averages charge the cut's jump at \((\log N)^{3/4}\) (the reviewer's reading, unverified). Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) on each \(B\cap H_t\): \((\log N)^{3/4}\) per unit perimeter, the cut included. Own statements. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) needs "every increment |jump|/delta_0 is 0 or at least y", which a product chain's walls (\(v=y^*\)) meet only at the fixed height \(y^*\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) needs the piled edges' cost small; lem:guided-chain-bound (b) needs "a family F_N of at most N^c unions of cells ... fixed before the points are drawn", which the half-planes meet and \(B\cap H_t\) does not; lem:local-factor-discrepancy (a) charges a cut at an odd position \(F(\ell_1)\); lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy bounds functions constant on "every partition of [0,1]^2 into dyadic squares of sides between 2^(-j_2) and 2^(-j_1)", so a cut at an odd position forces \(j_2=\ell_1\) and the charge of the finest level, as for the local charge; lem:separated-bundle-chains needs its piled edges on straight bundles, its (B2) "the strip \(S_b\) of the cells on the inner side of \(\Gamma_b\) at depth \(0,\dots,m_b\) ... lies in \(A_{t_b+m_b}\setminus A_{t_b+m_b+1}\)" and its (B4) \(\ell_b\ge2m_b\delta_0(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\); for \(h1_B\), whose layers are \(B\cap\{x<x_k\}\), the bundles are the straight runs of \(\partial B\) between consecutive walls, (B2) can fail only where a strip runs sideways into the next wall (vertical runs), and (B4) fails on every run whose multiplicity exceeds a constant of order \(y^*/(\log Y_b)^{1/4}\), since a run is no longer than one wall spacing, about \(y^*W/2\), while the pile's multiplicities reach about \(2/(Wy^*)\); the runs must also be straight while \(\Gamma\) wiggles (the reviewer's reading), so it does not apply to the pile's: none decides the cut set. Record search. "high multiplicity steep increments total variation Leighton Shor tube cell function" returned lem:multilevel-chain-bound, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging and lem:guided-chain-bound; "product chain column function times set half plane walls" returned lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, whose newer versions lem:loglog-mesh-deviation and lem:local-factor-discrepancy were read; "half plane intersection cut set Leighton Shor straight line union bound" returned lem:guided-chain-bound, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor, lem:mesh-function-discrepancy and lem:multilevel-chain-bound; none charges a straight cut at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit length for a set not fixed in advance.

Suggestion checked. The layer-cake identity was checked by hand: \(D(f)=\sum_if(X_i)-N\int f\) is linear and \(f=\int_0^\infty1_{\{f>t\}}dt\) for \(f\ge0\), and for \(h\) constant on columns and nonincreasing in \(x\), \(\{h1_B>t\}=B\cap\{x<x_t\}\), so \(D(h1_B)=\int_0^aD(1_{B\cap H_t})\,dt\) holds. What it gives was checked too: integrating the candidate bound, the term \((\log N)^{3/4}P(B\cap H_t)\) restricted to \(B\)'s own boundary integrates to \((\log N)^{3/4}\) times the total variation of \(h1_B\) across \(\partial B\), exactly lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b)'s charge there, so the reduction lowers the walls' charge (to \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit of their total variation, if the candidate bound holds) and leaves \(\partial B\)'s edges at the rate \(r_1\): if the candidate bound holds, it decides the product chains whose \(\partial B\) edges have \(\log v\) of order \(\log N\), and in any case not those at middle multiplicities. The candidate bound itself is unproved.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • The layer-cake reduction of product chains \(h1_B\) to sets \(B\cap H_t\) cut by vertical half-planes, with the candidate bound charging the straight cut \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per unit length; the identity and its integration are checked above (Suggestion checked), the candidate bound is not. Record. "half plane intersection cut set Leighton Shor straight line union bound": lem:guided-chain-bound (b) charges fixed half-planes at \(\sqrt{\log N}\), lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) cut sets at \((\log N)^{3/4}\); none charges a cut set's straight part at \(\sqrt{\log N}\).
  • Rectangles alone may not help: in a column of width \(W\) no horizontal wiggle above scale \(W\) fits, so an anisotropic local factor set by the shorter side charges the walls \(F(\ell_1)\) again, the gain coming from the cut's straightness, which a union over polynomially many positions covers. Record. "product chain column function times set half plane walls": lem:local-factor-discrepancy, whose squares are the only cells it allows; no anisotropic version is recorded.

Product chains: the walls reduce to runs anchored at the high side

18 October 2026 · Working proofs, reviewed in three passes · Anchored runs. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry continues pile-class-cap, the twelfth review's out-of-turn item, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) and its previous entry named the next attempt.

Question. The pile class charges entry asked for a bound for one set cut by a vertical half-plane, so that a product chain \(h1_B\) (\(h\ge0\) constant on columns and nonincreasing in \(x\), \(B\) a union of cells) is charged at the target through the layer cake. Which part of such a chain do the record's bounds decide?

Target form. The one-height bound of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) at \((4,4)\) on product chains.

Shortest route. conj:ultimate-matching at \((4,4)\) through the one-height bound. Taken in part: the cut-set step is made in the form the layer cake needs (lem:anchored-run-bound), which leaves one configuration, rows of \(B\) anchored at the side where \(h\) is largest; a first draft proved a side corollary before trying the plainest tool on the cut, which the reviewer found decides it (Process assessment).

Architecture test. Not decided. Of the twelfth review's outcomes, neither (A) nor (B): for product chains with \(h\) nonincreasing, the chain is at the target except for the variation of \(h\) along left-anchored runs of \(B\) (or of \(B^c\), when \(|D(h_{\rm hi})|\) and \(V'_{B^c}\) are at the target), and the middle values where the level strips are wide.

Owed attempt. The pile class entry named the cut-set bound through the layer cake. Made in part, reduced to the anchored runs (the form charging the cut at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) is not proved): the reviewer's row projection (its suggestion, checked here) shows each layer's cut paid by \(\partial B\) or by a run from \(x=0\), and summed over the layers this is the deterministic inequality lem:anchored-run-bound (a), proved directly row by row, so that lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) gives the bound without the layer cake, up to the anchored runs.

General statement. lem:anchored-run-bound, for every nonincreasing column function and every union of cells; cor:column-strip-localization, for every cell function and every partition into rectangles of cells.

Lemma (anchored-run bound)

Statement. Let \(h\ge0\) be constant on the columns of the mesh \(\delta_0\) and nonincreasing in \(x\), \(B\) a union of cells, \(g=h1_B\), \(V_B=\sum_e\delta_0h(x_e)\) over the inner edges \(e\) of \(\partial B\) (\(x_e\) the column of \(e\)'s \(B\)-cell), \(A_B=\sum_r\delta_0(h(0)-h(\rho_r))\) over the rows (\(\rho_r\) the right end of the run of \(B\)-cells of row \(r\) starting at \(x=0\), \(\rho_r=0\) if the row's first cell is not in \(B\); \(h(\rho)\) the value on the column whose left side is at \(\rho\), \(h(1)=0\)). (a) Deterministically, \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le2V_B+A_B\), \(\mathrm{TV}\) over inner edges as in lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor. (b) On the event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at \(\delta_0\) (any dyadic \(\delta_0\) in its range), \(|D(h1_B)|\le L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(2V_B+A_B)\). (c) With \(B^c\) the cells outside \(B\), \(V'_{B^c}\) as \(V_B\) read at \(e\)'s cell outside \(B\): \(|D(h1_B)|\le|D(h)|+L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(2V'_{B^c}+A_{B^c})\).

Proof. (a) The inner edges where \(g\) jumps are the edges of \(\partial B\), with jump \(h(x_e)\), and the vertical edges with \(B\) on both sides, the walls, with jump the difference of \(h\) across them. Each row splits into maximal runs of \(B\)-cells; along a run the walls' jumps add up to \(h(\text{first cell})-h(\text{last cell})\le h(\text{first cell})\), as \(h\) is nonincreasing. A run whose first cell is not at \(x=0\) has on its left an inner edge \(e\) of \(\partial B\) with \(h(x_e)=h(\text{first cell})\), and distinct runs have distinct left edges; the run starting at \(x=0\), if any, has walls adding up to \(h(0)-h(\text{last cell})\le h(0)-h(\rho_r)\). Summing over the runs times \(\delta_0\), the walls' variation is at most \(V_B+A_B\), and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le V_B+(V_B+A_B)\). (b) lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b), "every g constant on the cells has |sum_i g(X_i) - N int g| <= L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4) TV(g)", with (a). (c) \(h1_B=h-h1_{B^c}\), and (b) for \(B^c\), whose inner boundary edges are those of \(B\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \(h\) nonincreasing: the walls along a run add up to at most the run's first value, so the walls are paid by the run's left end; for \(h\) nondecreasing the same holds with right ends and runs anchored at \(x=1\), by reflection. \(h\ge0\): \(h(\text{last})\ge0\). The event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor: (b), and (c) through (b) for \(B^c\). (c) uses also the identity \(h1_B=h-h1_{B^c}\), which needs \(h\) defined on the whole square, and leaves \(D(h)\) to be bounded separately. Nothing on \(B\) or on the cost: (a) holds for every such \(h\) and \(B\), and (b), (c) on the event.

Degenerate cases. lem:anchored-run-bound at \(B=\emptyset\): \(0\le0\). \(B\) the whole square: \(V_B=0\), every row a run from \(x=0\) to \(1\), \(A_B=h(0)\), \(\mathrm{TV}=h(0)-h(\text{last column})\le A_B\); (c) gives \(|D(h)|\), the one-dimensional bound. \(h\) constant: no walls, \(\mathrm{TV}=V_B\), and \(A_B\) counts only the rows whole in \(B\).

Nonvacuity. At \(\delta_0=W=2^{-\ell_1}\) (the lemma has no cost hypothesis; for the witness to be a one-height chain of cost at most \(2\) at the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters, take \(d=y^*(\log N)^{1/2}\): its \(\partial B\) edges, \(v\approx h/W\le\sqrt N\), cost about \(\frac12(\frac12\log N)^{1/4}\int_{\partial B}h\le(\log N)^{1/4}\cdot3h(0)\to0\) with \(h(0)\approx(\log N)^{-1/2}\), and its walls about \(\psi_4^*(y^*/2)/(2d)\to0\); at \(h(0)\) of order one the cost exceeds \(2\), the reviewer's correction): \(h\) the staircase of \(Wy^*\) every \(d\) columns from \(h(0)\approx y^*/d\) down to \(0\) at \(x=1\), close to \(h(0)(1-x)\), and \(B\) the cells below the curve from \((0,\frac14)\) to \((1,\frac14)\) with a bump of height \(\frac12\) over \(x\in[\frac14,\frac34]\). The rows below \(\frac14\) are whole runs from \(x=0\), \(A_B\approx\frac14h(0)\), their walls adding up to the same; the rows from \(\frac14\) to \(\frac34\) are runs over \([\frac14,\frac34]\), their walls \(\frac12\cdot\frac12h(0)\) against their left ends' \(\frac12\cdot\frac34h(0)\): walls \(\approx\frac12h(0)\le\frac38h(0)+\frac14h(0)\), the step (a) adds being used on the bump's rows. Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) directly, \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\): the lemma is that bound after (a), so it gains nothing in order over it; what (a) adds is where the walls' variation is charged, at the runs' left ends, which at \((4,4)\) decides how the cost bounds it (Application). On this fixed witness lem:guided-chain-bound (b) with the family of the layers \(B\cap\{h>s\}\), at most \(1/W\) sets fixed in advance, decides it; the plainest uniform bound over all \(B\) is lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) itself.

Baseline. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) with \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\) uncharged by the cost: the walls inside \(B\) have increments \(y^*\), the cheapest, and their variation is bounded by the cost only through \(\psi_4^*(y^*/2)/y^*\), a constant, giving \((\log N)^{3/4}\) times a constant. Composed. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) on each layer \(B\cap\{h>s\}\) with the layer cake gives the same total variation; lem:guided-chain-bound (b) applied to each layer \(B\cap\{h>s\}\) separately needs every layer in a family fixed in advance, which holds for \(B\) from such a family and not for every \(B\); on the half-planes alone it bounds \(D(h)\), used in (c).

Corollary (column-strip localization)

Statement. On the event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, for every \(j\) with \(1\le j\le\ell_1\), every cell function \(g\) on the mesh \(2^{-j}\) and every partition of \([0,1]^2\) into rectangles \(R\) of cells, with sides \(s_R\le l_R\), \(M_R=\max_Rg^++\max_Rg^-\) and \(\Phi(R)=(2\log_2(2^js_R)+7)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\): \(|D(g)|\le L\sqrt N\sum_R\Phi(R)\,(V^0_j(g1_R)+8(l_R+4s_R)M_R)\), \(V^0_j\) the cell variation of lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (inner jumps times edge length, plus the edges on \(\partial[0,1]^2\) against \(0\)) and \(L\) its constant; on the event of lem:loglog-mesh-deviation the same holds with \(\sqrt{j+\log\log N}\) in place of \(\sqrt{\log N}\).

Proof. By linearity \(D(g)=\sum_RD(g1_R)\). For one \(R\), let \(k\) be the largest integer with \(2^{-k}\ge s_R\), so \(0\le k\le j\) and \(2^{-k}<2s_R\). lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) at the cell mesh \(2^{-j}\) and the coarse mesh \(2^{-k}\) gives \(|D(g1_R)|\le L\sqrt N\Phi_{j,k}(V^0_j(g1_R)+4\cdot2^{-k}\sum_Q(\max_Q(g1_R)^++\max_Q(g1_R)^-))\), the sum over the cells \(Q\) of side \(2^{-k}\); only those meeting \(R\) contribute, at most \(2(l_R2^k+2)\) of them (\(R\) meets at most two of their columns or rows across its short side), each at most \(M_R\), so the covering term is at most \(8(l_R+2\cdot2^{-k})M_R\le8(l_R+4s_R)M_R\); and \(2^{j-k}<2^{j+1}s_R\), so \(\Phi_{j,k}=(2(j-k)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\le\Phi(R)\). The loglog form: lem:tube-localized-discrepancy states (b) on that event with \(\sqrt{j+\log\log N}\) in \(\Phi\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The event: lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) for all \(k\le j\le\ell_1\) at once. \(j\ge1\): that lemma's range. Rectangles of cells: the count of coarse cells meeting \(R\). Nothing on \(g\) or on the partition beyond rectangles of cells: the conclusion holds for every cell function and every such partition (column strips, rows, mixed).

Degenerate cases. cor:column-strip-localization at \(g=0\): \(0\le0\). One rectangle, the square: \(s_R=1\), \(k=0\), lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) at \(k=0\) with covering \(40M\). Rectangles of one cell each: \(\Phi=7^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) and covering \(40\cdot2^{-j}M_R\) per cell, so the bound is of order \(2^{-j}\sqrt{N\log N}\sum_R|g|\), the plain per-cell count's order at \(j=\ell_1\): useful only where few rectangles carry large \(M_R\).

Nonvacuity. At \(j=\ell_1\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), \(N\) large, at the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters through its chain form: \(g=y^*W1_R\) on one rectangle \(R=J\times[\frac14,\frac34]\) of width \(|J|=W(\log N)^{10}\), the rest of the square one more rectangle on which \(g=0\) (split into at most four rectangles): \(\Phi(R)=(20\log_2\log N+7)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\le2\sqrt{\log N}\), \(V^0(g1_R)\le y^*W(2|J|+1)\), covering \(8(\frac12+4|J|)y^*W\), so the bound is about \(10y^*W\sqrt{N\log N}\). Plainest bound. The per-cell count restricted to the support, \(\|g\|_\infty\#\mathrm{supp}\,C\sqrt{NW^2\log N}\), gives \(\frac C2y^*W(\log N)^{10}\sqrt{N\log N}\), larger by \((\log N)^{10}\); lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) gives \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}y^*W(2|J|+1)\), larger by about \((\log N)^{1/4}\); the plainest uniform bound on the witness's family, lem:guided-chain-bound (b) over the at most \(N^4\) rectangles of cells, gives \(y^*W(P(R)\sqrt{7N\log N}+7\log N)\), the corollary's order: a fixed witness is decided by one set's bound, and the corollary adds uniformity over every cell function and partition.

Baseline. The plain per-cell count \(|D(g)|\le\|g\|_\infty\sum_{Q\in\mathrm{supp}\,g}|n_Q-NW^2|\), the step of lem:one-height-rounding that gives its "|D(h) - D(r)| <= C_0 Y sqrt(N log N)" from "0 <= h - r < Y delta", which decides any \(g\) with \(\|g\|_\infty\#\mathrm{supp}(g)\,W=O(1)\). Composed. lem:one-height-rounding applied to each rectangle's piece, its height \(Y\ge2e^{16}\) over its whole range, replaces the piece by a one-height chain within \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\) and bounds that chain not at all, the plain count again at large \(Y\); lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) on the whole square at its coarse mesh's whole range gives one \(\Phi\) for all rectangles, which the per-rectangle choice of \(k\) refines; lem:guided-chain-bound (b) applied to each rectangle's layers bounds only functions whose layers lie in a family fixed in advance, so composed over the rectangles it decides fixed witnesses and not the corollary's class; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) on each rectangle with linearity gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\sum_RV^0(g1_R)\), no gain.

Application: product chains at \((4,4)\)

Let \(g=h1_B\) be a one-height chain at \((4,4)\) on the mesh \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) of cost at most \(2\), \(h\) nonincreasing in \(x\) and constant on columns, its values multiples of \(Wy^*\) (every nonzero edge increment \(v_e\ge y^*\ge e^{19.28}\), thm:one-height-chain-reduction). Split \(h=h_{\rm lo}+h_{\rm hi}\), \(h_{\rm lo}=\min(h,WT)\), \(h_{\rm hi}=(h-WT)^+\), \(T=N^\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon<\frac12\), both nonincreasing.

High part. lem:anchored-run-bound (b) for \(h_{\rm hi}1_B\): an edge of \(\partial B\) with \(h_{\rm hi}(x_e)>0\) has \(v_e=h(x_e)/W\ge N^\varepsilon\), and \(\psi_4^*(u)\ge\frac12u(\log u)^{1/4}\) (the bound of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c)'s proof) gives \(Wh(x_e)\le4c_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\), \(c_e\) its cost, so \(V_B(h_{\rm hi})\le4\cdot2\,(\varepsilon\log N-1)^{-1/4}\) and \(2L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}V_B\le C\varepsilon^{-1/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\), at the target. What is left is \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}A_B(h_{\rm hi})\), the variation of \(h_{\rm hi}\) along the rows' runs of \(B\) anchored at \(x=0\), or by (c), at the price of \(|D(h_{\rm hi})|\) (a one-dimensional sum, at most \(h(0)\sup_x|F_N(x)-Nx|\), \(F_N\) the count of points left of \(x\), \(O(h(0)\sqrt N)\) in probability), the variation along the anchored runs of \(B^c\) with \(V'_{B^c}\) read at the cells outside \(B\), which differs from \(V_B\) on vertical edges by the jump of \(h\) across them.

Low part. cor:column-strip-localization with the level strips \(J_t=\{x:We^t\le h_{\rm lo}(x)<We^{t+1}\}\times[0,1]\), \(t<\log T\) (intervals, \(h\) monotone; the columns with \(h=0\) one more strip, where \(g=0\); and the columns with \(h\ge WT\) one more strip, where \(h_{\rm lo}=WT\), its \(V^0\) at most \(\sum_eW\cdot WT\) over the \(\partial B\) edges there plus \(7WT\), each such edge having \(W\cdot WT\le Wh(x_e)\le4c_e(\varepsilon\log N-1)^{-1/4}\), so with its \(\Phi\le C(\log N)^{3/4}\) it is at the target, its covering term \(40WT\) negligible), \(s=|J_t|\), \(l=1\): on each strip \(M\le We^{t+1}\) and \(V^0\le4c_t(t-1)^{-1/4}+7We^{t+1}\) (the \(\partial B\) part as above with \(v_e\ge e^t\), \(c_t\) the cost of those edges; walls and sides at most \(3We^{t+1}\); the square's boundary at most \(4We^{t+1}\)), so the low part is at most \(L\sqrt N\sum_t\Phi(J_t)(4c_t(t-1)^{-1/4}+47We^{t+1})\). Where \(|J_t|\le We^{Ct}\), \(\Phi(J_t)\le(2.9Ct+7)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) and the first terms sum to at most \(C'\sqrt{\log N}\sum_tc_t\le2C'\sqrt{\log N}\) (\(t^{3/4}(t-1)^{-1/4}\le2\sqrt t\)); the second to at most \(C''(\log N)^{3/4}WT\to0\). The cut between the two parts is in neither: \(h1_B=h_{\rm lo}1_B+h_{\rm hi}1_B\) exactly. Narrow strips hold when walls of jump \(Wy^*\) come every \(d\) columns, \(|J_t|\le Wd(e^{t+1}-e^t)/y^*+Wd\). At cost at most \(2\) with \(B\) of height of order one, the walls force \(h(0)=O(1)\), so the low part's region \(\{h<WN^\varepsilon\}\) is then a strip of width about \(dWN^\varepsilon/y^*\to0\) (the reviewer's remark): the low part has content only where \(h\) grows from \(W\) polynomially across a wide region, which needs \(C\gtrsim1/(2\varepsilon)\).

What remains. The anchored variation \(A_B(h_{\rm hi})\) (or \(A_{B^c}\)): \(B\) containing, in many rows, runs from the side where \(h\) is largest across many walls; and the low part's wide strips. The Instance, \(B=[0,1]\times[0,\frac12]\) with \(h\) linear, is all anchored rows, for \(B\) and \(B^c\) alike, and is decided by lem:guided-chain-bound (b) with the layer cake (its layers are rectangles fixed in advance), so it exercises neither result.

A set's boundary on a fixed line costs \(\sqrt{\log N}\); monotone one-height product chains come within \((\log N)^{1/12}\) of the target

18 October 2026 · Working proofs · Fixed line. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry continues pile-class-cap, by the twelfth review's out-of-turn Decision, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) and its last entry named this attempt.

Question. The anchored runs entry left the variation of \(h\) along runs of \(B\) from the side where \(h\) is largest. Does the walls' variation of a product chain cost only \(\sqrt{\log N}\)?

Target form. The one-height bound of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) at \((4,4)\), here for product chains \(h1_B\), \(h\) nonincreasing, in their part above \(WN^\varepsilon\).

Shortest route. Taken: the layer cake writes \(D(h1_B)\) as an integral over sets \(B\cap H_s\) cut by vertical lines, whose cuts integrate to the walls' variation; a bound charging a set's boundary on a fixed line at \(\sqrt{\log N}\), lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, proved here from two recorded lemmas, gives prop:fixed-line-product-chains.

Architecture test. Not decided. Of the twelfth review's outcomes, neither (A) nor (B): the part \(h\ge WN^\varepsilon\) of every nonincreasing product chain of cost at most \(2\) is at the target; the low part's middle multiplicities, non-monotone \(h\) and non-product chains are open.

Item history. The item's two earlier entries were read: the pile class charges, whose next attempt was "the layer-cake reduction (the reviewer's suggestion, unverified)", and the anchored runs, whose next attempt wrote \(h1_B=h1_{L_B}+h1_{B\setminus L_B}\), "the second with no anchored runs (each of its rows starts outside it)".

Owed attempt. The anchored runs entry named splitting \(B\) into its left-justified part \(L_B\) and the rest. Made, and replaced: by hand, each layer of \(h1_{L_B}\) is the subgraph \(\{x<\min(\rho(y),x_s)\}\), a set touching the line \(x=x_s\), so the split needs exactly a bound for sets touching a fixed line, which lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound gives for every such set, \(L_B\) or not; the split is then not needed.

General statement. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, for every union of cells in a vertical half-plane at every grid line; prop:fixed-line-product-chains, for every product chain of cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\) with \(h\) monotone on columns; cor:monotone-product-chain-bound, for every such chain and every such one-height chain.

Lemma (fixed-line boundary bound)

Statement. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound. On the intersection of the events of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at \(\delta_0=W=2^{-\ell_1}\) and of lem:guided-chain-bound (b) for the family of strips \([0,c)\times I\) and \([c,1)\times I\) (\(c\) on the grid, \(I\) an interval of rows; at most \(2W^{-3}\le2N^{3/2}\) sets), probability tending to one, for \(N\) large and every \(c\in(0,1]\) on the grid, \(H=\{x<c\}\), and every union \(A\) of cells of mesh \(W\) contained in \(H\): \(|D(1_A)|\le C_0\sqrt N\big((\log N)^{3/4}\ell_{\rm out}+\sqrt{\log N}\,\ell_{\rm line}\big)\), \(\ell_{\rm line}\) the length of the inner edges of \(\partial A\) on the line \(x=c\), \(\ell_{\rm out}\) that of the other inner edges of \(\partial A\), \(C_0\) depending only on \(L\), the constant of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor.

Proof. Let \(E=H\setminus A\). Each row of \(H\), the \(c/W\) cells of one row left of the line, is full (all in \(A\)), empty (all in \(E\)) or mixed; let \(J_A\), \(J_E\), \(M\) be these sets of rows. A mixed row has, inside \(H\), a vertical edge between a cell of \(A\) and one of \(E\), an inner edge of \(\partial A\) off the line, so \(W|M|\le\ell_{\rm out}\). A line edge of \(\partial A\) lies in a row whose last cell is in \(A\), a full or mixed row, so \(\ell_{\rm line}\le W|J_A|+W|M|\). Order the full and empty rows bottom to top, ignoring the mixed ones, and call an alternation a consecutive pair of opposite types; for each alternation, every column of \([0,c)\) passes from \(A\) to \(E\) (or back) between its two rows, so it holds a horizontal inner edge of \(\partial A\) there, and these edges, \(c/W\) of them, lie in disjoint row ranges for distinct alternations: with \(k\) alternations, \(kc\le\ell_{\rm out}\). Cut the rows into \(k+1\) bands by one row boundary inside each alternation's range; each band holds full rows of one type only, or none. A band \(I\) holding a full row is an \(A\)-band; the others are \(E\)-bands. With \(S_I=[0,c)\times I\), \(D(1_A)=\sum_ID(1_{A\cap S_I})\); write \(\ell_{\rm out}(S_I)\) for the inner edges of \(\partial A\) off the line lying strictly inside the band, the edges on its cut lines being counted separately, at most \(c\) per cut side. (i) An \(A\)-band: \(1_{A\cap S_I}=1_{S_I}-1_{E\cap S_I}\). The strip \(S_I\) lies in a family of at most \(2W^{-3}\le2N^{3/2}\) sets fixed in advance (\(W^{-2}\le N\); both sides' strips), so \(\log M_N+3\log N\le5\log N\) for \(N\) large, so lem:guided-chain-bound (b), "for any family of M_N unions of coarse cells fixed in advance, |D(1_S)| <= P(S) sqrt(N(log M_N + 3 log N)) + log M_N + 3 log N", gives \(|D(1_{S_I})|\le P(S_I)\sqrt{5N\log N}+5\log N\), with \(P(S_I)\le|I|\,1\{c<1\}+c\cdot\#\{\text{cut sides of }I\}\) (its left side and any side on \(y=0,1\) are not inner); \(|I|1\{c<1\}\le\ell_{\rm line}(I)+W|M\cap I|\) since the band's full rows are line rows, and the cut sides number at most \(2k\) over all bands. \(E\cap S_I\) has no empty row, so its edges on the line lie in mixed rows, at most \(W|M\cap I|\); its other inner boundary edges are edges of \(\partial A\) in \(S_I\) and edges on the band's cut sides, at most \(c\) per side; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), "every union A of cells of side delta_0 has |#(X in A) - N area(A)| <= L sqrt N (log N)^(3/4) P(A)", gives \(|D(1_{E\cap S_I})|\le L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\ell_{\rm out}(S_I)+W|M\cap I|+c\cdot\#\{\text{cut sides of }I\})\). (ii) An \(E\)-band: \(A\cap S_I\) has no full row, so its line edges lie in mixed rows, and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) gives \(|D(1_{A\cap S_I})|\le L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\ell_{\rm out}(S_I)+W|M\cap I|+c\cdot\#\{\text{cut sides of }I\})\). Summing over the bands. The remainders: \(\sum_I(\ell_{\rm out}(S_I)+W|M\cap I|+c\cdot\#\{\text{cut sides of }I\})\le\ell_{\rm out}+\ell_{\rm out}+2kc\le4\ell_{\rm out}\), the \(k\) cuts having two sides each and \(kc\le\ell_{\rm out}\). The strips: \(\sum_IP(S_I)\le(\ell_{\rm line}+W|M|)+2kc\le\ell_{\rm line}+3\ell_{\rm out}\). A strip with \(P(S_I)=0\) has no inner side, so it is the whole square (\(c=1\), one band) and \(D(1_{S_I})=0\); any other has \(P(S_I)\ge W\), so its additive term \(5\log N\le5(\log N/W)P(S_I)\le5\sqrt N(\log N)^{1/4}P(S_I)\) (\(W\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\)), and \(\sqrt{5N\log N}+5\sqrt N(\log N)^{1/4}\le5\sqrt{N\log N}\) for \(N\) large (\(\sqrt5\le2.24\), \(5(\log N)^{-1/4}\le2.76\) once \(\log N\ge11\)). Hence \(|D(1_A)|\le4L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\ell_{\rm out}+5\sqrt{N\log N}(\ell_{\rm line}+3\ell_{\rm out})\le C_0\sqrt N((\log N)^{3/4}\ell_{\rm out}+\sqrt{\log N}\,\ell_{\rm line})\), \(C_0=4L+15\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at \(W\): the parts \(E\cap S_I\) and \(A\cap S_I\), unions of cells of side \(W\). The event of lem:guided-chain-bound (b) for the strips: the strips, fixed in advance, at most \(2N^{3/2}\) of them, both sides' strips included so that the right-half-plane form holds on the same event. \(A\subseteq H\): the rows of \(H\) are the units of the classification and every line edge has its \(A\)-cell inside. \(W\ge(\log N)^{3/4}/\sqrt N\): the additive terms. Nothing else on \(A\) (any union of cells, Leighton–Shor or not) or on \(c\): the conclusion holds for every grid line and every such set; for a right half-plane \(\{x\ge c\}\) the same proof with rows read right to left gives the same bound, on the events of the same two lemmas for the strips \([c,1)\times I\).

Degenerate cases. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound at \(A=\emptyset\): \(0\le0\). \(A=H\): one full band, no alternation, \(\ell_{\rm out}=0\) and \(|D(1_H)|\le\sqrt{5N\log N}+5\log N\), the conclusion with \(\ell_{\rm line}=1\). \(A\) with no full row: one band, an \(E\)-band, lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) with \(\ell_{\rm line}\le\ell_{\rm out}\). \(c=1\): treated in the proof.

Nonvacuity. At the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters, through the proposition: \(c=\frac12\), \(A=[0,\frac12)\times[\frac12,1]\) minus one interior cell \(Q\) of a row \(r\): the rows above \(\frac12\) except \(r\) are full, \(r\) mixed, those below empty, one alternation, \(k=1\); the \(A\)-band's strip carries the line, \(\ell_{\rm line}=\frac12\) (\(Q\) is not in the column next to the line, so row \(r\) keeps its line edge), at \(\sqrt{\log N}\), and its remainder \(E\cap S_I=Q\) is nonempty, charged by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) at \(4W\); both steps of (i) are used. Plainest bound. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) on \(A\): \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}(\ell_{\rm out}+\ell_{\rm line})\), the line at \((\log N)^{3/4}\); on this fixed set lem:guided-chain-bound (b) with a family of one set decides it; the plainest uniform bound over all unions of cells in \(H\) is lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a), which the lemma improves on the line part; cor:fine-mesh-function-tube, "|D(H)| <= c_kappa sqrt(N log N) TV(H) + L sqrt N Phi_k (TV(H) + 12 W sum over W-cells Q of (max_Q H^+ + max_Q H^-)), Phi_k = (2(l_1 - k) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)", its \(W=2^{-k}\) a free dyadic scale, applied to \(H=1_A\) charges the whole \(\mathrm{TV}(1_A)\), the line edges included, at \(\Phi_k\): at \(k=0\) that is \((2\ell_1+5)^{3/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{3/4}\), and at \(k=\ell_1\) it is \(5^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) but the term \(12\cdot2^{-\ell_1}\sum_Q\max_Q1_A\) counts the cells of side \(2^{-\ell_1}\) meeting \(A\), \(12|A|2^{\ell_1}\) here, so at no \(k\) does it give the line part at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) on this witness.

Baseline. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a): every edge at \((\log N)^{3/4}\). Composed. lem:guided-chain-bound (b) applied to each band's strip separately, with linearity over the bands, and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) applied to each band's remainder alone: the lemma is this composition, the step added being the classification of rows and the count of alternations, which make the strips few and their sides charged to \(\partial A\).

Proposition (high part of nonincreasing product chains)

Statement. prop:fixed-line-product-chains. At \((4,4)\), on the event of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\): for every grid function \(g=h1_B\) on the mesh \(W\) with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and nonincreasing in \(x\), \(B\) a union of cells, and discrete cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\) (that of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)), and every \(\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\log N\ge18\), \(h_{\rm hi}=(h-WN^\varepsilon)^+\): \(|D(h_{\rm hi}1_B)|\le C_0\sqrt{N\log N}\,(8(\varepsilon/2)^{-1/4}+T(2))\), \(T(2)=4+4/\psi_4^*(1)\approx12.66\) the bound of lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a).

Proof. \(h_{\rm hi}\) is nonincreasing, so \(\{h_{\rm hi}1_B>s\}=B\cap H_s\), \(H_s=\{x<x_s\}\), \(x_s\) the left side of the first column with \(h_{\rm hi}\le s\), on the grid; by linearity and the layer cake, \(D(h_{\rm hi}1_B)=\int_0^{h_{\rm hi}(0)}D(1_{B\cap H_s})ds\). The inner boundary of \(B\cap H_s\) consists of the edges of \(\partial B\) whose \(B\)-cell lies in \(H_s\) and of the cut, the vertical edges on \(x=x_s\) with \(B\) on both sides; the edges of \(\partial B\) on that line are counted with the first, which the lemma's first term charges at \((\log N)^{3/4}\ge\sqrt{\log N}\), an upper bound. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound gives \(|D(1_{B\cap H_s})|\le C_0\sqrt N((\log N)^{3/4}\ell(\partial B\cap H_s)+\sqrt{\log N}\,\ell(\mathrm{cut}_s))\). Integrating: \(\int\ell(\partial B\cap H_s)ds=\sum_eWh_{\rm hi}(x_e)=:V\) over the inner edges of \(\partial B\); and an inner vertical edge \(w\) with \(B\) on both sides, between columns of values \(u>v\) of \(h_{\rm hi}\), is on the cut exactly for \(s\in[v,u)\), so \(\int\ell(\mathrm{cut}_s)ds=\sum_wW|\Delta_wh_{\rm hi}|\le\sum_wW|\Delta_wg|\le\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\) (\(t\mapsto(t-a)^+\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz; lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a), "every grid function g on a mesh delta with 1/delta an integer and discrete cost sum_e delta^2 psi_4^*(|Delta_e g|/(2 delta)) at most M has TV(g) <= T(M)"). An edge of \(\partial B\) with \(h_{\rm hi}(x_e)>0\) has increment \(v_e=h(x_e)/W\ge N^\varepsilon\), so \(v_e/2\ge e^{\varepsilon\log N}/2\ge e^{16}\) as \(\varepsilon\log N\ge18\), and \(\psi_4^*(u)\ge\frac12u(\log u)^{1/4}\) there (as in lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c)'s proof) gives \(Wh_{\rm hi}(x_e)\le W^2v_e\le4c_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\le4c_e(\varepsilon\log N-1)^{-1/4}\le4c_e(\varepsilon\log N/2)^{-1/4}\), \(c_e\) its cost, so \(V\le8(\varepsilon\log N/2)^{-1/4}\). Together \(|D(h_{\rm hi}1_B)|\le C_0\sqrt N(8(\log N)^{3/4}(\varepsilon\log N/2)^{-1/4}+T(2)\sqrt{\log N})\), the statement. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The lemma's event: each layer. \(h\) nonincreasing: each layer is \(B\) cut by one vertical line, a set in a left half-plane; for \(h\) nondecreasing the right-half-plane form of the lemma (its Hypotheses) gives the same bound. Cost at most \(2\): \(\sum c_e\le2\) and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\). \(\varepsilon\log N\ge18\): \(v_e/2\ge e^{16}\) for the lower bound of \(\psi_4^*\), and \((\varepsilon\log N-1)^{-1/4}\le(\varepsilon\log N/2)^{-1/4}\). No one-height hypothesis: the walls' variation is bounded by the total variation, which the cost bounds for every grid function (scope more general than the conditional draft's, which asked one-height chains).

Degenerate cases. prop:fixed-line-product-chains at \(B=\emptyset\) or \(h\le WN^\varepsilon\): \(h_{\rm hi}1_B=0\), \(0\le0\). \(B\) the square: \(V=0\), the walls are \(h\)'s jumps, and the bound is \(C_0T(2)\sqrt{N\log N}\), where the one-dimensional bound for \(D(h)\) gives \(O(h(0)\sqrt N)\) in probability.

Nonvacuity. At the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters: \(h\) falling from \(h(0)=Wy^*\lfloor1/(Wy^*)\rfloor\le1\) to \(0\) by one wall of increment \(y^*\) per column over the width \(w=(\log N)^{-1/2}\) (its at most \(1/(Wy^*)\) walls need width \(1/y^*\le w\)), and \(B\) the top half \([0,1]\times[\frac12,1]\) minus one vertical slit of one column, at a column in \((0,\frac w2)\), not column \(0\), where \(h\ge\frac12\), of height \(t=\frac12(\frac12\log N)^{-1/4}\) above \(y=\frac12\). Cost, from \(\psi_4^*(u)\le u(\log(1+u))^{1/4}\) for the record's \(\psi_4(t)=e^{t^4}-1\) (at the maximizer of \(ut-\psi_4(t)\), \(u=4t^3e^{t^4}\ge e^{t^4}-1\), so \(t\le\psi_4^{-1}(u)=(\log(1+u))^{1/4}\)): the walls, at most \(\frac1{Wy^*}\cdot\frac1{2W}\) edges of cost \(W^2\psi_4^*(y^*/2)\), at most \(\frac12\cdot\frac12(\log(1+y^*/2))^{1/4}\le0.53\) (thm:one-height-chain-reduction's \(y^*=Y/c\) with \(Y=e^{22}\) and \(c=C_1/2\ge7\), so \(\log(y^*/2)\le22-\log14\le19.36\), \(19.36^{1/4}\le2.10\)); the line \(y=\frac12\), edges of increment \(h(x)/W\le1/W\le\sqrt N\) on \([0,w)\), at most \(\frac w2(\frac12\log N)^{1/4}\to0\); the slit's sides, \(2t/W\) edges of increment at most \(1/W\le\sqrt N\), at most \(2t\cdot\frac12(\frac12\log N)^{1/4}=\frac12\); its top, one edge of the same increment, at most \(W\cdot\frac12(\frac12\log N)^{1/4}\to0\): cost at most \(1.1\) for \(N\) large. The recorded uniform bounds leave it above the target: lem:anchored-run-bound (b) has \(A_B\ge\frac12-t\), its (c) \(A_{B^c}=\frac12\), each charged \((\log N)^{3/4}\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) charges the slit's sides, of cost at least about \(\frac18\) by the lower bound on \(\psi_4^*\), at \((\log v)^{1/4}\ge(\frac12\log N-\log2)^{1/4}\), at \((\log N)^{1/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\). The proposition charges the walls at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) and the slit's sides, increment at least \(1/(2W)\ge N^{1/4}\), at the target, the step it adds. Plainest bound. This \(g\) is one fixed function, decided by its variance; the plainest uniform bounds over the class, lem:anchored-run-bound (b) and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), leave it above the target, as computed above; and it splits as \(h1_{[0,1]\times[\frac12,1]}-h1_{\rm slit}\), whose first part lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) decides at the target (its walls of increment \(y^*\), its line of cost tending to \(0\)) and whose second lem:anchored-run-bound (b) decides (the slit is not in column \(0\), so none of its rows starts at \(x=0\), \(A=0\), and \(V\) at most \(8(\frac14\log N-1)^{-1/4}\)), so a split into two recorded uniform bounds decides this witness too; no witness was found outside every such split, and what the proposition adds is one uniform bound over every monotone \(h\) and every \(B\), with no split to choose.

Baseline. lem:anchored-run-bound (b), \((\log N)^{3/4}(2V+A_B)\), and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), \(\sqrt{N\log N}(46+6\sum_ew_e(\log v_e)^{1/4})\), each above the target on part of the class. Composed. lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) applied to each layer alone gives \((\log N)^{3/4}(V+\mathcal W)\), the walls at \((\log N)^{3/4}\); lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) applied to the whole chain charges the high edges at \((\log N)^{1/4}\) above the target; lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound applied to each layer, the proposition. lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging gives on the witness only its (a), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\), used for the walls; its (b) at \(\delta_0=W\) compares \(g\) with its own averages, \(E_Wg=g\), and gives nothing. lem:one-height-rounding, at its height \(Y=e^{22}\), not \(y^*\), maps the witness to another one-height chain at an error \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), whose bound is the open question, so it decides nothing on it.

Corollary (monotone product chains)

Statement. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound. At \((4,4)\), on the events of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound and of lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) at \(\delta_0=W\), for \(N\) large: every grid function \(g=h1_B\) on the mesh \(W\) of cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\), \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\), \(B\) a union of cells, has (a) \(|D(g)|\le C_1(\log N)^{1/8}\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C_1\) universal; (b) on the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound as well, if \(h\)'s values are multiples of \(Wy^*\) (a one-height chain, thm:one-height-chain-reduction), \(|D(g)|\le C_2(\log N)^{1/12}\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C_2\) universal.

Proof. Let \(T=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\), \(h_{\rm lo}=\min(h,WT)\), \(h_{\rm hi}=(h-WT)^+\), so \(g=h_{\rm lo}1_B+h_{\rm hi}1_B\), both monotone. Since \(t\mapsto\min(t,a)\) and \(t\mapsto(t-a)^+\) are \(1\)-Lipschitz and \(\psi_4^*\) is nondecreasing, each part's increments are at most \(g\)'s and its cost at most \(2\). The low part has every increment at most \(T\), so lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), "|D(g)| <= (3/4) L_0 sqrt(N log N)(46 + 6 sum over edges with v_e >= 2e^16 of w_e (log v_e)^(1/2 - 1/alpha_d(e)))", at \((4,4)\) gives \(|D(h_{\rm lo}1_B)|\le\frac34L_0\sqrt{N\log N}(46+12(\log N)^{1/8})\). The high part is prop:fixed-line-product-chains at \(\varepsilon=(\log N)^{-1/2}\), where \(\varepsilon\log N=\sqrt{\log N}\ge18\) for \(N\) large: \(|D(h_{\rm hi}1_B)|\le C_0\sqrt{N\log N}(8\cdot2^{1/4}(\log N)^{1/8}+T(2))\). This is (a). (b) Let \(K\) be the largest integer with \(K\le N^{1/7}\) and \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y^*/2))^{1/3}\), and split at \(WT'\), \(T'=Ky^*\), a multiple of \(Wy^*\)'s step: \(h_{\rm lo}=\min(h,KWy^*)\) takes the values \(0,Wy^*,\dots,KWy^*\), so \(h_{\rm lo}1_B=Wy^*\sum_{k\le K}1_{A_k}\), \(A_k=B\cap\{h\ge kWy^*\}\), a nested chain at the one height \(y^*\ge2e^{16}\) with at most \(K\) layers and cost at most \(2\); lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), "hence |D(g)| <= C' sqrt(N log N) when K <= N^(1/7) and log K <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3)", gives \(|D(h_{\rm lo}1_B)|\le C'\sqrt{N\log N}\). The high part is the proposition at \(N^\varepsilon=T'\), \(\varepsilon\log N=\log K+\log y^*\ge(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y^*/2))^{1/3}-1\ge18\) for \(N\) large, so \((\varepsilon/2)^{-1/4}=(2\log N/(\varepsilon\log N))^{1/4}\le2(\log N)^{1/12}\) and \(|D(h_{\rm hi}1_B)|\le C_0\sqrt{N\log N}(16(\log N)^{1/12}+T(2))\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The two events: each part. Monotone \(h\): the proposition for the high part (both directions, its Hypotheses). Cost at most \(2\): both parts. The threshold \(T=e^{\sqrt{\log N}}\) balances the two charges, \(\sqrt{\log N}(\log T)^{1/4}\) for the low part and \((\log N)^{3/4}(\log T)^{-1/4}\) for the high part, equal at \(\log T=\sqrt{\log N}\); any other threshold gives a larger exponent. (b) adds: values multiples of \(Wy^*\), so the low part is a nested chain at one height, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d)'s class, its layer count \(K\) the step that bounds the threshold; the threshold \(KWy^*\) is the largest that condition allows. The conclusion holds for every such \(g\).

Degenerate cases. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound at \(B=\emptyset\): \(0\); at \(h\le WT\): the low part alone, lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a); at \(h\) with every value at least \(WT\) where positive: the high part alone, the proposition with \(T\) as threshold.

Nonvacuity. The proposition's witness, whose \(h(0)=Wy^*\lfloor1/(Wy^*)\rfloor\) is a multiple of \(Wy^*\): \(h\) falls to \(0\) by walls of increment \(y^*\), so it takes values below \(WT\) and below \(KWy^*\), and the slit's sides have increments at least \(N^{1/4}\), above both thresholds; its values are multiples of \(Wy^*\), a one-height chain; both parts are nonzero in (a) and in (b), and all three bounds are used, at the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters. Plainest bound. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) on the whole \(g\): \((\log N)^{1/4}\) above the target, against the corollary's \((\log N)^{1/8}\).

Baseline. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a): every monotone product chain within \((\log N)^{1/4}\) of the target. Composed. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) applied to the low part alone and prop:fixed-line-product-chains applied to the high part alone, with linearity: the corollary, the threshold over its whole range \(T\in[1,1/W]\) giving its best value at \(\log T=\sqrt{\log N}\). lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (b) at \(\delta_0=W\) compares \(g\) with itself and gives nothing on the witness; its (a) enters through the proposition.

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:anchored-run-bound charged the walls to the runs' left ends and left the anchored runs at \((\log N)^{3/4}\); the full rows of the lemma's proof are those anchored runs, layer by layer, and lem:guided-chain-bound (b) on strips charges them at \(\sqrt{\log N}\), so the lemma removes that entry's anchored term. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) bounds every class function at \(\sqrt{\log N}(\log v)^{1/4}\) per unit cost and already decides the low part when \(\log v\) is bounded, and the corollary composes it with the proposition. The lemma's steps are compositions of lem:guided-chain-bound (b) and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a); the step added is the row classification with the alternation count (the reviewer's suggestion, checked here step by step). lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, lem:two-mesh-partition-discrepancy and lem:local-factor-discrepancy charge a boundary's parts by mesh or localization, not by lying on a fixed line. The proposition is the layer cake with lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a) for the walls; the corollary is the proposition and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) split at one threshold. The nearest registered statements by wording: cor:fine-mesh-function-tube charges an indicator's whole perimeter at \(\Phi_k\), \((\log N)^{3/4}\) near \(k=0\), and neither it nor the lemma implies the other; lem:one-height-rounding carries a monotone product chain of cost \(M\) to a monotone one-height one of cost at most \(7M+(\psi_4^*(Y/2)/Y)T(M)\), so the corollary's (b), if proved at bounded cost rather than at cost \(2\), would give (a) at \((\log N)^{1/12}\); that is not covered here, (b) and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) being stated at cost at most \(2\). Three more by wording, each neither more general nor a special case: lem:separated-bundle-chains bounds nested chains whose steep edges lie on separated straight bundles, (B1)–(B4), and says nothing of a set's boundary on a fixed line, which lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound charges for every union of cells in a half-plane; thm:one-height-chain-reduction reduces the goal at \((4,4)\) to nested chains at the one height \(y^*\), and prop:fixed-line-product-chains bounds part of that class, monotone product chains above \(WN^\varepsilon\), with \(y^*\) entering only through the cost; lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) bounds chains under "|S| <= N^(1/6)/(log N)^2 and log|B| <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y_B/2))^(1/3)", the same count limit as lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), so it could serve for the low part of cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b) in place of (d), and it does not reach the residual, whose layer count exceeds that limit.

New mathematics. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound: on the events of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at the mesh \(W\) and of lem:guided-chain-bound (b) for strips, every union of cells of mesh \(W\) in a vertical half-plane at a grid line has its boundary on the line charged at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) and the rest at \((\log N)^{3/4}\). prop:fixed-line-product-chains: at \((4,4)\), for every grid function \(h1_B\) of cost at most \(2\) with \(h\) monotone on columns, the part above \(WN^\varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon\log N\ge18\), has discrepancy \(O(\varepsilon^{-1/4}\sqrt{N\log N})\). cor:monotone-product-chain-bound: every such grid function has discrepancy \(O((\log N)^{1/8}\sqrt{N\log N})\), and every such one-height chain \(O((\log N)^{1/12}\sqrt{N\log N})\), lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) taking the part below \(KWy^*\), \(\log K\) of order \((\log N)^{2/3}\).

Goal progress. Unchanged: the one-height bound is proved for no class at the target beyond the record's; monotone one-height product chains, the form of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)'s class with \(h\) monotone, are now within \((\log N)^{1/12}\) of it, from \((\log N)^{1/4}\). Bearing. At \((4,4)\), for fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), every monotone product chain's part above \(WN^\varepsilon\) is at the target, every monotone one-height product chain within \((\log N)^{1/12}\), and every monotone product chain within \((\log N)^{1/8}\) (the curve's parameters, the pair \((4,4)\)). Not covered. Monotone one-height product chains' edges of \(\partial B\) with \((\log N)^{2/3}\lesssim\log v_e=o(\log N)\), where the proposition's charge \((\log N)^{3/4}(\log v_e)^{-1/4}\) leaves an excess falling from \((\log N)^{1/12}\) at the lower end to \(O(1)\) where \(\log v_e\) is of order \(\log N\); \(h\) not monotone in \(x\); grid functions that are not of the form \(h1_B\).

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

"set inside half plane boundary on a fixed line charged sqrt log N straight part of the boundary discrepancy" returned lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, lem:guided-chain-bound and lem:band-family-discrepancy; none states it.
  • The split at \(We^{\sqrt{\log N}}\): checked here and registered as cor:monotone-product-chain-bound. Record. The same search, and lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) read in the turn.
  • Drop the reflection follow-up: adopted; the reflection moved the line term, its difference \(D(1_A-1_{\sigma A})\) jumping by \(2\) across the line. Record. No recorded reflection argument found by the same search.

Follow-up. Continuing. Next attempt: a new joint lemma, not a composition of recorded results, for the residual of cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b). The high part above \(KWy^*\) is \(Wy^*\sum_{k>K}1_{B\cap H_k}\), a nested chain at one height whose layers lie in half-planes; the lemma would be the fixed-line form of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), charging each layer's cut at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) as lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound does and its \(\partial B\) edges by (c)'s perimeter factor, summed over more than \(K\) layers, where (c) alone needs \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\). Smallest case. At most \(K\) layers: lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), "hence |D(g)| <= C' sqrt(N log N) when K <= N^(1/7) and log K <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3)", decides it at the target, one or two piled layers included; so the case the attempt adds is more than \(K\) layers, \(\log K\) above \((\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y^*/2))^{1/3}\), where (c)'s first term, charged once for the whole chain, \(T(2\log_2(Ky^2)+5)^{3/4}\), exceeds the target. Nontrivial because: the mechanism acts on the layers' perimeters \(P_k\), many layers sharing the same piled \(\partial B\) edges, which the cost bounds only in total: over the \(\partial B\) edges \(e\) with \(h_{\rm hi}(x_e)>0\), whose increments in \(g\) are \(v_e=h(x_e)/W\ge Ky^*\) and which carry \(m_e=h_{\rm hi}(x_e)/(Wy^*)\le v_e/y^*\) layers, \(\sum_kP_k=\sum_eWm_e\le\sum_eWv_e/y^*\le\frac{8}{Wy^*}(\log(Ky^*/2))^{-1/4}\), from \(W^2v_e\le4c_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\) and \(\sum c_e\le2\), the \(P_k\) here leaving out the cuts, which lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound charges. The per-layer route, lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) on each layer with Jensen for the concave \(P\mapsto P(2\log_2(1/(WP))+5)^{3/4}\), gives over \(n\) layers with \(P_k\ge1\) at most \(S'(2\log_2(n/(WS'))+5)^{3/4}\), where \(S'=\sum_k(P_k+\mathrm{cut}_k)\), since (b) bounds a layer by its whole inner perimeter, cut included, and \(\sum_k\mathrm{cut}_k\le T(2)/(Wy^*)\), so \(S'\le(8(\log(Ky^*/2))^{-1/4}+T(2))/(Wy^*)\); layers with \(P_k<1\) are outside (b) and carry (c)'s extra term \(L\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}y\delta_0\sum_{P_k<1}P_k\). That is (c)'s \((\log n)^{3/4}\) again, up to constants \(\sqrt N(\log(Ky^*))^{-1/4}(\log n)^{3/4}\), above the target only where \(\log n\gg(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(Ky^*))^{1/3}\), about \((\log N)^{8/9}\), and \((\log N)^{1/12}\) above it at \(\log n\approx\frac12\log N\), as cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b) gives; so the joint lemma has to beat \((\log n)^{3/4}\) through the cut charge, not through the perimeter factor, and the residual is \(\log n\) above about \((\log N)^{8/9}\). Plainest bound. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b), \((\log N)^{1/12}\) above the target. Own statements. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b) gives "\(C_2(\log N)^{1/12}\sqrt{N\log N}\)", not the target; lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) needs "K <= N^(1/7) and log K <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3)", which the residual's layer count exceeds; its (b) needs "inner perimeter P(A) >= 1", which holds at the average perimeter but not for every layer (those with \(P_k<1\) carry (c)'s extra term); at a layer perimeter \(P\approx\frac{8}{WKy^*}\), the average over a chain with more than \(K\) layers (the high part alone may have fewer), its factor \((2\log_2(Ky^*/8)+5)^{3/4}\) is of order \((\log K)^{3/4}\), at the target per unit perimeter, and summed by Jensen over \(n\) layers it is (c)'s bound, so (b) applied layer by layer gives what (c) gives and no more; lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound charges "\(\ell_{\rm out}\)" at \((\log N)^{3/4}\), the \(\partial B\) edges included, and bounds a set by its whole perimeter, as each recorded lemma does, so their charges do not combine on one layer without the new lemma; lem:multilevel-chain-bound needs "|S| <= N^(1/6)/(log N)^2 and log|B| <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y_B/2))^(1/3)", the same count limit. lem:separated-bundle-chains, for "a nested chain g = delta_0 sum_{k <= K} y_k 1_{A_k} with heights y_k in [2e^16, V] (K arbitrary)", gives \(C\sqrt{N\log N}(1+(\log V)^{1/4}+\eta_W)\), with \(V=y^*\) at the one height; applied to the high part's chain \(h_{\rm hi}1_B\), whose layers are \(A_k=B\cap H_k\), so that \(A_j\setminus A_{j+1}\) is \(B\) within the columns where \(h_{\rm hi}=jWy^*\), one level strip of \(h\): a \(\partial B\) edge lies on exactly the boundaries of the layers \(0<k\le m=h_{\rm hi}(x_e)/(Wy^*)\) and on no cut, so (B1) holds for a run whose edges all carry the same \(m\), and (B2) asks the run's strip of \(m+1\) cells deep to lie in \(B\) inside one level strip of \(h\) (for a vertical run a level strip at least \((m+1)W\) wide beside it, for a horizontal run all its columns in one level strip, the same for lem:staircase-bundle-chains's lattice paths and bands). For the residual edges \(m\approx v_e/y^*\) is about \(e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\), and (B4), "l_b >= max(2^(-l_1), 2 m_b delta_0 (log Y_b)^(1/4))", needs runs that long inside one level strip; where \(h\) is steep the level strips are narrow and both lemmas fail on every run, the proposition's witness included (one wall per column, level strips of width \(W\)), and edges left off bundles go into \(\eta_W\) at \((\log v_e)^{1/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{1/4}\) on the residual, worse than cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b). So the bundle lemmas decide only chains whose high-multiplicity \(\partial B\) edges lie on long runs inside wide level strips of \(h\), with \(B\) at least \(m+1\) cells deep and the strips disjoint, and the next attempt's case is mainly \(\partial B\) crossing narrow level strips, steep \(h\). lem:guided-chain-bound (b) needs "a family F_N of at most N^c unions of cells ... fixed before the points are drawn", which the layers \(B\cap H_k\), ranging over all unions of cells, are not; its (a) at \(\delta_0=W\), where the layers are already unions of cells of side \(2^{-\ell_1}\), with \(S=A\) and \(T\) empty gives \(|D(1_A)-D(1_S)|=0\), so the bound rests on \(D(1_S)\), which needs (b)'s fixed family.
