Monotone product chains meet the target

18 October 2026 · Working proofs · Monotone product chains. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry continues pile-class-cap, by the twelfth review's out-of-turn Decision, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) and its last entry named this attempt.

Question. The fixed line entry left the chains \(h1_B\), \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\), within \((\log N)^{1/12}\) of the target when one-height and within \((\log N)^{1/8}\) otherwise (cor:monotone-product-chain-bound). Is every such chain of cost at most \(2\) at the target?

Target form. The one-height bound of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) at \((4,4)\), here for every grid function \(h1_B\) with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\), whole, without a split at a threshold.

Shortest route. Taken: the layer cake of prop:fixed-line-product-chains, each layer \(B\cap H_s\) charged by the smaller of two recorded bounds, lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound when its boundary off the line is short and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) when it is long, and the layers summed over dyadic levels of \(h\) (lem:dyadic-level-sum), where a layer's off-line boundary is at most the mass of its level over the level's height.

Architecture test. Not decided. Of the twelfth review's outcomes, neither (A) nor (B): every chain \(h1_B\) with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\) and cost at most \(2\) is at the target, a subclass of the one-height chains (A) asks; chains of other forms are open.

Item history. The item's three earlier entries were read: the pile class charges, "Next attempt: the layer-cake reduction (the reviewer's suggestion, unverified)"; the anchored runs, "Next attempt: the anchored runs. The left-anchored part"; and the fixed line entry, whose next attempt was "a new joint lemma, not a composition of recorded results, for the residual".

Owed attempt. The fixed line entry named a joint lemma, the fixed-line form of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), as not a composition of recorded results. Made, and decided otherwise: before drafting it, the plainest composition was tried on the layer itself (AGENTS.md's plainest-bound item): the minimum of the two recorded per-set bounds already has the joint form, \(\ell(2\log_2(1+1/(W\ell))+5)^{3/4}\) off the line and \(\sqrt{\log N}\) on it (Step 1 below), so no new per-set lemma is needed, and the step the entry adds is the sum over levels.

General statement. lem:dyadic-level-sum, for every grid function \(h\ge0\) and every union of cells \(B\) with \(h1_B\) of cost at most \(2\); thm:monotone-product-chains, for every grid function \(h1_B\) of cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\) with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\).

Lemma (dyadic level sum)

Statement. lem:dyadic-level-sum. At \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), for \(N\) large, deterministically: for every function \(h\ge0\) constant on the cells of mesh \(W\) and every union \(B\) of such cells with discrete cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\), \(g=h1_B\), let \(\ell_s\) be the length of the inner edges of \(\partial B\) whose \(B\)-cell \(c\) has \(h(c)>s\), and \(\varphi(\ell)=\ell\,(2\log_2(1+1/(W\ell))+5)^{3/4}\) (\(\varphi(0)=0\)); then \(\int_0^\infty\varphi(\ell_s)\,ds\le42\sqrt{\log N}+C(\log\log N)^{3/4}\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. \(\varphi\) is increasing: with \(u=2\log_2(1+1/(W\ell))+5\ge5\) and \(q=1/(W\ell)\), \(\varphi'=u^{-1/4}(u-\frac{3}{2\ln2}\frac q{1+q})\ge u^{-1/4}(u-2.17)>0\). For an inner edge \(e\) of \(\partial B\) let \(c_e\) be its \(B\)-cell, \(v_e=h(c_e)/W=|\Delta_eg|/W\), and \(\mathrm{cost}_e\) its cost. Let \(a_0=2e^{16}W\), \(a_j=2^ja_0\), and \(L_j\) the length of the edges with \(h(c_e)>a_j\). For \(s\ge a_j\), \(\ell_s\le L_j\), and as \(\varphi\) is increasing, \(\int_{a_j}^{a_{j+1}}\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le a_j\varphi(L_j)\). With \(m_j=a_jL_j\) and \(v_j=a_j/W\), \(1/(WL_j)=v_j/m_j\); \(1+v/m\le(1+v)(1+1/m)\) and \((x+y)^{3/4}\le x^{3/4}+y^{3/4}\) give \(a_j\varphi(L_j)\le m_j(2\log_2(1+v_j)+5)^{3/4}+m_j(2\log_2(1+1/m_j))^{3/4}\). First sum: \(m_j=\sum_{e:h(c_e)>a_j}Wa_j\), so \(\sum_jm_j(2\log_2(1+v_j)+5)^{3/4}=\sum_eW\sum_{j:a_j<h(c_e)}a_j(2\log_2(1+a_j/W)+5)^{3/4}\le\sum_e2W^2v_e(2\log_2(1+v_e)+5)^{3/4}\), the \(a_j\) below \(h(c_e)\) summing to less than \(2h(c_e)\), over the edges with \(h(c_e)>a_0\), which have \(v_e>2e^{16}\). For them \(\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\ge\frac{v_e}4(\log(v_e/2))^{1/4}\) (the bound \(\psi_4^*(t)\ge\frac t2(\log t)^{1/4}\) for \(t\ge e^{16}\), recorded with lem:multilevel-chain-bound's proof), so \(W^2v_e\le4\,\mathrm{cost}_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\); and \(2\log_2(1+v)+5\le3.5\log(v/2)\) for \(v\ge2e^{16}\) (\(\log(1+v)\le\log(v/2)+0.70\), \(2.89\log(v/2)+7.02\le3.5\log(v/2)\) once \(\log(v/2)\ge11.5\)); so the sum is at most \(\sum_e8\cdot3.5^{3/4}\mathrm{cost}_e(\log(v_e/2))^{1/2}\le21\cdot2\sqrt{\log N}\), as \(\sum_e\mathrm{cost}_e\le2\) and \(v_e\le8/W^2\le N\) for \(N\) large (a cost-\(2\) edge has \(W^2\frac v4(\log(v/2))^{1/4}\le2\), and \(W^2\ge(\log N)^{3/2}/N\)). Second sum: \(\psi(x)=x(2\log_2(1+1/x))^{3/4}\) is increasing (\(2\ln(1+q)>\frac32\frac q{1+q}\)); the levels with \(m_j>0\) have \(a_j<\max_eh(c_e)\le8/W\), so number \(J\le\log_2(4/(e^{16}W^2))+1\le\log_2N\); \(M=\sum_jm_j\le\sum_e2Wh(c_e)\le2\,\mathrm{TV}(g)\le2T(2)\), \(T(2)=4+4/\psi_4^*(1)\) by lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a), "every grid function g on a mesh delta with 1/delta an integer and discrete cost sum_e delta^2 psi_4^*(|Delta_e g|/(2 delta)) at most M has TV(g) <= T(M)"; the levels with \(m_j<J^{-2}\) give at most \(J\psi(J^{-2})\le J^{-1}(2\log_2(1+J^2))^{3/4}\), the others at most \(M(2\log_2(1+J^2))^{3/4}\), together \(O((\log\log N)^{3/4})\). Below \(a_0\): \(\ell_s\le2/W\), the inner edges of the square, so \(\int_0^{a_0}\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le a_0\varphi(2/W)=4e^{16}(2\log_2\frac32+5)^{3/4}\), a constant. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Cost at most \(2\): \(\sum\mathrm{cost}_e\le2\), \(v_e\le8/W^2\) and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\). \((4,4)\): \(\psi_4^*\) and its lower bound for \(v_e>2e^{16}\). \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) and \(N\) large: \(8/W^2\le N\) and \(J\le\log_2N\). No monotonicity, no product form, no one-height values: \(h\) is any nonnegative grid function and \(B\) any union of cells (scope more general than the theorem's).

Degenerate cases. lem:dyadic-level-sum at \(B=\emptyset\), \(B\) the square, or \(h=0\): \(\ell_s=0\), the integral \(0\). \(h\le a_0\) everywhere: only the part below \(a_0\), a constant.

Nonvacuity. The theorem's witness below, at the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters: its slits put \(\ell_s\approx\frac n2\) for \(s<Wv_0\), one level of mass \(m\approx(\log v_0)^{-1/4}\), and the lemma bounds the integral by \((\log v_0)^{1/2}\) up to constants. Plainest bound. \(\varphi(\ell)\le\ell(2\log_2(1+1/W^2)+5)^{3/4}\), as \(\ell_s\ge W\) when positive, so \(\int\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le(\log N)^{3/4}\int\ell_s\,ds\le(\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\), of order \((\log N)^{3/4}\): the lemma replaces it by \(\sqrt{\log N}\), the step it adds being the levels.

Baseline. The plainest bound above, \((\log N)^{3/4}T(2)\). Composed. lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a) applied alone gives the plainest bound through \(\int\ell_s=\sum_eWh(c_e)\le\mathrm{TV}(g)\); with the cost of each edge used separately, \(W^2v_e\le4\,\mathrm{cost}_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\), it gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\sum\mathrm{cost}_e(\log v_e)^{-1/4}\), the factor \((\log N/\log v)^{1/4}\) above \(\sqrt{\log N}\) on edges of middle increment; lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) applied alone needs its count condition on the large layers; lem:anchored-run-bound applied alone to \(h1_B\), \(h\) monotone, charges its \(V_B=\int\ell_s\,ds\) and anchored term at \((\log N)^{3/4}\) each, the plainest bound's form, and is a discrepancy bound where the lemma is a deterministic inequality on the layers' perimeters.

Theorem (monotone product chains)

Statement. thm:monotone-product-chains. At \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), on the events of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound and of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound at \(\kappa=1\) (probability tending to one), for \(N\) large: every grid function \(g=h1_B\) on the mesh \(W\) with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\), \(B\) a union of cells, and discrete cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\), has \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. Take \(h\) nonincreasing (for \(h\) nondecreasing read the columns right to left and use the right half-planes, on the same events). Step 1, one layer. For \(s\ge0\) let \(H_s=\{h>s\}\), a left half-plane \(\{x<x_s\}\) with \(x_s\) on the grid, and \(A_s=B\cap H_s\); \(\ell_s\) is as in lem:dyadic-level-sum, here the inner edges of \(\partial B\) whose \(B\)-cell lies in \(H_s\), and \(\mathrm{cut}_s\) the length of the vertical edges on \(x=x_s\) with \(B\) on both sides. The inner boundary of \(A_s\) is these two sets (an edge of \(\partial B\) on \(x=x_s\) with its \(B\)-cell on the left is in the first, one with its \(B\)-cell on the right bounds neither), and \(\mathrm{cut}_s\le1\). If \(\ell_s<1\), lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, whose \(\ell_{\rm out}\le\ell_s\) and \(\ell_{\rm line}\le\ell_s+\mathrm{cut}_s\), gives \(|D(1_{A_s})|\le C_0\sqrt N((\log N)^{3/4}\ell_s+\sqrt{\log N}(\mathrm{cut}_s+\ell_s))\). If \(\ell_s\ge1\), the inner perimeter \(P=\ell_s+\mathrm{cut}_s\in[1,2\ell_s]\), and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b), "every union A of its cells with P(A) >= 1 has |D(1_A)| <= C_b sqrt N P(A)((2 log_2 max(1, 2^(l_1)/P(A)) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N))", at \(\delta_0=W=2^{-\ell_1}\), gives, as \(\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P)\le1+1/(W\ell_s)\), \(|D(1_{A_s})|\le2C_b\sqrt N(\varphi(\ell_s)+\ell_s\sqrt{\log N})\). Since \(2\log_2(1+1/(W\ell))+5\ge2\log_2(1/W)\ge\log N\) for \(\ell<1\) and \(N\) large, in both cases \(|D(1_{A_s})|\le C_1\sqrt N(\varphi(\ell_s)+\sqrt{\log N}(\mathrm{cut}_s+\ell_s))\), \(C_1=\max(C_0,2C_b)\). Step 2, the layer cake. \(D(g)=\int_0^\infty D(1_{A_s})\,ds\), and \(\int_0^\infty(\mathrm{cut}_s+\ell_s)\,ds=\sum_wW|\Delta_wh|+\sum_eWh(c_e)\le\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\), the first sum over the vertical edges with \(B\) on both sides, the second over the inner edges of \(\partial B\), where \(|\Delta_eg|=h(c_e)\), disjoint sets of edges. So \(|D(g)|\le C_1\sqrt N(\int_0^\infty\varphi(\ell_s)\,ds+T(2)\sqrt{\log N})\). Step 3: lem:dyadic-level-sum bounds the integral by \(42\sqrt{\log N}+C(\log\log N)^{3/4}\), so \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The event of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound: Step 1 for layers with \(\ell_s<1\), and its strips on both sides for \(h\) of either monotonicity. The event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound at \(\kappa=1\): Step 1 for \(\ell_s\ge1\), at \(\delta_0=W\), whose hypothesis \(\kappa\sqrt{\log N/N}\le\delta_0\le2^{-\ell_1}\) holds. \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\): each layer is \(B\) cut by one vertical line. Cost at most \(2\): \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\) in Step 2 and the lemma. \(N\) large: \(2\log_2(1/W)\ge\log N\) and the lemma. No one-height values and no condition on the number of layers (scope more general than cor:monotone-product-chain-bound (b), which asked values in \(Wy^*\mathbb Z\)).

Degenerate cases. thm:monotone-product-chains at \(B=\emptyset\) or \(h=0\): \(g=0\), \(0\le0\). \(B\) the square: \(\ell_s=0\), only the walls, and the bound is \(C_1T(2)\sqrt{N\log N}\), a factor \(\sqrt{\log N}\) above the one-dimensional bound for a function of \(x\) alone, \(\mathrm{TV}\cdot\sup_t|F_N(t)-Nt|\), of order \(\sqrt N\) times a factor tending to infinity arbitrarily slowly. \(h\equiv a\) constant: every layer with \(s<a\) is \(B\) itself, \(\mathrm{cut}_s=0\), and \(g=a1_B\) is one layer; for \(a\ge2e^{16}W\) lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) also decides it, for \(a<2e^{16}W\) the theorem's bound comes from the lemma's part below \(a_0\), a constant.

Nonvacuity. At the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters, a chain in which both regimes of Step 1 occur. With \(v_0\) the multiple of \(y^*\) nearest \(e^{(\log N)^{0.8}}\): \(h\) falls from \(h(0)=\frac12\), rounded to a multiple of \(Wy^*\), to \(Wv_0\) by walls of increment \(y^*\) over \([0,w_1)\), \(w_1=\frac1{2y^*}\) rounded up to the grid; \(h=Wv_0\) on a plateau \([w_1,w_1+\frac14)\); \(h\) falls to \(0\) by walls of increment \(y^*\) over the next \(v_0W/y^*\), rounded up. \(B\) is the square minus \(n\) vertical slits of one column and height \(\frac14\) in the plateau's columns, inside \([0,1]\times[\frac34,1]\), \(n\) the integer part of \(2(\log v_0)^{-1/4}/(Wv_0)\), at most \(\frac1{8W}\) for \(N\) large, the slits separated by at least one column so that none merge. Cost, from \(\psi_4^*(u)\le u(\log(1+u))^{1/4}\) for \(\psi_4(t)=e^{t^4}-1\) (at the maximizer of \(ut-\psi_4(t)\), \(u=4t^3e^{t^4}\ge e^{t^4}-1\), so \(t\le(\log(1+u))^{1/4}\), the reasoning of the fixed line entry's witness): the upper walls, at most \(\frac{1}{2Wy^*}\) wall columns of \(\frac1W\) edges of cost \(W^2\psi_4^*(y^*/2)\), at most \(\frac14(\log(1+y^*/2))^{1/4}\le0.53\), with \(\log(y^*/2)\le22-\log14\le19.36\) from thm:one-height-chain-reduction's \(y^*=Y/c\), \(Y=e^{22}\), \(c\ge7\); the slits' sides, \(n\cdot\frac1{2W}\) edges of increment \(v_0\), at most \(\frac{nWv_0}4(\log(1+v_0/2))^{1/4}=\frac12(\log(1+v_0/2))^{1/4}(\log v_0)^{-1/4}\le0.6\); the lower walls, at most \(\frac12Wv_0(\log(1+y^*/2))^{1/4}\to0\); the slits' bottom edges, \(n\) edges of increment \(v_0\), at most \(nW^2v_0(\log(1+v_0))^{1/4}\to0\): cost at most \(1.2\) for \(N\) large. The layers: for \(s\ge Wv_0\), \(A_s=H_s\), a half-plane, \(\ell_s=0\) and \(\mathrm{cut}_s=1\), the first case of Step 1 (lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) on these layers alone charges each at \((\log N)^{3/4}\), \(\frac12(\log N)^{3/4}\) over them); for \(s<Wv_0\), \(\ell_s\approx\frac n2\gg1\), the second case (lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound on these layers alone charges \((\log N)^{3/4}Wv_0\frac n2\approx(\log N)^{0.75}(\log v_0)^{-1/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{0.55}\)); and the lemma's level at \(Wv_0\), of mass \(m\approx(\log v_0)^{-1/4}\) with \(1/(WL)\approx v_0(\log v_0)^{1/4}\), contributes \((\log v_0)^{1/2}\). The recorded uniform bounds over the class leave it above the target: lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), at \(K=h(0)/(Wy^*)\) layers, \(\log K\) of order \(\log N\), charges \((\log N)^{3/4}\); its (d) and lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) need \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y/2))^{1/3}\), which fails; cor:monotone-product-chain-bound gives \((\log N)^{1/12}\) above the target; prop:fixed-line-product-chains's proof charges the slits' sides at \((\log N)^{0.55}\). Plainest bound. This \(g\) is one fixed function, decided by its variance, and also by a split of \(g\) at \(Wv_0\) into two chains each covered by one recorded bound; the plainest uniform bounds over the class, cor:monotone-product-chain-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c), leave it above the target, as computed; what the theorem adds is one bound at the target for every monotone product chain, with no split or threshold chosen for the function.

Baseline. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound: every chain of the class within \((\log N)^{1/8}\) of the target, one-height ones within \((\log N)^{1/12}\). Composed. lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound applied to each layer alone gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\int\ell_s\), the proposition's \((\log N)^{3/4}V\); lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) applied to each layer alone charges the cuts at the perimeter factor, \((\log N)^{3/4}\) for a layer of perimeter near \(1\), so the walls at up to \((\log N)^{3/4}T(2)\) (the witness's upper layers); their minimum per layer, summed by the lemma, is the theorem. cor:monotone-product-chain-bound composed over the class, its threshold over the whole range \(T\in[1,1/W]\) and its one-height split at every admissible \(K\), gives at best \((\log N)^{1/12}\) above the target on one-height chains and \((\log N)^{1/8}\) on the others: its split charges each part by one bound for the whole part, and no threshold makes both parts' charges \(\sqrt{\log N}\). lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging applied alone to the class gives its (a), \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\), used in Step 2, and no discrepancy bound, its (b) at \(\delta_0=W\) comparing each \(g\) with its own averages; lem:one-height-rounding applied alone, at its height \(Y=e^{22}\), maps each chain of the class to a one-height chain at an error \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), whose bound is the question, and on the witness, already one-height, it decides nothing; lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) applied alone to the one-height chains of the class needs "log|B| <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y_B/2))^(1/3)" for its large layers, which the witness's layers violate.

Record comparison. From the record's side: prop:fixed-line-product-chains took the layer cake and charged every layer by lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, losing \((\log N/\log v)^{1/4}\) on the boundary edges of middle increment; cor:monotone-product-chain-bound split at one threshold and composed it with lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) or lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d). The theorem supersedes both: for cor:monotone-product-chain-bound, on an intersection of events of probability tending to one (those of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, in place of lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a)'s), every chain of its class is at the target; for prop:fixed-line-product-chains, its \(h_{\rm hi}1_B\), \(h_{\rm hi}=(h-WN^\varepsilon)^+\), is again \(h'1_B\) with \(h'\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone, of cost at most \(2\) since \(|\Delta(h-t)^+|\le|\Delta h|\) and \(\psi_4^*\) is nondecreasing, so the theorem bounds it at \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\) without the factor \(\varepsilon^{-1/4}\); the proposition keeps its explicit constant on its smaller event. The theorem's Step 1 is the minimum of two recorded statements and Step 2 is the proposition's layer cake; the step added is lem:dyadic-level-sum, in which a layer's off-line boundary is at most its level's mass over the level's height, so that the perimeter factor becomes \((\log v_j)^{3/4}\) up to a term in \(\log(1/m_j)\): the class cap of the twelfth review's Attempt, "a curve of that length density can gain only on the roughly \(t\) dyadic scales between \(W\) and \(1/\ell_i\)", carried out where the classes are the dyadic levels of \(h\). lem:multilevel-chain-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (c) and (d) charge a chain's layers by one Jensen inequality over all of them, \((\log K)^{3/4}\), not level by level. The nearest by wording, each neither more general nor a special case of the two statements: lem:anchored-run-bound bounds \(D(h1_B)\) by \((\log N)^{3/4}(2V_B+A_B)\), a discrepancy bound where lem:dyadic-level-sum is a deterministic inequality on the layers' perimeters, and the theorem removes its anchored term and its factor on \(V_B\); lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging gives \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(M)\) and the mesh comparison, used in both proofs and implying neither; lem:one-height-rounding moves a grid function to a one-height chain at an error \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), and neither statement needs or gives it.

New mathematics. lem:dyadic-level-sum: at \((4,4)\), for every \(h\ge0\) and \(B\) with \(h1_B\) of cost at most \(2\), the perimeter factor of the layers' \(\partial B\) parts integrates to \(O(\sqrt{\log N})\). thm:monotone-product-chains: at \((4,4)\), on the events of lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, every grid function \(h1_B\) on the Leighton–Shor mesh with \(h\ge0\) constant on columns and monotone in \(x\), and cost at most \(2\), has discrepancy at most \(C\sqrt{N\log N}\).

Anchored increments meet the target; per-set charges at \(\sqrt{\log N}\) fail for continuous lower layers (cited)

18 October 2026 · Working proofs · Anchored increments. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

Chosen. The queue's head is local-completion-hall; this entry continues pile-class-cap in its extension, by the twelfth review's out-of-turn Decision, because it bears on conj:conjugate-class-discrepancy at \((4,4)\) through cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) and its last entry named this attempt.

Question. The monotone product chains entry reduced every chain \(h1_B\) to a per-layer bound charging each layer's cut at \(\sqrt{\log N}\), and asked first whether a single down-set, the layer of an \(h\) monotone in both coordinates, can cost \((\log N)^{3/4}\). What is the reach of the per-layer route, and what does the lower-layer bound leave?

Target form. The one-height bound of cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b) at \((4,4)\), here for every grid function on the mesh \(W\) of cost at most \(2\) whose nonzero increments are at least a fixed fraction of the larger adjacent value, whole, with no split at a threshold.

Shortest route. Taken for the class the per-layer route can reach: the level sum of lem:dyadic-level-sum used only that each counted edge's increment equals its larger value; rerun with the increment at least \(1/\lambda\) of it (lem:anchored-level-sum), and every layer of such a function is charged by the two recorded per-set bounds alone. For the rest: the source read below states that continuous lower layers carry discrepancy of order \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\) (expected maximum, lower bound by Shor, unread), so the hoped-for per-set charge \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per length fails for them, up to an unproved transfer to cells; increments that are a small fraction of their value then need a joint bound. A direct route for the first such instance, the bunched staircase stack, is named and sketched in the Follow-up (the reviewer's chaining over coarse monotone paths, checked here by hand): a smooth ramp at the stack's own width plus a step texture, each by Bernstein's inequality with a union over monotone paths and recorded bounds; the next entry is to prove it.

Architecture test. Not decided. Of the twelfth review's outcomes, neither (A) nor (B): the functions of thm:anchored-increment-functions with cost at most \(2\), a subclass of the grid functions (A) asks, are at the target; non-anchored chains are open.

Item history. The item's four earlier entries: the pile class charges, "Next attempt: the layer-cake reduction (the reviewer's suggestion, unverified)"; the anchored runs, "Next attempt: the anchored runs. The left-anchored part"; the fixed line entry, "a new joint lemma, not a composition of recorded results, for the residual"; and the monotone product chains, "retrieve the lower-layer discrepancy bound the reviewer recalls".

Owed attempt. The monotone product chains entry named: "retrieve the lower-layer discrepancy bound the reviewer recalls", read it on nested staircases, and if a single down-set can cost \((\log N)^{3/4}\), make the attempt a joint bound over nested staircases compared first with lem:staircase-bundle-chains. Made. Retrieved: Leighton and Shor, Tight bounds for minimax grid matching, with applications to the average case analysis of algorithms, MIT/LCS/TM-298, May 1986 (the technical-memo version of their Combinatorica paper), read from its PDF in the MIT repository, pages 7–8: "the maximum value of \(\Delta(R)\) over all up-right regions is \(O(\sqrt N\log^{3/4}N)\) with very high probability", up-right regions being "also known as lower layers", for \(N\) uniform points in a square of area \(N\), and "The lower bound was later improved to \(O(\sqrt N\log^{3/4}N)\) by Shor [21, 22]" as the text extraction prints it, a lower bound, so \(\Omega\) by context, on the expected maximum (the passage's earlier bounds are stated for "the expected maximum value"); the lower bound's proof, in Shor's papers, was not read. A lower layer of the unit square has boundary length at most \(2\), so the per-set form "every down-set \(D\) has \(|D(1_D)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}\,\ell(\partial D)\) with probability tending to one", which lem:dyadic-level-sum's reduction asks of the layers of an \(h\) monotone in both coordinates with \(B\) the square, contradicts that lower bound for continuous lower layers through one step not written out: the maximum changes by at most \(1\) when one point moves, so McDiarmid's inequality concentrates it within \(O(\sqrt N)\) of its mean. Its transfer to unions of \(W\)-cells was not proved: a crude count of its error, the points of the cells along a staircase, is about \(2NW\approx2\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\), of the order of the bound itself (the reviewer's heuristic, unverified, puts the true error at \(\sqrt N(\log\log N)^{3/4}\)); so the per-set form is refuted only up to that transfer, and lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound, whose Leighton–Shor sets, by the relationship note on lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, "live at that mesh" (\(2^{-\ell_1}\)), is the record's candidate for it, not read for this; its registered statement is a lower bound for the penalized class, \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4-(1/\alpha_1+1/\alpha_2)/2}\), not one for single sets. The joint bound: the theorem below covers nested staircases whose increments are anchored, lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) covers those of bounded multiplicity, and lem:staircase-bundle-chains covers piled monotone paths with spreading room (B2)–(B4); the remaining instance, a stack of staircases with steps of middle multiplicity, is the next attempt.

General statement. lem:anchored-level-sum, for every grid function \(g\ge0\) of cost at most \(2\) and every \(\lambda\ge1\); thm:anchored-increment-functions, for every grid function of cost at most \(2\) at \((4,4)\) whose nonzero increments between cells of one strict sign are at least \(1/\lambda\) of the larger absolute value, every \(\lambda\ge1\).

Lemma (anchored level sum)

Statement. lem:anchored-level-sum. At \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), for \(N\) large, deterministically: for every grid function \(g\ge0\) on the mesh \(W\) with \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\) and every \(\lambda\ge1\), call an inner edge \(e\) between cells \(c,c'\) \(\lambda\)-anchored if \(J_e=|\Delta_eg|>0\) and \(w_e=\max(g(c),g(c'))\le\lambda J_e\); let \(\ell_s\) be the length of the \(\lambda\)-anchored edges of \(\partial\{g>s\}\) and \(\varphi(\ell)=\ell\,(2\log_2(1+1/(W\ell))+5)^{3/4}\), \(\varphi(0)=0\). Then \(\int_0^\infty\varphi(\ell_s)\,ds\le16\lambda(3.5+\tfrac18\log_2\lambda)^{3/4}\sqrt{\log N}+C\lambda(\log\log N)^{3/4}\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. With \(u_e=\min(g(c),g(c'))\), \(e\in\partial\{g>s\}\) exactly when \(u_e\le s<w_e\); \(\varphi\) is increasing (lem:dyadic-level-sum's proof). Let \(a_0=2\lambda e^{16}W\), \(a_j=2^ja_0\), \(L_j\) the length of the \(\lambda\)-anchored edges with \(w_e>a_j\), \(m_j=a_jL_j\), \(v_j=a_j/W\). For \(s\ge a_j\) every counted edge has \(w_e>s\ge a_j\), so \(\ell_s\le L_j\) and \(\int_{a_j}^{a_{j+1}}\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le a_j\varphi(L_j)\le m_j(2\log_2(1+v_j)+5)^{3/4}+m_j(2\log_2(1+1/m_j))^{3/4}\), by \(1+v/m\le(1+v)(1+1/m)\) and \((x+y)^{3/4}\le x^{3/4}+y^{3/4}\). First sum: \(m_j=\sum_{e:w_e>a_j}Wa_j\) over the \(\lambda\)-anchored edges, so \(\sum_jm_j(2\log_2(1+v_j)+5)^{3/4}\le\sum_e2Ww_e(2\log_2(1+w_e/W)+5)^{3/4}\), the \(a_j\) below \(w_e\) summing to less than \(2w_e\), over the \(\lambda\)-anchored edges with \(w_e>a_0\). For them \(v_e=J_e/W\ge w_e/(\lambda W)>2e^{16}\), so \(\psi_4^*(v_e/2)\ge\frac{v_e}4(\log(v_e/2))^{1/4}\) (recorded with lem:multilevel-chain-bound's proof) gives \(Ww_e\le\lambda W^2v_e\le4\lambda\,\mathrm{cost}_e(\log(v_e/2))^{-1/4}\); and \(2\log_2(1+w_e/W)+5\le2\log_2\lambda+2\log_2(1+v_e)+5\le2\log_2\lambda+3.5\log(v_e/2)\le(3.5+\frac18\log_2\lambda)\log(v_e/2)\), by \(1+\lambda v\le\lambda(1+v)\), the inequality \(2\log_2(1+v)+5\le3.5\log(v/2)\) for \(v\ge2e^{16}\) of lem:dyadic-level-sum's proof, and \(\log(v_e/2)\ge16\). So the first sum is at most \(8\lambda(3.5+\frac18\log_2\lambda)^{3/4}\sum_e\mathrm{cost}_e(\log(v_e/2))^{1/2}\le16\lambda(3.5+\frac18\log_2\lambda)^{3/4}\sqrt{\log N}\), as \(\sum\mathrm{cost}_e\le2\) and \(v_e\le8/W^2\le N\) (lem:dyadic-level-sum's proof). Second sum: \(J_e\le8W^{-1}\), so the levels with \(m_j>0\) have \(a_j<\max w_e\le8\lambda/W\), \(2^j<4/(e^{16}W^2)\), and number \(J\le\log_2N\); \(M=\sum_jm_j\le\sum_e2Ww_e\le2\lambda\sum_eWJ_e\le2\lambda\,\mathrm{TV}(g)\le2\lambda T(2)\) by lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a); as in lem:dyadic-level-sum's proof the levels with \(m_j<J^{-2}\) give at most \(J^{-1}(2\log_2(1+J^2))^{3/4}\) and the others at most \(M(2\log_2(1+J^2))^{3/4}\). Below \(a_0\): \(\ell_s\le2/W\), so \(\int_0^{a_0}\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le a_0\varphi(2/W)=4\lambda e^{16}(2\log_2\frac32+5)^{3/4}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Cost at most \(2\): \(\sum\mathrm{cost}_e\le2\), \(v_e\le8/W^2\), \(J_e\le8/W\) and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\). \((4,4)\): \(\psi_4^*\) and its lower bound at \(v_e/2\ge e^{16}\). \(\lambda\ge1\): \(Ww_e\le\lambda W^2v_e\), \(v_e>2e^{16}\) above \(a_0\), \(1+\lambda v\le\lambda(1+v)\) and \(M\le2\lambda\,\mathrm{TV}\); \(\lambda\) has its whole range \([1,\infty)\), the bound growing linearly. \(N\) large: \(8/W^2\le N\), \(J\le\log_2N\). \(g\ge0\): \(\{g>s\}\) for \(s\ge0\) only. No nesting, product or one-height form, and edges not anchored are allowed: they are left out of \(\ell_s\). At \(\lambda=1\), with \(g=h1_B\), every edge counted by lem:dyadic-level-sum is counted here (its \(B\)-cell value is the larger value and the increment), so this lemma implies that one, its constant \(16\cdot3.5^{3/4}\le41\) below \(42\) (scope more general).

Refinement checked. lem:dyadic-level-sum: at \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), \(N\) large, for every \(h\ge0\) and union of cells \(B\) with \(h1_B\) of cost at most \(2\), \(\ell_s\) the length of the inner edges of \(\partial B\) whose \(B\)-cell \(c\) has \(h(c)>s\), \(\int_0^\infty\varphi(\ell_s)ds\le42\sqrt{\log N}+C(\log\log N)^{3/4}\). lem:anchored-level-sum at \(\lambda=1\), applied to \(g=h1_B\) (cost at most \(2\), the same hypothesis): an edge of \(\partial B\) with \(h(c)>s\) has larger value \(h(c)\) equal to its increment, so it is \(1\)-anchored and lies in \(\partial\{g>s\}\); hence the earlier \(\ell_s\) is at most the new one, \(\varphi\) is increasing, and the bound \(16\cdot3.5^{3/4}\sqrt{\log N}+C\lambda(\log\log N)^{3/4}\), with \(16\cdot3.5^{3/4}\approx40.9\le42\), implies the earlier one (same mesh, same pair, same \(N\) large).

Theorem (anchored increments)

Statement. thm:anchored-increment-functions. At \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), on the events of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at the mesh \(W\) and of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound at \(\kappa=1\) (probability tending to one), for \(N\) large: for every \(\lambda\ge1\) and every grid function \(g\) on the mesh \(W\) with discrete cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\le2\) such that every inner edge \(e\) whose cells \(c,c'\) carry values of one strict sign has \(\Delta_eg=0\) or \(\max(|g(c)|,|g(c')|)\le\lambda|\Delta_eg|\): \(|D(g)|\le C\lambda(1+\log\lambda)^{3/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. Step 0, signs. \(g=g^+-g^-\) and \(D(g)=D(g^+)-D(g^-)\); \(|\Delta_eg^\pm|\le|\Delta_eg|\) and \(\psi_4^*\) is nondecreasing, so each part costs at most \(2\). Every edge with \(\Delta_eg^+\ne0\) is \(\lambda\)-anchored for \(g^+\): if both values of \(g\) are positive, \(g^+=g\) there and the hypothesis applies; otherwise one value of \(g^+\) is \(0\) and its larger value equals its increment. The same holds for \(g^-\). So it suffices to take \(g\ge0\) with every edge of nonzero increment \(\lambda\)-anchored. Step 1, one layer. For \(s\ge0\), \(A_s=\{g>s\}\) is a union of cells whose inner boundary consists of edges of nonzero increment, so its inner perimeter \(P_s\) is the \(\ell_s\) of lem:anchored-level-sum. If \(P_s=0\), \(A_s\) is empty or the square and \(D(1_{A_s})=0\). If \(0<P_s<1\), lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) at \(\delta_0=W\) gives \(|D(1_{A_s})|\le L_f\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}P_s\le L_f\sqrt N\varphi(P_s)\), since \(2\log_2(1+1/(WP_s))+5\ge2\log_2(1/W)\ge\log N\) for \(N\) large. If \(P_s\ge1\), lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b), "every union A of its cells with P(A) >= 1 has |D(1_A)| <= C_b sqrt N P(A)((2 log_2 max(1, 2^(l_1)/P(A)) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N))", at \(\delta_0=W\), with \(\max(1,2^{\ell_1}/P_s)\le1+1/(WP_s)\), gives \(|D(1_{A_s})|\le C_b\sqrt N(\varphi(P_s)+P_s\sqrt{\log N})\). Step 2, the layer cake. \(D(g)=\int_0^\infty D(1_{A_s})ds\) and \(\int_0^\infty P_sds=\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\), so \(|D(g)|\le C_1\sqrt N(\int_0^\infty\varphi(\ell_s)ds+T(2)\sqrt{\log N})\), \(C_1=\max(L_f,C_b)\), and lem:anchored-level-sum bounds the integral; for \(N\) large \((\log\log N)^{3/4}\le\sqrt{\log N}\) and \(16(3.5+\frac18\log_2\lambda)^{3/4}\le C(1+\log\lambda)^{3/4}\). \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. The event of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at \(W\) (its \(\kappa=1\), \(\sqrt{\log N/N}\le W\)): Step 1 for \(P_s<1\). The event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound at \(\kappa=1\): Step 1 for \(P_s\ge1\), at the dyadic \(\delta_0=W\). The anchoring with \(\lambda\): Step 0 and lem:anchored-level-sum, every boundary edge of every layer being counted there; it is asked only of edges between cells of one strict sign, Step 0 anchoring the others at \(\lambda=1\). Cost at most \(2\): the lemma and \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\). \(N\) large: \(2\log_2(1/W)\ge\log N\) and the lemma. No one-height values, nesting form or bound on the number of distinct values.

Degenerate cases. lem:anchored-level-sum at \(g=0\), \(g\) constant, or \(g\) with no \(\lambda\)-anchored edge (a function whose every increment is below \(1/\lambda\) of its larger value): \(\ell_s=0\), the integral \(0\), which says nothing of such a \(g\); at \(g\le a_0\) everywhere, only the part below \(a_0\), a constant times \(\lambda\). thm:anchored-increment-functions at \(g=0\), or \(g\) constant on the square: no edge of nonzero increment, \(D(g)=0\). \(g=a1_A\), one set: anchored at \(\lambda=1\); the theorem contains lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d)'s case of one layer, which that lemma covers at levels \(a/W\ge2e^{16}\) only. \(\lambda=1\) in general: every nonzero increment has a zero on one side, so \(g^\pm=h1_B\) with \(B\) the support and \(h=g^\pm\), and the theorem is lem:dyadic-level-sum composed with the two per-set bounds, as in thm:monotone-product-chains with no cuts. \(\lambda\to\infty\): the hypothesis becomes vacuous and the bound grows linearly, consistent with the class becoming every function.

Nonvacuity. At the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters, \(\lambda=2\): pyramids. For \(u\in[2e^{16},4e^{16}]\) and \(K=\lceil(\log N)^{0.9}\rceil\), the pyramid \(P(u)\) is \(Wu\sum_{k=1}^K2^{k-1}1_{S_k}\), \(S_k\) the square of \(2(K-k)+1\) cells on a side around one cell; ring \(k\) has value \((2^k-1)Wu\), an edge of \(\partial S_k\) has increment \(2^{k-1}Wu\) and larger value \((2^k-1)Wu\le2\cdot2^{k-1}Wu\), so \(\lambda=2\), and \(\partial S_1\) borders zero. Cost, from \(\psi_4^*(t)\le t(\log(1+t))^{1/4}\) and \(\sum_{i\ge0}(2i+1)2^{-i}=6\): \(\mathrm{cost}(P(u))\le\sum_k4(2(K-k)+1)W^2\,2^{k-2}u(\log(1+2^{k-2}u))^{1/4}\le6\cdot2^KW^2u(\log(1+2^Ku))^{1/4}\). The witness \(g\) is \(n=\lfloor(24e^{16}2^KW^2(\log(1+2^{K+2}e^{16}))^{1/4})^{-1}\rfloor\) pyramids in disjoint blocks of side \((2K+1)W\) separated by zero cells, with distinct \(u_p=2e^{16}(1+p/n)\), \(p<n\): \(n\ge1\) and \(n(2K+1)^2\le W^{-2}/4\) for \(N\) large, as \(\log(2^KW^2)\approx0.69(\log N)^{0.9}-\log N\to-\infty\); cost at most \(1\). The four top edges of each pyramid alone cost at least \(4W^2\psi_4^*(2^{K-2}u)\ge2^{K-1}W^2u(\log(2^{K-2}u))^{1/4}\), together at least \(\frac1{50}\) for \(N\) large, on increments with \(\log v_e\ge0.69(\log N)^{0.9}\). Steps exercised: Step 0 trivially (\(g\ge0\); its mixed-sign case is not exercised, as a negated copy of a pyramid beside \(g\) would do); the lemma's anchoring at \(\lambda=2\) on the ring edges, which have both sides positive; Step 1's case \(P_s\ge1\) for most \(s\) (the layers are unions over many pyramids) and its case \(P_s<1\) near the maximum, where few pyramids remain. The recorded bounds applied to \(g\) itself leave it above the target: lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a)'s term is at least \(6\cdot\frac1{50}(0.69(\log N)^{0.9})^{1/4}\to\infty\); lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (b) charges \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}(g)\), with \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\ge\frac16(\log(2^Ku_{\max}))^{-1/4}\) (each pyramid's top edges have \(\mathrm{TV}\) at least \(\frac13\) of its cost bound over \((\log(1+2^Ku))^{1/4}\), and \(n\) times the cost bound is at least \(\frac12\)), of order \((\log N)^{0.525}\) over \(\sqrt N\); its (c) has smallest increment \(y=u\le4e^{16}\) and charges \((\log N)^{3/4}(\log(y/2))^{-1/4}\); lem:multilevel-chain-bound (c) needs distinct values \(2e^{16}W\) apart, while the \(u_p\) are \(2e^{16}/n\) apart; lem:one-height-rounding at a height \(Y\) costs \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), so \(Y\) bounded, and gives \(K'\ge2^K\cdot2e^{16}/Y\) layers with \(\log K'\ge0.69(\log N)^{0.9}>(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(Y/2))^{1/3}\), outside lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), and its (c) charges \(T(2\log_2(K'Y^2)+5)^{3/4}\), of order \((\log N)^{0.675}\); lem:staircase-bundle-chains and lem:separated-bundle-chains ask chain heights in \([2e^{16},V]\), while the gaps between distinct values are below \(2e^{16}W\); thm:monotone-product-chains asks \(h\) constant on columns, while a pyramid's central column carries \(K\) values; lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound bounds one set inside a half-plane, and a layer of the witness, many squares spread over the square, lies in no half-plane with its boundary on the line; lem:dyadic-level-sum with \(B\) the support counts only the \(\partial S_1\) edges, leaving the ring edges to the plainest per-layer charge \((\log N)^{3/4}\). Plainest bound. This \(g\) is one fixed function, decided by its variance; and, as the reviewer found, the recorded statements composed with linearity also decide it, in two ways. First, \(g=g'+2e^{16}\int_0^1G_tdt\), \(G_t\) the pyramids with \(p>tn\) at \(u=2e^{16}\): each part is a nested chain with heights \(2^{k-1}2e^{16}\ge2e^{16}\), \(K\) layers and cost at most \(1\), within lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) (\(\log K\le0.9\log\log N\)), whose bound holds for every chain on one event, so the integral over \(t\) is at most \(2C\sqrt{N\log N}\). Second, the split of \(g\) into its \(K\) step functions \(\sum_pWu_p2^{k-1}1_{S_k}\), each anchored at \(\lambda=1\): with \(D(\alpha g_k)=\alpha D(g_k)\) and \(\alpha\) raising the cost to \(2\), the \(\lambda=1\) composition gives each piece \(c_k(\log(1/c_k)/\log v_k)^{1/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\) up to constants, and the costs \(c_k\) fall geometrically below the top, so the sum is bounded. The plainest uniform bound over the class, lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) (the class has more than polynomially many members, so no union over them applies), leaves the witness above the target by its unbounded loss term computed above. So the witness checks the hypotheses and exercises the step at \(\lambda=2\), and no witness here escapes every recorded regrouping; what the theorem adds is one bound at the target for every anchored function with no regrouping chosen for the function. Whether every anchored function admits such a regrouping, which would make the theorem a corollary of the \(\lambda=1\) composition, was not checked.

Baseline. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a): every function of the class within \(\sum_{v_e\ge2e^{16}}w_e(\log v_e)^{1/4}\) of the target, unbounded on the witness; at \(\lambda=1\) the composition of lem:dyadic-level-sum with the per-set bounds, at the target. Composed. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) applied to the whole function, or to the parts \(g^\pm\) with the triangle inequality, gives its loss term \(\sum w_e(\log v_e)^{1/4}\), at most \(2(\log N)^{1/4}\) and unbounded on the witness; lem:dyadic-level-sum applied with \(B\) the support of \(g^\pm\) and \(h=g^\pm\) counts only the edges bordering zero, so it gives the theorem at \(\lambda=1\) and, for \(\lambda>1\), leaves every edge between two positive cells to the per-layer factor \((\log N)^{3/4}\); applied to a split of \(g\) into pieces anchored at \(\lambda=1\), with each piece scaled to cost \(2\) and linearity, it decides splits whose piece costs sum with bounded logarithmic weights, as on the witness (Plainest bound). lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (a) applied alone to each layer gives \((\log N)^{3/4}\mathrm{TV}\); lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (b) alone needs \(P\ge1\); their minimum per layer is Step 1, and summing it over the layers is the lemma; lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a) alone gives \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\) and no discrepancy bound; lem:one-height-rounding alone, at its height \(Y\), maps the class to one-height chains at an error \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), whose bound needs \(\log K\) small (above); lem:multilevel-chain-bound (b) applied alone to \(g\) as one chain needs \(\log|B|\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y_B/2))^{1/3}\) and heights at least \(2e^{16}\), which the chain of distinct values of the witness violates, while applied to the parts of a layer cake in \(u\) it decides the witness (Plainest bound).

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:dyadic-level-sum counted the boundary edges of \(B\), whose increment is their larger value; lem:anchored-level-sum counts every edge whose increment is at least \(1/\lambda\) of its larger value and implies the earlier lemma at \(\lambda=1\) (registered as a refinement). The step it adds is \(Ww_e\le\lambda W^2v_e\) and \(v_e>2e^{16}\) above \(a_0=2\lambda e^{16}W\), the rest of its proof being lem:dyadic-level-sum's. thm:anchored-increment-functions is Steps 1–2 of thm:monotone-product-chains with no cuts, applied to every layer of every anchored function; at \(\lambda=1\) it is a composition of recorded results. Nearest by wording, each neither more general nor a special case: thm:monotone-product-chains and prop:fixed-line-product-chains bound \(h1_B\) with \(h\) constant on columns, whose walls are not anchored and are charged by lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound, while anchored functions need no column form; cor:monotone-product-chain-bound is superseded by thm:monotone-product-chains and not by this theorem; lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound bounds one set in a half-plane, used by neither proof; lem:multilevel-chain-bound bounds functions whose distinct values are \(2e^{16}\delta_0\) apart with \(\log K\) small, by one Jensen inequality over the layers, while anchored functions may have any number of values at any gaps, and its values need not be anchored; lem:one-height-rounding moves a function to one height at an error \(C_0Y\sqrt{N\log N}\), used by neither; lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging (a) is used for \(\mathrm{TV}(g)\le T(2)\); lem:staircase-bundle-chains bounds piled monotone paths with room (B2)–(B4) and heights at least \(2e^{16}\), whose piles need not be anchored, while anchored functions need no room.

New mathematics. lem:anchored-level-sum: at \((4,4)\), for every \(g\ge0\) of cost at most \(2\) and \(\lambda\ge1\), the perimeter factor of the layers' \(\lambda\)-anchored edges integrates to \(O(\lambda(1+\log\lambda)^{3/4}\sqrt{\log N})\). thm:anchored-increment-functions: at \((4,4)\), on the events of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor and lem:cut-cell-variance-bound, every grid function on the Leighton–Shor mesh of cost at most \(2\) whose nonzero increments between cells of one strict sign are at least \(1/\lambda\) of the larger absolute value has discrepancy at most \(C\lambda(1+\log\lambda)^{3/4}\sqrt{N\log N}\); no instance beyond the record's regroupings (a layer cake in a parameter, pieces scaled by linearity) is known yet. From the source read, not a claim of this entry: the expected maximal discrepancy of continuous lower layers of the unit square is of order \(\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\) (Leighton–Shor, citing Shor's lower bound, unread), so the per-set charge \(\sqrt{\log N}\) per length fails for them, up to McDiarmid's concentration step and an unproved transfer to unions of cells.

Goal progress. Unchanged: cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)'s hypothesis asks every one-height nested chain, and the theorem proves it for those whose nonzero increments, multiples \(m_eWy^*\) of the height, satisfy \(m_e\ge k_e/\lambda\), \(k_e\) the index of the top layer through \(e\). Bearing. At \((4,4)\), every one-height chain whose every edge has its lower adjacent value at most \((1-1/\lambda)\) times the larger, \(m_e\ge k_e/\lambda\), any number of layers, is at the target (the curve's parameters, the pair \((4,4)\)); so are chains with \(h\) monotone in both coordinates whose staircase steps are such fractions, and with lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) those whose steps have bounded multiplicity. Not covered. Chains with increments that are a small fraction of their value and of large multiplicity, \(k_e/m_e\to\infty\) with \(m_e\to\infty\): first a stack of nested staircases whose steps, piles of multiplicity \(m\) with \(\log m=(\log N)^\theta\), \(0<\theta<1\), bunch closer than \(m\) cells, where lem:staircase-bundle-chains' strips do not fit (the evenly spaced stack is that lemma's); and mixtures of anchored and non-anchored increments on one edge set.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

Translate staircase stacks one cell apart with long boundaries meet the target, uniformly over the staircase

18 October 2026 · Working proofs · Monotone path ramps. Produced by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, reasoning effort set by the session).

The anchored increments entry left, as the first instance no recorded bound reaches, the bunched stack: nested staircases along translates of one monotone path, each step a pile of multiplicity \(m\), consecutive steps too close for lem:staircase-bundle-chains' strips. Is it at the target, and by which mechanism?

The ramp is bounded here by a chaining over coarse monotone approximations (lem:monotone-path-ramps), which the reviewer found to be a special case of the recorded lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split applied at the ramp's own mesh; that one-line route is the shortest, and the chaining is kept as a second proof. The item's five earlier entries: the pile class charges, "Next attempt: the layer-cake reduction (the reviewer's suggestion, unverified)"; the anchored runs, "Next attempt: the anchored runs."; the fixed line entry, "a new joint lemma, not a composition of recorded results, for the residual"; the monotone product chains, "retrieve the lower-layer discrepancy bound the reviewer recalls"; and the anchored increments, "the bunched stack, \(K\) nested staircases with disjoint boundaries along translates of one monotone path".

Owed attempt. The anchored increments entry named the bunched stack "written as a lemma for every monotone \(\Gamma\): \(g=\bar R+H\)", the ramp by the chaining over coarse monotone paths, \(\bar R-R\) by Bernstein with a union over paths, \(H\) by cor:fine-mesh-function-tube. Made: lem:monotone-path-ramps and cor:translate-staircase-stacks below, the coarsest level, unverified there, now proved. Before the method, the plainest composition was tried on the stack: the two-scale split \(g=E_wg+(g-E_wg)\) at the ramp width \(w\) charges the fine part by cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at its mesh \(w\), whose \(\Phi=(2\log_2(w/W)+5)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\) is of order \((\log K)^{3/4}\), about \((\log N)^{3/4}\) since \(\log K\approx\frac12\log N\), times \(a\), above the target; and the coarse part's increments over \(w\) are \(a/w=my^*\), on which lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a) loses \((\log(my^*))^{1/4}\), while lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b), (c) puts that coarse part at the target, \(a(\log(2/w))^{3/4}\approx(\log v)^{1/2}\) (the reviewer); the split fails on the fine part only when \(\log K>(\log N)^{2/3}(\log v)^{1/3}\). That one composition failing did not show a chaining was needed: lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, the record's tool for functions Lipschitz on cells, decides the ramp at once (Record comparison), and was not tried before the chaining was written.

General statement. lem:monotone-path-ramps, for every lattice profile of a down-set, every ramp width \(w\in W\mathbb Z\cap[W,2]\) and every height \(a>0\); cor:translate-staircase-stacks, for every one-height chain at \((4,4)\) of cost at most \(2\) whose layers are \(K\) diagonal translates of one lattice down-set in piles of one multiplicity \(m\), every \(K\) and \(m\).

Lemma (monotone path ramps)

Setting. Write \(t=x-y\in[-1,1]\) and \(s=x+y\). A down-set \(D\) of the square (closed under decreasing either coordinate) meets each line \(\{t=\mathrm{const}\}\) in \(\{s<\varphi_D(t)\}\), and \(\varphi_D\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz: along the boundary \(dx\ge0\ge dy\), so \(|ds|\le|dx|+|dy|=dt\), and the clipping by the square's bounds \(|t|\le s\le2-|t|\), themselves \(1\)-Lipschitz, keeps the constant. For a union of cells of the mesh \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), \(\varphi_D\) is piecewise linear with slopes \(\pm1\) and breakpoints and values in \(W\mathbb Z\): call such a function a lattice profile. For a lattice profile \(\varphi\), \(w>0\) and \(a>0\), the ramp is \(R(z)=a\rho((s-\varphi(t))/w)\), \(\rho(u)=\min(1,\max(0,-u))\): \(a\) below \(\varphi-w\), \(0\) above \(\varphi\), linear between.

Statement. lem:monotone-path-ramps. For \(X_1,\dots,X_N\) i.i.d. uniform on \([0,1]^2\) and \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\) the Leighton–Shor mesh, on the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split (probability tending to one), for every \(1\)-Lipschitz profile \(\varphi\) of a down-set, every \(w\in[2^{-\ell_1},2]\) and every \(a>0\), the ramp \(R\) has \(|\sum_iR(X_i)-N\int R|\le Ca\sqrt N((\log_2(4/w))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\), \(C\) universal. (The second proof below, by chaining, gives it for lattice profiles and \(w\in W\mathbb Z\) with an extra \(C(a/w+a)\log N\).)

Proof from the record. lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, "for every j with 1 <= j <= l_1 ... and every bounded G Lipschitz on each open cell of mesh 2^(-j): |sum_i G(X_i) - N int G| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(E_j G) + L sqrt(N log N) Lambda_j(G) ... for Lipschitz G, V_j(E_j G) <= 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|)", at \(G=R\) and \(j=j_0\) (\(2^{-j_0}\in[w,2w)\), \(j_0=1\) for \(w>\frac12\)): \(V_{j_0}(E_{j_0}R)\le8\int(|\partial_1R|+|\partial_2R|)\le Ca\); \(R\) is \(2\sqrt2a/w\)-Lipschitz (\(|\nabla(s-\varphi(t))|\le2\sqrt2\)) and constant off the strip \(\{\varphi-w<s<\varphi\}\), which meets at most \(C/w\) cells of side \(2^{-j_0}\le2w\), each of area at most \(4w^2\), so \(\Lambda_{j_0}(R)\le Ca\). Hence \(|\sum_iR(X_i)-N\int R|\le Ca\sqrt N((\log_2(2/w))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\), for every \(1\)-Lipschitz profile (lattice values not needed) and every \(w\in[2^{-\ell_1},2]\), without the term \(C(a/w+a)\log N\). The statement above is therefore a special case of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split; lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b), a newer version of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, gives the same with a uniform partition. \(\square\)

Second proof (chaining). Both sides are linear in \(a\); take \(a=1\). Let \(j_0\) be the dyadic level with \(2^{-j_0}\in[w,2w)\), so \(j_0\le\ell_1\) as \(w\ge W\). Step 1, approximations. For \(j_0\le j\le\ell_1\) let \(\varphi_j\) be the function linear between the nodes \(t_k=k2^{-j}\) with \(\varphi_j(t_k)=2^{-j}\lfloor2^j\varphi(t_k)\rfloor\). Since \(\varphi\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz, \(|\varphi_j-\varphi|\le2\cdot2^{-j}\) (interpolation and rounding), consecutive node values differ by at most \(2\cdot2^{-j}\), so \(\varphi_j\) is fixed by its first value and \(2^{j+1}\) increments in \(\{-2,\dots,2\}2^{-j}\): at most \(5^{2^{j+2}}\) choices for \(N\) large; and \(\varphi_{\ell_1}=\varphi\), the breakpoints and values of \(\varphi\) lying on \(W\mathbb Z\). Let \(R_j\) be the ramp of \(\varphi_j\), so \(R=R_{\ell_1}\) and \(R=R_{j_0}+\sum_{j_0\le j<\ell_1}(R_{j+1}-R_j)\). Step 2, the differences. \(\rho\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz, so \(f=R_{j+1}-R_j\) has \(|f|\le b_j=4\cdot2^{-j}/w\), and \(f\ne0\) only where \(s\) lies within \(w+3\cdot2^{-j}<7w\) below \(\max(\varphi_j,\varphi_{j+1})\) and within \(3\cdot2^{-j}\) above, a region of area at most \(9w\) (in the coordinates \((t,s)\) it has \(s\)-width at most \(9w\) over \(t\in[-1,1]\), and \(dx\,dy=\frac12dt\,ds\)). Bernstein's inequality for the i.i.d. \(f(X_i)\), variance at most \(9wb_j^2\): \(|\sum_if(X_i)-N\int f|\le\sqrt{18Nwb_j^2u}+b_ju\) with probability at least \(1-2e^{-u}\). A union over the at most \(5^{2^{j+3}}\) pairs \((\varphi_j,\varphi_{j+1})\) (in fact \(\varphi_j\) is fixed by \(\varphi_{j+1}\), as \(\lfloor2^j\varphi\rfloor=\lfloor\lfloor2^{j+1}\varphi\rfloor/2\rfloor\)), the at most \(2/W\) values of \(w\) and the levels, at \(u_j=2^{j+5}+3\log N\), fails with probability at most \(2(\log N)(2/W)N^{-3}\to0\); the families are fixed before the points are drawn. On this event the level \(j\) contributes at most \(\sqrt{18Nw}\cdot\frac{4\cdot2^{-j}}w(\sqrt{2^{j+5}}+\sqrt{3\log N})+\frac{4\cdot2^{-j}}w(2^{j+5}+3\log N)\), that is \(C\sqrt N(\sqrt{2^{-j}/w}+2^{-j}\sqrt{\log N/w})+C/w+C2^{-j}\log N/w\). Summed over \(j\ge j_0\), \(2^{-j}\le2^{-j_0}<2w\): \(\sum\sqrt{2^{-j}/w}\le\sqrt2/(1-2^{-1/2})\), \(\sum2^{-j}\sqrt{\log N/w}\le4\sqrt{w\log N}\le4\sqrt{2\log N}\), \(\sum C/w\le C(\ell_1-j_0)/w\le C\log N/w\) and \(\sum2^{-j}\log N/w\le4\log N\): in all \(C\sqrt{N\log N}+C(1/w+1)\log N\). Step 3, the coarsest level. Let \(E\) be the average over the dyadic cells of side \(2^{-j_0}\). (i) \(ER_{j_0}\) is constant on those cells, so lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b), "every H constant on the cells has |sum_i H(X_i) - N int H| <= L sqrt N (j^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) V_j(H)", at \(j=j_0\) (\(1\le j_0\le\ell_1\) when \(w\le\frac12\); for \(w>\frac12\) take \(j_0=1\)), with its (c), "For Lipschitz G its cell averages have V_j at most 8 int(|d_1 G| + |d_2 G|)", gives \(L\sqrt N(j_0^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\cdot8\int(|\partial_1R_{j_0}|+|\partial_2R_{j_0}|)\); and \(\int(|\partial_1R|+|\partial_2R|)\le\sqrt2\int|\nabla R|\le\sqrt2\cdot\) the length of the graph of \(\varphi_{j_0}\), at most \(4\) (coarea over the levels of \(R\), each a translate of that graph clipped to the square, of length at most \(2\sqrt5\), \(\varphi_{j_0}\) having slopes up to \(2\)), so (i) is at most \(C\sqrt N((\log_2(2/w))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\). (ii) \(F=R_{j_0}-ER_{j_0}\) has mean zero on every cell, \(|F|\le1\), and vanishes on the cells inside \(\{R_{j_0}=0\}\) or \(\{R_{j_0}=1\}\); the others meet the strip \(\{\varphi_{j_0}-w\le s\le\varphi_{j_0}\}\), at most \(C/w\) of them (the strip has width at most \(w\le2^{-j_0}\) and length at most \(2\sqrt2\)). Given the cell counts \(n_Q\), the points of each cell are i.i.d. uniform in it, so \(\sum_iF(X_i)\) is a sum of independent terms of mean zero, bounded by \(1\), of total variance at most \(\sum_Qn_Q\le(C/w)\cdot2N4^{-j_0}\le CNw\) on the event, of probability tending to one by Chernoff's bound, that every dyadic cell of side at least \(W\) has at most twice its mean count (\(NW^2\ge(\log N)^{3/2}\)); and \(N\int F=0\). Bernstein's inequality given the counts, with a union over the at most \(5^{2^{j_0+2}}\le e^{C/w}\) profiles \(\varphi_{j_0}\) and the values of \(w\), at \(u=C/w+3\log N\): \(|\sum_iF(X_i)|\le\sqrt{2CNw(C/w+3\log N)}+C/w+3\log N\le C\sqrt{N\log N}+C(1/w+\log N)\). Adding Steps 2 and 3 and restoring \(a\) gives the bound. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. Proof from the record: the event of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split; \(\varphi\) \(1\)-Lipschitz, for \(|\nabla(s-\varphi(t))|\le2\) and the strip's cell count; \(w\ge2^{-\ell_1}\), for \(j_0\le\ell_1\); no lattice values and no \(w\in W\mathbb Z\) (the statement holds in this more general form). Second proof, which alone uses lattice values and \(w\in W\mathbb Z\): \(X_i\) i.i.d. uniform: Bernstein's inequality in Step 2 (independence of the \(X_i\)) and, given the cell counts, in Step 3 (ii) (independence within cells), Chernoff's bound for the counts, and the event of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy. \(\varphi\) a lattice profile: \(\varphi_{\ell_1}=\varphi\), ending the chain at the mesh \(W\), and \(1\)-Lipschitz for the counts and the area bounds; a \(1\)-Lipschitz \(\varphi\) without lattice values gives the same bound with a final level at the mesh \(W\) added, an error at most \(2W/w\cdot\) on an area \(O(w)\), not used here. \(w\in W\mathbb Z\cap[W,2]\): \(j_0\le\ell_1\) and the union over at most \(2/W\) values; \(w\) has this whole range. \(a>0\): linearity only. No condition on the slope of \(\varphi\) in the square's coordinates: steep and flat parts are both slope \(\pm1\) in \((t,s)\).

Degenerate cases. lem:monotone-path-ramps at \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi\le|t|\) (the empty down-set): \(R=0\) inside the square, both sides \(0\). At \(\varphi\ge2-|t|+w\) (the whole square below the ramp): \(R=a\), \(\sum_iR(X_i)-N\int R=0\). At \(w=2\), the widest ramp: \(j_0=1\), the bound from the record \(Ca\sqrt{N\log N}\), the order of a Lipschitz function of constant \(a/2\) (lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound's class). At \(w=W\): Step 2 of the second proof is empty, and the ramp is a sharpened lower-layer indicator with the bound \(Ca\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\), of the Leighton–Shor order; that a lower layer can reach this order is the untested hypothesis drawn from the source cited in the anchored increments entry, whose proof was not read.

Corollary (translate staircase stacks)

Statement. cor:translate-staircase-stacks. At \((4,4)\), \(W=2^{-\ell_1}\), on the events of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, of cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at \(\delta_0=W\), of lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor at \(W\) and of Chernoff's bound for the \(W\)-cell counts (probability tending to one), for \(N\) large: for every lattice down-set \(D_0\) with profile \(\varphi\), every \(K\ge1\), \(m\ge1\), with \(D_i=\{s<\varphi(t)-2iW\}\) (\(D_0\) moved \(i\) cells down and left) and \(g=mWy^*\sum_{i<K}1_{D_i}\), the one-height chain whose layers are the \(D_i\), each \(m\) times, if its discrete cost \(\sum_eW^2\psi_4^*(|\Delta_eg|/(2W))\) is at most \(2\) and every \(\partial D_i\), \(i<K\), has grid length at least \(\ell_0>0\), then \(|D(g)|\le C(1+\ell_0^{-1})\sqrt{N\log N}\), \(C\) universal.

Proof. Let \(a=KmWy^*\), \(w=2KW\in W\mathbb Z\), \(v=my^*\). Cost: each \(\partial D_i\) has at least \(\ell_0/W\) edges of increment \(Wv\), and \(\psi_4^*(v/2)\ge\frac v4(\log(v/2))^{1/4}\) (\(v/2\ge y^*/2\ge e^{16}\)), so \(2\ge K\ell_0W\frac v4(\log(v/2))^{1/4}\), that is \(a\le8\ell_0^{-1}(\log(v/2))^{-1/4}\le4\ell_0^{-1}\); and \(v\le8/W^2\le N\). As \(\ell_0>0\), every \(D_i\) is nonempty, so \(K\le1/W\) and \(w\le2\). Case \(v\ge\sqrt{N/\log N}\): every nonzero increment over \(W\) is at least \(v\ge N^{1/3}\), and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c), "if every increment |jump|/delta_0 is 0 or at least y >= 2e^16 and sum_e delta_0^2 psi*_4(|jump|/(2 delta_0)) <= 2 ... for y >= N^c the discrepancy is at most 8 3^(1/4) c^(-1/4) L sqrt(N log N)", at \(c=\frac13\) gives the bound. Case \(v<\sqrt{N/\log N}\). Let \(R\) be the ramp of \(\varphi\) at width \(w\) and height \(a\), \(\bar R\) its \(W\)-cell averages, \(H=g-\bar R\); \(D(g)=D(R)+(D(\bar R)-D(R))+D(H)\), \(D\) the discrepancy against Lebesgue measure, which on cell functions is the cell-averaged one. On the line \(\{t=\mathrm{const}\}\), \(g=(a/K)\#\{i<K:s<\varphi-2iW\}\) and \(R=a\rho((s-\varphi)/w)\) differ by at most \(a/K\) at every point; a \(W\)-cell is a diamond in \((t,s)\), on which \(s-\varphi(t)\) varies by at most \(2W\), so \(R\) varies on it by at most \(2Wa/w=a/K\); so \(|g-R|\le a/K\), \(|R-\bar R|\le a/K\) and \(|H|\le2a/K\) (the bounds \(2a/K\), \(3a/K\) used below are larger), and \(H\), \(\bar R-R\) vanish off the cells meeting the strip \(\{\varphi-w-2W\le s\le\varphi+2W\}\), at most \(CK/W\) cells. (1) lem:monotone-path-ramps, by its proof from the record: \(|D(R)|\le Ca\sqrt N((\log_2(4/w))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\); and \(\log_2(4/w)=\log_2(2v/a)\), so for \(a\le1\), \(a(\log_2(4/w))^{3/4}\le Ca((\log v)^{3/4}+(\log(1/a))^{3/4})\le C\ell_0^{-1}(\log v)^{1/2}+C\), using \(a\le8\ell_0^{-1}(\log(v/2))^{-1/4}\) and \(a(\log(1/a))^{3/4}\le1\), and for \(a>1\), \(\log_2(4/w)\le\log_2(2v)\), so the term is at most \(Ca(\log v)^{3/4}\le C\ell_0^{-1}(\log v)^{1/2}\); in both cases at most \(C(1+\ell_0^{-1})\sqrt{\log N}\). (2) \(D(\bar R)-D(R)=-\sum_i(R-\bar R)(X_i)\), as \(\int(R-\bar R)=0\): given the \(W\)-cell counts, a sum of independent terms of mean zero bounded by \(a/K\), of variance at most \(CK/W\cdot2NW^2(a/K)^2=CNWa^2/K\); Bernstein's inequality with a union over the at most \(4^{2/W}\) profiles \(\varphi\) and the values of \(K\), at \(u=C/W\): \(C a\sqrt{N/K}+Ca/(KW)=Ca\sqrt{N/K}+2Ca/w\), at most \(Ca\sqrt N+Cv\). Alternatively, as the reviewer found, (2) is recorded: \(R-\bar R\) is Lipschitz on each \(W\)-cell with zero cell averages, so lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split at \(j=\ell_1\) gives \(L\sqrt{N\log N}\,\Lambda_{\ell_1}(R)\), and \(\Lambda_{\ell_1}(R)\le(CK/W)(2\sqrt2a/w)W^2=Ca\). (3) cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at \(\delta_0=W\) and its coarse mesh \(2W\) (\(k=\ell_1-1\)): \(|D(H)|\le c\sqrt{N\log N}\,\mathrm{TV}(H)+L\sqrt N\Phi(\mathrm{TV}(H)+24W\sum_Q(\max_QH^++\max_QH^-))\), \(\Phi=7^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\); \(\mathrm{TV}(H)\le\mathrm{TV}(g)+\mathrm{TV}(\bar R)\le2a+Ca\) (each \(\partial D_i\) of grid length at most \(2\), carrying increment \(a/K\); the cell averages of the Lipschitz \(R\) by lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (c)), and the covering sum is over at most \(CK/W\) cells of side \(2W\), each at most \(6a/K\): at most \(Ca\). So \(|D(H)|\le Ca\sqrt{N\log N}\). Adding (1)–(3), with \(a\le4\ell_0^{-1}\) and \(v<\sqrt{N/\log N}\), gives the bound. \(\square\)

Hypotheses, each with its step. \((4,4)\): \(\psi_4^*\)'s lower bound in the cost step and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c). Cost at most \(2\): \(a\le8\ell_0^{-1}(\log(v/2))^{-1/4}\) and \(v\le8/W^2\). \(\ell_0\): the cost step only; translates clipped by the square to short boundaries make the bound depend on it. One multiplicity \(m\) and diagonal translates: \(|g-R|\le2a/K\), the ramp being linear across the stack. \(y^*\ge2e^{16}\): \(v/2\ge e^{16}\). The events: each in its step. No bound on \(K\), \(m\) or the slope of the staircase.

Degenerate cases. cor:translate-staircase-stacks at \(K=1\): one set at height \(mWy^*\), contained in lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) for one layer. At \(m=1\): every edge has multiplicity \(1\), also decided by lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) at \(M=1\). \(D_0\) empty or the square: \(g\) constant, \(D(g)=0\). \(\ell_0\to0\): the bound degrades, the corollary being stated with \(\ell_0\).

Nonvacuity. At the pair \((4,4)\) of the curve's parameters: \(D_0\) the down-set below a staircase that alternates, on blocks of \(t\)-length \(1/8\), runs of horizontal and of vertical edges (slope in \(x,y\) alternating between \(0\) and \(\infty\)), through the centre, its translates for \(i<K\) staying of grid length \(\ell_0\ge1\); \(m\) with \(v=my^*\) the multiple of \(y^*\) nearest \(e^{(\log N)^{1/2}}\), and \(K=\lfloor(2W\psi_4^*(v/2))^{-1}\rfloor\), so that the cost, at most \(2KW\psi_4^*(v/2)\cdot\) per unit grid length \(2\), is at most \(2\): \(K\approx(Wv(\log v)^{1/4})^{-1}\), \(\log K\approx\frac12\log N\), and \(K\le1/(4W)\) so the translates fit. Steps exercised: the corollary's Case two, \(v<\sqrt{N/\log N}\); the ramp at \(w=2KW\approx2/(v(\log v)^{1/4})\), with \(\ell_1-j_0\approx\log_2(w/W)=\log_2(2K)\approx\frac12\log_2N\) levels in the second proof; a staircase with both steep and flat parts; the union over staircases in (2). For this fixed \(D_0\), lem:guided-chain-bound (b) with \(F_N=\{D_i:i<K\}\), at most \(N\) sets fixed before the points are drawn, and linearity, \(|D(g)|\le(a/K)\sum_i(P(D_i)\sqrt{4N\log N}+4\log N)\), decides the witness, and with \(F_N\) all the at most \(1/W\) translates of \(D_0\) every stack of translates of one fixed \(D_0\), every \(K\) and \(m\): \((a/K)\sum_iP(D_i)=\mathrm{TV}(g)\le8(\log(v/2))^{-1/4}\) by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) and \(a=KWv\le v\), so \(|D(g)|\le C\sqrt{N\log N}+Cv\log N\), at the target for \(v<\sqrt{N/\log N}\) and with no \(\ell_0\), the larger \(v\) by the corollary's Case one (the reviewer's finding, checked); what the corollary adds is uniformity over \(D_0\), the staircase chosen after the points. The recorded bounds applied to \(g\) with \(D_0\) free, and to its parts: lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b) with \(M<m\) charges the piles at \((\log v)^{1/4}=(\log N)^{1/8}\) over the target; lem:staircase-bundle-chains needs \(m+1\) bands of room between piles (B2), while consecutive piles are one diagonal cell apart; lem:band-family-discrepancy (b), (c) need a graph of bounded slope in one orientation, while \(\partial D_0\) has runs of each orientation of length \(\frac18\); lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) at \(y=v\) charges \((\log N)^{3/4}(\log v)^{-1/4}=(\log N)^{5/8}\); lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) at the \(Km\) layers needs \(\log(Km)\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(y^*/2))^{1/3}\), while \(\log K\approx\frac12\log N\); lem:multilevel-chain-bound (c) has \(K\) distinct values with \(\log K\approx\frac12\log N>(\log N)^{2/3}\), outside its \(K\le e^{(\log N)^{2/3}}\), and its (b) needs \(\log K\le(\log N)^{2/3}(\log(v/2))^{1/3}=(\log N)^{5/6}\), which \(\frac12\log N\) exceeds for \(N\) large; per-set bounds summed over the \(K\) translates, each a lower layer at height \(a/K\), give \(a\sqrt N(\log N)^{3/4}\), \(a\approx(\log v)^{-1/4}\), that is \((\log N)^{5/8}\) over \(\sqrt N\); blocks of consecutive translates are smaller stacks of the same form; the two-scale split at \(w\) (Owed attempt) leaves \((\log K)^{3/4}a\); thm:monotone-product-chains and cor:monotone-product-chain-bound ask \(h\) constant on columns, while the staircase's horizontal runs make \(g\) vary along columns; thm:anchored-increment-functions, with lem:anchored-level-sum, asks every increment at least \(1/\lambda\) of the larger value, while the inner piles have increment \(v\) at values up to \(Kv\), \(K\to\infty\); lem:dyadic-level-sum counts only boundary edges of the support, the outer pile, and leaves the inner piles to the per-layer factor; lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound bounds a set inside a half-plane with boundary on its line, while the translates' boundaries are staircases, on no line. Plainest bound. This \(g\) is one fixed function, decided by its variance; the plainest uniform bound over the class, a union over its at most \(4^{2/W}N^2\) members with Bernstein's inequality, gives \(\sqrt{2N\sigma^2u}+bu\) with \(u\approx1/W\), \(b=a\) and \(\sigma^2\le a^2\), of order \(a\sqrt{N/W}\), far above the target; lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a), the plainest recorded uniform bound, leaves \((\log N)^{1/8}\); what the corollary adds is one bound at the target for every translate stack, at every multiplicity.

Baseline. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (b): every translate stack within \((\log(my^*))^{1/4}\) of the target; lem:staircase-bundle-chains: the evenly spaced stack at the target. Composed. lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound applied alone to \(g\), or with linearity to blocks of translates, keeps the factor \((\log(my^*))^{1/4}\) on each block; lem:staircase-bundle-chains applied alone to blocks needs (B2) room inside each block, which bunched translates lack at every block size above one translate, and one translate per block is the per-set sum above; lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) applied alone decides \(my^*\ge N^{c}\) (Case one of the proof) and nothing below; lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (a) applied alone to each translate is the per-set sum; cor:fine-mesh-function-tube applied alone at its mesh \(w\) is the two-scale split, \((\log K)^{3/4}\); lem:band-family-discrepancy (b) applied alone to the ramp, in the square's coordinates, needs a bounded slope, which the staircase lacks in both orientations; lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d) and lem:multilevel-chain-bound applied alone to \(g\) need \(\log K\) small; lem:mesh-function-discrepancy (b), (c) applied alone to \(E_wR\) is Step 3 (i) of the second proof; with lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split's cellwise remainder \(\Lambda_j\), which covers the levels between \(w\) and \(W\), it decides the ramp whole (the proof from the record); lem:guided-chain-bound (b) applied with linearity to the translates of one fixed staircase decides every stack of that staircase (Nonvacuity).

Record comparison. From the record's side: lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split bounds every bounded function Lipschitz on the cells of a mesh \(2^{-j}\) by the cell averages' variation at \(j^{3/4}\) and a cellwise Lipschitz remainder; applied at the ramp's own mesh it gives lem:monotone-path-ramps for every \(1\)-Lipschitz profile, without lattice values and without the \((a/w)\log N\) term, so the lemma is a special case of it (registered with that relation), and its chaining proof is a second proof, not a new result; lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b), a newer version of lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, gives the same. lem:band-family-discrepancy bounds bands along graphs of bounded slope; the ramps of monotone profiles need no slope bound, and the record's cellwise split covers them. For the stacks: lem:guided-chain-bound (b) with linearity decides every stack of translates of one staircase fixed before the points are drawn; lem:staircase-bundle-chains bounds piled monotone paths with room (B2)–(B4) and allows distinct paths; cor:translate-staircase-stacks asks no room, asks translates one cell apart, and holds uniformly over the staircase, which is what it adds. It is a composition of recorded statements (the reviewer's second pass): the ramp by lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split at \(j_0\), the cell-averaging step by the same lemma at \(j=\ell_1\) (or by Bernstein's inequality with a union over the at most \(4^{2/W}\) staircases, the proof written above), the texture by cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at its coarse mesh \(2W\), and large \(v\) by lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c); what is not in the record is the decomposition \(g=R+(\bar R-R)+H\) along the stack. The nearest by wording are related in the spec: lem:mesh-function-discrepancy, lem:lipschitz-class-lower-bound (the order at \(w=2\)), lem:grid-flow-duality (wording only); lem:dominant-level-split refines lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split's cost-bounded corollary for functions whose larger partial is at least \(y\), neither more general nor a special case of the ramp lemma, which needs no cost bound. Beside the corollary, each neither more general nor a special case: thm:anchored-increment-functions and lem:anchored-level-sum (anchored increments, while a stack's inner piles are not anchored), thm:monotone-product-chains (\(h\) constant on columns, while a staircase stack varies along columns), lem:dyadic-level-sum (the support's boundary only), lem:fixed-line-boundary-bound (a set in a half-plane with boundary on its line, while staircases lie on no line).

New mathematics. cor:translate-staircase-stacks: at \((4,4)\), every one-height chain of cost at most \(2\) whose layers are \(K\) translates of one lattice down-set one diagonal cell apart, each \(m\) times, with boundaries of grid length at least \(\ell_0\), has discrepancy at most \(C(1+\ell_0^{-1})\sqrt{N\log N}\), every \(K\) and \(m\), uniformly over the down-set, by a composition of recorded statements along the decomposition into ramp, cell averaging and step texture; for a down-set fixed in advance lem:guided-chain-bound (b) already gave it, with no \(\ell_0\). lem:monotone-path-ramps, every ramp along any down-set's boundary at the order \(a\sqrt N((\log_2(4/w))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})\), is a special case of lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, here with a second proof by chaining over coarse monotone approximations, which carries an extra \(C(a/w+a)\log N\). No step of either is new beyond the decomposition.

Goal progress. Unchanged: cor:coarse-discrete-sufficiency (b)'s hypothesis asks every one-height nested chain, and the corollary proves it for the stacks of translates one cell apart with boundaries of grid length at least \(\ell_0\). Bearing. At \((4,4)\), every stack of \(K\) translates of one lattice down-set one diagonal cell apart, in piles of one multiplicity, with boundaries of grid length at least a fixed \(\ell_0\), is at the target uniformly over the down-set (the curve's parameters, the pair \((4,4)\)); and, by lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split, a ramp of height \(a\) and width \(w\) along any monotone path is charged \((\log_2(4/w))^{3/4}\), the \(\frac34\) power of the number of dyadic scales between \(w\) and \(1\), the scales between \(W\) and \(w\) costing nothing beyond \(\sqrt{\log N}\). Not covered. Translates spaced \(p\ge2\) cells apart with \(p\le m\) (a sketch for them is listed among the reviewer's suggestions); stacks of distinct nested staircases; piles of varying multiplicity; chains mixing these with anchored increments; and translates clipped by the square to grid length below every fixed \(\ell_0\), small corner down-sets among them.

Reviewer's suggestions, unverified

  • Translates spaced \(p\) cells apart, \(D_i=\{s<\varphi-2ipW\}\), \(1\le p\le m+1\): \(w=2pKW\), the texture by cor:fine-mesh-function-tube at the coarse mesh \(pW\), \(\Phi\approx(2\log_2p+5)^{3/4}\), the covering term still \(Ca\); in all \(a(\log p)^{3/4}\le C(\log v)^{1/2}\), and for \(p\ge m+1\) lem:staircase-bundle-chains has room, so translates at every spacing. Record. "function Lipschitz on each cell cellwise remainder partition adapted local width nested profiles interpolating ramp" returned lem:tube-localized-discrepancy, lem:band-family-discrepancy, lem:local-factor-discrepancy, lem:mollified-smooth-part and lem:cellwise-lipschitz-split; none bounds translates at a spacing \(p\ge2\).
  • Blocks: keeping the corollary's \(a\)-dependence, \(Ca_b\sqrt N((\log(2v/a_b))^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N})+Cv_b\log N\) per block, summed with Jensen's inequality on \(a(\log(1/a))^{3/4}\), handles \(n\) blocks of translates at one \(v\) when \(\log n\lesssim(\log N)^{2/3}(\log v)^{1/3}\). Record. The same search; no recorded statement bounds unions of translate blocks.
  • Distinct nested staircases: the piecewise-linear interpolating ramp has \(1\)-Lipschitz level curves and \(|G-R|\le a/K\); lem:local-factor-discrepancy (b) on a partition with cells of the local stack width, and the texture at a coarse mesh of the local gap, heuristically give \(a\sqrt N[(\log1/w)^{3/4}+(\log r)^{3/4}+\sqrt{\log N}\cdot\) (mean over minimal gap per cell)\(]\), at the target unless gaps are very uneven inside one cell, which a split into clusters with the block suggestion would handle; a plain joint chaining with a union over groups costs about \(a\sqrt N\) per level and is unlikely to work; no counterexample found. Record.
